stands.title: Siren `duration`: the dispatcher reads a bare number as milliseconds, the siren model reads the same key as seconds
stands.evidence: Quotes verified verbatim. custom_dp_dispatcher.go:669 `func (d *CustomDPDispatcher) dispatchSiren(` … :675-680 `if durRaw, ok := p["duration"]; ok {` / `dur, err := anyToDuration(durRaw)` / `cfg.Duration = dur`; :681 `} else if secRaw, ok := p["duration_seconds"]; ok {` … :686 `cfg.Duration = time.Duration(sec * float64(time.Second))`. anyToDuration at :1077, numeric branch :1089 `return time.Duration(ms * float64(time.Millisecond)), nil` with the doc comment :1076 `//   - number (float64, int, …): treated as milliseconds`. Model side: internal/model/custom/siren/payload.go:97-99 inside `s.RegisterService("turn_on", …)` (registered at :90-91): `if d, err := payload.ParamFloat64(params, "duration"); err == nil {` / `dur := time.Duration(d * float64(time.Second))` / `cfg.Duration = dur`. Both sides are live and reach the same siren.TurnOn(cfg): dispatcher — cmd/openccu-loom/daemon.go:767 `customDPDispatcher := adapter.NewCustomDPDispatcher(reg).SetAuditRecorder(auditRec)`, consumed by internal/north/rest/handlers/custom_data_points.go:384 and internal/north/rest/ws/custom_data_points.go:157 and (MQTT cdp-invoke topic) internal/central/adapter/mqtt_sink.go:303 `return s.cdpDispatch.InvokeCustomDP(...)` from internal/north/mqtt/command_subscriber.go:1303; registry handler — internal/north/mqtt/command_subscriber.go:533 subscribes `base+"/+/+/+/+/custom/+/set/+"` → handleServiceMethod (:761) → cdpSink.InvokeChannelService (:797) → internal/central/adapter/mqtt_sink.go:342 `return src.Invoke(ctx, method, params, priority)`, i.e. the siren's own ServiceRegistry handler. Neither site is test-only. The dispatcher's siren branch never consults "seconds" (only "duration"/"duration_seconds"), unlike onTimeParam at :985-1009 whose comment reads `// canonical key is "seconds" (a JSON number of seconds) — the shape every SPA CDP widget emits`; the SPA's own SirenTile.svelte:148 invokes turn_on with no params, so the exposed callers are REST/WS/MQTT clients.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, dispatchSiren would have routed "duration" through onTimeParam/requireOnTime (as dispatchSwitch turn_on_for and dispatchIrrigation do) or anyToDuration's numeric branch would have multiplied by time.Second — I would have seen `time.Second` at custom_dp_dispatcher.go:1089 or an `onTimeParam(p)` call at :675. Line 1089 reads `time.Millisecond` and :676 reads `anyToDuration(durRaw)`, so the two units differ.
stands.reason: Both spellings are live on the same operation, and they already disagree on a concrete input. Divergence reaches the wire, not just the type: cfg.Duration goes to siren.TurnOn (internal/model/custom/siren/siren.go:326-330) which calls custom.EncodeTimerDuration; that function (internal/model/custom/mixins.go:219-249) converts to seconds and truncates via `clamp` → int32. Guard: internal/central/adapter/custom_dp_dispatcher_test.go:2208 (`TestDispatchSwitch_TurnOnFor_DurationBareNumberMilliseconds`) pins the ms reading for the generic switch path only; the siren tests at :1102 and :1114 use `"duration": "5s"` (string) and `duration_seconds: 5.0` — no bare-number siren case, and no test compares the two planes. One correction to the candidate's damage text: with cfg.Duration == 0 the siren is not left on indefinitely — siren.go:331-336 falls back to `s.duration.DefaultDuration()` when a duration DP exists; the caller still silently gets a duration it did not ask for.
stands.divergence: params {"duration": 30} on a siren turn_on. REST/WS/MQTT-cdp-invoke plane: anyToDuration(30.0) = 30ms → EncodeTimerDuration(30ms) → secs 0.03 → clamp → DURATION_VALUE=0, DURATION_UNIT=S. MQTT per-service-method plane (.../custom/siren/set/turn_on): 30 * time.Second → DURATION_VALUE=30, DURATION_UNIT=S. Same key, same device, wire values 0 vs 30. Second diverging input: {"seconds": 30} — dispatchSiren ignores the key entirely (cfg.Duration stays 0, no error), the model handler also ignores it; every other timed op in the dispatcher accepts it.
stands.deadCopy: none — both sides have production callers
stands.guard: none for this pair; custom_dp_dispatcher_test.go:2208 covers only the switch path
stands.secondReason: Survived every bite. Quotes and line numbers current. Sameness: the strongest defence — 'two readings of one datum, each right for its caller' — only half holds. The model's seconds reading is defensible as HA's own siren vocabulary on the HA command_topic, but the dispatcher's siren reading is NOT defensible as the invoke plane's own convention: the invoke plane's canonical timed key is `seconds` (custom_dp_dispatcher.go:986-989, `// The canonical key is "seconds" (a JSON number of seconds) — the shape every SPA CDP widget emits`), used by every other timed op (:297, :752, :760, :804), and dispatchSiren accepts neither `seconds` nor the helper — it invents a third vocabulary (`duration` = ms, `duration_seconds`). Divergence reproduced by reading both paths: params {"duration": 30} on the invoke plane yields DURATION_VALUE=0 / DURATION_UNIT=S on the wire; the same JSON on `<central>/<iface>/<dev>/<ch>/custom/<name>/set/turn_on` yields DURATION_VALUE=30 / UNIT=S. The mirror case also diverges: {"duration": "5s"} is 5 s on the invoke plane and is silently dropped by the model handler (payload.ParamFloat64, internal/payload/params.go:75-79, ParseFloat("5s") fails → the `err == nil` guard skips the assignment). Damage is observable on the wire, not merely typed. Two corrections to the candidate text, neither fatal: (1) the caller does not get 'no duration' — siren.go:331-336 falls back to `s.duration.DefaultDuration()` only when cfg.Duration <= 0, and 30 ms is > 0, so the fallback does NOT fire and the device is written a literal 0; (2) severity lowered from high to medium because no in-repo caller emits the divergent input — SirenTile.svelte invokes `turn_on` with no params at all (`onClick={() => invoke("turn_on")}`, :148) — so reaching it requires a third-party REST/WS/MQTT client, and the invoke params for siren turn_on are documented nowhere in assets/openapi.yaml or docs/ (grep for a siren duration unit returned nothing).

stands.title: LINK-profile constraint matching is implemented twice and the two copies have already drifted on float equality and on numeric strings
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false I would have seen one of two things: the same comparison on both sides (both `floatsEqual` or both `!=`, both parsing strings or both refusing them), or one matcher with no non-test caller. I saw neither — the two bodies differ verbatim at three points, and grep for callers returned a production file for each (uischema_link.go:144 and link_profiles_adapter.go:130, wired at ws_adapters.go:221). A third control: had the two surfaces been reading different archives or different value sources, the divergence would be moot; both resolve to ccudata.ProfilesFS() and to CcuBackend.GetLinkParamset.
stands.reason: Two live copies of the same decision, already differing in three verified ways, with no guard tying them together. The damage is what the candidate states: the SPA LINK form and the WS link-profiles command can report different active profiles for the same link at the same moment.
stands.divergence: Three concrete inputs, each read out of the code or the archive rather than assumed. (1) Numeric string: current = {"SHORT_ON_TIME": "0"} (Go string) against a fixed constraint value 0 — adapter toFloat("0") = (0, true) → constraint satisfied → matchActiveProfile can return that profile's id; store toFloat64("0") = (0, false) → profileMatches returns false at store.go:434-437 for the whole profile → MatchActiveProfile returns 0. (2) Float tolerance: current["SHORT_DIM_STEP"] = 0.049999999 against the archive's fixed value 0.05 — that constraint exists, verified in the data: DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER.json.gz carries SHORT_DIM_STEP fixed 0.05 in 26 profiles, UNIVERSAL_ACTOR.json.gz likewise, 2853 non-integer fixed values in the archive overall. Adapter: 0.049999999 != 0.05 → no match. Store: |diff| = 1e-9 <= 1e-6 → match. (3) Sender-type aliasing, a fourth drift at the enclosing site: the adapter resolves the sender key through senderTypeAliases + _VIRTUAL_ stripping (link_profile.go:60-64, :68-89), the store does a bare map lookup (store.go:284-286 `profs, ok := bucket[senderChannelType]`, and GetLinkProfiles at store.go:236-239 likewise; only the *receiver* is aliased, store.go:211-216). I decompressed all 66 archives: no file carries a `_VIRTUAL_` sender key, none carries SHUTTER_CONTACT_TRANSCEIVER or MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER; PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER appears in 14 files and SHUTTER_CONTACT in 31. So for senderType "SHUTTER_CONTACT_TRANSCEIVER" the adapter finds the SHUTTER_CONTACT profile set and can report an active id, while the store finds nothing and the WS command returns no profiles at all. The premise that the CCU reports these spellings comes from the repo's own comment at link_profile.go:50-56 ("Without this mapping ... the active-profile detector returns 0 for every link originating from a HmIP-RF device"), not from a live CCU read.
stands.deadCopy: neither — both sides have a production caller (uischema_link.go:144 / uischema_adapter.go:404 for the adapter copy; link_profiles_adapter.go:130 via cmd/openccu-loom/ws_adapters.go:221 for the store copy)
stands.guard: none
stands.secondReason: Survived every bite. Quotes and line numbers are current and verbatim. Sameness holds: both copies decode the same embedded archive, receive the same paramset map from the same backend call, and both document themselves as porting the same reference match_active_profile — this is one rule written twice, not one datum read two ways (the type difference, raw JSON vs typed struct, is a representation choice made in ccudata for UI pass-through, not a different question being asked). Liveness holds for both: the adapter copy backs the SPA's REST ui-schema for LINK and MASTER, the store copy backs the declared WS command links.get_profiles. Divergence is established from history rather than from a convention: the tolerance fix landed in exactly one copy (98b00086, store only) while the other is untouched since the initial release, and the commit's own changelog describes the user-visible defect that copy still has — a device reporting no active profile instead of the right one. Damage is therefore not prospective but present on the SPA side, over 2853 non-integer fixed constraints measured in the shipped archive. No guard ties the copies. The two weaker claimed inputs (numeric strings, sender aliasing) are real code divergences whose live occurrence I could not establish from any source, and I have said so rather than counting them as evidence.

stands.title: The post-trigger-disarm transition exists twice and the restore copy never schedules the auto-rearm
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, the grep for scheduleAutoRearmIfConfigured would have returned a second production call site inside restore.go (or restore.go:525-531 would assign a.autoRearmMode / call e.scheduleAutoRearm), and autorearm_test.go would contain a restart driven from the triggered state rather than only after a live disarm. Both greps returned the opposite.
stands.reason: Confirmed as a live divergence with a second, already-observable difference beyond the missing timer: the restore copy also omits the `disarmed_post_trigger` journal entry (hmenum.AlarmJournalClassDisarm) and the a.cancelTimers() call, so an operator reading the journal after a restore-completed post-trigger disarm sees the incident close with no disarm entry at all, while the live path emits one. Severity high because a zone configured with auto_rearm_s is left permanently unprotected on this path and the persisted state row carries no evidence of it.
stands.divergence: Zone cfg: PostTrigger=disarm, AutoRearmSeconds=30, armed full, window sensor trips, daemon killed while triggered, restarted after the trigger window has elapsed (restore.go:465 `deadline.Sub(now) <= 0` → restore.go:475 finishTriggeredOnRestore). Live path (same zone, no restart): zone → disarmed AND scheduleAutoRearmIfConfigured sets a.autoRearmMode=full plus a 30s timer, journals `auto_rearm_scheduled`, and the zone re-arms to full after 30s. Restore path: zone → disarmed with a.autoRearmMode empty, no timer in timers_json, no `auto_rearm_scheduled` and no `disarmed_post_trigger` journal entry, and the zone never re-arms.
stands.deadCopy: neither — both copies have production callers
stands.guard: none. autorearm_test.go has two restore tests (TestAutoRearm_RestoreResumesTheRemainingQuietPeriod:198, TestAutoRearm_RestoreElapsedWhileDownRearmsImmediately:218) but both call triggerAndDisarm(h) first (autorearm_test.go:44-53), which completes the disarm live via finishTriggered so autoRearmMode is already persisted before h.restart. restore_test.go:385 TestRestore_TriggeredWindowElapsedDisarmPolicy does drive the gap path but its zone config (defaultZoneConfig + PostTrigger=disarm) sets no AutoRearmSeconds and it asserts only h.wantState("eg", disarmed) plus fireCount()==0.
stands.secondReason: Quote, line numbers, liveness of both copies and the divergence all hold; nothing upstream filters the input (PostTrigger and AutoRearmSeconds are ordinary zone config, and the restored a.mode carries the pre-incident mode the live copy uses). One narrowing to the candidate's second observable difference: the missing a.cancelTimers() is not observable on this path — neither restore.go:416 nor :475 has scheduled a state timer before the call (scheduleStateTimer only runs on the implausible-clock branch at :454 and the remaining>0 branch at :479, both of which return), so cancelTimers would be a no-op there. The missing `disarmed_post_trigger` Disarm-class journal entry is real and observable. High severity stands: a configured zone is left permanently unprotected after a crash-restart that lands past the trigger window.

stands.title: The ENUM wire-form decision is answered three different ways, and the descriptor-derived flag has no consumer
stands.evidence:
All three quotes verified verbatim.

(a) The descriptor-derived rule: internal/model/generic/datapoint.go:1905-1912 `// EnumValueIsIndex reports whether ENUM values for this parameter should be\n// sent as integer indices (HM devices) rather than string values (HmIP\n// devices).` / `func (d *DataPoint[T]) EnumValueIsIndex() bool {\n\treturn d.enumValueIsIndex\n}`, computed at datapoint.go:366 from `enumValueIsIndexFromDescriptor(cfg.Descriptor)` (datapoint.go:1933-1953: TYPE == ENUM, non-empty VALUE_LIST, and MIN parseable as a plain integer with no '.'/'e'/'E'). `grep -rn "EnumValueIsIndex\|enumValueIsIndex" --include="*.go" .` returns hits only at datapoint.go:275, 276, 366, 1903, 1905, 1911, 1912, 1924, 1933 and in internal/model/generic/datapoint_unconfirmed_status_test.go:366-415. No production caller anywhere.

(b) internal/model/generic/action_select.go:131-144 always sends the label once VALUE_LIST is non-empty: `\t// When a VALUE_LIST is present the wire value is the string label, not the\n\t// integer index. Devices without a VALUE_LIST use integer indices — those\n\t// callers should use TriggerIndex directly.` … `\t_ = idx // index validated above; not used for the wire call when labels are present` … `return a.Writer.SetValue(ctx, a.Key.ChannelAddress, hmenum.Parameter(a.Key.Parameter), label, priority)`.

(c) internal/model/generic/select.go:50-58 and :61-74 always send the integer: `SetLabel` resolves via `labelIndex` and tail-calls `s.SetIndex(ctx, int32(idx), priority)`, which ends in `return s.sendAndObserve(ctx, idx, idx, priority)` (select.go:58).

Both (b) and (c) are live: internal/central/adapter/datapoint_resolver.go:132-136 and :168-170 build an ActionSelect for a write-only parameter with a VALUE_LIST; :150-151 builds a Select for a read+write ENUM.

The cited gold standard says the opposite of what the Go comment claims it says. action_select.go:119-122 states `// The distinction mirrors the _enum_value_is_index logic in the reference\n// implementation (action_select.py:43-60): a non-empty VALUE_LIST with at\n// least one entry means "send the string label"; an empty list means\n// "send the integer index".` The cited lines, /Users/markus/Documents/GitHub/aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/generic/action_select.py:43-53, read `def _prepare_value_for_sending(...)` … `if self._values and value in self._values:` / `# For string-based ENUMs (HmIP), send the string value directly.` / `# For index-based ENUMs (HM), convert string to index.` / `if self._enum_value_is_index:` / `return self._values.index(value)` / `return str(value)`. VALUE_LIST presence is the precondition, not the answer; the answer is the flag. select.py:44-47 and action.py:35-38 consult the same flag. The reference source of the flag is data_point.py:1405-1410: `# HM devices use integer MIN/MAX/DEFAULT → send as index.\n# HmIP devices use string MIN/MAX/DEFAULT → send as string.` — the same rule the Go port computes and then never reads.
stands.negativeControl: Had the flag been consumed, `grep -rn "EnumValueIsIndex"` would have returned a call site outside internal/model/generic/datapoint.go and *_test.go; it returns none. Had the reference agreed with the Go comment, aiohomematic select.py:44-47 and action_select.py:51-53 would have read `return str(value)` unconditionally instead of branching on `if self._enum_value_is_index:`. Had the two Go paths agreed with each other, Select.SetLabel would have passed `label` to sendAndObserve rather than `int32(idx)`.
stands.reason: Confirmed as stated, and stronger than the candidate framed it: the descriptor-derived flag is not merely a third opinion, it is the gold standard's rule, ported faithfully (datapoint.go:1933-1953 mirrors data_point.py:1405-1410) and then wired to nothing, while the two live paths each hard-code one branch of it. The Go comment that justifies the ActionSelect branch misquotes its own cited line range. Severity high: these are writes that reach real CCU hardware, both directions are wrong for one device family, and nothing anywhere pins the wire form. I do not claim to know what the CCU returns for a wrong-form write — the candidate's 'fault -5' is unverified and would need a live write — but 'which form is intended' is answered by the repo's own designated reference, not by a convention I supplied.
stands.divergence: Two concrete separating inputs, in opposite directions. (1) HmIP shape — TYPE=ENUM, VALUE_LIST ["AUTO-MODE","MANU-MODE"], MIN a JSON string, OPERATIONS read+write: enumValueIsIndexFromDescriptor returns false (datapoint.go:1938-1941, parseFloat on a quoted MIN fails), so the reference (select.py:45-47) sends the string "MANU-MODE"; the Go Select.SetLabel sends int32(1). (2) HM shape — VALUE_LIST ["OFF","ON"], MIN the integer 0, OPERATIONS write-only: the flag is true, so the reference (action_select.py:51-52) sends index 1; the Go ActionSelect.TriggerLabel sends the string "ON" (action_select.go:138-144). The two live Go paths also disagree with each other on one descriptor: an ENUM with VALUE_LIST ["OFF","ON"] and integer MIN writes the string "ON" when the parameter is write-only and int32(1) when the same parameter is readable — the READ bit is the only thing that differs.
stands.deadCopy: internal/model/generic/datapoint.go:1905-1912 — (*DataPoint[T]).EnumValueIsIndex has no production caller; the field is computed at datapoint.go:366 on every DataPoint and read only by internal/model/generic/datapoint_unconfirmed_status_test.go:376, :390, :401, :414.
stands.guard: None on the wire form. The four EnumValueIsIndex tests (datapoint_unconfirmed_status_test.go:366-415) assert only that the flag computes correctly from the descriptor — they would stay green with every write path sending the wrong form, because nothing reads the flag.
stands.secondReason: Confirmed, and the damage leg is now measured rather than asserted. I first attacked the divergence with the repo's own snapshot data and found the *supporting* fleet argument (used by an earlier audit, notes/audits/2026-08-16-post-0.61-audit-findings.json:627: '16999/16999 ENUM dps integer-MIN … zero string-based ENUMs exist') is an artefact: tests/integration/model_snapshot_test.go:415 emits `Min: decodeTyped(desc.Min, desc.Type)` and decodeTyped sends ENUM through coerceInt (:582-583), which maps a non-numeric string to 0 (:635-643). The snapshot therefore cannot distinguish MIN forms, and both my own recount (16999/16999 int, 868/868 int) and the earlier audit's are void. So I measured the wire source the repo actually pins — github.com/SukramJ/godevccu v0.2.2 (go.mod:6), internal/embed/data/paramset_descriptions, 399 files — counting ENUM parameters that carry a VALUE_LIST, by MIN JSON type and OPERATIONS. VALUES paramset: str-MIN read+write = 64 (e.g. HmIPW-STHD WINDOW_STATE MIN="CLOSED", HEATING_COOLING MIN="HEATING"; HmIP-eTRV-B1 WINDOW_STATE), int-MIN read+write = 25, str-MIN write-only = 471 (ACCESS_AUTHORIZATION, DOOR_COMMAND, SELF_CALIBRATION), int-MIN write-only = 10 (HM-RC-19-B BACKLIGHT/BEEP/UNIT, SHEV_POS). Both wrong directions are instantiated: the 64 str-MIN writable VALUES enums route to Select, which sends int32 where the reference sends the label; the 10 int-MIN write-only enums route to ActionSelect, which sends the label where the reference sends the index. And pkg/hmproto/parameter.go:23 `Min json.RawMessage` confirms the Go side preserves the wire form, so the flag would report the right answer if anyone read it. Severity stays high: operator-reachable writes on real device families, contradicting the repo's designated CCU-side gold standard in both directions, with the deciding flag dead and no by_design entry.

stands.title: The device-to-channel address rule is re-derived in six places, in three different spellings — and two of the six copies have no production caller at all
stands.evidence:
All eight quoted lines verified verbatim, plus a ninth the candidate missed. `grep -n "prefix := \|like := " internal/store/sqlite/*.go` returns exactly:
  channel_flags.go:119 `prefix := deviceAddress + ":"`
  measurements.go:1217 `prefix := deviceAddr + ":%"`
  measurements.go:1234 `prefix := deviceAddr + ":%"`  (missed by the candidate)
  measurements.go:1844 `prefix := deviceAddress + ":"`
  master_values.go:186 `prefix := strings.TrimRight(deviceAddress, ":") + ":"`
  paramsets.go:259 `like := deviceAddress + ":%"`
  paramsets.go:311 `prefix := strings.TrimRight(deviceAddress, ":") + ":"`
  recording_overrides.go:124 `prefix := deviceAddress + ":"`
  values_cache.go:433 `prefix := strings.TrimRight(deviceAddress, ":") + ":"`
The owner of the grammar is pkg/hmtypes/address.go:16 `const addressSeparator = ':'` with ChannelAddress()/DeviceAddress()/SplitChannelAddress(); it exposes no join-a-device-to-its-channel-prefix helper, so all nine sites bypass it.
Liveness (grep for callers, _test.go excluded):
  values_cache.DeleteDevice — LIVE: internal/central/adapter/values_cache_evict.go:60, internal/central/cachereset/cachereset.go:337, cmd/hmcli/cache.go:300, cmd/openccu-loom/values_cache_handler_adapter.go:46
  master_values.DeleteDevice — LIVE: internal/central/adapter/master_values_evict.go:64, cachereset.go:349, cmd/hmcli/cache.go:303
  paramsets.DeleteDevice — LIVE: cachereset.go:329, cmd/hmcli/cache.go:311
  channel_flags.DeleteDevice — LIVE: internal/central/adapter/channel_flags_evict.go:67
  measurements.go:1217/1234 (readEnergyTier/foldRawEnergy) — LIVE via QueryEnergy ← cmd/openccu-loom/energy_handler_adapter.go:56
  measurements.DeleteDevice — NO production caller; only measurements_test.go:401,451,776
  recording_overrides.DeleteDevice — NO production caller; only recording_overrides_test.go:85
  paramsets.GetChannelAddressesByParamsetKey — NO production caller; the only non-test call, internal/central/coordinators/device.go:1436, resolves to the identically-named in-memory ParamsetRegistry method (internal/central/registry/paramset.go:179), not the store.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, the nine sites would have read one identical expression, or delegated to a single helper in pkg/hmtypes. The grep would then have returned one spelling (or a hmtypes call). It returned three distinct spellings across six files. For the dead-copy half: had it been false, grep for `DeleteDevice(` outside internal/store/sqlite would have shown a measurement/override evictor or cachereset branch; internal/central/adapter contains exactly three evict files (channel_flags, master_values, values_cache) and cachereset.clearUnit touches exactly four stores (Devices, Paramsets, Values, Master).
stands.reason: Confirmed, but the damage is not the one the candidate wrote. The claimed "cleanup fan-out over six tables on device removal" does not exist: MeasurementStore.DeleteDevice (measurements.go:1838) and RecordingOverrideStore.DeleteDevice (recording_overrides.go:118) have no production caller — measurement history across all three tiers and the recording overrides are NEVER purged when a device is unpaired, which is exactly the resurfacing measurements.go:1846-1851's own comment says the multi-tier delete exists to prevent. That is the stronger finding (a copy with no production caller). The drift half is real too: the DeviceRemovedEvent fan-out drives three live copies from one input (ev.Address) — values_cache_evict.go:60 and master_values_evict.go:64 use the TrimRight spelling, channel_flags_evict.go:67 uses the raw one.
stands.divergence: deviceAddress = "ABC12:" (trailing colon). master_values.go:186 / values_cache.go:433 / paramsets.go:311 → prefix "ABC12:" → `LIKE 'ABC12:' || '%'` → deletes ABC12:0, ABC12:1, … ; channel_flags.go:119 / measurements.go:1844 / recording_overrides.go:124 → prefix "ABC12::" → `LIKE 'ABC12::%'` → deletes nothing. On the DeviceRemovedEvent path all three of those live evictors read the same ev.Address, so that one input clears values_cache and master_values while leaving channel_flags. Reachability caveat, stated as unverified: nothing between internal/central/rpcserver/xmlrpc_server.go:393 → coordinators/device.go:784 → the event validates the address (no hmtypes.IsDeviceAddress call on that path), so whether the CCU's deleteDevices callback can deliver a trailing-colon address is a firmware question the repo does not answer. Second, fully reachable diverging input: measurements.go:1217/1234 build `deviceAddr + ":%"` for `channel_address LIKE ?` with NO ESCAPE clause at all (measurements.go:1095, :1105), while every DELETE declares `ESCAPE '\'` — see store-sqlite-c003.
stands.deadCopy: internal/store/sqlite/measurements.go:1838 (MeasurementStore.DeleteDevice) and internal/store/sqlite/recording_overrides.go:118 (RecordingOverrideStore.DeleteDevice) — test-only. Also internal/store/sqlite/paramsets.go:251 (GetChannelAddressesByParamsetKey, the `":%"` spelling) — test-only; the live method of that name is internal/central/registry/paramset.go:179.
stands.guard: None for the join direction. tests/contract/address_rule_single_source_test.go:46 (TestAddressSplittingHasOneSource) guards only the split direction and matches on `strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(fn.Name.Name), "deviceaddress")` (:57) — the store's prefix builders are expressions inside methods named DeleteDevice, so the guard structurally cannot see them. Per-store prefix-safety tests exist (internal/store/sqlite/master_values_test.go:245, values_cache_test.go:217, both using DEVICE vs DEVICE2) but each pins one store in isolation; nothing compares the stores to each other, and neither uses a trailing-colon input.
stands.secondReason:
Survives on the dead-copy half, which is the stronger half and is fully verified: measurement history across all three tiers and every recording override survive an unpair, while the doc comments of both methods claim the removal caller. The candidate's ordering is right.

I could NOT reproduce the drift half's damage, and downgrade it to unverified: the two spellings only meet on one reachable input on the DeviceRemovedEvent path (values_cache + master_values use TrimRight, channel_flags does not), and they diverge only for an address with a trailing colon. Every other consumer is spelling-consistent — cachereset.go:329/337/349 and cmd/hmcli/cache.go:300-311 drive only paramsets/values/master, all three TrimRight. ev.Address on the removal path originates in coordinators/device.go:789 from CCU-supplied addresses (xmlrpc_server.go:393 → callback_handlers.go:609 / HandleDeleteDevices) with no hmtypes address validation anywhere between, so whether a trailing-colon address can arrive is a firmware property the repository does not carry. Reported as unverified, not as a defect.

stands.title: Address-keyed first-match resolution routes writes to the alphabetically first central, for addresses the code itself enumerates as repeating on every CCU
stands.evidence: Both quotes verified verbatim. devices.go:226-234: `deviceAddr := deviceAddressOf(channelAddress)` / `for _, u := range a.registry.List() {` / `dev, ok := u.ModelRegistry.Get(deviceAddr)` / `if !ok { continue }` / `return a.writer.SetValue(ctx, u.Name(), dev.InterfaceID, channelAddress, parameter, value, priority)`. devices.go:53-63 carries the cited comment word for word, including "the virtual-remote roots (BidCoS-RF, BidCos-Wir, HmIP-RCV-1) and the INT000* group devices repeat verbatim on every CCU" and "Resolving them correctly needs the central alongside the address, which the callers of this facade do not carry today." The ordering claim is not a convention I supplied: internal/central/central_registry.go:302-311 `func (r *Registry) List() []*Unit { ... sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Name() < out[j].Name() }) ... }`. The repeated-address class is enumerated in source: internal/routingkey/uniqueid.go:41-43 lists `"BidCoS-RF": {}`, `"HmIP-RCV-1": {}` and uniqueid.go:26 `const internalAddressPrefix = "INT000"`; corroborated at internal/central/interface_id.go:19, internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:1349-1350, internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:649-650.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, either the facade would carry a central (a `central string` parameter or a {central} path segment on the device routes), or Registry.List would not impose a name order. I checked both: internal/north/rest/router.go:849-850 mounts `pr.With(op).Put("/devices/{addr}/channels/{no}/data-points/{param}/value", handlers.PutDataPointValue(d.Devices, d.DPWriter))` — address-only, no central segment — and central_registry.go:309 sorts by Name(). A false claim would also have shown a test registering two centrals that share a device address and asserting the write lands on the named one; grep over internal/ and tests/ found none.
stands.reason: Both copies are live production code, both on write paths. DataPointWriterAdapter is constructed at cmd/openccu-loom/daemon.go:766 `dpWriterAdapter := adapter.NewDataPointWriterAdapter(reg, valueWriter)` and mounted twice: daemon_rest_mount.go:318 `DPWriter: d.dpWriterAdapter` (consumed by router.go:785 `handlers.WebhookInboundValue(d.DPWriter)` — POST /api/v1/webhook/value, which takes a bare address, webhook_inbound.go:98-99) and daemon_rest_mount.go:761 `Writer: d.dpWriterAdapter` into the MCP mount. DevicesAdapter.Device is equally live: it backs `d.Devices` on every /devices/{addr}/... route, including the main value write, whose handler resolves through it (handlers/devices.go:929-931 `addr := chi.URLParam(r, "addr")` / `d, ok := idx.Device(addr)`) rather than through DPWriter (devices.go:851 takes `_ DataPointWriter`). Severity high: the failure mode on a multi-CCU deployment is a write actuating a channel on the wrong CCU with no error, and the intended channel being unreachable from every address-keyed surface — the daemon's own routing keys namespace per central precisely because this class of address is not unique. The blast radius is bounded to that address class; ordinary device serials are globally unique.
stands.guard: None. The only tests touching DataPointWriterAdapter are internal/central/adapter/adapter_test.go:83,:94 (single central) and device_admin_paths_test.go:334 (nil-writer guard). No test registers two centrals holding the same device address and asserts which one a write reaches, so a change of resolution rule — or of Registry.List's ordering — would go unnoticed.
stands.divergence: The two copies implement the identical rule, so they do not disagree with each other; the concrete diverging input is against intent. With centrals named "ccu-a" and "ccu-b" both reporting the virtual-remote root, `SetValue(ctx, "BidCoS-RF:1", PRESS_SHORT, true, prio)` strips to "BidCoS-RF" (deviceAddressOf, devices.go:237-243), takes registry.List()[0] = ccu-a (central_registry.go:309) and dispatches `a.writer.SetValue(ctx, "ccu-a", ...)`; the same call can never reach ccu-b's BidCoS-RF:1, which returns no error and no indication of the substitution. Same for any INT000* group channel. A secondary, real divergence between the two copies: devices.go:65 guards `if a.registry == nil { return nil, false }` while SetValue (devices.go:223) guards only the writer and would nil-deref on `a.registry.List()` — not reachable in production, since daemon.go:766 always passes reg.
stands.deadCopy: Neither. Both copies have production callers (DPWriter via webhook + MCP; DevicesAdapter.Device via every address-keyed REST device route).
stands.secondReason: Survives as a routing defect, though not as a duplication finding — and I am separating the two. As a *duplicate*, it dies on its own terms: the candidate itself states 'the two copies implement the identical rule, so they do not disagree with each other', and devices.go:216-218 cross-references the limitation to the canonical comment on DevicesAdapter.Device, so silent drift between them is not the risk. What survives, and what the title actually claims, is the routing bug, and it survives every bite. Quotes current and verbatim. Liveness traced from the composition root to three distinct live surfaces (webhook value POST, MCP set_datapoint, PUT device channel value). The divergence is not against a convention I supplied: the name-sort is at central_registry.go:309, the repeating-address classes are enumerated in the repo's own routingkey layer which acts on them by namespacing per central, and the correct shape (a `*On` variant) already ships for paramsets. Damage is observable and silent: with centrals ccu-a and ccu-b, a write to a CUX*/BidCoS-RF/INT000* channel actuates ccu-a and returns 202, ccu-b's identically-addressed channel is unreachable from every address-keyed surface, and CentralOf reports ccu-a as its owner. I hold severity at high rather than lowering it, because the CUxD prefix (uniqueid.go:28-31) puts ordinary user-facing devices in the colliding class, and because webhook_inbound.go accepts and then ignores the very field an operator would use to avoid it. That the limitation is documented in a comment does not discharge it — the comment names the blocker ('the callers of this facade do not carry [the central] today') while one caller demonstrably does carry it and is dropped on the floor.

stands.title: Device/channel/model lookups drop the central and take the alphabetically-first hit on addresses the file itself documents as repeating across CCUs
stands.evidence: Quotes verified verbatim. internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:2768 `func lookupDevice(reg *central.Registry, address string) (model, name string) {`, :2772 `for _, u := range reg.List() {`, :2773 `if d, ok := u.ModelRegistry.Get(address); ok {`, :2774 `return d.Model, d.Name()` — the signature takes no centralName at all. Same shape at :2756 `func lookupDeviceObject(reg *central.Registry, address string) *device.Device {` and :2784 `func lookupChannel(reg *central.Registry, deviceAddress string, channelNo int) *device.Channel {`. Live production callers, all holding centralName: :1521 `model, name := lookupDevice(b.registry, deviceAddr)` inside `func (b *EventBridge) publishValueChangedMQTT(ctx context.Context, centralName string, ...)` (:1514); :1660 `dev := lookupDeviceObject(b.registry, deviceAddr)` inside `func (b *EventBridge) refreshDeviceAvailability(ctx context.Context, centralName, iface, deviceAddr, parameter string)` (:1659); plus :1400, :1479, :1737, :1858, :2719. The chain is live, not test-only: eventbridge.go:1281 `func (b *EventBridge) onValueChanged(centralName string, e hmevent.DataPointValueChangedEvent)` -> :1282 `b.dispatchLive(...)` -> :1337 `published := b.publishValueChangedMQTT(ctx, centralName, envKind, e)`. Registry ordering verified at internal/central/central_registry.go:302-311: `// List returns every registered unit sorted by name for stable // iteration.` ... `sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Name() < out[j].Name() })`. Address repetition verified from the repo's own comment at eventbridge.go:647-652: `// Both retractions are scoped to the removal's own central. Device // addresses are unique per CCU but repeat verbatim across CCUs — the // virtual remote (HmIP-RCV-1), the BidCoS pseudo devices and the // INT000* internal devices carry the identical address everywhere — so // an unscoped discovery sweep would clear the other centrals' live // entities along with this one's.`
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, lookupDevice/lookupDeviceObject/lookupChannel would carry a centralName parameter and resolve through `b.registry.Get(centralName).ModelRegistry`, and `reg.List()` would not appear in their bodies. Two things would also be absent that are present: the :647-652 comment asserting that addresses repeat verbatim across CCUs, and internal/central/adapter/eventbridge_device_removed_scope_test.go:30-46, which registers `ccu-01` and `ccu-02` and calls `c.ModelRegistry.Put(device.New(device.Config{... Address: addr ...}))` with `const addr = "HmIP-RCV-1"` on BOTH — i.e. the repo already builds the colliding registry the unscoped walk misreads, just for the removal path.
stands.divergence: Registry holding centrals `ccu-01` and `ccu-02`, both with a device at address `HmIP-RCV-1` (exactly the fixture eventbridge_device_removed_scope_test.go:30-46 builds). A value change on ccu-02's `HmIP-RCV-1:1` enters publishValueChangedMQTT with centralName="ccu-02". `lookupDevice` walks `reg.List()`, which is name-sorted ("ccu-01" < "ccu-02"), so it returns ccu-01's `d.Model` and `d.Name()`; the topic is built from centralName="ccu-02". Scoped resolution returns ccu-02's model/name; unscoped returns ccu-01's. The sharpest single instance is inside ONE function: refreshDeviceAvailability resolves the device unscoped at :1660 (`lookupDeviceObject(b.registry, deviceAddr)` -> ccu-01's device -> `online := dev.Available()`) and then, twenty-two lines later at :1682, resolves the bus scoped (`u, ok := b.registry.Get(centralName)`) and publishes `hmevent.DeviceLifecycleEvent{... CentralName: centralName, Address: deviceAddr, Available: online}` on ccu-02's bus — ccu-01's reachability verdict announced as ccu-02's, in the same call.
stands.deadCopy: Neither side is dead. Both the unscoped helpers (eventbridge.go:2756/2768/2784, seven production call sites) and the scoped form (`b.registry.Get(centralName)` at eventbridge.go:714, 843, 1682) have live production callers.
stands.guard: None. The only tests touching these helpers are internal/central/adapter/eventbridge_helpers_test.go:103-152, which assert only the nil-registry and address-not-found branches (`lookupDeviceObject(nil, "DEV001")`, `lookupDevice(reg, "NOSUCH")`); none registers two centrals with a colliding address. internal/central/adapter/eventbridge_device_removed_scope_test.go:29 (TestEventBridgeDeviceRemovedRetractsOnlyTheOwningCentral) guards the removal/retraction path only — it would stay green if every lookup* helper kept walking the whole registry.
stands.reason: Both sites are live production code, the quotes are exact, the diverging input is concrete and already materialised as a fixture elsewhere in the package, and the correctly scoped resolution sits inside one of the very functions that gets it wrong. Severity high because the damage is silent and cross-installation: wrong model/name/channel-type/custom-DP Source published under another CCU's topic, and a foreign device's `Available()` driving both the retained availability topic and the DeviceLifecycleEvent that the WebSocket device-lifecycle plane and the Matter reachability forward consume (eventbridge.go:1652-1657). It only bites a multi-CCU install on the repeated address classes, but multi-CCU is ADR 0002 first-class and the repo has already shipped one fix for this exact collision on the removal path.
stands.secondReason: Every quote is verbatim at the cited line, the sort order is read from the source rather than assumed, all sites are on the live bus-dispatch path, the diverging input is documented by four separate production comments and already materialised as a fixture, and the correctly scoped resolution sits twenty-two lines below the wrong one inside the same function. The only defect in the finding is a wrong directory on one site (adapter/central_registry.go -> central/central_registry.go); the line number and content are exact.

stands.title: deriveTargetChannels mints channel keys unbounded while the bit table and the validator only cover an 8x3 grid
stands.evidence:
Quotes verified verbatim. week_profile_filter.go:246-248: `for actorIdx, group := range groups {` / `for subIdx, member := range group.Channels {` / `key := fmt.Sprintf("%d_%d", actorIdx+1, subIdx+1)` — no bound on either index. channel_keys.go:29-54 `var channelKeyBitmask = map[string]uint32{` lists exactly "1_1"…"8_3", 24 entries, and its own comment at :24-28 says "NOT established: which key addresses which channel … So a wrong entry here would be invisible to every test we have." datapoint.go:653-656: `bit, ok := ChannelKeyToBitmask(channelKey)` / `if !ok {` / `dp.restoreScheduleEnabled(previousEnabled, previousHold)` / `return fmt.Errorf("weekprofile: unknown channel key %q", channelKey)`. simple.go:158 `channelPattern  = regexp.MustCompile(`^[1-8]_[123]$`)`.

Both sides live. Generator: week_profile_filter.go:126 inside attachNonClimateWeekProfileToDevice, whose keys are registered on the DP (:149-151 `for k := range targets { wp.RegisterChannel(k, true) }`), turned into published ChannelSwitches (:152-160) and surfaced as available_target_channels (rest/handlers/week_profile.go:124-141). Consumer: ChannelKeyToBitmask is called from datapoint.go:648,653 (SetScheduleEnabled) and adapter/schedule_enabled.go:42,136,163 — reached from REST PUT /devices/{addr}/channels/{no}/week_profile/channel-locks/{key} (router.go:875 → handlers/week_profile.go:202), from WS, and from MQTT command_subscriber.go:79.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, some device would have had to keep group.Channels at ≤3 members and the group count at ≤8. I enumerated instead of assuming: internal/model/custom/profile_configs.go:261 `SecondaryChannels:               []int{1, 2, 3}` (profile IPRGBW, the only config in the file with three secondaries — `grep -n 'SecondaryChannels:               \[\]int{[0-9], [0-9], [0-9]'` returns that one line). With PrimaryChannel 0 + PrimaryChannelSet true (:259-260) that is 1 primary + 3 secondaries = 4 members, so subIdx+1 reaches 4. Had the key generator been bounded, `fmt.Sprintf("%d_%d", …)` would have been preceded by a range check; it is not.
stands.reason: Reachable on shipped hardware, verified end to end. IPRGBW is registered for device types "hmip-rgbw" (profiles.go:1219-1228) and "hmip-lsc" (:1109-1118), each with Channels {Channel: 1, Role: Primary}. addChannelGroupsToDevice computes groupNo = base.Channel + PrimaryChannel = 1+0 = 1 (materialize.go:251), so ScheduleRelevantChannelGroups (custom/schedule_targets.go:97-102) yields one group with members [1 (primary), 2, 3, 4] and deriveTargetChannels mints "1_1","1_2","1_3","1_4". The device really carries the schedule surface: ../godevccu/internal/embed/data/device_descriptions/HmIP-RGBW.json declares VCU5629873:1..:4 UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_RECEIVER and VCU5629873:5 UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_WEEK_PROFILE, and its paramset description has WEEK_PROGRAM_CHANNEL_LOCKS in :5 VALUES plus 01_WP_* in :5 MASTER — so findScheduleChannel matches and the DP is attached with four target keys. Consequence: the REST handler's 404 gate passes (handlers/week_profile.go:191 `if _, ok := wp.ScheduleEnabled()[key]; !ok` — "1_4" IS registered), then SetScheduleEnabled returns `weekprofile: unknown channel key "1_4"` and the handler answers 502 (week_profile.go:203). The broadcast path is worse and silent: datapoint.go:645-651 ORs only keys the table knows, so an "enable all" write omits 1_4's bit while the optimistic local state at :631-634 already reports it changed. Severity raised to high: a published, operator-visible switch that can never be written on a shipped device family, plus a silent state divergence on the aggregate path.
stands.divergence: Concrete and current: channel key "1_4", minted for every HmIP-RGBW (and HmIP-LSC, HmIP-DRG-DALI-shaped) device. weekprofile.ChannelKeyToBitmask("1_4") returns (0, false) — the map at channel_keys.go:29-54 stops at "1_3": 1<<2. deriveTargetChannels returns it as a first-class target with ChannelNo 4. The two sides therefore already disagree on the same key today: TargetChannelBitsFrom accepts it (bit = 4-1 = 3, rawconvert.go:981) so schedule ENTRIES can target it, while the CHANNEL-LOCK path rejects it. `grep -rn '"1_4"' --include='*.go'` returns nothing anywhere in the repo — no test covers the key at all.
stands.guard: none. internal/model/weekprofile/channel_keys_test.go:28-42 pins AllChannelKeys against channelKeyBitmask (both are 8x3, so they agree trivially) but never against deriveTargetChannels. No test asserts that every key deriveTargetChannels produces resolves through ChannelKeyToBitmask.
stands.deadCopy: schedule.SimpleEntry.Validate's `^[1-8]_[123]$` (internal/model/schedule/simple.go:158, applied at :206-209) is effectively dead as a bound: its only entry point is Simple.Put (simple.go:342-351), and Put has no production caller for simple schedules — the REST write path assigns straight into the map at internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:867 `s.Entries[e.SlotNo] = schedule.SimpleEntry{…}`. ValidateFor/ValidateAll (simple.go:228, :365) likewise have no production caller. So the candidate's "SimpleEntry.Validate would also reject the key" is true of the code but never runs in production; the only live rejection is ChannelKeyToBitmask. weekprofile.AllChannelKeys (channel_keys.go:59) also has no production caller.
stands.secondReason: Survived every bite. The quotes are exact, the four-key derivation is computed from the profile tables rather than assumed, the device family is real and its schedule surface is in the fixture data, and the consequence is observable twice over. Per-key path: the SPA/REST switch for "1_4" renders (RegisterChannel put it in ScheduleEnabled), the handler's 404 gate lets it through, and SetScheduleEnabled returns `weekprofile: unknown channel key "1_4"` -> HTTP 502 for a control the daemon itself published. Aggregate path is worse: datapoint.go:614-615 optimistically flips every key including 1_4, then :647-650 ORs only keys the table knows, so 1_4's bit is never written and the CCU echo can never correct the local state (the echo is parsed through the same 24-bit table, so 1_4 is absent from it too) — a permanent silent divergence between reported and actual state. A third surface confirms the same 8x3 assumption is baked in elsewhere: schedule.SimpleEntry's channelPattern `^[1-8]_[123]$` (simple.go:158, applied at :207) rejects "1_4" as a schedule TARGET too, while weekprofile.TargetChannelBitsFrom (rawconvert.go:972-987) happily assigns it bit 3 — so the two sides already disagree on the same key today. Zero test coverage. High is the right severity.

stands.title: Per-central scoping of un-ignore rules is modelled in the store but discarded by the composition root
stands.evidence: Both quotes verify verbatim. parser.go:61-68 reads `// Central scopes the entry to one CCU (central.Unit.Name). Empty means / // the entry is global and matches every central — the default for / // entries built by [ParseUnIgnore], which has no central context of its / // own. A caller that persists un-ignore rules per central (multi-CCU is / // first class, ADR 0002) stamps this field before calling / // [ParameterDecider.LoadUnIgnore] so the entry cannot decide visibility / // for a central it was never registered against.` followed by `Central string`. visibility_wiring.go:178 reads exactly `if err := visReg.LoadUnIgnore(strings.NewReader(strings.Join(union, "\n"))); err != nil {`, fed by the union built at :140-157 across `reg.Names()`. ParseUnIgnoreRules (parser.go:228-254) builds every entry via ParseUnIgnoreLine (:92-…), which constructs `&UnIgnoreEntry{Parameter:…, IsSimple:true, Comment:comment}` and never assigns Central — so every production entry carries Central=="". Grep across the repo for a Central assignment on an UnIgnoreEntry returns exactly one site, and it is a test: `internal/store/visibility/central_scope_test.go:24  d.LoadUnIgnore([]UnIgnoreEntry{{Parameter: param, IsSimple: true, Central: "central-a"}})`. Grep for each of the five *ForCentral decider methods (IsParameterIgnoredForCentral, ShouldSkipParameterForCentral, IsParameterHiddenForCentral, IsUnIgnoredForCentral, IsUnIgnoredCustomOnlyForCentral) returns only their own definitions, decider.go's internal delegations passing the literal "" (`decider.go:143  return d.IsParameterIgnoredForCentral("", model, …)`, `:533`, `:557`), and central_scope_test.go — no production caller. Every live consumer uses the central-agnostic variant: `internal/store/visibility/operation_mode.go:262 decider.IsUnIgnored(dev.Model, …)`, `:328 decider.IsParameterIgnored(dev.Model, …)`, `:401/409 markIfInternal`, `internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:2061 p.visibility.Parameter().IsUnIgnoredCustomOnly(`, `internal/store/visibility/registry.go:137/156`. So the `central` dimension of ignoreCacheKey (types.go:20-27) is the empty string on every production lookup, and the guard at decider.go:617 `if e.Central != "" && e.Central != central { continue }` never fires. The operator-facing contract is per-central: assets/openapi.yaml:5693 `summary: Replace the un-ignore pattern list for a central (admin)`, and the store row is keyed by central (handlers/visibility.go:25 `List(ctx, centralName string)`).
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, one of two greps would have produced a non-test hit: (a) a production assignment stamping UnIgnoreEntry.Central before LoadUnIgnore — grep `Central:` / `.Central =` under internal/ and cmd/ returns only central_scope_test.go:24; (b) a production call to any *ForCentral method — grep of all five names returns only definitions, decider.go's own ""-passing delegations, and the same test file. I also checked the opposite direction: a fleet-wide-by-design reading would have left no per-central plumbing at all, yet parser.go:68, types.go:33/51 and decider.go:617 all exist and are exercised only from a test.
stands.reason: The knowledge "which CCU this un-ignore rule was registered for" is carried by SQLite (per-central rows, per-central REST PUT) and then thrown away at the composition root, which newline-joins every central's patterns into one string and parses it with a function that has no central context. Three separate store-side mechanisms encode the scoping and all three are dead in production. Worse, the two doc sites assert the opposite of the running system: decider.go:126-131 states `Callers that know which central they are answering for — every production call site does, since multi-CCU is first class (ADR 0002) — must use [ParameterDecider.IsParameterIgnoredForCentral] instead`, while zero production call sites do; and cmd/openccu-loom/visibility_adapter.go:96-115 documents the contradictory intent in the same binary — `patterns are central-agnostic — central A un-ignoring a parameter un-ignores it for central B too`. Severity high because the surface is operator-facing and per-central by contract (openapi.yaml:5693), the divergence is live today rather than latent, and ADR 0002 is a named hard rule.
stands.divergence: Take the exact input the repo's own test already persists: `store.Replace(ctx, "ccu-01", []string{"ACTIVE"}, "test")` (cmd/openccu-loom/ws_adapters_domain_paths_test.go:517) — one pattern, persisted for ccu-01 only, with ccu-02 holding no patterns. Store side: the row exists only under central ccu-01. Composition-root side: applyVisibilityUnIgnore unions it to `"ACTIVE"` and ParseUnIgnore yields `UnIgnoreEntry{Parameter:"ACTIVE", IsSimple:true, Central:""}`. Query for a device on ccu-02 (HmIP-PSM, VALUES, parameter ACTIVE): matchesUnIgnoreLocked (decider.go:612-641) skips the `e.Central != ""` guard because Central is empty, hits `if e.IsSimple { if paramset == ParamsetKeyValues { return true } }` → un-ignored on ccu-02. Had the store's model been honoured (Central=="ccu-01", lookup central "ccu-02"), decider.go:617 would have continued and the parameter would have stayed ignored on ccu-02 — which is exactly what internal/store/visibility/central_scope_test.go:29 asserts for BOOST_TIME with a hand-stamped entry.
stands.deadCopy: The per-central copy is the dead one: UnIgnoreEntry.Central (parser.go:68), the Central dimension of ignoreCacheKey/IgnoreCacheKey/UnIgnoreCacheKey (types.go:22/33/51) and all five *ForCentral methods (decider.go:149, :498, :525, :538, :564) have no production caller. The live path is the central-agnostic one, always called with "".
stands.guard: None over the wiring. The two existing tests contradict each other and neither covers the seam: internal/store/visibility/central_scope_test.go:19 TestUnIgnoreDoesNotLeakAcrossCentrals constructs the entry itself with `Central: "central-a"`, so it proves the decider CAN scope, never that production stamps the field — a bracketing test in this project's own vocabulary. cmd/openccu-loom/ws_adapters_domain_paths_test.go:488 TestVisibilityAdapter_LoadUnIgnore_TouchesSiblingCentralsDevicesToo deliberately pins the fleet-wide behaviour (`the un-ignore patterns are unioned across every central into ONE shared ParameterDecider`) and would fail if per-central scoping were introduced. tests/e2e/visibility_test.go and tests/integration/visibility_unignore_test.go both run a single central and cannot see the leak.
stands.secondReason: Survived all five bites. The quotes are current and verbatim (one citation range is wrong — the adapter's contradictory sentence is at :150-152, inside the same function, not at :96-115). The two sites are not two readings of one datum: SQLite stores a genuine (central_name, pattern) partition and the decider has a matching Central dimension, but the composition root newline-joins every central's patterns into one stream and parses it with ParseUnIgnore, which has no central context, so every entry lands with Central=="". Liveness is inverted from the usual refutation: the store/decider scoping is what has no production caller, while the live path is the flat union — the stronger form of the finding, and TestUnIgnoreDoesNotLeakAcrossCentrals is a bracketing test that hand-constructs the entry production can never produce. The divergence reproduces without substituting any convention: for `Replace(ctx,"ccu-01",["ACTIVE"])` with ccu-02 holding no rows, matchesUnIgnoreLocked skips the :617 guard (Central=="") and returns true at :622 for a ccu-02 VALUES lookup; had the store's model been honoured it would have continued at :617 and stayed ignored, which is exactly what central_scope_test.go:29 asserts. Nothing filters upstream — handlers/visibility.go validates pattern syntax only and uses req.CentralName solely for the SQLite key and an existence check (visibility_adapter.go:144). Damage is observable on REST/MQTT/SPA via the per-DP IsUnIgnored mark and contradicts both the OpenAPI summary and the concept document. Two qualifications on severity, neither fatal: the effect needs a multi-CCU install AND a pattern that matches devices on the sibling central (always true for a bare simple pattern, model-dependent for a complex one), and the adapter comment shows the flat behaviour was at least noticed, so this is partly a deliberate-vs-documented conflict rather than a pure oversight. High still stands because decider.go:125-131's assertion that every production call site is central-aware is verifiably false, ADR 0002 is a named hard rule, and the surface is operator-facing.

stands.title: The LT-gated OnOff cluster block is declared four times, and the four copies already disagree
stands.evidence:
All four quotes check out verbatim. switch/matter.go:54 `matterAttrStartUpOnOff       uint32 = 0x4003`, :59 `matterFeatureOnOffLT uint32 = 0x01`, :71 `matterOnOffClusterRevision uint16 = 6`. generic/switch_matter.go:54 `matterGenericSwitchAttrStartUpOnOff       uint32 = 0x4003`, :59 `matterGenericFeatureOnOffLT uint32 = 0x01`, :71 `matterGenericOnOffClusterRevision uint16 = 6`. light/matter.go:72 `matterAttrOnOffStartUpOnOff       uint32 = 0x4003`, :87 `matterFeatureOnOffLT      uint32 = 0x01`, :129 `matterOnOffClusterRevision uint16 = 6`. siren/matter.go:99 `matterAttrOnOffStartUpOnOff       uint32 = 0x4003`, :108 `matterFeatureOnOffLT uint32 = 0x01`, :134 `matterOnOffClusterRevision        uint16 = 6`. The cross-file comment reference is real — siren/matter.go:104-106: "so this projection must advertise it (and its four gated attributes + three gated commands below), the same as internal/model/custom/switch/matter.go's Switch projection." All four also duplicate the identical 7-line matter.js citation block (`on-off.element.ts:30-36`) verbatim.

THE COPIES ALREADY DISAGREE. Siren omits Toggle (0x02) entirely — it declares no `matterCmdToggle` (siren/matter.go:127-128 declare only Off/On), its `MatterAcceptedCommands` (siren/matter.go:375-383) returns Off, On, OffWithEffect, OnWithRecallGlobalScene, OnWithTimedOff, and its `MatterInvoke` (siren/matter.go:317-338) has no Toggle case, so a Toggle invoke falls to `default:` → `errMatterUnknownCommand`. The other three all list `matterCmdToggle` (switch:353, light:425, generic:339). Siren's own justification at :372-374 — "Toggle (0x02) is absent — Siren has no toggle command in its wire surface" — is not a conformance argument: matter.js HEAD packages/model/src/standard/elements/on-off.element.ts:40 declares `Command({ name: "Toggle", id: 0x2, access: "O", conformance: "!OFFONLY", ... })`, i.e. mandatory unless the OFFONLY feature bit is advertised, and siren/matter.go:250 returns `matterFeatureOnOffLT` (0x01) as its FeatureMap — LT only, no OFFONLY. So the siren endpoint advertises a FeatureMap under which Toggle is mandatory and then answers AcceptedCommandList without it.

Sharing is already the established pattern in this codebase and was not used here: all four sources mount the *shared* stubs `wire.Groups{}` / `wire.ScenesManagement{}` from internal/north/matter/cluster/wire (switch/matter.go:96-100, generic/switch_matter.go:410-414), while the OnOff constants stay copied. switch/matter.go:30-31 even names the intended home: "the cluster-protocol package internal/north/matter/cluster/onoff/ may later import them" — that directory does not exist (ls internal/north/matter/cluster: closure, core, cover, light, lock, measurement, thermo, wire).
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false I would have seen either a single declaration of the LT attribute/feature/command set imported by all four projections (the way wire.Groups is imported), or four sets that agree element-for-element. Concretely: `grep -rn matterFeatureOnOffLT` would have returned one declaration site rather than four (switch:59, light:87, siren:108, generic:59), and the four MatterAcceptedCommands bodies would have contained the same six command constants. Neither held.
stands.reason: One domain decision — what an OnOff cluster carrying the LT feature must advertise — is written out independently in four packages, with the matter.js citation copied along rather than the values. The divergence is not hypothetical: siren already ships a FeatureMap/AcceptedCommandList pair that contradicts on-off.element.ts:40, which is the silent pair-abort shape the candidate names. A revision bump or a newly LT-gated attribute has four edit sites and no guard tying them together.
stands.divergence: siren omits Toggle 0x02 from both AcceptedCommandList and MatterInvoke while advertising FeatureMap=LT(0x01) only; matter.js on-off.element.ts:40 gives Toggle conformance "!OFFONLY", so it is mandatory for that FeatureMap. The other three projections all include it.
stands.secondReason: Survives every bite. Quotes current, sameness real (identical rule, identical copied citation, four prefixes), all four sites live, divergence reproduced end-to-end from the matter.js element file to the rejecting default branch, and the damage is observable: a controller reading AcceptedCommandList (0xFFF9) on a siren endpoint sees no Toggle, and one that invokes 0x02 anyway gets an error status instead of a state flip. The only correction is a one-line citation slip in the candidate's evidence (Toggle is on-off.element.ts:39, not :40).

stands.title: The OnOff/0x010A Matter block is hand-transcribed in four packages while a generated single source (schema.ClusterRevisions) sits unused by all of them
stands.evidence: Four const blocks carry the same OnOff identity, each with its own hand-copied matter.js citation: custom/switch/matter.go:35-72 (`matterDeviceTypeOnOffPlugInUnit uint16 = 0x010A`, `matterClusterOnOff uint32 = 0x0006`, attrs 0x4000-0x4003, `matterFeatureOnOffLT uint32 = 0x01`, cmds 0x40/0x41/0x42, `matterOnOffClusterRevision uint16 = 6`); custom/siren/matter.go:78-134 (same, `matterAttrOnOff*` names); generic/switch_matter.go:35-71 whose header states `The constants mirror those in \`model/custom/switch/matter.go\` (the rich Switch projection)`; custom/light/matter.go:110-129 (OnOff cluster + LT commands + `matterOnOffClusterRevision uint16 = 6`; light uses device types 0x0100/0x0101, not 0x010A — the candidate is wrong on that detail only). A generated single source exists and none of the four imports it: internal/north/matter/schema/clusters.go:6 `Code generated by script/generate_matter_schema.go from notes/parity/matter/matter-schema-snapshot.json — DO NOT EDIT`, containing `0x0006: 6,  // OnOff`. Guard coverage is uneven: custom/switch, custom/siren and custom/light each compare their own constant against the snapshot (switch/parity_matterjs_test.go:78, siren/parity_matterjs_test.go:162 → `{matterClusterOnOff, "OnOff", matterOnOffClusterRevision}`), but internal/model/generic has no snapshot parity test at all (grep for `loadMatterSchema` in internal/model returns only climate, cover, light, lock, siren, switch), and its only check is tautological: generic/switch_matter_test.go:191 `if !ok || v != matterGenericOnOffClusterRevision`. The third-hand row internal/north/matter/schema/parity_test.go:108 `{0x0006, "OnOff", 6}` is a literal typed into the test, not a read of any package constant — its own header says `Update the constant in the cluster source file, then update codeRev here`.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false I would have found the four projections importing one shared declaration (internal/north/matter/schema or a shared onoff package) or a guard that reads every package's revision constant and compares them. Concretely: if matter.js HEAD bumped OnOff to revision 7, `make test` would go red in custom/switch, custom/siren and custom/light and stay green in internal/model/generic — the bridge would then advertise revision 7 on custom-DP endpoints and revision 6 on every generic switch endpoint, from one daemon.
stands.reason: One domain decision (the OnOff cluster's Matter identity for the bridge) declared four times, with the mirroring stated in a comment rather than enforced, and with the fourth copy outside the parity net that guards the other three. Exactly the drift class CLAUDE.md forbids hand-coding for.
stands.divergence: The copies already disagree on the derived command set for the *same* device type 0x010A: custom/switch/matter.go:353, generic/switch_matter.go:339 and light/matter.go:425 enumerate Toggle (0x02); siren/matter.go:375-387 does not, and siren/matter.go:341 rejects it (`default: return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: 0x%02X", errMatterUnknownCommand, cmdID)`). The siren comment declares this deliberate (`Toggle (0x02) is absent — Siren has no toggle command in its wire surface`), but matter.js on-off.element.ts:40 marks it `conformance: "!OFFONLY"` — mandatory unless the OFFONLY feature is advertised, and siren advertises LT, not OFFONLY. So two endpoints of one bridge present device type 0x010A with different AcceptedCommandLists, and no guard compares them.
stands.deadCopy: none of the four is dead; all four are live projections.
stands.guard: per-package snapshot parity for switch/siren/light; nothing for internal/model/generic; internal/north/matter/schema/parity_test.go:108 compares a hand-typed literal, not the constants.
stands.secondReason: Survives, with two scope corrections that do not kill it. Correction 1: schema.ClusterRevisions carries ONLY the revision number — the package holds clusters.go, devicetypes.go, timed.go, writable.go and no attribute-ID, command-ID or FeatureMap-bit table — so the 'generated single source' covers exactly one line of each block, not the block. Correction 2: only three packages declare device type 0x010A (switch, generic, siren); light declares 0x0100/0x0101 and duplicates the OnOff *cluster* half only. What survives all five bites: sameness — the revision 6 is one datum with a generated source, not two readings for two callers; liveness — all four constants are read on the wire path via MatterRead(0xFFFD) (switch:166, siren:252, generic:192, light:261) while daemon_matter.go:4077 serves the *generated* value to the REST endpoint-inspector, so two live sources already answer the same question; divergence — reproduced below; damage — a controller reading AcceptedCommandList on device type 0x010A gets {0x00,0x01,0x02,0x40,0x41,0x42} from a Switch and {0x00,0x01,0x40,0x41,0x42} from a Siren, and a Toggle invoke on a Siren falls into siren/matter.go:339 `default: return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: 0x%02X", errMatterUnknownCommand, cmdID)`. The parity net is also weaker than the schema test's own comment claims: parity_test.go:59 lists `model/generic/switch_matter.go → matterGenericOnOffClusterRevision` as covered, but the test body only compares its own hand-written literal `{0x0006, "OnOff", 6}` (:108) against the schema and never reads any of the four constants — and internal/model/generic has no parity_matterjs_test.go at all (loadMatterSchema appears only under internal/model/custom/{siren,lock,switch,light,climate,cover}). So the schema parity test is itself a fifth copy, and its coverage comment is refuted.

stands.title: One wire label, two vocabularies: INTRUSION_ALARM is Critical smoke on the Matter plane and explicitly not-smoke on the safety/calculated planes
stands.evidence: hmenum declares the vocabulary with a reasoned exclusion: smoke_alarm_status.go:27-29 `SmokeDetectorAlarmStatusIntrusionAlarm … = "INTRUSION_ALARM"` with `It is a command the domain sent, not a detection the device made.`, and :38-41 `smokeDetectorAlarmStatusSmokeLabels = []string{PRIMARY_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM}` under the comment `INTRUSION_ALARM is deliberately absent … Treating it as smoke makes the domain report its own siren command as the cause of a fire.` Its two consumers read it, not literals: safety/classify.go:40 `var smokeActiveValues = hmenum.SmokeDetectorAlarmStatusSmokeLabels()` and calculated/derived_binary.go:174 `OnValues: hmenum.SmokeDetectorAlarmStatusSmokeLabels()` with `OffValues: []string{"IDLE_OFF", "IDLE_ON", "INTRUSION_ALARM"}`. The siren package declares a second, unconnected vocabulary — smoke.go:23-28 `type SmokeAlarmStatus string` with the same four literals — and its Matter projection maps the excluded label to a fire: matter.go:416-421 `func smokeStatusToAlarmState(st SmokeAlarmStatus) uint8 { switch st { case SmokeStatusPrimaryAlarm, SmokeStatusIntrusion: return matterSmokeAlarmCritical`, with matter.go:409 documenting `PRIMARY_ALARM / INTRUSION → Critical (2)` and smokeStatusToExpressedState (:432-440) turning that into `matterExpressedStateSmokeAlarm`. SmokeSiren is a live Matter endpoint source (matter.go:27 `_ interfaces.MatterEndpointSource = (*SmokeSiren)(nil)`, MatterDeviceType 0x0076 at :399). No conversion exists between the two types: grep shows siren's constants are used only inside internal/model/custom/siren, and hmenum's only in safety/ and calculated/.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, the siren package would have consumed hmenum's constants (or its Matter mapping would have excluded SmokeStatusIntrusion the way safety and calculated do), and the same label would produce the same verdict on both planes. Concretely, with today's code an operator-triggered intrusion siren on an HmIP-SWSD sets SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS=INTRUSION_ALARM, and the daemon simultaneously publishes SMOKE_ALARM=off (derived_binary.go:174-176) and SmokeCOAlarm SmokeState=Critical / ExpressedState=SmokeAlarm to Apple Home. Nothing in notes/parity/by_design.md records that divergence — grep for INTRUSION there returns nothing; notes/concepts/security-safety-concept.md:521-530 documents only the exclusion side.
stands.reason: The same VALUE_LIST is declared twice as two Go types, and the second declaration's consumer reverses a decision the first one documents in prose. This is not two defensible readings of one datum: Matter's SmokeCOAlarm SmokeState=Critical means the detector sensed smoke, so the bridge reports the installation's own siren command as a fire — the exact failure hmenum's comment names.
stands.divergence: INTRUSION_ALARM: Critical/SmokeAlarm on the Matter plane (siren/matter.go:418) vs. excluded from smoke on the safety classifier and the derived SMOKE_ALARM sensor (classify.go:40, derived_binary.go:174-176). Second, smaller one: siren/smoke.go:158 `IsActive` treats anything but IDLE_OFF as firing, so it also counts INTRUSION_ALARM (defensible there — the sounder really is sounding) but would count IDLE_ON as an alarm while matter.go's default branch maps it to Normal and derived_binary.go:175 maps it to off.
stands.missingInput: Whether the HmIP-SWSD paramset's VALUE_LIST actually carries a fifth label IDLE_ON, and in what order. hmenum/smoke_alarm_status.go:11-14 asserts a four-label list `[IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM]` and states `The device's own value list is the only authority`; the repo's own wire-snapshot fixtures declare five in a different order (tests/contract/wire_snapshots/generator_test.go:638, snapshot_pin_test.go:648, reference_compare_test.go:548: `[IDLE_OFF, IDLE_ON, PRIMARY_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM]`), siren/state_change_test.go:49 uses a third order, and notes/concepts/security-safety-concept.md:548 calls IDLE_ON `ein Label, das kein HmIP-SWSD-Paramset je emittiert`. I cannot resolve this from the repo, so I judge only the INTRUSION_ALARM leg and leave the IDLE_ON leg unjudged — reading it off a live SWSD paramset description is the missing measurement.
stands.guard: none couples the two vocabularies; the safety/calculated side is anchored to hmenum by construction, the Matter side to siren's own type.
stands.secondReason: Survives every bite. The quote is current and the mapper is live. Sameness: this is not two defensible readings of one datum — the attribute is literally SmokeState, gated by the SMOKE feature, typed AlarmStateEnum whose Critical is the smoke-detected level, so 'the detector's sensor state' is the only reading; the two Go types are a genuine duplicate vocabulary for one VALUE_LIST, not a wire-vs-domain pair. Divergence reproduced: on the same device, the same wire label INTRUSION_ALARM yields SmokeCOAlarm SmokeState=Critical(2) + ExpressedState=SmokeAlarm(1) on the Matter plane while the derived SMOKE_ALARM sensor reports off and the safety classifier does not count it as smoke. Damage is observable and safety-relevant: an Apple/Google controller announces a smoke alarm while the installation is only using the detector as an intrusion sounder — the exact failure hmenum's comment names — and the repo's own ADR 0012:312 says INTRUSION_ALARM belongs on BooleanState, not on the smoke cluster. Two things I could NOT confirm and which are therefore not part of the verdict: (a) the candidate's IDLE_ON sub-point about smoke.go:158 `return st != SmokeStatusIdleOff && st != "", true` — SmokeSiren.IsActive's only production caller is internal/alarm/outputs/reconcile.go:62 `return observed && active && dev.IsIntrusion()`, which ANDs with IsIntrusion, so IDLE_ON cannot reach an alarm output there; the sirenOnOffServer that reads IsActive for the OnOff attribute is the plain Siren, a different type. (b) A side observation, verified but outside the finding: hmenum's own comment asserts the VALUE_LIST is `[IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM]`, while every pinned wire snapshot carries five values in a different order — tests/contract/wire_snapshots/snapshot_pin_test.go:648 `ValueList: []string{"IDLE_OFF", "IDLE_ON", "PRIMARY_ALARM", "SECONDARY_ALARM", "INTRUSION_ALARM"}`. Neither Go type declares IDLE_ON. This does not cause a defect (both consumers match by label, not index) but it does refute the comment's stated data-source property.

stands.title: The combined-parameter acceptance set is declared in three packages; the contract guard binds the live copy to a dead one
stands.negativeControl: Had the backends copy been derived from either exported set, `grep -n 'parameterCombined' internal/client/backends/combined.go` would have shown a reference to `hmenum.ParameterCombinedParameter` rather than the bare string `"COMBINED_PARAMETER"`; and had value.ConvertableParameters been live, the grep for IsConvertableParameter would have hit a non-test file. Both greps returned the positive (duplicated / dead) result.
stands.reason:
One decision — which parameters carry a combined wire encoding — is made three times, and the guard pins the two copies that do not gate the read path. TestConvertableParameterSetsAgree (tests/contract/convertable_parameter_parity_test.go:22-54) loops only over `value.ConvertableParameters` and `parameter.ConvertableParameters`; backends is not imported by that file. The membership is identical today (both list COMBINED_PARAMETER and LEVEL_COMBINED), so there is no live disagreement — the finding is structural.

The blast radius is larger than the candidate stated. Adding a third combined parameter to both exported sets (the only way to keep the guard green) leaves backends untouched, and BOTH paths break, not just the read path: on read, callback_handlers.go:293 falls through and the opaque combined string is published to the bus as a value; on write, interface_client_orchestration.go:324-330 routes to `c.CommandTracker().AddCombinedParameter(...)` and returns unconditionally, while AddCombinedParameter is `values, ok := backends.ParseCombinedParameter(parameter, value); if !ok || len(values) == 0 { return nil }` (command_tracker.go:127-130) — so the optimistic record is dropped entirely rather than merely mis-decomposed.
stands.divergence: No membership disagreement today: all three sets are {COMBINED_PARAMETER, LEVEL_COMBINED}. The disagreement is in coverage — the guard binds copy 1 (live write) to copy 2 (no production caller) and never reaches copy 3 (live read, and the actual parser behind the write path).
stands.deadCopy: internal/model/value.ConvertableParameters / value.IsConvertableParameter (internal/model/value/converter.go:33-46) — read only by its own package test and by tests/contract/convertable_parameter_parity_test.go.
stands.guard: tests/contract/convertable_parameter_parity_test.go:22 TestConvertableParameterSetsAgree — binds internal/parameter to internal/model/value only; internal/client/backends is not in its import list.
stands.secondReason: Survives. Quotes current, sameness real (one datum — which wire parameter names carry a combined encoding — spelled as a map of hmenum.Parameter, an array of hmenum.Parameter, and two string literals), and this is the strong case the brief names: the guard pins the live write-path copy to a copy with NO production caller, while the copy that gates the live read path and backs the actual parser is never reached by it. TestConvertableParameterSetsAgree's own comment asserts the opposite — "a combined-parameter write would route correctly on one path and not the other" implies both are live paths; one is test-only. Damage on drift is worse than the candidate stated and I reproduced both legs: adding a third combined parameter to both exported sets keeps the guard green, and (read) callback_handlers.go:293 falls through so the opaque combined string is published as a value; (write) interface_client_orchestration.go:324 routes to CommandTracker().AddCombinedParameter and returns unconditionally, while that method is `values, ok := backends.ParseCombinedParameter(parameter, value); if !ok || len(values) == 0 { return nil }` (command_tracker.go:127-130) and ParseCombinedParameter's switch `default: return nil, false` (combined.go:62-64) — so the optimistic record is dropped silently rather than mis-decomposed. High severity stands on the guard's false coverage claim, not on a present bug.

stands.title: The runtime delay_new_device_creation toggle never reaches the CUxD callback handler
stands.evidence:
Quotes verified verbatim. central_bringup.go:303-307: `want := cc.Behavior.DelayNewDeviceCreationEnabled()` / `if h.cbHandlers == nil || h.cbHandlers.DelayNewDeviceCreation() == want {` / `continue` / `}` / `h.cbHandlers.SetDelayNewDeviceCreation(want)`. cuxd_wiring.go:174-197: `handlers := NewCallbackHandlers(unit, logger)` … `handlers.SetDelayNewDeviceCreation(cc.Behavior.DelayNewDeviceCreationEnabled())` / `binrpcCallbackServer.Register(initID, handlers)` … `cbHandlers = handlers` — `cbHandlers` is declared at cuxd_wiring.go:173 as a function-local `var cbHandlers *CallbackHandlers` and is used only at cuxd_wiring.go:244 and 304-305 (`cbHandlers.Stop()`); it is never returned or handed to the BringUpManager.

Liveness of both sides: `wireCUxDInterface` is called from production at ccu_wiring.go:720; `runXMLRPCActivation`'s sibling handler comes from `registerCentralCallbacks` (ccu_wiring.go:632-645), whose sole assignment into the handle is central_bringup.go:388 `callbackURL, binRPCCallbackAddr, cbHandlers, deregister := registerCentralCallbacks(...)` → :396 `cbHandlers: cbHandlers,`. Repo-wide grep for `cbHandlers` returns exactly the sites above plus one test.

The flag is read at callback_handlers.go:560 `if h.delayNewDeviceCreation.Load() {` inside `NewDevices` (callback_handlers.go:543), i.e. per-handler-instance state.
