The threshold that lives at tracker.go:220-225 is re-expressed as a call pattern at seven live sites and cannot be expressed any other way with today's Tracker API, and four of the seven are guarded only against the pattern, not the effect — so a threshold change to three samples, or de-duplication inside Record, leaves those tests green.

But the finding's stated consequence is wrong for two of its three unguarded legs. `health.ServiceAvailability` treats UNHEALTHY on a non-critical, non-interface component exactly as it treats DEGRADED: tracker.go:385-392 sets `worst = StatusDegraded` for UNHEALTHY, and :393-396 sets the same for DEGRADED. isCriticalComponent (:460-463) `return name == "sqlite" || name == "central"` excludes mqtt and matter; isInterfaceComponent excludes "mqtt" by name (:475) and "matter" / "matter.bridge" by the hyphen and dot rules (:488, :491). So drift at the MQTT and Matter sites changes the per-component badge on the diagnostic surface and nothing else — not the /health verdict the finding invokes. Only the recovery-failed leg sits on an interface component (`component(e.InterfaceID)`, health_wiring.go:71-77), where it feeds the "every interface unhealthy" rule at :402.

A second erosion found while attacking: on the ordinary recovery path the escalation record at :160 is already redundant, because RecoveryStartedEvent (connection_recovery.go:1024) has just driven the same component to DEGRADED via health_wiring.go:145, so a lone unhealthy sample would reach UNHEALTHY anyway. It is load-bearing only on the exhausted path (connection_recovery.go:1002), which publishes RecoveryFailedEvent with no preceding RecoveryStartedEvent in that run. Real, worth an entry, but a display-status regression at most sites — low, not medium.

It is not two readings of one datum for two callers — it is one question ("which profile is active for this link?") answered twice over one embedded archive by two functions that give different answers for the same input, on two live WS surfaces (links.get_profiles vs links.get_form_schema) that a single SPA link-editor session hits back to back. The type system does not force it: the adapter's json.RawMessage constraint struct exists so the full profile payload can be forwarded to the SPA verbatim, which does not prevent it decoding through the store's matcher. Damage is observable: the same link is reported as profile N by the WS profile list and pre-selected as Expert (0) by the UI schema, or the reverse via the string case.

WHAT I COULD NOT CLOSE, stated as unverified rather than assumed: whether a live LINK paramset read actually delivers a value inside the tolerance band or a string-typed value. The transports argue in that direction (XML-RPC decode.go:129 parses to float64; BIN-RPC decode.go:168 reconstructs from a 30-bit mantissa; both toFloat switches declare a float32 case, i.e. their authors expected float32 to arrive) but neither the source nor any fixture pins a concrete live value that lands there, and I did not read a CCU. The reader's 1.0000001 is lifted from store_test.go:679 — it is the store's own synthetic test input, not a measured read, and I decline to cite it as proof the divergence fires today. The finding is confirmed on the measured function-level divergence plus the absent guard, which is what makes it a defect regardless of which input arrives: nothing in the repo will notice when the two drift further.

stands.title: The unit fallback table keys on a normalised unit spelling that the descriptor does not carry
stands.evidence: Quotes verified verbatim. metadata.go:266-271 — `var sensorMetadataByUnit = map[string]Metadata{` / `"%":    {ValueBehavior: hmenum.ValueBehaviorInstantaneous},` / `"bar":  {…}` / `"°C":   {Quantity: hmenum.QuantityTemperature, …}` / `"g/m³": {ValueBehavior: hmenum.ValueBehaviorInstantaneous},`. Lookup is exact: metadata.go:471-473 `func MetadataByUnit(unit string) Metadata {` / `return sensorMetadataByUnit[unit]`. uischema_adapter.go:454-456 quoted correctly. The reader flagged this low because it could not see the callers; I resolved that. TWO CALLER SHAPES EXIST TODAY. (a) The model layer passes the CLEANED unit: internal/model/generic/quantity.go:52-56 `// Unit-fallback as last resort. Use the cleaned unit so spelling` / `// quirks ("Lux" vs "lx") don't break the lookup.` / `if cleaned := CleanupUnit(param, d.Descriptor.Unit); cleaned != "" {` / `if q := parameter.MetadataByUnit(cleaned).Quantity; …`, and the same at quantity.go:85-88 for ValueBehavior. (b) The MQTT discovery builder passes the RAW descriptor unit: internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:581 `if cls := resolveSensorStateClass(ev.Model, ev.Parameter, ev.descUnit()); cls != "" {` and discovery.go:559 `if dc := componentDeviceClass(comp, ev.Model, ev.Parameter, ev.descUnit()); dc != "" {`, where internal/north/mqtt/bridge.go:304-309 is `func (e Event) descUnit() string {` / `if d := e.genericDesc(); d != nil {` / `return d.Unit` — the unnormalised wire value. That value reaches `parameter.MetadataFor(deviceModel, param, unit)` (discovery_metadata.go:80, :91) whose third tier is `return MetadataByUnit(unit)` (metadata.go:488). The same file normalises for DISPLAY only, 170 lines later: discovery.go:752-755 `if _, has := body["unit_of_measurement"]; !has {` / `if cleaned := generic.CleanupUnit(hmenum.Parameter(ev.Parameter), ev.descUnit()); cleaned != "" {`. Raw spellings are real, not hypothetical: a scan of ../godevccu/internal/embed/data/paramset_descriptions/*.json finds UNIT `"100%"` on 2200 descriptors, `"% rF"` on 29, `"degree"` on 12, `"Lux"` on 6, against the canonical `"°C"` on 282. GUARD: none for the mismatch. internal/parameter/metadata_test.go:202 `TestMetadataByUnit` exercises only the canonical keys.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, every production call site would have wrapped the unit — I would have seen `generic.CleanupUnit(...)` inside the argument to resolveSensorStateClass/componentDeviceClass exactly as it appears at discovery.go:753, or `descUnit()` would itself return the cleaned string. It does not: bridge.go:306 returns `d.Unit` untouched, and no CleanupUnit call appears anywhere on the discovery.go:559/:581 argument path.
stands.reason: One live caller (the MQTT/HA discovery builder, the surface where device_class and state_class actually matter) feeds the firmware's raw spelling into an exact-match table keyed on canonical forms, while another live caller feeds the cleaned form. The dependency is stated at neither the table (metadata.go:266) nor the lookup (metadata.go:471). Raised from the reader's `low` because the missing input is now measured and the affected plane is the one that drives HA long-term statistics.
stands.divergence: Concrete input: descriptor `{"ID":"LEVEL_REAL","TYPE":"FLOAT","OPERATIONS":5,"FLAGS":1,"UNIT":"100%"}` (read+event, visible; present on HM-LC-Dim1T-FM-2, HM-LC-Dim1PWM-CV, HM-LC-DW-WM and ~15 more in ../godevccu/internal/embed/data/paramset_descriptions/). LEVEL_REAL appears in neither `metadataByParam` nor `metadataByDeviceAndParam` (grep of internal/parameter/metadata.go: no hit) nor in the MQTT entity-description tables (grep of internal/north/mqtt: no hit), so both paths fall through to the unit tier. Model layer: `CleanupUnit("LEVEL_REAL","100%")` → fixUnitReplace hit `"100%": "%"` (internal/model/generic/unit_cleanup.go:47) → `MetadataByUnit("%")` → `{ValueBehavior: Instantaneous}`. MQTT layer: `MetadataFor(model,"LEVEL_REAL","100%")` → `MetadataByUnit("100%")` → zero `Metadata{}` → `resolveSensorStateClass` returns "" → no `state_class` in the discovery payload, while discovery.go:753 still stamps `unit_of_measurement: "%"`. Net: a `%` sensor HA will not keep long-term statistics for. Corroborating: the two other read-only `100%` sensors, DIRT_LEVEL and SMOKE_LEVEL, only escape this because a hand-written override re-adds it — internal/north/mqtt/entity_description_rules_sensors.go:202 `"DIRT_LEVEL": {Key: "DIRT_LEVEL", StateClass: "measurement", UnitOfMeasurement: "%", …}` and :205 for SMOKE_LEVEL, applied later at discovery.go:613 `body["state_class"] = desc.StateClass`. Residual uncertainty, stated as such: I did not verify that LEVEL_REAL survives the custom-light absorption and visibility gate to be published as a standalone MQTT sensor — internal/model/custom/light/light.go:420-451 consumes it as the RF dimmers' effective level. The function-level divergence is measured; the end-to-end emission for that one parameter is unverified.
stands.deadCopy: neither — internal/model/generic/quantity.go:54,:87 and internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:559,:581 are both production paths
stands.guard: none
stands.secondReason:
Survived. The quotes are exact. This is not one datum read two ways for two callers: it is one lookup table, one exact-match accessor, and two caller shapes that disagree about which spelling the accessor takes — with the disagreement occurring inside a single discovery-body builder, which decides at line 581 that the raw unit is the right key and at line 753 that the cleaned one is. The dependency is documented at neither the table (metadata.go:266) nor the accessor (metadata.go:471), which is why the raw-unit call sites read as correct.

The damage is narrow but real and it is observable: LEVEL_REAL is the single parameter that survives every other rescue, and I closed the leg the reader left open — the RfDimmer profile binds it with Visible(), which forces CDPVisible, the one custom-DP usage the discovery gate is written to pass. Its discovery payload therefore ships a `%` unit with no `state_class`, so HA records no long-term statistics for the effective level of every RF dimmer. That DIRT_LEVEL and SMOKE_LEVEL escape only via hand-written per-parameter overrides is corroboration, not coincidence: the general rescue that should have caught all three (PERCENTAGE_FALLBACK, priority -100) is defeated by the same raw-vs-cleaned mismatch at entity_descriptions_table.go:120.

Unverified, and I am not treating it as verified: I read this end to end in the source and in ../godevccu descriptor fixtures; I did not run a daemon and observe the emitted payload. Every step of the chain is quoted above, so the inference is traceable, but the emission itself is reasoned, not measured.

stands.title: The lock ENCODE half lives in the adapter while the model owns the DECODE half
stands.evidence:
Both quotes verified verbatim. schedules.go:922-933 reads exactly `case "user_permission":` / `case "granted": e.Level = 1.0` / `case "not_granted": e.Level = 0.0` / `e.Duration = weekprofile.FormatTimeBaseFactor(lockPermissionDurationBase, lockPermissionDurationFactor)` / `// Permission slots target channels >= 2_x.` / `if len(e.TargetChannels) == 0 { e.TargetChannels = []string{"2_1"} }`. The duration constants are adapter-local: schedules.go:684-687 `const ( lockPermissionDurationBase = 7 // HOUR_1 ; lockPermissionDurationFactor = 31 // -> sentinel "always" )`. lock.go:87-89 reads exactly `// Sole owner of the threshold: both read paths call this rather than` / `// restating 0.5, so the boundary moves in one place.` and lock.go:73-74 `// Sole owner of the rule: the REST/WS read path and the week-profile read` / `// path both call this, so a lock slot cannot get two different verdicts.`

IMPORTANT NARROWING: the door_lock half of the candidate's claim is refuted. schedules.go:911 `level, durBase, durFactor, ok := lockActionRawFor(e.LockAction)` delegates to schedules.go:681 `return schedule.EncodeLockAction(schedule.LockAction(action))`, so LEVEL 1.0/0.0 and the (7,31) pair for door-lock actions come from schedule.LockActionTable (lock.go:29-33), not from the adapter. Only the user_permission branch carries adapter-local literals.

Both sides live: applyLockEncoding reached from serializeSimpleScheduleWithDomain (schedules.go:1017, PutSimpleSchedule); DetectLockMode/DetectLockPermission reached from two production readers — schedules.go:759,766 (REST/WS) and week_profile_io.go:178,184 (defaultChannelLoader.Load → MQTT Zeitplan attrs).
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, applyLockEncoding's user_permission branch would have called a schedule-package encoder (the way its door_lock sibling calls schedule.EncodeLockAction at schedules.go:681) and the 0.5 threshold in lock.go:38 would have had a paired exported write constant. It does neither: `grep -rn 'lockPermissionDurationBase' --include='*.go'` returns only the adapter definition at schedules.go:685 and its single use at schedules.go:929 — no model-side counterpart exists.
stands.reason: The write-side permission encoding (LEVEL 1.0/0.0, duration base/factor 7/31, default target "2_1") and the mode default "1_1" are stated only in internal/central/adapter/schedules.go, while the two rules that read them back — the 0.5 threshold and the "1_" prefix rule — declare themselves sole owners in internal/model/schedule/lock.go. Nothing couples them. The guards near this code do not close the gap: TestSerializeSimpleScheduleWithDomainLock (schedule_coerce_test.go:287-320) iterates schedule.LockActionTable and therefore only guards the door_lock half that already delegates; TestLockRuleCrossPlane (lock_rule_cross_plane_test.go:16-27) explicitly compares the two READ planes against each other and never against the write side ("never against a literal, so neither plane is checked against its own copy of the rule"); TestApplyLockEncodingUserPermissionGranted/NotGranted (infra_nil_guards_test.go:386-412) restate the adapter's own literals 1.0 / 0.0 / "2_1", so they would move with the adapter and stay green if the model's threshold moved. Severity medium: a divergence corrupts a door-lock schedule on a real device, but it takes a code change (or the input below) to trigger.
stands.divergence: A live diverging input exists today. Entry hmapi.SimpleScheduleEntry{LockMode: "user_permission", Permission: "granted", TargetChannels: []string{"1_3"}}: the write side preserves the caller's actor-1 target (schedules.go:931 `if len(e.TargetChannels) == 0` only defaults when empty — and internal/central/adapter/infra_nil_guards_test.go:414-425 pins this preservation with "3_2") and writes LEVEL 1.0, DURATION_BASE 7, DURATION_FACTOR 31. Both read planes then return a different thing than was written: schedule.DetectLockMode(["1_3"]) = LockModeDoorLock (lock.go:76-83, first char '1' and second '_'), and schedule.DetectLockAction(1.0, 7, 31) = LockActionUnlock (lock.go:31 `LockActionUnlock: {level: 1.0, durBase: 7, durFactor: 31}`). So a slot saved as "user permission = granted" reads back on REST/WS and on the MQTT Zeitplan attributes as a door-lock "unlock" action. Nothing rejects it on the way in: schedule.SimpleEntry.ValidateFor's lock branch (simple.go:261-285) checks mode/action/permission exclusivity but never the target-channel/mode consistency, and ValidateFor has no production caller at all (grep: only comments at schedules.go:703,710,714 and simple.go:364-368).
stands.guard: none. Nearest: TestSerializeSimpleScheduleWithDomainLock (internal/central/adapter/schedule_coerce_test.go:287) covers door_lock only and drives from schedule.LockActionTable; TestLockRuleCrossPlane (internal/central/adapter/lock_rule_cross_plane_test.go) compares read plane against read plane by construction. No test writes a permission slot and reads it back through DetectLockPermission.
stands.deadCopy: neither — both sides have production callers. But schedule.SimpleEntry.ValidateFor (internal/model/schedule/simple.go:228), the only place that could reject the diverging input, has no production caller.
stands.secondReason: The structural claim survives the attack intact and is stronger than stated: the model already owns the door-lock encode (EncodeLockAction) but owns no permission encode at all, so the split is a half-finished centralisation rather than a stylistic accident — and the two encodings collide on (1.0, 7, 31), which makes the model's "1_" prefix rule the only disambiguator between an adapter-written "permission granted" and a model-decoded "unlock". Move lockPermissionThreshold outside [0.0, 1.0], or repoint DetectLockMode's actor prefix, and every permission slot on a real HmIP-DLD decodes inverted or as the wrong mode on both REST/WS and MQTT, with no guard firing: the write-side guards restate the adapter's literals and the cross-plane guard compares the two READ planes only. Reachable, observable, unguarded — worth a backlog entry.

stands.title: The rega package's five doc comments instruct only half the ReGa charset rule; the canonical decoder is unexported in another package
stands.evidence: All quotes verified verbatim. internal/client/rega/runner.go:315 `// URL-encoded; callers should apply url.QueryUnescape before display.` — same instruction at :345 (GetServiceMessages: "Name, DeviceName, and each entry of Rooms and Functions are URL-encoded; callers should apply url.QueryUnescape before display."), :474 (GetProgramDescriptions), :484 (SysvarUsageProgram: "Name is URL-encoded; callers apply url.QueryUnescape before display."), :530 (GetSystemVariableDescriptions: "...should apply url.QueryUnescape before use."). internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:1616-1618 `// Every ReGa consumer must go through this function rather than calling` / `// url.QueryUnescape directly — the Latin-1 transcode below is the half that` / `// is easy to forget and impossible to repair once the value has been seeded.` and the implementation at :1619-1634 does QueryUnescape then `if !utf8.ValidString(s) { s = latin1ToUTF8String(s) }`. internal/client/backends/ccu_groups.go:348-351 `// jsEscape mirrors JavaScript escape(): ... HMServer decodes the group name as ISO-8859-1, so this is what keeps umlauts intact (e.g. "Süd" -> "S%FCd").` Liveness: `decodeRegaField` has 12 production call sites (hub_wiring.go:984,985,986,1163,1170,1451,1491,1496,1532,1533,1537,2286 and device_pipeline.go:1363); the runner methods it decodes are the production hub path. Decisive extra fact the candidate did not state: `decodeRegaField` is **unexported** in package `adapter`, so no consumer outside `internal/central/adapter` can follow the comment's own instruction — there is no exported canonical decoder to route to. The failure has already occurred twice in this tree: hub_wiring_charset_test.go:8-11 ("reproduces the real bug") and device_pipeline.go:1352-1360 ("skipping it left values such as an IP_ADDRESS data point's \"192.0.2.40\" seeded into the model as the literal \"172%2E18%2E4%2E40\""). Today no production consumer follows the bare-unescape advice: the only bare `url.QueryUnescape` on ReGa output in production is device_pipeline.go:1309, which unescapes the *key* (ASCII address/param) and routes the string *value* through decodeRegaField at :1363. Test-only followers of the bad advice exist: tests/integration/rega_test.go:222 and :229 call `neturl.QueryUnescape` on `assigned.ChannelAddress` / `assigned.Description` with no transcode.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false I would have seen either (a) the rega doc comments naming the transcode or a canonical decoder, or (b) an exported decoder in a shared package that the comments could point at. Both greps came back empty: `grep -rn "decodeRegaField" --include="*.go" .` returns only package-internal `adapter` hits, and the five runner comments say `url.QueryUnescape` and nothing else. Conversely, had I found a production caller outside `adapter` doing bare unescape on runner output, this would have been a live corruption bug rather than a latent one.
stands.reason: Two authorities describe one rule and they disagree: the producer's five doc comments state a one-step rule (URL-unescape), the consumer's canonical decoder implements a two-step rule (URL-unescape + conditional Latin-1 transcode) and explicitly says the second step is 'impossible to repair once the value has been seeded'. The encode half in ccu_groups.go (jsEscape) is the *inverse* function, not a third copy — that part of the candidate's framing is imprecise and I do not count it as duplication. The live defect is the comment claim, made worse by the canonical decoder being unexported: a caller in any other package literally cannot comply. Severity medium rather than low because the exact corruption has already shipped twice in this repo, and because it is irreversible — json.Marshal rewrites the raw 0xFC to U+FFFD on the way out of every north-bound plane.
stands.divergence: Input "Wassersensor Sp%FCle" (a real program condition summary from the CCU). Following runner.go:315's instruction — `url.QueryUnescape` alone — yields the byte sequence "Wassersensor Sp\xFCle", which is invalid UTF-8; json.Marshal emits "Wassersensor Sp�le". `decodeRegaField` yields "Wassersensor Spüle". The pair is pinned as case 1 of internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring_charset_test.go:14.
stands.guard: internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring_charset_test.go:12 TestDecodeRegaFieldLatin1 pins the decoder itself (six cases incl. "Wassersensor Sp%FCle" and the already-UTF-8 "K%C3%BCche" no-op). NOTHING pins consumers to it: there is no test forbidding a bare url.QueryUnescape on rega output. tests/contract/rest_path_decode_test.go:53 does match on `url.PathUnescape/QueryUnescape` selectors but it governs REST path params, not the rega surface — it would not fire.
stands.deadCopy: Neither side is dead. Both decodeRegaField and the runner methods have production callers.
stands.secondReason: Survives quote, sameness and divergence. It is not a two-readings-of-one-datum pair: runner.go's instruction and hub_wiring.go's instruction are the same rule stated twice, and one of them is wrong. What it does NOT survive is the damage bite at full weight, so I downgrade medium to low. I traced every production caller of the five methods: hub_wiring.go:978 (GetProgramDescriptions), :1160 (GetSystemVariableDescriptions), :1475 (GetServiceMessages), :1520 (GetAlarmMessages), :2280 (SysvarUsagePrograms) — all five live in internal/central/adapter and every field they touch goes through decodeRegaField / decodeRegaFields (:984-986, :1163, :1170, :1491-1504, :1532-1537, :2286). Nothing in production follows the incomplete instruction, so current user-visible exposure is zero and the finding is preventive. I also reject the severity rationale's 'has already shipped twice': both prior corruptions are fixed and pinned (hub_wiring_charset_test.go; the IP_ADDRESS case documented at device_pipeline.go:1355-1361), so that is history, not present exposure. Two things keep it worth a backlog entry rather than a dismissal: the drift is visible and irreversible when it happens (U+FFFD after json.Marshal), and the in-repo corroboration is concrete — the backends copies (ccu_extended.go:225, :306) read the same scripts and apply neither step, which is exactly the failure the comment invites. Note also that ccu_groups.go's jsEscape is the inverse (encode) function, not a third decoder; the finding already concedes that and I agree — I dropped it from the site list.

stands.title: CcuBackend.GetAllDeviceData's two branches return incompatible key grammars, the interface documents a third, and the whole method is dead in production while the live seed path re-derives the grammar
stands.evidence: Quotes verified verbatim (candidate's line numbers are 1-7 lines off in places; real ones given here). internal/client/backends/ccu_extended.go:545 `func (b *CcuBackend) GetAllDeviceData(ctx context.Context) (map[string]map[string]any, error) {`, ReGa branch :547-562 `// The ReGa script returns a flat {"DPName": value, ...} map where` / `// the keys are dot-separated DP names (e.g. "HmIP-RF.ADDR:1.LEVEL").` … `out := make(map[string]map[string]any, len(flat))` / `for k, v := range flat { out[k] = map[string]any{"value": v} }`; JSON-RPC branch :566-580 `raw, err := b.json.Call(ctx, "Interface.getAllDeviceData")` … `for addr, inner := range outer { if m, ok := inner.(map[string]any); ok { out[addr] = m } }`. internal/client/backends/backend.go:154-158 `// GetAllDeviceData returns all current parameter values for all devices on` / `// the interface in one call (where supported). Used during discovery to` / `// pre-populate the value cache.` — the interface comment does NOT itself state a key grammar; the third shape is stated one layer up at internal/client/interface_client_orchestration.go:340 `// The returned map is keyed by channelAddress → paramName → value.` (candidate attributes it to the interface; the wording is at the orchestration wrapper). Liveness by grep of `FetchAllDeviceData|GetAllDeviceData` across the whole repo: the ONLY non-test reference to `InterfaceClient.FetchAllDeviceData` is its own definition at interface_client_orchestration.go:342 plus a justification string in tests/contract/empty_absent_failed_collapse_test.go:33. Every other caller is a `_test.go` fake or test. The live path is internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:1296 `seedValues`, called from device_pipeline.go:936 and load_refresh.go:31, which runs `hmenum.RegaScriptFetchAllDeviceData` directly at :1303 and re-derives the grammar at :1309-1313 `key, err := url.QueryUnescape(rawKey)` / `parts := strings.SplitN(key, ".", 3)` / `if len(parts) != 3 { continue }` / `channelAddr, parameter := parts[1], parts[2]`.
stands.negativeControl: Had the dead-copy half been false, `grep -rn "FetchAllDeviceData" --include="*.go" .` would have shown a call from cmd/, internal/central/ or internal/north/ outside a _test.go file. It shows none — only the definition, a contract-test justification string, and test fakes. Had the branch-divergence half been false, the ReGa branch would have parsed and re-keyed the flat map the way seedValues does; instead it wraps each flat key verbatim under a literal "value" sub-key.
stands.reason: Three statements of one output grammar, no two of which agree, and the one with a production caller is not the one in the backend. Confirming the candidate's three-rules point by reading both copies: seedValues applies url.QueryUnescape to the key (:1309), excludes edge-trigger parameters (`if hmenum.IsEdgeTriggerParameter(...) { continue }`, :1321-1322), and decodes string values through decodeRegaField (:1363) — the backend copy at ccu_extended.go:552-561 does none of the three. Severity medium, not high: nothing breaks today because nothing calls it, but the documented contract at interface_client_orchestration.go:340 is a trap — the first real caller written against it seeds keys the ModelRegistry cannot resolve, silently (every resolution failure in seedValues is a bare `continue`).
stands.divergence: Wire input for channel 00021BE9957782:4, parameter LEVEL, value 0.5. ReGa branch: the script emits {"HmIP-RF.00021BE9957782%3A4.LEVEL": 0.5}, so the method returns map["HmIP-RF.00021BE9957782%3A4.LEVEL"] = {"value": 0.5} — interface prefix retained, colon still percent-encoded, parameter name buried in the key, one sub-key literally named "value". JSON-RPC branch: the CCU returns {"00021BE9957782:4": {"LEVEL": 0.5}}, so the method returns map["00021BE9957782:4"]["LEVEL"] = 0.5. A caller written to the documented contract (`data["00021BE9957782:4"]["LEVEL"]`) gets 0.5 on the JSON-RPC branch and a miss on the ReGa branch — and the ReGa branch is the one the comment at :551 calls "the canonical path" (`// wire:inline reason=rega-preferred-fallback`, :564).
stands.guard: None. internal/client/backends/ccu_extended_test.go:732 TestCcuGetAllDeviceDataDispatch and :723/:754 exercise the method's own branches; no test compares the two shapes to each other or to the documented contract, and no test compares the backend copy to seedValues. The seed path has its own tests (device_pipeline_test.go:928, :983, :1051) that never touch the backend method.
stands.deadCopy: internal/client/backends/ccu_extended.go:545 CcuBackend.GetAllDeviceData and its sole wrapper internal/client/interface_client_orchestration.go:342 InterfaceClient.FetchAllDeviceData. Neither has a production caller anywhere in cmd/, internal/central/, internal/north/ or internal/store/ — only _test.go fakes. The live grammar lives in internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:1296.
stands.secondReason: Survives quote, sameness, liveness and divergence, with one framing correction. Correction first: the title's 'the interface documents a third [grammar]' does not hold. backend.go:154-158 reads `// GetAllDeviceData returns all current parameter values for all devices on` / `// the interface in one call (where supported). Used during discovery to` / `// pre-populate the value cache. Returns [ErrUnsupported] for backends` / `// without this capability.` — it states no key grammar at all. So there are two grammars, not three, and the only doc that states one (orchestration:340) agrees with the JSON-RPC fallback and contradicts the branch the code itself calls canonical (:567 'the canonical path is the ReGa script above'). That is the sharper form of the finding, and it still stands. Sameness holds: this is one method with one signature answering one question, not two readings for two callers — the type system does not force the shapes apart, the ReGa branch chooses to wrap under a literal "value" sub-key. Liveness attack does not kill it and per the brief strengthens it: the entire chain GetAllDeviceData ← FetchAllDeviceData ← nothing is dead in production, while the live seed path re-implements the read with three extra rules the backend copy lacks — so the backend copy's tests (ccu_extended_test.go:732 TestCcuGetAllDeviceDataDispatch) stay green over a contract nothing exercises. Damage is where I downgrade medium to low: nothing observable changes today, no user-visible symptom exists, and the cost is entirely borne by a future first caller. One input I deliberately did not assume: whether ReGa's UriEncode percent-encodes ':' is a firmware behaviour the repo does not state, so I dropped the finding's '%3A' detail. The divergence does not depend on it — the three-dotted-component key with an interface prefix is readable directly from the script and from SplitN(key, ".", 3).

stands.evidence: Quotes verified verbatim. rgbw.go:120-121 inside NewRGBWLight: `		MinKelvin:  2000,` / `		MaxKelvin:  6500,`. init.go:316-330 `kelvinBoundsFromChannel` reads the descriptor: `	dp := ch.Parameter(hmenum.ParameterColorTemperature)` … `	if len(desc.Min) > 0 { _ = json.Unmarshal(desc.Min, &lo) }` … `	return int32(lo), int32(hi)`. init.go:250-252 in newDaliConstructor passes the literals `		}, rebased),` / `		2000, 6500,` / `	), nil`. Both sides are live production paths: init.go:64 `r.MustRegisterConstructor(hmenum.DeviceProfile("IPRGBW"), newRGBWConstructor)`, init.go:51 `…("IPDRGDALI"), newDaliConstructor`, init.go:74 `…("RfDimmer_Color_Temp"), newColorTempConstructor`; the sole production caller of kelvinBoundsFromChannel is init.go:306. The descriptor is reachable at the RGBW site: profile_configs.go:256-265 puts `hmenum.FieldColorTemperature: Bare(hmenum.ParameterColorTemperature)` on the IPRGBW primary channel, configFromChannel (init.go:168-175) passes that same `ch` as cfg.Channel, and hmenum/parameter.go:42 defines `ParameterColorTemperature Parameter = "COLOR_TEMPERATURE"`. Downstream consumers of the literals: payload.go:681/1001/1029 publish min_kelvin/max_kelvin, rgbw.go:386-390 clamps SetKelvin.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false I would have seen one of two things: a second production caller of kelvinBoundsFromChannel inside NewRGBWLight / newDaliConstructor (repo-wide grep for the symbol returns only init.go:306 and its definition), or descriptors declaring MIN=2000 / MAX=6500 so both rules agree. Neither holds — the fixtures declare 1000/10200.
stands.divergence: godevccu paramset fixture HmIP-RGBW.json, VCU5629873:1 VALUES COLOR_TEMPERATURE: {MIN: 1000, MAX: 10200, UNIT: 'K', TYPE: 'INTEGER'} (identically for :2..:4; HmIP-DRG-DALI.json VCU7338277:1..:48 and HmIP-LSC.json VCU7603954:1). Fed that channel, kelvinBoundsFromChannel returns (1000, 10200); NewRGBWLight / newDaliConstructor return (2000, 6500) for the same channel. Consequence today: HA/MQTT is told min_kelvin=2000/max_kelvin=6500 and rgbw.go:386-390 clamps a user-requested 1500 K up to 2000 K and 8000 K down to 6500 K on hardware whose own descriptor declares 1000–10200 K.
stands.deadCopy: neither — both copies have production callers (init.go:51/64 for the literals, init.go:74 for the descriptor read)
stands.guard: none for the coupling. The only test touching it pins the literal in the wrong direction: internal/model/custom/light/rgbw_colortemp_combined_test.go:132 `if r.MinKelvin != 2000 {` — it would go red if someone fixed the RGBW side, and stays green while the two rules disagree.
stands.reason: One datum (the fixture's declared hardware colour-temperature range) is resolved by two different rules inside one package, and a real device descriptor already makes them disagree by 1000 K at the bottom and 3700 K at the top. The descriptor-reading helper sits in the same file that hard-codes the literals for the two other constructors.
stands.secondReason: Every attack line fails to kill it. The quote is current. The datum is one datum: the hardware colour-temperature range for a channel, resolved by a descriptor read for one constructor and by a hard-coded literal for two others in the same file. Liveness holds on the literal side (IPRGBW, IPDRGDALI, and hmip-lsc via IPRGBW at profiles.go:1110 are all registered profiles). The divergence reproduces from the source rather than a convention. Damage is observable on both a write path and a published payload. One qualification worth carrying into the fix, measured not assumed: the descriptor-reading helper's only production caller is newColorTempConstructor / RfDimmer_Color_Temp, whose devices are hm-lc-dw-wm and hm-dw-wm (profiles.go:639), and neither fixture's channels carry a COLOR_TEMPERATURE parameter at all — VCU0000115:1 and VCU0000098:1 list only DIRECTION/LEVEL/LEVEL_REAL/ON_TIME/RAMP_TIME/etc. So in the measured fleet kelvinBoundsFromChannel always returns (0,0) and color.go:296-303 substitutes the same 2000/6500. That makes the finding stronger, not weaker: the only rule that ever produces a device-specific answer is the one that never runs, while the three devices that do carry the descriptor are exactly the ones pinned to the literal. Also noted: init.go:239-241 carries a truncated rationale, `// newDaliConstructor builds a DRGDaliLight for the HmIP-DRG-DALI.` / `// Kelvin bounds match` — the sentence ends there, so no source is cited for 2000/6500. I looked for one: the Python reference exposes no Kelvin bounds at all (aiohomematic/model/custom/light.py has only _MAX_KELVIN = 1000000, the mireds conversion constant), and homematicip_local never sets min/max either, so the pair is loom-local and undocumented. Not a blocker to acting, but the fix should decide deliberately rather than assume the literal encodes a known hardware limit.

stands.title: The colour / kelvin / effect half of IsStateChangeFull can never fire — Go has no virtual dispatch and no subtype overrides the hooks
stands.evidence: Quotes verified verbatim. light.go:1038-1042: `func (l *Light) commandedHSColor() (HSColor, bool)        { _ = l; return HSColor{}, false }` and the four siblings, preceded by light.go:1028-1030 `// type. ColorLight / ColorTempLight / EffectLight override the` / `// relevant accessor; Light itself returns \`(_, false)\` so a generic` / `// Light without these capabilities reports "not commanded".`. light.go:998-1001: `	if args.HSColor != nil {` / `		if hs, ok := l.commandedHSColor(); !ok || hs != *args.HSColor {` / `			return true`. A repo-wide grep for commandedHSColor / commandedColorTempKelvin / commandedEffect / commandedOnTime / commandedRampTime returns exactly ten lines, all in light.go: the five definitions (:1038-1042) and the five call sites (:999, :1004, :1009, :1014, :1019) — no override with a *ColorLight / *ColorTempLight / *EffectLight / *RGBWLight receiver exists anywhere, and no file outside light.go mentions the names. The three live callers pass exactly one of the affected fields: color.go:214 `	if !l.IsStateChangeFull(StateChangeArgsFull{HSColor: &hs}) {`, color.go:377 `	if !l.IsStateChangeFull(StateChangeArgsFull{ColorTempKelvin: &kelvinU16}) {`, effect.go:179 `	if !l.IsStateChangeFull(StateChangeArgsFull{Effect: &effectLabel}) {`.
stands.negativeControl: Had the doc comment been true, the grep for those five names would have returned at least one definition with a non-*Light receiver (in color.go or effect.go) plus the cached state it reads. It returns only the five *Light stubs and the five call sites — and even a subtype definition would not change the outcome, because the call happens inside (*Light).IsStateChangeFull, which resolves statically to the base method.
stands.divergence: Call ColorLight.SetColor(ctx, 120, 50, prio) twice with an already-observed on-state: the second call reaches light.go:994, IsStateChange(false,false,nil) returns false (light.go:944-958), then commandedHSColor() returns (HSColor{}, false) → `!ok` → IsStateChangeFull returns true → the HUE/SATURATION put_paramset is written to the CCU again. The suppression the doc-comment at color.go:192-193 promises ("Returns nil without writing when IsStateChangeFull reports no change") never triggers. Identical for ColorTempLight.SetKelvin (any repeated Kelvin) and EffectLight.SetEffect (any repeated effect index).
stands.deadCopy: The colour/kelvin/effect/on-time/ramp-time half of the suppression rule is the dead copy: its only implementations are the (_, false) stubs, so five of the six branches of IsStateChangeFull are decision-free. The live suppression is the on/off/brightness half in IsStateChange (light.go:944), which reads real state via commandedIsOn / commandedBrightness.
stands.guard: none. No test file in the repo references IsStateChangeFull or StateChangeArgsFull; the only two hits are prose in internal/central/adapter/custom_dp_dispatcher_test.go:462 and dispatcher_converters_test.go:261, which assert nothing about the colour branches.
stands.reason: The comment asserts a property of the code ("ColorLight / ColorTempLight / EffectLight override the relevant accessor") that the code does not carry — a refuted consumer claim of exactly the shape the release sweep hunts. The effect is a documented, exercised suppression path that is structurally unable to suppress, so every repeated colour, colour-temperature and effect command reaches the CCU (radio duty cycle on HmIP), and a future fix must add state or an interface, not a shadow method.
stands.secondReason: The structural claim is airtight and the language rules out the escape route: even if ColorLight declared its own commandedHSColor, the call inside (*Light).IsStateChangeFull binds statically to Light's method, so shadowing on an embedding type could not change the outcome — the fix must add state or an interface, exactly as the finding says. Tracing the values: SetColor/SetKelvin/SetEffect pass TurnOn=false, TurnOff=false, Brightness=nil, so IsStateChange (light.go:945-960) either returns true (state not yet observed) or falls through to `return false`; in the fall-through case the HSColor/Kelvin/Effect block is reached, the hook returns ok=false, `!ok` short-circuits and IsStateChangeFull returns true. There is no input for which it returns false while one of those three fields is non-nil. Corroboration I did not expect to find and which closes the 'maybe it was never meant to bite' defence: the package's own guard test asserts nothing. light_color_write_guard_test.go:27-28 is titled `// TestSetColorGuardSuppressesRepeat verifies that a second SetColor call with` / `// the same hue+saturation does not produce a second write.`, but its body ends at :55-57 with `// The first SetColor already proves the guard path exists; suppression` / `// only fires after the state is actually observed. We just verify the` / `// function returns nil without error on a second call — write count may` / `// or may not advance depending on optimistic-state tracking.` — no comparison of len(w.calls) at all. The sibling TestSetColorGuardAllowsChange does assert, which is why the pair reads as covered. One refinement to the damage wording, measured rather than assumed: there is a lower-level dedup at generic/datapoint.go in sendAndObserve — `// Burst-skip — silently no-op when the same value is in flight.` / `if snap := d.optimistic.Snapshot(); snap.Active && valuesClose(snap.Value, typed) { return nil }` — so a repeat issued while an unconfirmed write is still in flight is dropped there. It does not rescue the intended guard: once the CCU confirms and the optimistic window closes, the repeated HUE/SATURATION put_paramset, COLOR_TEMPERATURE set or PROGRAM set does reach the CCU. So 'every repeated command reaches the CCU' should read 'every repeated command outside the optimistic in-flight window reaches the CCU'.

stands.title: The ch<N>/vch<N> custom-DP name grammar is implemented a second time in the MQTT discovery adapter, and the two branch differently
stands.evidence: Both quotes are accurate. namedata.go:114-117: `cName := stripChannelAddressSuffix(channelName)` / `if cName == channelName {` / `return naming.NameData{DeviceName: deviceName, ChannelName: channelName}`; namedata.go:123-134: `isOnlyPrimary := channel.IsCustomDPPrimaryChannel() && channel.HasSinglePrimaryCustomDP()` / `if isOnlyPrimary || channel.IgnoreMultipleChannelsForName() {` … `marker := "vch"` / `if channel.IsCustomDPPrimaryChannel() { marker = "ch" }`. discovery_aggregate.go:597-611: `if insp.IsCustomDPSecondaryChannel() { return fmt.Sprintf("vch%d", ev.ChannelNo) }` then `if insp.IsCustomDPPrimaryChannel() { if insp.HasSinglePrimaryCustomDP() { return "" } … if ig, ok := ev.Channel.(IgnoreMultipleChannelsForNameInspector); ok && ig.IgnoreMultipleChannelsForName() { return "" } return fmt.Sprintf("ch%d", ev.ChannelNo) }`. BOTH LIVE: device.BuildCustomDataPointName is called from internal/north/rest/handlers/custom_data_points.go:255 (customDPNameData, production); displayChannelName is called from internal/north/mqtt/discovery_aggregate.go:307 and internal/north/mqtt/discovery_notify.go:65 (production discovery payload builders). The adapter's own comment concedes the duplication (internal/north/mqtt/channel_name_parity_test.go:32).
stands.negativeControl: Had the branch orders been equivalent, tracing both functions on the same channel would have produced the same marker for every input class. It does not: I traced the model's early return at namedata.go:115 (no `:N` in the channel name → returns before any marker is computed) against the adapter, which computes a marker from ev.ChannelNo alone and never inspects the channel name. Had the model NOT consulted the ignore flag for secondaries, line 124 would have read `isOnlyPrimary || (channel.IsCustomDPPrimaryChannel() && channel.IgnoreMultipleChannelsForName())`; it does not.
stands.divergence: Concrete diverging input available today: HmIP-DRSI4 (internal/model/custom/profiles.go:981-984 registers IPSwitch primaries on channels 6/10/14/18 → HasSinglePrimaryCustomDP is false) whose channel 10 carries an operator-assigned CCU name without a `:N` suffix (e.g. "Küche"). Model: baseChannelName → "Küche", stripChannelAddressSuffix("Küche") == "Küche" → early return at namedata.go:115-117 → ParameterName "" (no marker). Adapter: displayChannelName → "ch10". The parity test's own fixture forces the name "Galerie:3" precisely to dodge that early return (channel_name_parity_test.go:43-46: "The `:N` suffix is what puts the model on its marker path — without it BuildCustomDataPointName returns before ever computing one"), so the existing guard cannot see it. NOT reachable today: the candidate's headline case (secondary channel + IgnoreMultipleChannelsForName → model "" vs adapter "vch<N>"). *Lock is the only implementer of IgnoreMultipleChannelsForName (internal/model/custom/lock/lock.go:277), and every lock profile declares `SecondaryChannels: nil` (profile_configs.go:238 IPLock, :718 RfLock, :45 IPButtonLock, :569 RFButtonLock); channels only receive a CDP when they are in the profile's relevant set (internal/model/custom/materialize.go:186-188 + relevantChannels :289-311), so a Lock CDP never lands on a group secondary. That half is latent, not live.
stands.guard: internal/north/mqtt/channel_name_parity_test.go:TestDisplayChannelNameAgreesWithTheModel — exists, but covers only the plain-primary and plain-secondary branches with a forced `:N` channel name; no IgnoreMultipleChannelsForName case, no operator-named (non-`:N`) channel.
stands.reason: The grammar is genuinely implemented twice, both copies are on production paths, and the branch orders differ. Severity medium because the artefact that drifts is the HA entity name — HA derives entity_id from it, so a divergence silently renames entities and breaks user automations, while the REST/UI name stays put. Downgraded from the candidate's reasoning in one respect: the specific lock-secondary damage it names cannot occur with the shipped profile set; the reachable disagreement today is the non-`:N` operator channel name, which the guard's fixture deliberately avoids.
stands.secondReason: Survived every attack. The quotes are verbatim and current; both copies are on live paths (REST/SPA vs MQTT discovery); they read the same three channel predicates and both cite the same reference rule, so this is one grammar written twice, not one datum read two ways; the type system does not force it (the same package already exposes `ChannelNamer` at internal/north/mqtt/bridge.go:373-375 and BuildChannelEvent uses it at discovery_aggregate.go:127-131, so the adapter has access to everything the model reads); and the diverging input reproduces by reading. One correction to the finding's damage clause: the DRSI4/"Küche" disagreement is not a future rename — it is the SHIPPED state today (HA "<device> ch10" vs REST "Küche"), i.e. a cross-surface label disagreement of exactly the shape tests/contract/naming_authority_test.go:19-26 was written for ("FROST_PROTECTION on an HmIP-BWTH … was \"Frostschutz\" over REST and \"Frostschutz ch1\" over MQTT discovery"). The entity_id/automation-breakage framing applies to future drift of the duplicated marker branches, not to current behaviour; medium severity holds on the repo's own precedent that this class already shipped a user-visible bug once, with the existing parity guard blind to the live case by fixture construction.

stands.title: The channel→device address grammar is re-derived inline in the data point
stands.evidence: Quotes verified verbatim. datapoint.go:2137-2141: `	// Derive device address from channel address by stripping the \":N\" suffix.` / `	deviceAddr := key.ChannelAddress` / `	if i := lastColon(deviceAddr); i >= 0 {` / `		deviceAddr = deviceAddr[:i]` / `	}`; datapoint.go:2152-2154: `// lastColon returns the index of the last ':' in s, or -1 when absent.` / `// Inlined to avoid importing strings for a single call.` / `func lastColon(s string) int {`. The canonical owner exists and is widely used: pkg/hmtypes/address.go:69-76 `// DeviceAddress returns the device part of address, stripping the channel` / `// suffix if present. "ABC:1" → "ABC"; "ABC" → "ABC".` / `func DeviceAddress(address string) string {` / `	if before, _, ok := strings.Cut(address, ":"); ok {` — 19 production call sites (internal/alarm, internal/history/recorder.go:355, internal/central/coordinators/event.go:543, internal/store/devicedetails/cache.go:109, pkg/hmevent/security.go:131, …). `grep -rn "hmtypes.DeviceAddress" internal/model/` returns NOTHING, so the model package never uses it. The two rules are not the same rule: hmtypes cuts at the FIRST colon, datapoint.go at the LAST. datapoint.go already imports hmtypes (datapoint.go:18), so the stated rationale ("avoid importing strings") does not explain the private copy.
stands.negativeControl: Two independent controls. (1) Had the model delegated, `grep -rn "hmtypes.DeviceAddress" internal/model/` would have returned the call site; it returns nothing, and `grep -n lastColon internal/model/generic/*.go` returns the private helper at datapoint.go:2140,2152,2154 plus only test uses. (2) Had the repo's own single-source guard covered this copy, `internal/model/generic/datapoint.go` would appear in the guard's `found` slice and, being absent from `addressSplittersOutsideHmtypes` (address_rule_single_source_test.go:32-36, which lists only coordinators/link.go, adapter/devices.go, queryfacade.go), TestAddressSplittingHasOneSource would fail on a clean tree. I did not run the test (read-only), but its filter at :61 skips every method (`fn.Recv != nil`) and every function whose lowercased name lacks "deviceaddress" — the split here lives inside the method GetEventDataFor and a helper named lastColon, so both conditions exclude it by construction.
stands.reason: Confirmed, and stronger than the candidate framed it on two counts. First, the copy is on a DEAD path: `grep -rn "GetEventData" .` across the whole repo returns only the definitions (datapoint.go:2114-2141) and test callers (datapoint_validity_test.go:432,448; datapoint_event_at_test.go:20,36); `grep -rn "generic.EventData\|.EventData{"` returns no production use. So the tests exercise a last-colon rule while every live consumer of the same datum goes through hmtypes.DeviceAddress's first-colon rule — exactly the pattern the brief flags as the stronger finding. Second, the repo already has a dedicated guard for precisely this rule (TestAddressSplittingHasOneSource) whose own comment at :22-27 records that the copies which existed when it was written "carried three different behaviours between them, first colon versus last colon versus two spellings of the leading-colon edge case" — and it cannot see this one. The same blind spot leaves at least four further live splits unmeasured, all inside functions not named for the address: internal/central/central.go:1107 `base, _, _ := strings.Cut(channelAddress, ":")` (first colon), internal/central/coordinators/event.go:301 `addr, suffix, found := strings.Cut(channelAddress, ":")` (first colon), internal/central/adapter/climate_link_peer_refresh.go:60 `if idx := strings.LastIndex(channelAddr, ":"); idx > 0 {` (last colon), internal/routingkey/uniqueid.go:89 `if before, _, ok := strings.Cut(address, ":"); ok {` (first colon). Severity medium is for the guard gap, not for today's behaviour of the dead method.
stands.divergence: No input reachable today makes the two answer differently, and I will not invent one: for every address matching pkg/hmtypes/address.go:20 `^[0-9a-zA-Z-]{5,20}:\d{1,3}$` there is exactly one colon, so first-colon and last-colon agree. The divergence class the repo itself records is multi-separator addresses — address_rule_single_source_test.go:29-30: `// The entries left search BACKWARDS, which is a different rule rather than a` / `// stale copy: a link address may carry more than one separator.` On such an input `A:B:1` hmtypes.DeviceAddress returns `A` while datapoint.go returns `A:B`. Whether a link address actually reaches DataPoint.Key.ChannelAddress is a value the source does not carry — the guard's own comment leaves it as an open question ("Folding them without establishing what they actually receive would be a guess") — so I report it as an unresolved divergence class, not a demonstrated one.
stands.deadCopy: internal/model/generic/datapoint.go:2136 GetEventDataFor (and its lastColon helper at :2154) — the whole GetEventData/GetEventDataFor/EventData surface has no production caller; only internal/model/generic/datapoint_validity_test.go:432,448 and datapoint_event_at_test.go:20,36 reach it.
stands.guard: tests/contract/address_rule_single_source_test.go TestAddressSplittingHasOneSource is the guard for exactly this rule, and it is blind here: its filter (:61) skips methods (`fn.Recv != nil`) and only inspects functions whose lowercased name contains "deviceaddress". No guard would fail if datapoint.go's copy drifted from hmtypes.
stands.secondReason: Survived all five bites. Quotes exact, path provably dead (tests exercise a last-colon rule no production caller reaches, while every live consumer of the same datum goes through hmtypes' first-colon rule), repetition not forced by the type system or imports, and the repo's own dedicated guard for this exact rule is structurally blind to it — receiver methods, closures, and any helper not named '*deviceaddress*' pass through the filter at address_rule_single_source_test.go:59 unseen. I found one site beyond the candidate's list (rpc_recorder.go:358/366, a duplicate of the duplicate). Severity stays medium and belongs to the guard gap alone: no observable behaviour changes today because nothing calls the method.

stands.title: hmtypes.ToBool is the pkg-level truthy rule and has no production caller; internal/parameter re-implements the identical set, and six other sites use different sets
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, `grep -rn "hmtypes.ToBool" --include="*.go" . | grep -v _test.go` would have named at least one production file, and the same grep for ConvertReadValue would have shown a caller outside internal/parameter. Both returned only definitions and doc comments. Had the two token sets differed, the two verbatim `case "y", "yes", "t", "true", "on", "1":` lines would not have matched character for character.
stands.reason: Duplication and dead-copy both hold, and the dead-copy half is stronger than raised: neither cited copy is on a live path, so the shared package's stated truthy rule is unreachable AND its supposed live twin is unreachable too. Severity stays medium rather than high because drift between the two dead copies cannot break a running daemon today, and two of the live divergences are deliberate and documented (internal/parameter/coerce.go:121-129: "Different boundaries, different tolerances — keep both, do not unify."). Correction to the damage text: 'y' is not "silently false" on the live ingresses — it is rejected with an error or an ok=false, which fails loudly.
stands.divergence: Between the two cited copies: input " true" (one leading space). pkg/hmtypes/support.go:82 ToBool(" true") returns (false, nil) — it lower-cases but never trims; internal/parameter/converter.go:241 isBoolTrueString(" true") returns true. Between the LIVE paths: input "y". internal/model/hub/sysvar.go:799 (`case "true", "t", "yes", "y", "on", "1":`) accepts it as true for a sysvar write; internal/parameter/coerce.go:152-156 — the live REST/paramset write boundary reached from internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:877 and internal/central/adapter/paramsets.go:329 — returns `fmt.Errorf("parameter: cannot coerce %q to bool", v)`; internal/north/mqtt/command_subscriber.go:1011 parseBoolPayload("y") returns ok=false and the command is dropped.
stands.deadCopy: Both. siteA (pkg/hmtypes/support.go:82 ToBool) has zero production callers — only pkg/hmtypes/support_test.go. siteB (internal/parameter/converter.go:241 isBoolTrueString) is reachable only through ConvertReadValue (converter.go:141), which itself has zero production callers — only two _test.go files.
stands.guard: None. No test compares any two of the eight truthy sets. pkg/hmtypes/support_test.go and internal/parameter/converter_reference_parity_test.go each exercise their own copy in isolation, so they stay green through any drift. script/reachability/main.go cannot report either copy: :664 auto-whitelists every symbol under pkg/hmtypes and :680 every symbol under internal/parameter.
stands.secondReason: Survives, but I downgrade medium->low. Every measurable half holds: the pkg-level rule has zero production callers, its internal twin is dead as well, and the live boundaries genuinely disagree on "y". What does not survive is any damage story. Nothing a running daemon does can change if the two dead copies drift — no code path reaches either. The live disagreements are not one rule copied: they are three different write boundaries (sysvar ReGa write, device-parameter/REST coerce, MQTT payload) whose tolerance differences are stated and defended in the source itself (coerce.go:121-129), and the odd one out fails loudly rather than silently. The finding reduces to "a public package documents a truthy rule the daemon does not run" — a real dead-surface defect, but not worth medium.

stands.title: Most of the ported pkg/hmtypes helper surface has no production caller while internal packages re-implement the same rules
stands.evidence: Raw symbol grep (`grep -rn "\bNAME\b" --include="*.go" .` filtered to exclude _test.go and pkg/hmtypes/ itself) returns ZERO hits outside the package for: CleanupTextFromHTMLTags, HashSHA256, ElementMatchesKey, ChangedWithinSeconds, GetRxModes, SupportsRxMode, IsHost, IsIPv4Address, IsIPv6Address, FindFreePort, FixXMLRPCEncoding, IsChannelAddress, IsDeviceAddress, IsParamsetKey. Qualified grep adds ToBool=0, MaxCacheAge=0, InitTime=0, hmtypes.ChannelAddress=0 production (2 test). No dot-import and no alias of pkg/hmtypes exists (only `import "github.com/SukramJ/openccu-loom/pkg/hmtypes"`, checked repo-wide), so the qualified grep is complete. LIVE side of the same package: hmtypes.SplitChannelAddress 16 production callers, hmtypes.DeviceAddress 20, hmtypes.ChannelNo 2 — so the candidate's "the address split is done inline at ~15 sites" is only half right; the pkg splitter IS live, and separately eight production sites split a channelAddress with LastIndex/LastIndexByte (internal/alarm/intents.go:468, internal/central/queryfacade.go:530, internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:2285, mqtt_sink.go:71 and :162, eventbridge.go:2624 and :2635, climate_link_peer_refresh.go:60) while pkg/hmtypes/address.go:84 SplitChannelAddress uses `strings.Cut(address, ":")` (first colon). PathData: two same-named types. pkg/hmtypes/path_data.go:15 has four string fields and renders `central/<central>/device/<model>/<chan_addr>/<param>`; the live one is internal/model/naming/pathdata.go:85, whose MQTTState (:137-152) renders `fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s/%s/%s/%d/%s/%s", base, central, iface, address, ChannelNo, bucket, kind)`. The candidate's siteB quote verifies: internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:984 "description:      decodeRegaField(d.Description),".
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, the raw symbol grep for any one of those names would have named a production file outside pkg/hmtypes — as it does for SplitChannelAddress (16 hits), DeviceAddress (20) and ChannelNo (2), which is the control running green in the same command. Had hmtypes.PathData been live, `grep -rn "hmtypes.PathData"` would have hit outside the package; it returns nothing while `naming.PathData` returns ~60 production hits.
stands.reason: The dead-surface claim is measured, not inferred, and the whole listed set is dead. Two corrections to the reasoning: (a) FixXMLRPCEncoding and decodeRegaField are inverse transforms, not two copies of one rule, so 'the live equivalent' is imprecise — but FixXMLRPCEncoding still has zero callers of any kind; (b) hmtypes.SplitChannelAddress/DeviceAddress ARE live, so the address family is split between live and dead members rather than wholly superseded. Severity medium, not high: pkg/ is a declared public surface (CLAUDE.md, 'pkg/ — public surface'), so an exported helper with no internal caller is not automatically dead code — but a reader of the shared package is told a rule the daemon does not run, and the one mechanism that could have flagged it is deliberately blinded.

The finding survives, but only in a narrower form than its own damage clause states; three of its supporting sub-claims die under attack and I am recording the surviving core, not the framing.

This is not the EnumLabel/EnumLabelFromWire shape (one datum read two ways for two callers, each right for its caller): the different null semantics on the MQTT side ARE deliberate and documented at eventbridge.go:3242-3249, but nothing in the source states any reason for colour to be absent, and the REST side's openapi description ("Opaque; carried verbatim for a lossless round-trip") states the opposite intent. REFUTED — the layering/ownership framing in the title. "Authored in internal/central rather than in the plane that owns the wire contract" presumes an ownership rule the repo does not state and its code contradicts: HA payload authorship lives outside internal/north/mqtt by design across the codebase — internal/model/custom/climate/payload.go:141-142 sets `body["json_attributes_topic"]` and `body["json_attributes_template"]` and defines the Jinja template at :164-174; the state DTO lives in internal/payload/state.go:57. So the ownership half is an architectural preference, not a measured defect.

REFUTED — `slot_no` is not lost. eventbridge.go:3231 `out[strconv.Itoa(slot)] = simpleEntryJSON(sched.Entries[slot])` carries the slot number structurally as the map key. The evidence's "none of those four keys" is wrong on one of four; only three colour fields are actually dropped.

REFUTED — the schedule_api_version "drift". The claim that one stamp "is supposed to name the contract" and now has two values is an assumption the source does not carry. v1.0 (eventbridge.go:3447) stamps the Zeitplan sensor's json_attributes dict; v2.0 (climate/payload.go:387) stamps the climate entity's state payload — two different entities carrying two different, non-overlapping payload shapes (the Zeitplan climate branch, :3449-3462, emits no schedule_data at all). Undamaging by the finding's own admission, and unsourced as a single contract.

Severity stays medium: real functional gap on a published plane, read-only display, no control path affected. The actionable item is three missing keys in simpleEntryJSON plus a round-trip guard, not a relocation of the payload authorship.

The sameness holds: `"rest-operator"` and `"ws-operator"` are each declared twice, in packages with no shared type or constant, and the engine closes an authorization decision (code bypass at engine.go:648, rate-limit exemption at facade.go:180/278) on string equality against the north-bound copy — a drift in either adapter would silently code-gate and rate-limit an operator surface with nothing failing, since no test pins the pair. The SAMENESS: this is not two readings of one datum for two callers — DiscoveryUniqueID has no caller at all, and its doc comment claims the role that routingkey.CanonicalUniqueID actually fills, so it is a second copy of one rule rather than a second rule. The DIVERGENCE: reproduced by reading both paths. stands.title: Home Assistant template shapes are built inside the domain model, and nothing consumes them
stands.evidence:
Quotes verified verbatim. internal/model/hub/messages.go:881-886: `// AdditionalInformationIndexed returns the indexed-dict form of the` / `// alarm-messages list that HA's MQTT json_attributes_template expects:` / `// keys "alarm_1" .. "alarm_n" mapped to the alarm's Name`. :897-900: `// Counter returns the number of active alarm messages — i.e. the` / `// length of the message set. HA's MQTT statistics-template expects` / `// the active-alarm count`. :922: `out[key] = fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s", dev, msgs[i].Name)`.

Caller census (grep over *.go, whole repo):
- `AdditionalInformationIndexed` — 4 hits total: the two definitions (:887, :913) and internal/model/hub/hub_test.go:326,333. ServiceMessages.AdditionalInformationIndexed (:913) has ZERO references repo-wide, not even a test.
- `AlarmMessages.Counter()` (:901) — callers: internal/model/hub/hub_test.go:301,313 only.
- `AdditionalInformation() []map[string]any` (:822, :860) — no interface in the repo declares that signature (grep `AdditionalInformation() []map[string]any` returns only the two definitions). The two production capability-assertion sites both require the map form and take `device.ParameterDataPoint`: internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:2036 `AdditionalInformation() map[string]any` and internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:1118 `if ai, ok := dp.(interface{ AdditionalInformation() map[string]any }); ok {`. The candidate's type-mismatch claim is exact.

What the live HA path actually does: internal/central/adapter/hub_mqtt_publisher.go:424 `b.PublishAlarmMessages(ctx, centralName, hubModel.Messages, msgs)` with `msgs := hubModel.Messages.List()`; internal/north/mqtt/bridge.go:1463 `body, err := json.Marshal(items)` — the raw []AlarmMessage struct list. The discovery body at internal/north/mqtt/hub_discovery.go:568-571 reads `"value_template": "{{ value_json | length }}"` and `"json_attributes_template": `{"messages": {{ value_json | tojson }} }``. So HA is fed a list and derives the count with `| length` — never the indexed dict, never Counter().

Additional finding the candidate did not name: internal/model/hub/messages.go:127 `func (a *AlarmMessages) Count() int` has a byte-identical body to Counter() (:901) — `a.mu.RLock(); defer a.mu.RUnlock(); return len(a.messages)` — and Count() IS live: cmd/openccu-loom/ws_adapters.go:299, internal/north/rest/handlers/hub_data_points.go:144, internal/model/hub/payload.go:287.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, `grep -rn AdditionalInformationIndexed --include="*.go" .` would have returned a hit under internal/north/ or internal/central/ outside _test.go, and the alarm-messages discovery body would carry a template referencing `alarm_1`-style keys instead of `{{ value_json | length }}` / `{{ value_json | tojson }}`. Both greps came back with only definitions and tests; `grep -rn "alarm_1\|message_1" --include="*.go"` outside messages.go returned nothing.
stands.reason: Confirmed on both legs. Leg 1: the HA presentation shape (indexed dict, "<device>: <name>" join, the redefined counter) sits in internal/model/hub and has no production consumer, so the assertion about what HA's json_attributes_template / statistics-template expects is untestable from the core and is contradicted by the only template the daemon actually publishes. Leg 2: AlarmMessages.Counter() is an exact duplicate of the live AlarmMessages.Count() with a divergent doc comment; the dead copy is the one carrying the HA justification. Severity medium rather than low because the pair Count/Counter is the classic silent-drift shape — a future change to the live Count() leaves the HA-justified Counter() behind with no guard to notice. Guard status: internal/model/hub/hub_datapoint_properties_test.go:90 and hub_test.go:324 exercise the shapes against themselves; no test ties either to a published payload, so nothing would fail if the shapes drifted from HA's real expectation.
stands.deadCopy: internal/model/hub/messages.go:887 (AlarmMessages.AdditionalInformationIndexed — test-only), :913 (ServiceMessages.AdditionalInformationIndexed — zero references repo-wide), :901 (AlarmMessages.Counter — test-only, duplicate of the live Count at :127), and :822/:860 (AdditionalInformation []map[string]any — no interface in the repo declares that signature).
stands.divergence: Input: two active alarms, `{ID:"a1", Name:"Fenster offen"}` and `{ID:"a2", Name:"Tür offen"}`. Live MQTT path publishes to the alarm-messages state topic `[{"id":"a1","name":"Fenster offen",...},{"id":"a2","name":"Tür offen",...}]`, which HA renders as count `2` via `{{ value_json | length }}` and attributes `{"messages": [ ... ]}`. AdditionalInformationIndexed on the same input returns `{"alarm_1":"Fenster offen","alarm_2":"Tür offen"}` — a shape no topic carries. Separately, the doc at :885-886 asserts "the dict follows the same order as [AlarmMessages.List] (timestamp-desc)"; a Go map[string]string carries no order, so only the index assignment follows List order, not the returned dict.
stands.guard: none — internal/model/hub/hub_datapoint_properties_test.go:90 and internal/model/hub/hub_test.go:324 pin the model shapes against themselves; no test compares them to a published discovery or state payload, and no test relates Counter() to Count().
stands.secondReason: Survived. All three attacks failed. Quote: current and verbatim. Sameness: Counter() and Count() are not two readings of one datum — the bodies are identical (`len(a.messages)` under the same RLock) and no interface forces the second name (`grep "Counter() int"` matches only the definition). Liveness: the live alarm path is hub_mqtt_publisher.go:421-427 -> Bridge.PublishAlarmMessages (bridge.go:1455) -> `json.Marshal(items)` of the raw []hub.AlarmMessage; neither indexed helper nor Counter is on it. Damage is where the finding is weakest, and why I drop it to low: both symbols are unreachable, so drift cannot be observed at any surface today. What survives as real is (a) dead code carrying an unverifiable assertion about HA's templates, and (b) an additional false doc claim the candidate only half-flagged.

stands.title: MQTT-discovery component vocabulary and an English UI label live in the model
stands.evidence:
Quote verified verbatim. internal/model/hub/program.go:176-186: `// Principal role: unchanged identity and topics.` / `Component: "switch",` … `Key:        ProgramRoleExecute,` / `Component:  "button",` / `NameSuffix: "Execute",`.

Both sides live. Producer: Program.MQTTRoles (program.go:170) is reached via internal/north/mqtt/bridge.go:1361 `return ra.MQTTRoles(b.cfg.Base, b.resolvedCentral(centralName))` and bridge.go:1425. Consumer: internal/north/mqtt/hub_discovery.go:453-454 `if role.NameSuffix != "" {` / `displayName += " " + role.NameSuffix` — appended verbatim, no translation. BuildProgramDiscoveryRoles has four production call sites: internal/central/adapter/hub_mqtt_publisher.go:191, :782, :803, :939.

The repo's own rule, applied everywhere else in the same file: internal/north/mqtt/hub_discovery.go:566 `"name": d.tr("discovery.alarm_messages")`, :877 `d.tr("discovery.system_health")`, :917 `d.tr("discovery.connection_latency")`, :959 `d.tr("discovery.last_event_age")`, with internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:226-231 `func (d *DefaultDiscoveryBuilder) tr(key string) string { … return d.Translations.T(d.Locale, key) }`.

`grep -rn "execute\|Execute" internal/i18n/catalogs/de.json internal/i18n/catalogs/en.json` returns nothing — there is no catalogue key for this string in either language.

Component vocabulary: internal/model/hub/program.go:177 and :185 are the only `Component:` literals under internal/model (grep). They duplicate the typed set at internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:105 `HAComponentSwitch HAComponent = "switch"` and :116 `HAComponentButton HAComponent = "button"`. DiscoveryItem.Component is a plain string (hub_discovery.go builds it as `string(HAComponentSensor)` elsewhere), so a model-side literal is never checked against the typed vocabulary.
stands.negativeControl: Had the localisation claim been false, either the catalogues would carry a `discovery.*execute*` key (grep found none in en.json or de.json) or hub_discovery.go:453 would route the suffix through `d.tr` / `d.Translations.T` the way lines 566, 877, 917 and 959 do for every sibling entity name. It reads `displayName += " " + role.NameSuffix` — raw concatenation.
stands.reason: Confirmed, with one half qualified. The English-string half is a live, operator-visible defect: "Execute" is declared in internal/model and concatenated untranslated onto an HA entity name, while every other hub entity name in the same builder resolves through the i18n catalogues. Fixing it requires editing internal/model, exactly as the candidate states. The component-vocabulary half is real duplication but is documented as deliberate: internal/payload/mqtt_addressable.go:80-82 `// Component is the consumer-facing control kind ("switch", "button", // …). The model decides; the bridge only transcribes it.` and cites ADR 0011 ("every fact about a source — what it is, what topics it owns, which HA component it surfaces as — is declared on the model object itself"). So Component-in-the-model is by design; what is not defended anywhere is that it bypasses the typed HAComponent vocabulary, leaving a model-side typo unvalidated all the way to the broker. Severity medium on the strength of the localisation leg alone.
stands.deadCopy: neither — both sides are live; Program.MQTTRoles is consumed through internal/north/mqtt/bridge.go:1361/1425 and rendered at internal/north/mqtt/hub_discovery.go:453.
stands.divergence: Locale `de`, a CCU program named "Rollladen Abend". The execute button's HA entity name comes out as "Rollladen Abend Execute" (program.go:186 concatenated at hub_discovery.go:454), while the alarm-messages sensor on the same bridge and the same locale comes out as "Alarmmeldungen" (internal/i18n/catalogs/de.json:31 via hub_discovery.go:566). Same operator, same daemon, one name German and one English.
stands.guard: none — `grep -rn 'Execute"' --include="*_test.go" .` returns no hit, no test pins the suffix or requires it to resolve through a catalogue, and no test asserts role.Component against the mqtt.HAComponent set.
stands.secondReason: Survived, with the candidate's own qualification intact. Liveness of both ends is real: producer Program.MQTTRoles (program.go:170) is reached via internal/north/mqtt/bridge.go and consumer buildProgramRole is reached from four production call sites in internal/central/adapter/hub_mqtt_publisher.go (:191, :782, :803, :939 — all non-test). Sameness attack on the component half fails to kill but does blunt it: the model-side `Component` is not duplicated data, it is the single declaration ADR 0011 asks for (payload/mqtt_addressable.go:79-81), and the type system does not force it — MQTTRole.Component is declared `string` (mqtt_addressable.go:81), so internal/payload would have to import the north-bound HAComponent type to tighten it, which is the layering the ADR avoids. What is not defended anywhere is that the model-side literal bypasses the typed vocabulary entirely: `role.Component == ""` is the only validation (hub_discovery.go:438), so a model-side typo ("buton") transcribes straight to the discovery topic. The localisation half stands unqualified and carries the severity on its own.

stands.title: The diagram store parses and validates the SPA-owned config document, and the two sides already disagree on the series cap
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, one of two things would have shown up: assets/openapi.yaml's DiagramConfig.config would carry a `series`/`central` sub-schema (making the generated SPA type the single source and the Go struct tags derived), or a test would assert the Go tags against the SPA's DiagramSeries. I read the schema at :12852-12858 — it is an untyped `object` documented as opaque — and grepped tests/ plus assets/ui/src/**/*.test.ts for the pair; the only hits are Go tests that hard-code the same literals as the validator they test (diagram_configs_test.go:21,129,133), which is self-referential, and tests/contract/multi_ccu_scope_test.go:521-525, which exempts the store from CCU scoping and says nothing about the blob's keys. For the cap half, the control is Diagrams.svelte blocking a 9th row — it does not.
stands.reason: The mechanism the candidate names is real: json.Unmarshal into diagram_configs.go:73-77 ignores unknown keys, so renaming `series` on the SPA side leaves cfg.Series nil, the :82 cap check and the :85 central loop both run over zero elements, and validateDiagram returns nil — the multi-CCU routing-safety check becomes a silent no-op that still returns 200. But that is the hypothetical; the cap divergence below is real today, which is what carries the severity.
stands.divergence: Concrete input: a diagram with 9 fully-picked series. assets/ui/src/routes/Diagrams.svelte:122-125 `function addSeries() { if (!draft) return; draft.rows = [...draft.rows, emptyRow()]; }` appends without bound, and save() at :143-150 rejects only the empty case (`if (series.length === 0)` → `diagrams.error.series_required`). There is no 8-row limit and no i18n key for one — grep over assets/ui/src/lib/i18n.ts for diagrams.*series/limit/max returns only `diagrams.field.series`, `diagrams.series.add/remove/label`, `diagrams.picker.series`, `diagrams.error.series_required`. The POST therefore goes out and diagram_configs.go:82-84 returns `sqlite: diagram invalid: at most 8 series`, mapped to handlers.ErrDiagramInvalid (cmd/openccu-loom/diagram_config_adapter.go:47-50) and rendered as HTTP 400 with the store's raw English string as the problem detail (handlers/diagram_configs.go:94-95), which Diagrams.svelte:172 shows verbatim in a toast. So: SPA says valid, store says invalid, and the operator sees an untranslated store-internal sentence. The 64 KiB cap has the same asymmetry (SPA does not measure the blob at all).
stands.deadCopy: neither — both sides have production callers (store via daemon_rest_mount.go:836; SPA type via Diagrams.svelte:153).
stands.guard: none
stands.secondReason: Split verdict on the two halves, and the load-bearing half survives. The candidate's *mechanism* claim — rename `series` on the SPA side and json.Unmarshal silently yields nil, turning the multi-CCU central check into a 200-returning no-op — is real as written but hypothetical: nothing renames it today, so on its own it would not earn a backlog entry. What carries the finding is the divergence that exists now, and I reproduced it by reading both paths: nine fully-picked series is constructible in the editor (unbounded addSeries, no disabled add button), passes every SPA check, is POSTed, and comes back 400 with an untranslated store-internal sentence rendered verbatim in a toast. The damage attack does not kill it — the drift is observable, in the operator's own UI, in whichever language they run. The sameness attack does not kill it either, but sharpens the shape: this is not one rule implemented twice, it is one rule implemented once in the store and mirrored nowhere — neither in the SPA nor in the OpenAPI contract, whose description actively denies the caps exist. The fix therefore is not deduplication but publishing the constraint (schema `maxItems`, an SPA bound, an i18n key), which is what a backlog entry should say.
