Both raw splits are present and the excuse entry is still required, so the claim holds.
stands.reason: Two independent implementations of the same channel->device split, feeding the same registry lookup. Severity medium rather than low because the climate copy is invisible to the repo's own guard: TestAddressSplittingHasOneSource (tests/contract/address_rule_single_source_test.go:46) only inspects free functions whose name contains "deviceaddress" (line 58: `!ok || fn.Recv != nil || !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(fn.Name.Name), "deviceaddress")`). The climate split lives in a closure named `resolveChannel`, so the guard neither reports nor excuses it — while queryfacade.go IS on the ratchet at line 35. When they drift further nothing fails; the symptom is a silent ModelRegistry miss (resolveChannel returns nil, the peer is dropped with no log).
stands.divergence: Input ":1" — climate_link_peer_refresh.go:60 uses `idx > 0`, so LastIndex returns 0 and the guard fails: devAddr stays ":1". queryfacade.go:530 uses `idx >= 0` and returns "". The guard's own comment (address_rule_single_source_test.go:25-26) records exactly this family: "first colon versus last colon versus two spellings of the leading-colon edge case". Whether a leading-colon or multi-colon address ever reaches either site is NOT established by any source I read — no production code constructs a two-colon address (grep for centralName+":"+address style composition returned nothing outside tests), and the guard itself leaves that question open at lines 28-31. I am not asserting reachability.
stands.deadCopy: neither — both sites have production callers (cited above)
stands.guard: tests/contract/address_rule_single_source_test.go:46 TestAddressSplittingHasOneSource covers the queryfacade side only, and only as a recorded exemption (line 35). It cannot see the climate side: line 58 filters to free functions whose identifier contains "deviceaddress". No test compares the two behaviours.
stands.secondReason: The duplication half survived every attack: the copy is real, the reuse target is a method on the pointer the function already holds, both paths are wired in production, and the repo's own guard provably cannot see the closure. The divergence half died: I reproduced ":1" — climate keeps ":1", queryfacade returns "" — but at both sites the next step is ModelRegistry.Get, and Get("") can never hit because Put refuses an empty address (internal/central/registry/model_registry.go:28-33 `if d == nil || d.Address == \"\" { return }`), while Get(":1") misses for the same reason no device is keyed that way. Both spellings therefore yield nil and the disagreement is unobservable. Severity dropped medium -> low: this is a reuse / guard-coverage item, not a latent defect. Nothing in any source I read establishes that a leading-colon or colon-bearing address reaches either site; I do not assert reachability either way.

stands.title: schedule adapter's private splitChannelAddress disagrees with hmtypes on the no-channel sentinel, on a live unvalidated CCU write path
stands.evidence: Quotes verified verbatim. internal/central/adapter/schedule_query_adapter.go:128 `func splitChannelAddress(channelAddress string) (device string, channelIdx int) {`, preceded at :126-127 by `// splitChannelAddress separates "<dev>:<chn>" into its components. // Returns (channelAddress, 0) when the suffix is missing.` Body scans backwards and, on a non-digit suffix, `return channelAddress, 0` — the WHOLE string as the device part. hmtypes.SplitChannelAddress (pkg/hmtypes/address.go:84-98) cuts at the first colon and returns (before, -1, false). BOTH SIDES LIVE. Adapter copy: called at schedule_query_adapter.go:37, :53, :67 and internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:306-307 (CopyClimateProfile), and the adapter is constructed in the composition root at cmd/openccu-loom/ws_adapters.go:118 `schedQueryAdapter := adapter.NewScheduleQueryAdapter(w.schedulesDomain)`. hmtypes copy: internal/north/mqtt/discovery_aggregate.go:449, internal/store/patches/patches.go:182, and twelve internal/model/custom/*/topology.go call sites.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, splitChannelAddress("0001ABCD") would have returned a no-channel sentinel matching hmtypes (-1/false) rather than 0 — internal/central/adapter/schedule_query_adapter_test.go:22-27 asserts the opposite — or internal/north/rest/handlers/schedules.go would validate the caller-supplied address with hmtypes.IsChannelAddress before the call. Neither is present: the only check on that field is `if body.TargetChannelAddress == ""` at handlers/schedules.go:305.
stands.divergence: Input "0001ABCD" (a plain device address, no channel suffix): the adapter copy returns ("0001ABCD", 0) — pinned by internal/central/adapter/schedule_query_adapter_test.go:22 and internal/central/adapter/schedule_coerce_test.go:199-202 — while hmtypes.SplitChannelAddress returns ("0001ABCD", -1, false), pinned by pkg/hmtypes/address_test.go:111-116. Reachable: `POST /api/v1/devices/{addr}/channels/{no}/schedule/copy-profile` with body `{"target_channel_address":"0001ABCD", ...}` — the field is checked non-empty only (internal/north/rest/handlers/schedules.go:305) and flows to SchedulesDomain.CopyClimateProfile (schedules.go:307), so a malformed target is silently redirected to channel 0 of a real device instead of rejected. Second diverging input "0001ABCD:NOPE": adapter returns device = "0001ABCD:NOPE" (colon retained, pinned by schedule_coerce_test.go:207-210), hmtypes returns device = "0001ABCD".
stands.deadCopy: Neither — both implementations have production callers (adapter: schedule_query_adapter.go:37/53/67 + schedules.go:306-307; hmtypes: mqtt/discovery_aggregate.go:449, store/patches/patches.go:182, twelve custom/*/topology.go sites).
stands.guard: tests/contract/channel_ordinal_parser_test.go — `TestChannelOrdinalParsersDelegateToHmtypes`, and it deliberately does NOT fail: line 29 records this exact file in `materializeChannelNoHandRolledParsers` as "splitChannelAddress: backwards scan, sentinel 0; same open question as paramsets.go". No test compares the two implementations' results, so the sentinel disagreement is recorded prose, not an enforced contract.
stands.reason: Higher severity than #0 because both copies are live and the sentinel choice decides an operator-visible outcome on a CCU WRITE path: with sentinel 0, a target_channel_address that carries no channel suffix silently addresses channel 0 and a week profile is written there; with the hmtypes sentinel the caller could be rejected. The guard's own comment states the direction and sentinel questions are open, so the divergence is known but unresolved rather than benign.
stands.secondReason: The structural core survived every bite — quote accurate, both copies reachable from wired production routes, the diverging input unfiltered upstream, and the returned number decides which paramset address is written. But two of the finding's own claims are dead and its severity rests on them, so I confirm it at low, not medium. (1) 'a week profile is written there' is refuted: PutClimateSchedule reads the target's MASTER description first (schedules.go:1011) and filters the climate slot keys against it (:1046, filterClimateScheduleByDescKeys), so a channel-0 target — MAINTENANCE on HmIP, which declares no ENDTIME_/TEMPERATURE_ keys — empties the payload and the call fails at :1055 before any putParamset. A wire write happens only if the description comes back empty (len(descKeys)==0 skips both filters), and even then the CCU's -5 fault is swallowed as a false positive (:1058-1073) rather than a profile landing on channel 0. (2) 'with the hmtypes sentinel the caller could be rejected' is refuted: hmtypes rejects nothing, it returns ok=false, and no schedules caller consumes an ok; worse, -1 is not an error value in this domain but device.ChannelNumberDevice, so a naive swap would route the same malformed input to a device-level MASTER write instead of to a rejection. What is left is real but narrow: a malformed or device-root target yields a 404/500 instead of a 422, and the device-root channel is unaddressable through the string-form APIs. That is worth one fix — teach the helper the domain's own -1 — but it is not a silent stray CCU write. Note the two sentinels are also not one rule read twice: -1 means 'absent' in hmtypes and 'the bare device-level paramset' in the schedules domain, which is why the recorded open question is a real design question and not a mechanical de-duplication.

stands.title: source display-name fallback exists in three copies; one has no caller at all
stands.evidence: Canonical copy, pkg/hmevent/security.go:72-79: `// DisplayName is the label a consumer shows for this source: its resolved` / `// name, or its channel address when the name has not been resolved yet. …` / `func (r SecuritySourceRef) DisplayName() string {` / `\tif r.Name != "" {` / `\t\treturn r.Name` / `\t}` / `\treturn r.ChannelAddress` / `}`, wrapped by `func SourceDisplayNames(refs []SecuritySourceRef) []string` at :89. Second copy, internal/north/mqtt/alarm_publisher.go:100-115: `// alarmSourceNames returns the display names of the refs, falling back` / `// to the channel address when a source has no name.` / `func alarmSourceNames(refs []hmevent.SecuritySourceRef) []string {` / `\tif len(refs) == 0 { return nil }` / `\t… switch { case refs[i].Name != "": … case refs[i].ChannelAddress != "": … }`. Third copy, internal/model/security/snapshot.go:161-176: `// SourceNames returns the display names of the notification's sources,` / `// falling back to the channel address for an unnamed one.` / `func (n Notification) SourceNames() []string {` — body byte-for-byte the same switch as alarmSourceNames. Liveness: `hmevent.SourceDisplayNames` has three production callers (internal/security/render.go:99, internal/north/mqtt/security_reconcile.go:295 and :366); `alarmSourceNames` has two (internal/north/mqtt/alarm_publisher.go:272, :307). `SourceNames` has zero — `grep -rn 'SourceNames' .` over the whole repo (all file types, tests included) returns only alarm_publisher.go:100,102,272,307 (the differently-named alarmSourceNames) and snapshot.go:161,163, i.e. the declaration and its own doc comment. The containing type is live (internal/security/render.go:75 constructs security.Notification, internal/north/rest/handlers/security.go:202 maps it), so this is a dead method on a live type. The comment at pkg/hmevent/security.go:82-88 asserts the dedup is complete — `// The rule lives with the type because every surface that lists sources needs` / `// it — the security renderer in the domain and the MQTT reconciler both had` / `// byte-identical copies, and a copy of a display rule diverges silently: one` / `// plane starts showing addresses where another shows names.` — while two further surfaces (the MQTT alarm publisher, the domain Notification) still carry their own copies.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, `grep -rn 'SourceDisplayNames|\.DisplayName()'` would have shown alarm_publisher.go and snapshot.go delegating to the shared helper instead of open-coding the fallback, and `grep -rn 'SourceNames'` would have returned a production call site for the snapshot.go method. Both greps were run; neither result appeared.
stands.reason: Three implementations of one operator-visible rule, one of which no code reaches. Per-ref behaviour is identical today, so no message currently disagrees — the defect is structural: a change to the fallback (e.g. preferring DeviceAddress, or appending the parameter) lands in one plane only, and the MQTT `open_sensors` array would then disagree with the REST/notification rendering. Severity medium rather than high because nothing is wrong on the wire right now and the only behavioural difference found is invisible (below).
stands.divergence: Only one input separates the live copies, and it is masked: zero refs. `hmevent.SourceDisplayNames(nil)` returns a non-nil empty slice `[]string{}` (pkg/hmevent/security.go:90 `out := make([]string, 0, len(refs))` with no early return), while `alarmSourceNames(nil)` and `Notification.SourceNames()` return untyped `nil` (alarm_publisher.go:103, snapshot.go:164 `if len(...) == 0 { return nil }`). That would be `[]` vs `null` in JSON, but the only field fed by the nil-returning copy is `OpenSensors []string `json:"open_sensors,omitempty"`` (internal/north/mqtt/alarm_publisher.go:54), and omitempty drops both. For every non-empty ref list the three copies return identical values. No input was found on which the live copies disagree observably.
stands.deadCopy: internal/model/security/snapshot.go:163 — `func (n Notification) SourceNames() []string` has no caller anywhere in the repo, production or test.
stands.guard: none. No test names both `SourceDisplayNames` and `alarmSourceNames`/`SourceNames`: `grep -rn 'SourceDisplayNames|alarmSourceNames' --include='*_test.go' .` returns nothing. internal/north/mqtt/alarm_publisher_test.go:603 and cmd/openccu-loom/alarm_arm_failure_wiring_test.go:111 assert open_sensors content through the alarm copy only, so a drift in the pkg copy leaves them green.
stands.secondReason: Survives. Quotes and line numbers are current; the three bodies implement one rule over one input type with no type-system pressure to repeat it; one copy (internal/model/security/snapshot.go:163) has zero callers of any kind, which is the stronger shape — it is exported API surface documented as the display rule that no code exercises. The severity is correctly medium and I did not find grounds to raise it: nothing is wrong on the wire today, the only measurable difference (nil vs []) is swallowed by omitempty, and the damage is prospective — a change to the fallback in pkg/hmevent would reach the security plane (`source_names`, notification placeholders) but leave the MQTT alarm plane's `open_sensors` behind. The one honest weakening: the dead copy cannot itself drift into a user-visible disagreement, since it publishes nothing; its cost is as a trap for the next caller and as documented-but-unexercised surface.

stands.title: CPV level decode is implemented twice and the copies already disagree; the exported, documented copy has no production caller
stands.evidence: Live copy, internal/client/backends/combined.go:145-151: `func convertCpvLevelHmip(value string) (any, bool) {` / `\tn, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(value))` / `\tif err != nil { return nil, false }` / `\treturn float64(n) / 100, true` / `}`, and :158-171 `func convertCpvLevelHm(value string) any {` / `\tv := strings.TrimSpace(value)` / `\tif !strings.HasPrefix(v, "0x") && !strings.HasPrefix(v, "0X") { return v }` / `\tn, err := strconv.ParseUint(v[2:], 16, 64)` / `\tif err != nil { … return v }` / `\treturn float64(n) / 100 / 2`. Second copy, internal/model/value/converter.go:109-128: `// ConvertCPVToHMLevel converts a BidCos CPV hex string back to a` / `// floating-point level (0..1).` / `func ConvertCPVToHMLevel(cpv string) (float64, bool) {` / `\tvar raw int` / `\tif _, err := fmt.Sscanf(cpv, "%v", &raw); err != nil { return 0, false }` / `\treturn float64(raw) / 100 / 2, true` / `}` and `func ConvertCPVToHMIPLevel(cpv string) (float64, bool) {` / `\tvar raw int` / `\tif _, err := fmt.Sscanf(cpv, "%d", &raw); err != nil { return 0, false }` / `\treturn float64(raw) / 100, true` / `}`. Same scale constants (/100 for HmIP, /100/2 for HM), different parsers. Liveness: the backends copy is reached from production at internal/central/adapter/callback_handlers.go:293 (`if backends.IsCombinedParameter(parameter) {`) and :434 (`parsed, parsedOK := backends.ParseCombinedParameter(parameter, raw)`), and from internal/client/reliability/command_tracker.go:127 (`values, ok := backends.ParseCombinedParameter(parameter, value)`); combined.go:91 and :118-119 call the two converters. `grep -rn 'ConvertCPVToHMIPLevel|ConvertCPVToHMLevel' --include='*.go' .` returns only internal/model/value/converter.go itself (:13 doc, :109,111,119,123) and two test files (converter_test.go:113-131, converter_extra_test.go:100-118) — zero production callers. The package doc asserts the opposite role, converter.go:13-16: `// 2. [ConvertCPVToHMLevel] / [ConvertCPVToHMIPLevel] — the BidCos` / `// "hex level" → float64 decode for COMBINED_PARAMETER channels. The` / `// encode direction lives in internal/parameter.ConvertHMLevelToCPV,` — the encode half of that sentence is true (internal/parameter/converter.go:269, called from internal/model/custom/cover/blind.go:346), the decode half is not: COMBINED_PARAMETER decode runs through backends.
stands.negativeControl: Had the copies been equivalent, the differential run below would have printed no DIVERGE line and identical (value, ok) pairs on all 20 inputs. Had internal/model/value been the live decoder, the caller grep would have shown a non-test importer — I ran it across the whole repo and every hit outside the declaration is in *_test.go.
stands.reason: Two implementations of one wire decode, one of them exported, doc-commented as the canonical COMBINED_PARAMETER decoder, covered by its own green tests, and called by nothing. That is the trap shape: the next caller who needs a CPV decode will find the exported, documented, tested copy and get different answers from the live path on real firmware strings. The measured divergences are not exotic — `0x64` is exactly the wire form the HM branch emits (internal/model/custom/cover/blind.go:346 builds `"0xc8,0x64"`), and feeding it to the exported HmIP decoder silently yields level 0 instead of an error. Severity medium, not high: nothing on the live path is wrong today, because the divergent copy is unreachable.
stands.divergence: Measured, not inferred: I compiled verbatim copies of all four functions into a standalone program outside the repo (a scratch directory outside the repo) and ran both families over the same inputs. HmIP path: input "0x64" → backends.convertCpvLevelHmip returns (nil, false), which aborts the surrounding ParseCombinedParameter and drops the whole update; value.ConvertCPVToHMIPLevel returns (0, true), i.e. a valid level of 0. Input "50abc" → backends (nil, false); value (0.5, true). HM path: input "100" (decimal, no 0x prefix) → backends.convertCpvLevelHm returns the raw string "100" (type string, passed through to the model layer); value.ConvertCPVToHMLevel returns (0.5, true). Input "200" → backends "200" (string); value (1, true). Inputs "0", "100", "50", " 50 ", "08", "+50", "-10", "", "xyz" agree on the HmIP path; "0x00", "0xc8", "0x64", "  0x64  ", "0X64" agree on the HM path.
stands.deadCopy: internal/model/value/converter.go:111 (ConvertCPVToHMLevel) and :123 (ConvertCPVToHMIPLevel) — exported, but no production caller; the only references are internal/model/value/converter_test.go:125 and internal/model/value/converter_extra_test.go:112.
stands.guard: none. No test exercises both families: `grep -rln 'ConvertCPVToHMIPLevel' --include='*_test.go' .` yields only internal/model/value/converter_extra_test.go, which does not import internal/client/backends. tests/contract/level_combined_encoding_test.go:144 pins the backends decoder against internal/parameter.ConvertHMLevelToCPV (the encoder) and never mentions internal/model/value. Both suites stay green under any drift between the two decode copies.
stands.secondReason: Survives. Line numbers and quotes are current, the two families decode the same datum in the same direction (the package doc at converter.go:13-16 names the exported pair as the COMBINED_PARAMETER decode, which is the live path's job), the exported pair has zero production callers, and the divergence is measured rather than inferred. One point where I would soften the finding's own wording: the specific scenario "0x64 is the wire form the HM branch emits, and feeding it to the exported HmIP decoder yields 0 instead of an error" cannot occur on the live path — blind.go:346 sends hex only on the LEVEL_COMBINED/HM branch, and blind.go:351 sends decimals on the COMBINED_PARAMETER/HmIP branch, so no live code crosses the families. The damage is therefore entirely prospective: a future caller reaching for the exported, documented, test-covered pair gets 0.5 where the live path returns the string "100", and a silent level 0 where the live path drops the update. Medium is the right severity for that; nothing is wrong on the wire today.

The two copies have already drifted in three respects beyond the shared allowlist, which is the concrete proof that they are maintained independently. stands.guard: None comparing the two. stands.divergence: Three inputs on which the two copies already disagree today. stands.title: parameter.FloatTolerance documents the CCU-echo comparison and has no production caller; the live comparator uses a tolerance 4 orders looser
stands.evidence:
diff.go:25-28 verbatim: "// FloatTolerance is the relative epsilon used by [Diff] when comparing / // float values. CCU firmware rounds floats in transit, so bit-exact / // comparison produces false mismatches. / const FloatTolerance = 1e-6", applied at diff.go:69 `Match:   rel <= FloatTolerance`. Its stated cause matches converter.go:56 `return math.Round(v*1_000_000) / 1_000_000` — the wire encoder's own 6-decimal rounding.

DEAD: `grep -rn "FloatTolerance|parameter\.Diff|DiffResult" --include=*.go .` returns only internal/parameter/diff.go plus two unrelated test names (internal/model/generic/optimistic_test.go:381, internal/store/linkprofile/store_test.go:672 — both just borrow the word in a test name). `grep -rn "\bDiff(" --include=*.go .` excluding tests returns exactly one line, the declaration diff.go:33. The only callers are internal/parameter/parameter_test.go:797-846. `Diff` is exercised by its own package test and by nothing else.

LIVE: optimistic_helpers.go:48-59 `func valuesClose[T comparable](a, b T) bool` compares `math.Abs(roundToTwoDecimals(af)-roundToTwoDecimals(bf)) < 1e-9`, i.e. anything equal after rounding half-up to 2 decimals (roundToTwoDecimals, :65-70). Nine production call sites, all in internal/model/generic/datapoint.go: 590, 1049, 1055, 1073, 1089, 1614, 1748, 2009, 2059 — including the optimistic-confirmation seam at :1614 `if snap := d.optimistic.Snapshot(); snap.Active && valuesClose(snap.Value, typed)`. So the confirmation decision the dead constant documents is in fact taken at 1e-2 granularity, not 1e-6.

SCOPE CORRECTION on the candidate's other three sites: they are not the same decision and are not re-derivations of an echo tolerance. linkprofile/store.go:485 `return math.Abs(a-b) <= 1e-6*scale` sits in `floatsEqual`, whose own doc (:477-482) says it compares "a live paramset read that round-trips through float32" against "an archive constraint" — profile matching, not echo confirmation. schedule/lock.go:52 `if math.Abs(level-raw.Level()) < 1e-6 && durBase == ...` is a lookup-table identity match inside DetectLockAction. adapter/schedules.go:1351 and :1359 compare a slot temperature against the derived base temperature to merge contiguous periods. Same numeric literal, three different questions.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, `grep -rn "FloatTolerance\|parameter\.Diff"` over non-test Go files would have returned at least one call site outside internal/parameter — a client or central path feeding sent/got into Diff. It returned only the declaration file. And had the two tolerances agreed, valuesClose would have compared against a relative epsilon rather than rounding both operands to two decimals first.
stands.reason: Two comparators answer the same question ("did the CCU echo what we sent"): the documented, reasoned one is unreachable from production, and the one the daemon actually runs is four orders of magnitude looser than its stated rationale. Tuning FloatTolerance changes nothing, which is the stronger form of the duplicate — a test keeps the dead copy green while the live path uses the other. The candidate's framing of linkprofile/lock/schedules as a third and fourth re-derivation of the same decision does not hold; those are different comparisons that happen to share the literal.
stands.deadCopy: internal/parameter.Diff / internal/parameter.FloatTolerance — callers: internal/parameter/parameter_test.go only (lines 797, 801, 808, 812, 819, 828, 832, 839, 846). Zero production callers.
stands.secondReason: Confirmed as stated on both legs (dead documented comparator; live comparator ~3.7 orders looser in absolute terms at unit magnitude), but downgraded to low. Damage today is zero: nothing calls Diff, so the two cannot drift into disagreement — the only cost is the trap that a future author finds the exported, documented, reasoned comparator and gets 1e-6 relative where the whole daemon uses a 2-decimal band. Note the finding is mis-shelved as a duplicate-literal item: 1e-6 occurs exactly once in production code (diff.go:28); valuesClose uses 1e-9 and converter.go uses 1_000_000. The actionable defect is dead exported code with a doc comment claiming a role it does not fill, not a drifting constant.

stands.title: Two live implementations of the CCU 13-slot weekday expansion, disagreeing on over-capacity, and one hard-codes the terminator the same file imports as a constant
stands.evidence:
climate.go:372-374 verbatim: "// ClimateEndOfDayMinutes is [ClimateEndOfDay] expressed as minutes since / // midnight. / const ClimateEndOfDayMinutes = 24 * 60". The firmware citation the candidate mentions is at weekprofile/slot.go:113-114 ("its reader breaks on the first slot whose ENDTIME is 1440 (www/config/easymodes/etc/hmipChannelConfigDialogs.tcl:3009)"), not at climate.go:374 — the constant itself is cited to the CCU editor at climate.go:377-382. Adapter copy: `func expandWeekday(wd hmapi.ClimateWeekday) ([]rawSlot, error)` at schedules.go:1514, called at :1397 (serializeClimateSchedule) and :1430 (serializeClimateScheduleBare), whose outputs become the `P<n>_ENDTIME_<day>_<n>` / `ENDTIME_<day>_<n>` paramset keys. weekprofile copy: `climateWeekdayToSlotsExpand` at rawconvert.go:372, reached from ClimateToRaw (:245) and ClimateToRawWire (:277), called from adapter/schedule_io.go:284, :441, :548 and adapter/week_profile_io.go:71.

HARD-CODED TERMINATOR CONFIRMED: schedules.go:1552 `if cursor < 1440 {`, :1553 `stretches = append(stretches, stretch{end: 1440, temp: wd.BaseTemperature})`, :1556 same, :1568 `out[i] = rawSlot{endMin: 1440, temp: wd.BaseTemperature}` — four literals, in a file that already imports the package and uses the constant 66 lines later at :1634 `m = min(m, schedule.ClimateEndOfDayMinutes)` and :1637 `return schedule.ClimateEndOfDay`. THE COPIES ALREADY DISAGREE on over-capacity. Adapter, schedules.go:1559-1562: `if len(stretches) > schedule.MaxClimateSlots { return nil, fmt.Errorf("too many periods: yielded %d slots, max %d", ...) }` — fails loudly. weekprofile: climateWeekdayToSlotsExpand appends without a count check and hands off to fillUpWeekdaySlots, whose doc at slot.go:108-109 says "pads ws to exactly 13 slots ... Any slots beyond 13 are trimmed" and whose body (slot.go:122-126) copies only `no >= 1 && no <= slotCount` — silent truncation. The gap is reachable on the ClimateToRawWire path only: schedule.ClimateWeekday.Validate (climate.go:90-116) enforces full 00:00–24:00 coverage so gap-fill adds nothing, but ValidateWire (climate.go:124-127) deliberately drops that rule while validateWeekdayStructure still allows up to MaxClimatePeriods = MaxClimateSlots = 13 periods (climate.go:38,47,62-64). Seven gapped periods expand to 7 periods + 7 gap fills + 1 trailing = 15 entries: the adapter would return "too many periods: yielded 15 slots, max 13"; weekprofile drops entries 14 and 15 — including the trailing 24:00 terminator — and writes a day that never reaches 1440.

FOURTH SITE, weaker: climate/matter.go:366-372 `// into the 0..1440 minutes-of-day range Matter / // ScheduleEntry expects` then `if v < 0 || v > 1440 { return 0, false }` (repeated at :377, :382, :387) — a read-side range bound, not a gap-fill terminator. stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, either the adapter's serializeClimateSchedule would have delegated to weekprofile.ClimateToRaw (or vice versa) — leaving one expansion — or schedules.go:1552-1568 would have used schedule.ClimateEndOfDayMinutes exactly as the same file does at :1634. They already differ where it matters: an over-capacity day is a hard error on one path and a silently truncated schedule on the other. The adapter copy additionally re-decides the terminator as a bare literal in a file that already carries the canonical constant.
stands.divergence: over-capacity handling: adapter/schedules.go:1559-1562 returns "too many periods: yielded %d slots, max %d"; weekprofile/slot.go:122-126 silently drops slots past 13, including the 24:00 terminator, on the ClimateToRawWire (CopyProfileTo) path.

The load-bearing third leg — 'an over-capacity day is a hard error on one path and a silently truncated schedule on the other' — is refuted as a live divergence: the truncating branch exists but no production input can reach it, so nothing observable differs today. Severity therefore drops from medium to low: this is a maintenance duplicate (two edit sites if the slot count, gap-fill rule or terminator ever changes) with no current wrong output. stands.title: The 153/500 mired bound is decided in four places; one copy is dead, one copy's own comment is already false, and the two live planes clamp differently
stands.evidence:
All four declarations are real. color.go:400-403 `const ( maxKelvinScale = 1_000_000 / maxMireds      = 500 / minMireds      = 153 )`. payload.go:895-900 `const ( pythonMinMireds = 153 / pythonMaxMireds = 500 ) / minMireds := pythonMinMireds / maxMireds := pythonMaxMireds`, with the reciprocal re-spelled at :902 `minMireds = int(1e6 / float64(l.MaxKelvin))` and :905, and again at :193 `return int32(1e6 / mireds), true`. matter_color.go:165-166 `matterMinMireds uint16 = 153 // ≈ 6535 K / matterMaxMireds uint16 = 500 // ≈ 2000 K` plus :263 `v := 1_000_000 / k` and :278. colorcontrol_server.go:45-51 `return ColorControlServerConfig{ MinMireds: 153, // ≈ 6535 K / MaxMireds: 500, // ≈ 2000 K / InitialMireds: 370, ... }`. (Cited lines 192/401/402 are off by one against the file; 193/401-403 are the real lines.)

DEAD COPY: `grep -rn "matter/cluster/light" --include=*.go .` excluding _test.go returns nothing. NewColorControlServer / DefaultColorControlServerConfig have callers only in internal/north/matter/cluster/light/colorcontrol_parity_matterjs_test.go, colorcontrol_number_of_primaries_test.go and colorcontrol_write_through_test.go. The same control on the wire package's decoders: `grep -rn "DecodeOffWithEffect|DecodeOnWithTimedOff|OffWithEffectRequest|OnWithTimedOffRequest"` outside onoff.go returns only internal/north/matter/cluster/wire/onoff_test.go — so the wire OnOff surface is test-only in its entirety, not just its constants.
stands.divergence: The copies already behave differently on the same LT semantics. (1) Toggle: switch:63, light:112 and generic:63 declare `matterCmdToggle = 0x02` and dispatch it; siren declares no Toggle and documents the omission at matter.go:371-372 — "Toggle (0x02) is absent — Siren has no toggle command in its wire surface" — while advertising the same LT feature bit and the same three LT commands. (2) GlobalSceneControl: switch/matter.go:280-288 and generic/switch_matter.go:271-278 both cite "matter.js OnOffServer.ts:158-169 also clears GlobalSceneControl here" and call `globalSceneControl.Store(false)` / `.Store(true)`; siren carries the same 0x4000 attribute but returns a constant — matter.go:238-240 `case matterAttrOnOffGlobalSceneControl: // See the sirenOnOffServer doc comment: static false, this projection has no scene engine to flip it live. return false, true` — so the same matter.js rule is implemented in two of the four copies and deliberately stubbed in a third. stands.reason: One Matter-spec decision (the LT-gated OnOff command ids, the LT FeatureMap bit, and the four LT attribute ids) is declared five times: four live copies under internal/model and one exported, unreferenced copy in the package whose name says it owns the wire contract. A matter.js-driven correction applied at internal/north/matter/cluster/wire/onoff.go changes nothing that reaches an endpoint, and a correction applied to one model package leaves three endpoint types advertising the old set — the drift class the project's own Matter rule (CLAUDE.md: hand-coding constants "produces silent Apple/Google pair-aborts") exists to prevent.
stands.deadCopy: internal/north/matter/cluster/wire/onoff.go — OnOffCmdOff/On/Toggle/OffWithEffect/OnWithRecallGlobalScene/OnWithTimedOff (:15-20) plus DecodeOffWithEffect and DecodeOnWithTimedOff and their request structs: referenced only from wire/onoff_test.go. The model dispatchers take the command payload as `_ any` (e.g. siren/matter.go:317) and never decode it, so the timed-off / effect payload fields are parsed nowhere in production.
stands.guard: none found: no parity test compares the four model constant blocks against each other or against wire/onoff.go.
stands.secondReason: One immutable Matter datum declared five times, four of them live on endpoints and one exported but referenced by nothing — the inverted 'copy with no production caller' shape. The one guard that reads AcceptedCommandList skips exactly these commands: tests/integration/matter_cluster_conformance_test.go:282-284 `if cmd.Conformance != "M" || cmd.Direction == "response" { continue }`, and matter.js marks OffWithEffect / OnWithRecallGlobalScene / OnWithTimedOff conformance "LT", not "M". The finding is a latent hazard plus dead exported code, so medium is the ceiling.

stands.title: The 8-member keypress-parameter set is declared twice: hmenum.ClickEvents (data-point + visibility plane) and event.clickParams (trigger-event plane)
stands.evidence: pkg/hmenum/parameter.go:200 `var ClickEvents = map[Parameter]struct{}{` with ParameterPress, PressCont, PressLock, PressLong, PressLongRelease, PressLongStart, PressShort, PressUnlock. internal/model/event/event.go:287 `var clickParams = map[hmenum.Parameter]struct{}{` with the same eight `hmenum.Parameter*` members, written as a second literal (not derived from ClickEvents). Consumers are disjoint: ClickEvents is read via `param.IsClickEvent()` at datapoint_resolver.go:173 (`return generic.NewButton(withKind(cfg, generic.KindButton))`) and :181, at device_pipeline.go:1224 (`if !param.IsClickEvent() { continue }`), and copied wholesale into the visibility ignore table at store/visibility/rules.go:169 `"HmIP-PS": copyParamSet(hmenum.ClickEvents),`. clickParams is read only inside event.Classify (event.go:57) and event.Sources (event.go:80); Classify is the trigger authority — coordinators/event.go:277-285 states "[event.Classify] is the sole authority: click parameters become keypresses" — and is also the gate at north/mqtt/discovery.go:403 `if kind, known := event.Classify(hmenum.Parameter(ev.Parameter)); known && kind != event.KindKeypress`, adapter/eventbridge.go:2462 and adapter/callback_handlers.go:860.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false I would have found either (a) event.clickParams defined as `hmenum.ClickEvents` or built by ranging over it, or (b) a test naming both identifiers and asserting set equality. Neither exists: `grep -rn 'clickParams' --include=*.go .` returns only internal/model/event/event.go (lines 57, 79, 80, 287) and `grep -rln 'clickParams\|ClickEvents' tests/` returns nothing.
stands.reason: One domain fact — which parameters are keypresses — is encoded as two independent literals in two packages, each feeding a different surface (button data point + HmIP-PS event suppression vs. KindKeypress triggers for coordinator, MQTT discovery, eventbridge, the data-point-less forwarding path). Nothing ties them.
stands.divergence: No divergence today: the two member lists are byte-identical (8 identical parameters). The exposure is prospective — an added keypress parameter in one set only, with no guard to catch it.
stands.guard: None. tests/contract/suppression_reader_test.go pins reader counts for adapter/visibility tables only (ImpulseEvents, buttonActionParameters, ignoreDevicesForDataPointEvents); it never compares ClickEvents to clickParams.
stands.secondReason: Survives the attack on all five bites. Quotes current. Sameness holds: both maps answer the single question 'is this parameter a keypress', and the repo itself distinguishes a genuinely different question with a differently-populated third set (hmenum.parameter.go:225 edgeTriggerParameters, which adds ParameterCodeID and ParameterCodeState for dedup suppression) — so a same-membership second literal is a copy, not a second reading. Both sites live: DP shape/visibility on one, KindKeypress on MQTT + REST/WS + eventbridge on the other. Damage is concrete and one-sided: adding a ninth PRESS_* to hmenum only gives it a Button data point and an HmIP-PS ignore entry but Classify returns not-known, so coordinators/event.go:286 and callback_handlers.go:861 emit nothing; adding it to clickParams only gives a keypress kind with no button. channel.go:1216-1219 documents this exact failure having already happened once with a north-bound copy: 'a copy of an enumerable domain set silently caps its holder at the size its author knew about: the MQTT plane knew only keypresses and never published the impulse and device-error kinds the model had all along.'

stands.title: SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS vocabulary declared in three packages, and the "INTRUSION_ALARM is not smoke" rule is contradicted inside the repo
stands.evidence: hmenum/smoke_alarm_status.go:19 "SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus values, in VALUE_LIST order" then IDLE_OFF (:22), PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM; :40 `var smokeDetectorAlarmStatusSmokeLabels = []string{PRIMARY_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM}` with :55 "INTRUSION_ALARM is deliberately absent … Treating it as smoke makes the domain report its own siren command as the cause of a fire." — consumed by internal/model/safety/classify.go:40 `var smokeActiveValues = hmenum.SmokeDetectorAlarmStatusSmokeLabels()` ("the classifier is one of its two consumers, not a second definition"). siren/smoke.go:24-28 re-declares the same wire vocabulary as its own type: `SmokeStatusIdleOff/PrimaryAlarm/SecondaryAlarm/Intrusion`, and smoke.go:158 `return st != SmokeStatusIdleOff && st != "", true`. siren/matter.go:417-419 `case SmokeStatusPrimaryAlarm, SmokeStatusIntrusion: return matterSmokeAlarmCritical`, documented at :409-411 "PRIMARY_ALARM / INTRUSION → Critical (2) — local alarm fires". calculated/derived_binary.go:174-175 `OnValues: hmenum.SmokeDetectorAlarmStatusSmokeLabels(), OffValues: []string{"IDLE_OFF", "IDLE_ON", "INTRUSION_ALARM"}` and :183 `OffValues: []string{"IDLE_OFF", "IDLE_ON", "PRIMARY_ALARM", "SECONDARY_ALARM"}` — `IDLE_ON` appears in no enum in the repo.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, siren would have typed its status against hmenum (e.g. `hmenum.SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus` returned from Status()) and matter.go would have branched on hmenum.SmokeDetectorAlarmStatusSmokeLabels; and a captured HmIP-SWSD paramset descriptor carrying the VALUE_LIST would have turned up. Neither: `grep -rn 'SmokeStatus\|SmokeAlarmStatus' --include=*.go .` outside internal/model/custom/siren returns only safety/classify_test.go:98/104, and the only VALUE_LISTs in the tree are hand-written Go test fixtures.
stands.reason: One wire ENUM's vocabulary is declared three times (hmenum type, siren type, calculated string literals), and the "means fire" decision hmenum owns and documents is made a second time in siren/matter.go with the opposite answer for INTRUSION_ALARM: safety/classify.go treats it as not-smoke, calculated lists it under SMOKE_ALARM OffValues, while smokeStatusToAlarmState reports SmokeCOAlarm Critical for it to Matter controllers.
stands.divergence: Already disagreeing, on a label present in the repo: INTRUSION_ALARM → not smoke (hmenum :40-58, safety/classify.go:40, safety/activation.go:44 "where 'not index 0' reads the installation's own siren command as a fire") vs. Critical smoke alarm (siren/matter.go:418). Second, weaker divergence: `IDLE_ON` exists only in calculated's OffValues, in a stale matter.go:409 comment, and in test fixtures — no enum carries it (notes/concepts/security-safety-concept.md:548 still cites a `SmokeStatusIdleOn` at smoke.go:26 that no longer exists).
stands.missingInput: The authoritative HmIP-SWSD SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS VALUE_LIST (member set and order). The repo carries no captured paramset descriptor; the only lists are hand-authored test fixtures and they disagree with each other and with hmenum: tests/contract/wire_snapshots/snapshot_pin_test.go:648 `[IDLE_OFF, IDLE_ON, PRIMARY_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM]`, internal/model/custom/siren/state_change_test.go:49 `[IDLE_OFF, IDLE_ON, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM]`, hmenum's comment `[IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM]` (4, no IDLE_ON). So whether IDLE_ON exists and what the true ordinal order is cannot be settled here — the duplication and the INTRUSION contradiction can, and are, above. Note the runtime index→label resolution reads the device's own ValueList (custom.EnumLabelValue), so the ordering in hmenum's comment is not load-bearing for that path.
stands.guard: A contract test pins that the smoke set excludes INTRUSION (safety/classify_test.go:104 TestClassifySmokeAlarmStatusExcludesIntrusion), but it covers only the safety classifier — nothing checks siren's or calculated's copies against hmenum.
stands.secondReason: Both halves survive. The vocabulary really is declared three times, and siren's copy is not forced: siren imports pkg/hmenum already and hmenum imports nothing from siren, so no cycle justifies the local type. The divergence is present, not prospective, and it is the strongest bite: the same wire label INTRUSION_ALARM produces 'not smoke' on the MQTT/REST binary sensor (derived_binary.go:175 OffValues) and in the alarm classifier (classify.go:40 via the shared accessor), and SmokeState = Critical (2) to a Matter controller (matter.go:418-419 → :461). matter.js's own doc for that attribute is 'whether the device's smoke sensor is currently triggering a smoke alarm', which INTRUSION_ALARM by hmenum's documented reading is not — so the mapping contradicts the gold standard as well as the sibling packages. hmenum's own claim at :47-49 that 'every consumer that decides smoke from this parameter reads it here' is refuted by matter.go, which decides it and does not.

stands.title: SEQUENCE_OK and the device-error prefixes are each declared twice — data-point suppression in adapter, event classification in model/event — and the two error rules are not the same rule
stands.evidence: datapoint_resolver.go:68-73 `// ImpulseEvents is the set of parameter names treated as impulse events. // Parameters in this set are not created as standalone data points …  var ImpulseEvents = map[string]struct{}{ "SEQUENCE_OK": {}, }` (raw string), read at :48 `if isImpulseEvent(string(param))`. event.go:298 `var impulseParams = map[hmenum.Parameter]struct{}{ hmenum.ParameterSequenceOK: {}, }`, read by Classify at :60 → KindImpulse. datapoint_resolver.go:83-85 `func isDeviceErrorEvent(parameter string) bool { return strings.HasPrefix(parameter, "ERROR") || strings.HasPrefix(parameter, "SENSOR_ERROR") }`, used at :58 to suppress the data point. event.go:309 `var errorPrefixes = []string{ "ERROR", "SENSOR_ERROR" }`, used by event.go:36-47 `isDeviceErrorParam`: `if s == pfx || strings.HasPrefix(s, pfx+"_")`. The coupling is real: callback_handlers.go:852-869 forwardDataPointLessEvent ("publishes the device-trigger event for a parameter that has no data point but does classify") gates on `modevent.Classify`, and coordinators/event.go:277-285 names Classify "the sole authority".
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, adapter.ImpulseEvents would have been defined from event.impulseParams (or vice versa) and isDeviceErrorEvent would have called event's matcher. Instead the two files hold independent literals and independent matching code; `grep -rn 'impulseParams\|errorPrefixes' --include=*.go .` hits only internal/model/event/event.go, and `grep -rn 'ImpulseEvents\|isDeviceErrorEvent'` hits only internal/central/adapter (plus tests).
stands.reason: The same domain fact — this parameter is an impulse / a device error, so it gets a trigger event instead of a stateful data point — is decided once in internal/central/adapter (suppress the DP) and once in internal/model/event (emit the Kind), with no shared source. Extending one side alone yields a stateful data point next to its trigger, or a parameter with neither surface.
stands.divergence: The two device-error rules are already not the same rule: the adapter uses a bare `strings.HasPrefix(parameter, "ERROR")`, so any parameter matching /^ERROR[^_]/ (or /^SENSOR_ERROR[^_]/) loses its data point, while event.isDeviceErrorParam requires an exact match or a trailing underscore and would classify it as nothing — no DP and no event. I found no such parameter in the tree: every ERROR-prefixed name present is ERROR, ERROR_ALARM_TEST, ERROR_CODE, ERROR_JAMMED, ERROR_NON_FLAT_POSITIONING, ERROR_OVERHEAT, ERROR_OVERLOAD, ERROR_SMOKE_CHAMBER (grep over *.json), so today the rules agree on observed inputs and disagree only in shape. The impulse sets agree exactly.
stands.guard: tests/contract/suppression_reader_test.go:107-112 pins that adapter.ImpulseEvents has ≥1 reader inside internal/central/adapter — it never mentions event.impulseParams, so it stays green while the two sets drift.
stands.secondReason: Survives. Quotes current (one line number off by one, corrected above, not material). The sameness holds because callback_handlers.go:328-337 wires the two halves into one path: suppress-the-DP is only safe because Classify keeps the parameter, and Classify is only reached because the DP is absent. The divergence in the error rule is real in shape and I reproduced both returns: for a hypothetical `ERRORCODE`, datapoint_resolver.go:85 `strings.HasPrefix(parameter, "ERROR")` is true → :58 returns nil → no data point, while event.go:44 requires `s == "ERROR"` or `HasPrefix(s, "ERROR_")` → false → Classify not-known → callback_handlers.go:862 returns → the value reaches no plane at all. Damage is therefore observable and total for any such name, and the same silent-drop shape is what the comment at :331-336 says already shipped once ('a reported fault produced nothing anywhere — no device-trigger event, no WebSocket broadcast, and no record on the channel's event group').

stands.title: Two full implementations of the cp_maintenance.cgi firmware POST with two copies of the http/https allowlist; only the CcuBackend copy is reachable in production
stands.evidence: ccu_extended.go:1083-1089: `func (b *CcuBackend) DownloadFirmware(ctx context.Context, firmwareURL string) error { … if !strings.HasPrefix(firmwareURL, "http://") && !strings.HasPrefix(firmwareURL, "https://") { return fmt.Errorf("ccu.DownloadFirmware: only http/https scheme allowed, got %q: %w", firmwareURL, ErrUnsupported) }` then `uploadURL := strings.TrimRight(b.baseURL, "/") + "/config/cp_maintenance.cgi"` with form {sid, action=download_firmware, url}. methods.go:821-824: `func (c *Client) DownloadFirmware(ctx context.Context, firmwareURL string) error { if !strings.HasPrefix(firmwareURL, "http://") && !strings.HasPrefix(firmwareURL, "https://") { return c.wrap("download_firmware", fmt.Errorf("only http/https scheme allowed, got %q: %w", firmwareURL, hmerr.ErrUnsupported)) }` then `uploadURL := base + "/config/cp_maintenance.cgi"` with the same three form fields. Live path: REST handlers/ccu_maintenance.go:286 `svc.DownloadFirmware(...)` → adapter/ccu_maintenance.go:188 `return backend.DownloadFirmware(ctx, firmwareURL)` on the backend from primaryBackendOf. The backend never delegates to the typed client: backends/ccu.go:31 `json Caller // may be nil; disables JSON-RPC-only calls`, wired at adapter/jsonrpc_caller.go:21 `type jsonrpcCaller struct{ client *jsonrpc.Client }` whose only method is the generic `Call(ctx, method, args...)`. The 27-name overlap is real: a script comparing `func (c *Client) X(` in jsonrpc/methods.go with `func (b *CcuBackend) X(` in internal/client/backends/ yields exactly 27 shared names, including DownloadFirmware.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, `grep -rn 'DownloadFirmware' --include=*.go .` would show a non-test reference to a *jsonrpc.Client value, or the backend body would forward to it. It does not: outside methods.go the only hits are the adapter/REST/domain path, test fakes, and the wiring pin — plus the jsonrpc copy's own unit tests.
stands.reason: One security-shaped decision (which firmware-URL schemes the daemon will hand the CCU) plus one wire shape (POST /config/cp_maintenance.cgi with sid/action/url) is implemented twice in full, and only the CcuBackend implementation is on the shipping path. Tightening or widening the obvious-looking jsonrpc copy changes nothing that runs, while its tests stay green.
stands.deadCopy: jsonrpc.Client.DownloadFirmware (methods.go:821) has no production caller anywhere — CORRECTION to the candidate, which says "no caller anywhere including tests": it does have test callers, internal/client/transport/jsonrpc/methods_test.go:1125 TestDownloadFirmwareSuccess and :1169 TestDownloadFirmwareInvalidScheme. That makes the finding stronger, not weaker: the scheme check is covered by a passing test on the copy production never executes.
stands.divergence: The copies already differ below the allowlist: the live backend returns unclassified errors (`fmt.Errorf("ccu.DownloadFirmware: CCU returned HTTP %d", resp.StatusCode)`, ccu_extended.go:1124) and bounds the response with `readLimitedResponse(resp.Body, maxDownloadResponseSize)`, while the dead copy wraps sentinels (`hmerr.ErrInternalBackendException`, `hmerr.ErrNoConnection`, `hmerr.ErrAuthFailure` for a missing sid vs. the backend's `ErrUnsupported`) and drains with `io.Copy(io.Discard, …)`. Both use a 10-minute timeout under two different constant names (backends/ccu.go:23 firmwareDownloadTimeout, jsonrpc/methods.go:29 firmwareTransportDownloadTimeout). The scheme allowlist itself is identical in both.
stands.secondReason: Survives every bite. Quotes exact, line numbers current, both wire shapes identical down to the form field names, and the dead half is confirmed dead by an exhaustive grep rather than by inspection of one file. This is the stronger shape the brief names: jsonrpc/methods_test.go holds eleven tests (TestDownloadFirmwareSuccess through TestDownloadFirmwareNilHTTPClient) that all stay green while the code they exercise never runs, so a security-shaped edit to the obvious-looking transport copy — widening or tightening the scheme allowlist — is fully tested and has zero production effect. The already-present behavioural divergence below the allowlist (unclassified errors + bounded read on the live path vs. hmerr sentinels + unbounded drain on the dead one, and two distinct 10-minute constants at backends/ccu.go:23 firmwareDownloadTimeout and jsonrpc/methods.go:29 firmwareTransportDownloadTimeout) shows the two have already drifted in everything except the one line the candidate calls a duplicate.

stands.title: SysVar.createEnum params built twice — an inline semicolon join in the live CcuBackend and joinSemicolon in the unreachable jsonrpc.Client, with the wire provenance comment on the dead copy

stands.reason: The same wire contract — SysVar.createEnum with a semicolon-joined valList — is built by two independent code paths, and the one that carries the documented provenance (methods.conf / createenum.tcl) is the one production never executes. stands.deadCopy: jsonrpc.Client.CreateSystemVariableEnum (methods.go:445) and its helper joinSemicolon have no production caller. CORRECTION to the candidate's "has no caller at all": internal/client/transport/jsonrpc/methods_test.go:683 TestCreateSystemVariableEnum ("verifies the value list is semicolon-joined") calls it — a green test guarding the unshipped copy, which strengthens the finding.
stands.divergence: None today: both build the identical params map {name, valList, internal: 0, chnID: -1} and the identical separator, and the read side splits on the same ";" (hub_wiring.go:1193). The exposure is that the two are unlinked and the authority comment sits on the dead one.
stands.guard: tests/contract/wiring_pins/ contains no pin for this pair; the only test touching the separator is the one on the dead copy.
stands.secondReason: Survives. Quotes exact including the provenance comment, and the placement claim is the finding's point: the only citation of www/api/methods.conf and sysvar/createenum.tcl in this code path sits on the copy production never executes, while the shipping builder at ccu.go:639 carries only the bare note `// Join as semicolon-separated CCU wire format.` A correction traced back to that ReGa source lands where nothing runs, and jsonrpc/methods_test.go:683-697 (`TestCreateSystemVariableEnum verifies the value list is semicolon-joined`) stays green either way. The duplication is not forced: joinSemicolon is a package-private helper in transport/jsonrpc while backends builds its own inline copy, and backends already imports nothing that prevents sharing. Damage on drift is real though narrow — the separator is the wire contract read back at hub_wiring.go:1193, so a change on one side alone either produces an unparseable valList on the CCU or silently leaves the live path on the old shape.

stands.title: The <param>_STATUS grammar is declared twice and both declarations are live on opposite halves of one pairing — but the hmenum copy is not dead, and its comment's claim is
stands.evidence: pkg/hmenum/parameter.go:304 `const statusParameterSuffix = "_STATUS"`, used by StatusPair (`return Parameter(s + statusParameterSuffix), true`, :319), IsStatusPair (:325) and BasePair (:336). internal/model/generic/datapoint.go:1965 re-spells the same grammar as a literal: `func DetectStatusParameter(parameter string, paramset map[string]struct{}) (string, bool) { status := parameter + "_STATUS" … }`. The two halves of one pairing then run off different declarations: the pipeline attaches the sibling with generic's literal — device_pipeline.go:2076 `if statusName, hasStatus := generic.DetectStatusParameter(name, paramNames); hasStatus {` → `sp.SetStatusParameter(statusName, paramset[statusName].ValueList)` — while the event path recognises the incoming status event with hmenum's constant: callback_handlers.go:311 `if base, isPair := hmenum.Parameter(parameter).BasePair(); isPair {` → `su.UpdateStatusFromWire(...)`, and eventbridge.go:1613 / :2119 likewise.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, one of the two would have called the other (device_pipeline would construct the name via hmenum.Parameter(name).StatusPair()), and grep for `statusParameterSuffix`/`BasePair()` would have shown a single production grammar. Concretely: change `statusParameterSuffix` in pkg/hmenum and the live pairing breaks in half — the pipeline still attaches `<X>_STATUS` sibling DPs, the callback stops recognising `<X>_STATUS` events as status, and pkg/hmenum/parameter_test.go stays green because it only round-trips StatusPair against BasePair.
stands.reason: One decision ("which parameter is another's quality sibling") written twice — once as a named constant with methods, once as an inline literal — with each copy live on a different half of the same flow. That is the coupling that makes the duplication matter, and it is stronger than the candidate's framing.
stands.divergence: None today: both spell `_STATUS`, so no input currently disagrees. The visibility leg is a different decision and I refute it as part of this candidate: store/visibility/rules.go:277 `ignoredParametersEndPattern = regexp.MustCompile(\`.*(_OVERFLOW|_OVERRUN|_REPORTING|_RESULT|_STATUS|_SUBMIT)$\`)` is one of six wildcard ignore suffixes deciding UI/entity exposure, not the pairing grammar.
stands.deadCopy: Only the forward direction is unused: `StatusPair()` is called from pkg/hmenum/parameter_test.go:22,57 alone. `IsStatusPair()`/`BasePair()` — which share `statusParameterSuffix` — have three production callers (callback_handlers.go:311, eventbridge.go:1613, eventbridge.go:2119), so the candidate's "the hmenum copy has no production caller" is refuted. The comment claim IS refuted: parameter.go:300-303 says `Custom data points use this to count optimistic-update confirmations even when the CCU mirrors the value back on the status channel`, but the live handler does the opposite on purpose — callback_handlers.go:301-310 routes the status value to `UpdateStatusFromWire` precisely so it never reaches the base DP's value path, and the only consumers I found are UpdateStatusFromWire / IsStatusValid (generic/datapoint.go:487, :1342; custom/aggregate_status.go:87-97). No code counts optimistic confirmations from a `_STATUS` event.
stands.guard: pkg/hmenum/parameter_test.go round-trips StatusPair↔BasePair inside one package; nothing pins generic.DetectStatusParameter's literal to hmenum's constant.
stands.secondReason: Survives the sameness, liveness and quote bites, and the caller grep strengthens it beyond the candidate's own framing. Sameness: this is one rule (which parameter is another's quality sibling), not one datum read two ways — the forward direction is spelled in both places, once as a method on the named constant and once as an inline literal, and Go does not force the repetition since internal/model/generic already imports pkg/hmenum. stands.title: RollbackReason declared three times, one declaration entirely unreferenced, and the live hop is an unchecked string conversion
stands.evidence: Three independent declarations, each `type RollbackReason string` with the identical triple. hmenum/command.go:19-26: `type RollbackReason string` … `RollbackReasonTimeout RollbackReason = "timeout"` / `RollbackReasonSendError RollbackReason = "send_error"` / `RollbackReasonValueMismatch RollbackReason = "mismatch"`. generic/optimistic_helpers.go:25-41 and optimistic/tracker.go:49-62 repeat the same type name and the same three values, both with a doc comment asserting the strings are stable because they travel to REST/MQTT/audit. The crossing is unchecked: device_pipeline.go:1602 and :1625, inside `pub.OnAnyRollback(func(reason generic.RollbackReason, …)`, both build `Reason:  hmenum.RollbackReason(reason),` for `hmevent.DataPointOptimisticRolledBackEvent`, whose field is `Reason  hmenum.RollbackReason` (catalogue.go:286). Grep `optimistic.RollbackReason` over the whole tree: zero hits (exit 1) — and the only references to the tracker's constants anywhere are the declaration lines themselves; the package is imported only by generic/datapoint.go and generic/optimistic_helpers.go, neither of which names the type. Extra: `RollbackReasonValueMismatch` is declared in all three packages and emitted from none — every production rollback call site is Timeout or SendError (datapoint.go:1623, :1645, :1649, :1775, :1799).
stands.negativeControl: Had the vocabulary been single-sourced, generic would import hmenum's type and the conversions at :1602/:1625 would not exist (the field assignment would be `Reason: reason`); had the optimistic package's copy been live, `optimistic.RollbackReason` would have returned at least one hit — it returns none, including from tests.
stands.reason: One vocabulary — the wire strings shipped to REST, MQTT and audit — is declared three times across three packages, and the value that actually reaches the event is produced by a conversion that accepts any string. Adding or renaming a reason on the generic side compiles cleanly and publishes a string hmenum never declared, with no error and no test that would notice; and one of the three declarations (internal/model/optimistic) has no reference at all, so a maintainer editing it changes nothing while believing otherwise.
stands.deadCopy: internal/model/optimistic/tracker.go:49-62 — the type and all three constants are unreferenced tree-wide. Additionally `RollbackReasonValueMismatch` is emitted from no production path in any of the three packages.
stands.secondReason: Survived every bite. Quotes accurate and current; the repetition is genuinely one vocabulary written three times, not one datum read two ways; and it is not forced — pkg/hmenum is a leaf that imports no repo package, so generic could use hmenum.RollbackReason directly. The liveness attack strengthened it: internal/model/optimistic's declaration is fully unreferenced dead code, an orphan of the tracker consolidation its sibling file documents, so a maintainer editing it changes nothing while its own comment claims the strings "travel through events / logs to clients (REST, MQTT, audit)". The generic->hmenum hop is a bare named-string conversion with no guard, so a reason added or renamed on the generic side compiles and publishes a value hmenum never declared. One honest qualifier on damage, which is why this is medium and not high: the wire contract does not declare an enum (openapi.yaml:11974 is a free `type: string`) and the WS layer stringifies the value verbatim, so a drifted reason would not fail schema validation or crash anything — it would reach clients silently as a value the daemon's own declared vocabulary does not contain. The crisp, immediately actionable part is deleting the unreferenced internal/model/optimistic declaration; collapsing generic's copy onto hmenum's is the durable fix for the unchecked hop.

stands.title: The `modified_at` wire field is emitted in three formats across planes, and the constant's doc comment names as its source a function that uses a different one
stands.negativeControl: Had the comment's claim held, bridge.go:2164 would read `timestampLayout` or an equivalent padded literal; a repo-wide grep for `"2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000000Z07:00"` returns exactly three hits (generic/payload.go:194, client/payload.go:70, client/payload.go:75) and none of them is in internal/north/mqtt.

A modification observed at 12:00:00.5s emits `"2026-09-03T12:00:00.500000000Z"` from the REST/generic payload path and `"2026-09-03T12:00:00.5Z"` from the MQTT alias-mirror and WS paths, and a bare epoch float from the canonical MQTT slot-state envelope. Both string forms re-parse as RFC3339, so a parsing consumer copes; a fixed-width or string-comparing consumer does not, and the comment actively points a future reader at the wrong source.
stands.divergence: Same JSON key `modified_at`, three encodings in production: 9-digit-padded RFC3339 string (generic/payload.go), trimmed RFC3339Nano string (mqtt bridge ×3, ws payloads), epoch seconds as float64 (payload/wrapper.go via eventbridge.go).
stands.guard: None found: no test pins the two planes' `modified_at` rendering against one another.
stands.secondReason: Survived every bite. The quote is exact and the line numbers current; the comment names a specific function whose layout differs, so a future reader following the citation gets the wrong answer -- precisely the class the pre-release comment-claims sweep exists to catch. The divergence is active, not hypothetical: one logical DP change surfaces as "...T12:00:00.123456700Z" on the generic/REST payload and "...T12:00:00.1234567Z" on WS/MQTT. And the published REST contract (openapi.yaml:9147 "RFC3339Nano") is refuted by its own producer at devices.go:1095, which is a spec defect rather than a style one.

stands.title: Countdown timer-kind tokens declared by the engine and re-declared as an acceptance set in the REST handler
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, the handler would have compared against an exported engine symbol (e.g. `engine.TimerKindExit`) or the engine constants would have appeared in the handler's import graph. `grep -rn 'exit_delay\|entry_delay' --include='*.go'` returns two independent const blocks (timers.go:17-18, alarm.go:81-82) plus test literals, and no exported engine token — which is the positive result.
stands.reason:
One domain decision ("which timer kinds are a user-facing countdown") is made twice, and the copies already disagree on a third surface. The REST handler filters to exit/entry; ws/alarm_panel.go:386-391 builds the SAME DTO with no filter — `if snap.TimerKind != "" && snap.TimerRemaining > 0 { st.Countdown = &hmapi.AlarmCountdown{Kind: snap.TimerKind, ...} }` — and that DTO is returned by the `alarm.state` WS read command (ws/alarm_panel.go:236-241). assets/openapi.yaml:13531 constrains that field to `enum: [exit_delay, entry_delay]`, and the SPA types it as `kind: "exit_delay" | "entry_delay"` (assets/ui/src/lib/stores/alarmPanel.svelte.ts:29). A zone in pre-alarm or triggered state therefore emits `kind: "pre_alarm"` / `"trigger_time"` over WS while REST emits no countdown at all. internal/north/mcp/tools_alarm.go:85 (`CountdownKind: z.TimerKind`) is a third unfiltered consumer.

One part of the candidate's claim is REFUTED and should not be repeated: handlers/alarm_state_test.go does NOT stay green on an engine-side rename. TestAlarmState_ExitDelayCountdown (alarm_state_test.go:93-120) arms a real engine (`fx.eng.Arm(...)`) and then asserts `zone.Countdown.Kind != alarmCountdownExit`; a renamed engine token makes `alarmCountdown` return nil and the test fails at `t.Fatal("countdown = nil, want an active exit-delay countdown")` (:115-116). Only alarm_countdown_test.go:26 feeds the handler's own copy (`TimerKind: alarmCountdownEntry` on a hand-built `engine.ZoneSnapshot`) and would stay green. So the seam is partly covered on the REST side; it is uncovered on the WS and MCP sides.
stands.divergence: REST filters the timer kind to {exit_delay, entry_delay}; WS (ws/alarm_panel.go:386) and MCP (tools_alarm.go:85) pass any non-empty kind through the same `hmapi.AlarmCountdown` DTO whose openapi enum and SPA type admit only those two.
stands.guard: Only the handler-local copy is exercised in isolation (alarm_countdown_test.go:26); alarm_state_test.go:93 does cross the seam via a real engine. No guard covers the WS/MCP path.
stands.secondReason: Survives every bite. The quote is current; the sameness holds (one question — "is this timer a user-facing countdown" — answered by an engine-owned token set, a hand-copied REST acceptance pair, and two unfiltered surfaces); both sites are live (the WS command is registered and documented in wsapi.json, the MCP tool is a shipped verb); and the divergence is reproducible rather than hypothetical: for a zone in pre-alarm, REST GET /alarm/state returns no `countdown` while the WS `alarm_panel.state` command returns `{kind: "pre_alarm", remaining_s: N, total_s: 0}` against an openapi enum that admits only exit_delay/entry_delay. The WS copy also omits TotalS entirely (no `total_s` is set at :386-391, and hmapi.AlarmCountdown.TotalS has no omitempty, so it serialises as 0) — a third, independent divergence in the same hand-built DTO. Damage is observable: a WS client typed off types.generated.ts receives an out-of-enum value, and any client seeding the SPA's countdown map from the WS snapshot instead of REST would pass the store's guard (alarmPanel.svelte.ts:120-128 checks only presence and typeof) and render a pre-alarm as an exit-delay ring with total 0 (AlarmOverview.svelte:513-517 falls through `cd.kind === "entry_delay" ? … : …` to the exit label). The SPA as shipped uses REST (`api.getAlarmState()`, alarmPanel.svelte.ts:101), so no user-visible bug today — which is why this is medium, not high.

stands.title: OnOff cluster id, OnOffPlugInUnit device type and the LT-gated attribute block hand-declared in four model packages
stands.evidence:
Every cited line is verbatim. `matterGenericSwitchClusterOnOff uint32 = 0x0006` (generic/switch_matter.go:37) and `matterGenericSwitchAttrOnTime uint32 = 0x4001` (:52); `matterClusterOnOff uint32 = 0x0006` (custom/switch/matter.go:37) and `matterAttrOnTime uint32 = 0x4001` (:52); `matterClusterOnOff        uint32 = 0x0006` (custom/siren/matter.go:81) and `matterAttrOnOffOnTime             uint32 = 0x4001` (:97); `matterClusterOnOff        uint32 = 0x0006` (custom/light/matter.go:49) and `matterAttrOnOffOnTime             uint32 = 0x4001` (:70). schema/devicetypes.go:577-584 carries the mapping the candidate names: `0x010A: { // OnOffPlugInUnit

stands.title: The 8-member click-event set is spelled twice across packages (three times counting the edge-trigger superset), and the narrower 6-member Matter press family three more times inside internal/model/generic
stands.evidence: Quote check passes on every cited line. pkg/hmenum/parameter.go:200 `var ClickEvents = map[Parameter]struct{}{` with exactly ParameterPress, ParameterPressCont, ParameterPressLock, ParameterPressLong, ParameterPressLongRelease, ParameterPressLongStart, ParameterPressShort, ParameterPressUnlock. internal/model/event/event.go:287 `var clickParams = map[hmenum.Parameter]struct{}{` with the identical eight, qualified `hmenum.` — no shared source, no cross-reference between the two files. The set used to be // duplicated in this file and exported for the EventBridge to share; a copy // of an enumerable domain set caps its holder at the size its author knew // about, which is why this plane published only keypresses while the model // had known three event kinds all along.`

Likewise, had the three generic press switches been one decision, two of the three would have called isPressParameter; grep for ParameterPressLongRelease outside tests returns six distinct non-test sites in internal/model/generic, and no call from action.go or matter.go into button.go's helper.

A new PRESS_* spelling added to one yields a data point with no keypress classification, or a classification with no data point, and no test fails. Nothing here is two readings of one datum: the six-member family is a deliberate narrowing of the eight (button.go:410-413 documents why PRESS_LOCK / PRESS_UNLOCK stay out), which makes the eight-vs-six split legitimate — but the three spellings *of the six* are one decision written three times. stands.divergence: None present. All copies currently agree member-for-member; the exposure is that nothing makes them agree.
stands.deadCopy: None — every copy has a live production caller (cited above).
stands.guard: No guard pins ClickEvents against clickParams, and none pins the three generic press switches against each other; the only tests touching these sets iterate one copy in isolation.
stands.secondReason: Survives on all five bites. Quotes are current. The eight-vs-six split is legitimate and the first pass was right to say so (button.go:410-413 documents PRESS_LOCK/PRESS_UNLOCK carrying keymatic semantics), but the three copies *of the six* inside one package are one decision written three times where a package-level helper already exists two files over.
