All three are observable on a north-bound plane and none fails a test. One correction to the first pass: internal/north/mqtt/discovery_aggregate.go:28 `func isPressParameter(p string) bool` is NOT a fourth copy — it delegates (`event.Classify(...)`, :29) and its doc comment at :22-27 records that the copy was deliberately removed. That is the fix pattern this finding wants applied to the remaining copies, and it is already in the tree.

stands.title: The thermostat OFF sentinel 4.5 is spelled three times in the climate profile, re-asserted as a descriptor bound from internal/store/patches, and the RF mode-OFF path expresses the same decision as Capabilities.MinTemperature — which already differs from the IP literal
stands.evidence: Every cited quote verified verbatim. climate.go:639 `const offTemperature = 4.5` (function-local to MinTemp, with `const defaultTemperatureStep = 0.5` on the next line); the bump is climate.go:658-661 `v := resolve()` / `if v == offTemperature { return v + defaultTemperatureStep }`, where resolve() step 2 is `if lo, ok := c.setpoint.DescriptorMin(); ok { return lo }` (climate.go:651-653) and step 3 `return c.Capabilities.MinTemperature` (:655). climate.go:706 `const offTemperatureConst = 4.5`, package-level, used only at climate.go:737-741 `if !hasTemp || temp <= offTemperatureConst || temp < minTemp { if minTemp > offTemperatureConst { return minTemp }; return offTemperatureConst + 0.5 }`. climate.go:1526 `params[hmenum.ParameterSetPointTemperature] = 4.5` under `case ModeOff:` in the IP mode writer. internal/store/patches/patches.go:252 `wantMin := json.RawMessage(`4.5`)` (with `wantMax := json.RawMessage(`30.5`)` on :253) for `Model: "HM-CC-VG-1", Parameter: hmenum.ParameterSetTemperature, Paramset: hmenum.ParamsetKeyValues`, Reason "CCU returns invalid MIN/MAX bounds for virtual heating groups". The coupling is real: HM-CC-VG-1 is an RF-kind profile, and paramForSetpoint (climate.go:2159-2163) returns `hmenum.ParameterSetTemperature` for every non-IP kind, so the patched descriptor MIN is exactly what MinTemp's step 2 reads and compares against its own local 4.5. init.go:58 `MinTemperature: 4.5` (BasicClimateCapabilities), also init.go:92 (RFThermostatCapabilities) and init.go:138 (rfCapabilities). Fourth, unlisted spelling of the same decision: climate.go:1554-1556, the RF ModeOff path, writes `hmenum.ParameterManuMode: c.Capabilities.MinTemperature, hmenum.ParameterSetTemperature: c.Capabilities.MinTemperature` — the OFF setpoint as a capability read rather than a literal. grep for `4\.5|offTemperature` across the package returns two declarations plus climate.go:1526, which uses neither.
stands.negativeControl: Had this been one decision with references, the grep would have returned exactly one declaration and three or four uses of it. It returns two declarations (climate.go:639, :706) that never reference each other, a bare literal at :1526 that references neither, and a fifth statement of the same value from a different package (patches.go:252). Had the patch been decoupled from MinTemp, paramForSetpoint would have returned a parameter other than SET_TEMPERATURE for the RF kinds — it returns SET_TEMPERATURE for every kind except KindIP (climate.go:2159-2163).
stands.reason: One domain decision — "4.5 °C on the setpoint means OFF, not a selectable temperature" — is stated five independent times: two consts in one file, one bare literal on the IP mode-OFF write path, one descriptor bound authored in internal/store/patches, and one capability preset. Change the patch to 5.0 (or the IP literal alone) and MinTemp's equality test stops firing, so the OFF sentinel becomes a selectable setpoint on every surface reading the descriptor range. Beyond drift exposure there is a divergence already present in the tree, which is why I raise it as measured fact rather than hypothesis — see the divergence field. I am not calling that divergence a defect: deciding whether an IP thermostat should be sent 4.5 while its profile advertises a 5.0 floor needs the device-side semantics of SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE, which the source does not carry. The duplication itself is confirmed independently of that question. Severity medium rather than high because no copy is currently mis-valued relative to its own documented intent.
stands.divergence: Present, between the IP and RF spellings of the mode-OFF write. climate.go:1526 (IP) writes the literal 4.5, while climate.go:1555 (RF) writes c.Capabilities.MinTemperature. For IP profiles that value is 5.0 — init.go:74 `MinTemperature: 5.0` in IPThermostatCapabilities and init.go:118 in ipCapabilities, both commented "5–30 °C range". So on an IP thermostat with no TEMPERATURE_MINIMUM DP and no setpoint descriptor MIN, MinTemp() returns 5.0 (the bump never fires, since 5.0 != offTemperature) while ModeOff writes 4.5 — half a degree below the profile's own advertised floor. On RF profiles the two agree, because rfCapabilities.MinTemperature is itself 4.5 (init.go:138). Whether the IP literal or the IP capability floor is the intended value is not decidable from the source.
stands.guard: No test pins the two consts, the literal and the patch bound to one value.
stands.secondReason: The core survives, two of the five claimed sites do not. Surviving: climate.go:639, :706 and :1526 are three spellings of one decision ("4.5 on the setpoint means OFF") inside a single file, two of them named consts, one of them a function-local const shadowing a package-level const that is already in scope. Damage is observable: change offTemperatureConst to 5.0 and MinTemp()'s bump keeps firing on its own local 4.5 while temperatureForHeatMode() moves, so an OFF→HEAT transition writes a setpoint MinTemp() still reports as unreachable; change the const pair and leave :1526 and the IP OFF write silently keeps the old sentinel. Refuted as sites: internal/store/patches/patches.go and internal/model/custom/climate/init.go:58/:138 are not spellings of the OFF sentinel. patches.go writes a MIN/MAX *pair* — `wantMin := json.RawMessage(`4.5`)` at :253 (the cited :252 is the enclosing `Apply: func(pd *hmproto.ParameterData) bool {`, off by one) and `wantMax := json.RawMessage(`30.5`)` at :254, under `Reason: "CCU returns invalid MIN/MAX bounds for virtual heating groups"` (:251) — that is one device's descriptor range restored from device semantics, and it pairs with 30.5 exactly as init.go's rfCapabilities pairs `MinTemperature: 4.5` (:138) with `MaxTemperature: 30.5` (:139). A range floor that happens to coincide with the sentinel is a shared *value*, not a shared *rule*; folding them in would license a rename that silently moves an HM-CC-VG-1 descriptor bound. The finding should be narrowed to the three climate.go sites before it is acted on.

stands.title: Host acceptance is decided by two validators with different grammars, and the stricter public one in pkg/hmtypes has no production caller
stands.evidence: Both quotes verified at the cited lines. internal/config/config.go:2098-2101 `// centralHostLabel matches one DNS label. Underscores are tolerated — // nonstandard, but common on home LANs — and hyphens must stay inside // the label.` / ``var centralHostLabel = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-zA-Z0-9_]([a-zA-Z0-9_-]*[a-zA-Z0-9_])?$`)``, and config.go:2168 `if trimmed != "" && len(host) <= 253 {` inside validateCentralHost, whose loop is `for _, label := range strings.Split(trimmed, ".") { if !centralHostLabel.MatchString(label) { ok = false; break } }` (:2169-2174) — no per-label length cap anywhere in that function. It is the live gate: internal/config/config.go:2065 `if err := validateCentralHost(i, cc.Host); err != nil { return err }`, inside the `for i := range c.Centrals` loop of the config validator. The second copy: pkg/hmtypes/support.go:62-63 `func isValidHostname(host string) bool {` / `if host == "" || len(host) > 253 {`, then :67-72 `if lbl == "" || len(lbl) > 63 { return false }` and `if !hostnameLabel.MatchString(lbl) { return false }` against support.go:56 ``hostnameLabel = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9]$|^[A-Za-z0-9]$`)`` — no underscore in that character class. Exported behind support.go:119 `func ValidateHost(host string) error` and :133 `func IsHost(host string) bool { return ValidateHost(host) == nil }`. Repo-wide grep for `ValidateHost(`, `IsHost(` and `isValidHostname(` returns only the declarations in pkg/hmtypes/support.go and call sites inside pkg/hmtypes/support_test.go (:103, :110, :118, :127, :135, :138, :485). No production caller in any package.
stands.negativeControl: Had hmtypes been the shared implementation, config.validateCentralHost would call hmtypes.ValidateHost instead of re-deriving the 253 cap and its own label regex — config.go:2157-2184 contains the full re-derivation and no hmtypes reference. Had the public helper been live, the grep for `ValidateHost(`/`IsHost(` would have returned at least one non-test, non-pkg/hmtypes hit; it returns none. Both checks are the same grep that would have shown the opposite result had the claim been false.
stands.reason: One trust-boundary decision — is this string an acceptable CCU host — implemented twice with materially different grammars, and the public, stricter implementation is exercised only by its own package's tests. Any later surface that reaches for the obvious public helper (a REST central editor, the first-run wizard) will reject hosts the config file accepts, splitting the decision in two along a seam no test crosses. The dead-copy shape makes this worse rather than better: pkg/hmtypes/support_test.go stays green while the live daemon never runs that code. This is not an EnumLabel/EnumLabelFromWire pair — neither validator is specialised to a different caller or input encoding; both answer the identical question about the identical kind of string.
stands.divergence: Present and demonstrable on inputs, from the regexes themselves rather than from any assumption. (1) Underscores: `ccu_1` matches centralHostLabel (character class `[a-zA-Z0-9_]`, deliberate per the comment at config.go:2098-2100) and fails hostnameLabel (`[A-Za-z0-9]`), so config accepts what hmtypes.IsHost rejects. (2) Label length: config applies no per-label cap, hmtypes rejects any label over 63 chars (support.go:67-69), so a 100-character single label under the 253 total is accepted by config and rejected by hmtypes. (3) Trailing dot: config strips it before label-splitting (`trimmed := strings.TrimSuffix(host, ".")`, :2167) while measuring the 253 cap on the untrimmed `host`; hmtypes measures the trimmed-of-whitespace string and splits without stripping a trailing dot, so `example.com.` yields an empty final label and is rejected there.
stands.deadCopy: pkg/hmtypes/ValidateHost (support.go:119) and IsHost (:133), with their shared isValidHostname (:62) — referenced only from pkg/hmtypes/support_test.go.
stands.secondReason: Survives every bite. Quotes current (support.go:55 in the original is the hostnameLabel doc comment, the regexp is at :56 — a one-line pointer slip, not a bad quote). Sameness holds: both answer "is this string an acceptable host" about the same kind of string, and neither is specialised to a different caller or wire encoding, so this is not an EnumLabel/EnumLabelFromWire pair. The dead-copy shape is the sharp end — pkg/ is this repo's declared public surface (CLAUDE.md, Repository Structure), so hmtypes.IsHost is exactly the helper a later REST central editor or the first-run wizard would reach for, and it would then reject `ccu_1`, a spelling the config file accepts on purpose (the comment at config.go:2098-2100 says so). No test crosses that seam because no test can: support_test.go stays green against code the daemon never runs. Damage on drift is a config file that validates and a UI that refuses the same value. Incidental observation while verifying, outside the finding: the doc comment written for validateCentralHost (config.go:2103-2108, ending `// URLs. The TCP port has its own config field.`) is followed with no blank line by validateCentralNames' own comment at :2109, so Go attaches the whole block to validateCentralNames and validateCentralHost at :2157 is undocumented.

stands.evidence: Set membership verified by reading both declarations in full: pkg/hmenum/parameter.go:200-210 and internal/model/event/event.go:287-296 each hold exactly ParameterPress, ParameterPressCont, ParameterPressLock, ParameterPressLong, ParameterPressLongRelease, ParameterPressLongStart, ParameterPressShort, ParameterPressUnlock — same eight, same order, differing only in the `hmenum.` qualifier, with no shared source and no cross-file reference. Consumer split verified: internal/central/adapter/datapoint_resolver.go:173 `if param.IsClickEvent() {` (and again at :181) plus internal/store/visibility/rules.go:169 `"HmIP-PS": copyParamSet(hmenum.ClickEvents),` read the hmenum copy; internal/model/event/event.go:57 `if _, ok := clickParams[p]; ok {` inside Classify, reached from internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:403 `if kind, known := event.Classify(hmenum.Parameter(ev.Parameter)); known && kind != event.KindKeypress {` and internal/central/coordinators/event.go:284 `kind, ok := event.Classify(hmenum.Parameter(parameter))`, reads the model copy. The cited comment is verbatim at internal/central/coordinators/event.go:276-278: `// [event.Classify] is the sole authority: click parameters become // keypresses, SEQUENCE_OK an impulse, and the ERROR / SENSOR_ERROR prefixes // a device error. stands.negativeControl: Had the two been one set, internal/model/event/event.go:287 would read from hmenum.ClickEvents; grep for ClickEvents across the repo returns internal/store/visibility/rules.go:169 and two visibility test files and nothing in internal/model/event. Had a guard pinned them equal, grep of *_test.go for both names would have shown a test naming both — it shows no test that mentions clickParams at all.
stands.reason: Confirmed on the same evidence as const-PRESS_LONG_RELEASE-1; this candidate is the strict subset of it covering only the two cross-package copies, and I report it as its own confirmed verdict rather than folding it in. One qualification on the comment claim: coordinators/event.go:277 asserts Classify is the sole authority over *event kind* — keypress vs impulse vs device error — which is accurate for the trigger-publishing path it documents. It does not claim authority over data-point shape, which datapoint_resolver.go:173 decides from the other copy. The candidate's framing ("the comment asserting single authority makes the second copy easy to miss") is fair as a readability hazard but should not be read as the comment being false. stands.guard: No test compares hmenum.ClickEvents with event.clickParams; the only tests naming either iterate hmenum.ClickEvents alone (internal/store/visibility/rules_test.go:345, event_suppression_test.go:29/:55/:61) and would not notice a member added to or removed from clickParams.
stands.secondReason: The technical claim survives — it is the strict subset of const-PRESS_LONG_RELEASE-1 and rests on the same verified reads — and the first pass's qualification of the comment claim is right on the source: coordinators/event.go:277 scopes its authority to *event kind* ("click parameters become keypresses, SEQUENCE_OK an impulse, and the ERROR / SENSOR_ERROR prefixes a device error", :277-279), which is accurate for publishDeviceTriggerFor; it says nothing about data-point shape, which datapoint_resolver.go:173 decides from the hmenum copy. So the comment is a readability hazard, not a false claim, and reporting it as false would have been the error. My one dissent is at the report level, not the code level: this is not a second finding. Every site, every consumer and every remedy it names is contained in const-PRESS_LONG_RELEASE-1, whose scope is strictly larger; acting on it twice would produce two backlog entries for one change. Fold it in and drop the id.

stands.title: The six-token CCU truth set is duplicated into an exported pkg/hmtypes helper with no production caller, and the two copies already differ on whitespace
stands.evidence: Verified verbatim. internal/parameter/converter.go:241-243 `func isBoolTrueString(s string) bool {` / `switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)) {` / `case "y", "yes", "t", "true", "on", "1":`, called from the read-path cast at :194 `return isBoolTrueString(v)` inside the `case hmenum.ParameterTypeBool, hmenum.ParameterTypeAction:` branch. pkg/hmtypes/support.go:82-88 `func ToBool(value any) (bool, error) {` … `case string:` / `switch strings.ToLower(v) {` / `case "y", "yes", "t", "true", "on", "1":`. `grep -rn "ToBool" --include="*.go" .` returns, for the identifier hmtypes.ToBool, only pkg/hmtypes/support.go:78/82/94 and pkg/hmtypes/support_test.go (lines 20-66). Every other hit is an unrelated test name containing the substring (e.g. internal/model/value/converter_test.go:71 TestFromHomematicValue_IntToBool). The candidate's refutation of the other two truth tables also checks out: internal/parameter/coerce.go:122-128 says `// asBool's truth table differs on purpose from … ParamBool` and `// Different boundaries, different tolerances — keep both, do not unify.`, and coerce.go:151 / internal/model/generic/coerce.go:58 use a different four/five-token set including a false branch.
stands.negativeControl: Had hmtypes.ToBool been live, the grep above would have listed a non-test file outside pkg/hmtypes; it lists none. Had the sets differed, the two `case` lines would not be byte-identical — they are (`case "y", "yes", "t", "true", "on", "1":` at converter.go:243 and support.go:88).
stands.deadCopy: pkg/hmtypes.ToBool (pkg/hmtypes/support.go:82) — exercised only by pkg/hmtypes/support_test.go. It is on the published pkg/ surface, so it reads as the daemon's contract while the daemon uses internal/parameter.isBoolTrueString.
stands.divergence: The copies already disagree on whitespace-padded input. converter.go:242 applies `strings.TrimSpace` before the switch; support.go:87 applies only `strings.ToLower`. For the wire string `" true "` the live read path yields true and the exported helper yields (false, nil) — silently, since the string branch never errors. Whether the CCU emits padded booleans is not established by anything in the repo, so this is a latent, not an observed, divergence.
stands.reason: One decision — which CCU-reported strings count as boolean true — is encoded twice, once in the live read path and once on the published surface with no caller. The dead copy is the stronger half of the finding: widening or narrowing the live set (its comment ties it to the reference `to_bool` at support/__init__.py:129) leaves the exported one behind with nothing failing, and a client reading pkg/hmtypes takes the stale copy for the contract.
stands.guard: None. No test compares the two token sets.
stands.secondReason: Nothing in the attack landed. One decision — which CCU-reported strings count as boolean true — is written twice with identical six-token bodies, one live (converter.go:194, the read-path cast for every BOOL/ACTION parameter) and one exported on the public pkg/ surface with zero production callers, kept green by its own test. The copies already differ: for the wire string " true " the live path returns true and the exported helper returns (false, nil), silently, because the string branch never errors. Severity lowered from medium to low, and the reason is stated rather than assumed: the divergence is not observable inside the daemon (nothing calls ToBool), the deadness is already tracked in notes/parity/dead-code-production-only.json under an auto-whitelist, and nothing in the repo establishes that the CCU emits whitespace-padded booleans — so the damage is confined to an external Go consumer of pkg/hmtypes taking the stale copy for the contract. stands.title: The virtual-remote ADDRESS datum has two homes; the dead one in internal/client names the HmIP interface, not the HmIP virtual-remote device
stands.evidence: Quote verified verbatim. interface_client.go:1082-1090: `func (c *InterfaceClient) VirtualRemote() (string, bool) {` / `case hmenum.InterfaceHmIPRF:` / `\t\treturn "HmIP-RF", true` / `case hmenum.InterfaceBidCosRF:` / `\t\treturn "BidCoS-RF", true` / `\treturn "", false`. Its doc comment at :1080-1081 asserts `// CUxD / VirtualDevices / wired interfaces` / `// have none → returns ("", false).` — uniqueid.go:40-44: `var virtualRemoteRoots = map[string]struct{}{` / `\t"BidCoS-RF":  {},` / `\t"BidCoS-Wir": {},` / `\t"HmIP-RCV-1": {},` / `}`, consumed live at :121 `_, ok := virtualRemoteRoots[addressRoot(address)]` (needsCentralPrefix, reached from exported GenerateUniqueID :145 and NeedsCentralScope :105) and at :157 in GenerateChannelUniqueID. — mqtt_sink.go:59-62: `// virtual remote ("HmIP-RCV-1") is the one mixed-case address in a CCU's` / `// inventory, and writing with the upper-cased form faults with` / `// "Invalid device".` — pkg/hmenum/device_model.go:18-20 states the intended single home: `// This is the MODEL axis. The virtual-remote ADDRESS roots are a different` / `// datum with a different home (internal/routingkey), and they feed published` / `// identity (unique ids, retained MQTT topics); do not merge the two sets.` — External confirmation of the address, read from the source and not assumed: ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/const.py:2095-2099 `VIRTUAL_REMOTE_ADDRESSES: Final[tuple[str, ...]] = (` / `    "BidCoS-RF",` / `    "BidCoS-Wir",` / `    "HmIP-RCV-1",` / `)`. `"HmIP-RF"` is the interface name, not a device address: pkg/hmenum/interface.go:22 `InterfaceHmIPRF         Interface = "HmIP-RF"`. — Caller census: `grep -rn "VirtualRemote()" --include="*.go" .` returns exactly three hits for this method — the declaration at interface_client.go:1082 and two tests (interface_client_test.go:186, interface_client_deep_test.go:559); `grep -rn "VirtualRemote() (" --include="*.go"` finds no interface declaring the method, so no implicit production caller exists.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false I would have seen one of two things, and I ran both checks: (a) the caller grep would have returned at least one non-_test.go call site or an interface embedding `VirtualRemote() (string, bool)` — it returned only the declaration plus two _test.go files; (b) the two sources would have agreed — `virtualRemoteRoots` would contain `"HmIP-RF"`, or `VirtualRemote()` would return `"HmIP-RCV-1"` for `InterfaceHmIPRF`. Neither holds. The control fires in the opposite direction on the BidCos entry, which is the same datum and does agree: `VirtualRemote()` returns `"BidCoS-RF"` (capital S, the CCU device address) and `virtualRemoteRoots` carries `"BidCoS-RF"` — even though the enum spells the interface differently (`InterfaceBidCosRF Interface = "BidCos-RF"`, interface.go:23). So the mechanism distinguishes agreement from disagreement on adjacent entries of the same map.
stands.reason: One domain fact — the CCU's virtual-remote device addresses — is written down twice as literals. internal/routingkey holds the live copy (three roots, reached from GenerateUniqueID / GenerateChannelUniqueID / NeedsCentralScope, i.e. published unique_ids and retained MQTT topics); internal/client holds a second, per-interface copy behind `VirtualRemote()`. This is not the `EnumLabel` vs `EnumLabelFromWire` pattern — the two are not two readings each correct for its caller, they are the same string set keyed two ways, and hmenum/device_model.go:18-20 explicitly names internal/routingkey as the datum's single home. The dead copy disagrees on two inputs, not one. First, HmIP: `"HmIP-RF"` is the interface identifier, while the HmIP virtual remote's device address is `"HmIP-RCV-1"` per routingkey, mqtt_sink.go:60 and the reference const.py. Second, BidCos-Wired: `VirtualRemote()` documents wired interfaces as having no virtual remote and returns ("", false), while `virtualRemoteRoots` carries `"BidCoS-Wir"`, hmenum carries the wired model `"HMW-RCV-50"`, and coordinators/device.go:712-715 states `// [hmenum.IsVirtualRemoteModel] — one exact model per bus family (BidCos-RF,` / `// BidCos-Wired, HmIP-RF), so the result covers Wired-Bus and IP-RF` / `// interfaces alike.` Severity is medium, not high: with no production caller nothing is broken today. The finding is that the two tests pin the wrong HmIP address as if it were specification, so a future caller adopting `VirtualRemote()` — the natural thing to reach for from a client — would write to `HmIP-RF`, which mqtt_sink.go:60 records the CCU faulting as "Invalid device", and both tests would stay green. Note the live inventory path does not use either literal: coordinators/device.go:716-727 derives virtual-remote addresses from the CCU's own descriptions via `hmenum.IsVirtualRemoteModel(d.Type)`, which is a third and data-driven answer.
stands.deadCopy: internal/client/interface_client.go:1082 `VirtualRemote()` — zero production callers; only internal/client/interface_client_test.go:186 and internal/client/interface_client_deep_test.go:559. No interface in the repo declares the method, so it cannot be reached via a method set either.
stands.divergence: HmIP-RF: `VirtualRemote()` returns "HmIP-RF" (interface_client.go:1085) vs "HmIP-RCV-1" in virtualRemoteRoots (uniqueid.go:43), mqtt_sink.go:60 and aiohomematic const.py:2098. BidCos-Wired: `VirtualRemote()` returns ("", false) and documents wired as having none (interface_client.go:1080-1081) vs "BidCoS-Wir" in virtualRemoteRoots (uniqueid.go:42) and the "HMW-RCV-50" model in hmenum/device_model.go:23.
stands.guard: tests/contract/routing_key_contract_test.go:112-114 pins the routingkey copy against the golden fixtures ("BidCoS-RF:1", "BidCoS-Wir:1", "HmIP-RCV-1:1"); nothing pins the internal/client copy against it, which is why the disagreement survived.
stands.secondReason: The finding survives every bite. The quotes are current and verbatim. The sameness attack fails on the function's own internal inconsistency: it returns the interface constant for HmIP and the address spelling ("BidCoS-RF", capital S, distinct from the interface constant "BidCos-RF") for BidCos, so it cannot be one datum read correctly two ways. The liveness attack strengthens rather than weakens it — VirtualRemote() has zero production callers while routingkey feeds published unique_ids and retained MQTT topics, so the wrong value sits behind a green test with nothing exercising it. The divergence is reproducible from the enum's only HmIP value and is not normalised anywhere. Damage is the one genuinely weak leg and it is why medium, not high, is right: nothing observable changes today; the cost is a dead literal that a test (interface_client_test.go:175 `{hmenum.InterfaceHmIPRF, "HmIP-RF", true},`) pins as if it were specification, which a future caller reaching for the client-side accessor would adopt and land on the "Invalid device" fault mqtt_sink.go:59-61 documents. Two corrections to the candidate's supporting prose, neither touching the verdict: (1) only interface_client_test.go:175 pins the wrong HmIP address — interface_client_deep_test.go:559 asserts only the VirtualDevices case ("", false), which is correct; (2) the candidate calls coordinators/device.go:716-727 "the live inventory path", but `grep -rn "GetVirtualRemoteAddresses(|GetVirtualRemotes("` excluding _test.go finds only the two definitions — that data-driven third answer is itself test-only today, so the sole live copy of the address datum is internal/routingkey.

stands.title: The two wire→Go reply converters accept different value sets and different integer widths
stands.evidence:
Quotes verified verbatim. xmlrpc_caller.go:113-138: `func xmlRPCValueToGo(v xmlrpc.Value) any {` / `switch x := v.(type) {` / `case xmlrpc.NilValue:` / `case xmlrpc.StringValue:` / `case xmlrpc.IntValue:` `return int(x)` / `case xmlrpc.BoolValue:` / `case xmlrpc.DoubleValue:` / `case xmlrpc.ArrayValue:` / `case xmlrpc.StructValue:` / `}` / `return nil` — there is no DateTimeValue and no Base64Value case. ordered_caller.go:24-54 carries both: `case xmlrpc.DateTimeValue:` / `return x.Time().Format(xmlrpc.ISO8601CompactLayout)` / `case xmlrpc.Base64Value:` / `return base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(x))`, and `case xmlrpc.IntValue:` / `return int64(x)`.

The decoder does produce both kinds: internal/client/transport/xmlrpc/decode.go:143-158 `case "dateTime.iso8601":` … `return DateTimeValue(t), nil` and :160-169 `case "base64":` … `return Base64Value(raw), nil`.

stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, one site would read the other (a shared package-level `var` referenced twice, or ccu_wiring passing cuxdIngestBackoff). Both are independent literals — ccu_wiring's is a function-local `:=` inside wireInterface, cuxd's a package-level `var` in another file — and the grep shows no cross-reference. Had the comment's "Same shape" claim been stale, the two element lists would differ; they are character-for-character identical, so this is a duplication finding, not a stale-comment finding.
stands.reason: Two independent literals encode one policy, with a comment asserting their equality and nothing enforcing it. Severity low, not medium: the ladders are identical today, so nothing is broken now, and the consequence of future drift is a differently-sized boot retry window on one interface family — an interface that exhausts the ladder is still walked to DISCONNECTED by its activation loop (ccu_wiring.go:1417 / cuxd_wiring.go:400), so the recovery pipeline still repairs it on the next probe success. stands.divergence: None today. Both slices are exactly `{1s, 2s, 5s, 10s, 15s}` — a ~33 s window on both paths. I looked for a diverging input and there is none: the divergence is latent, and would appear the moment either literal is tuned.
stands.deadCopy: Neither. ccu_wiring.go:1340 feeds ccu_wiring.go:1343 in the XML-RPC interface bring-up; cuxd_wiring.go:368 feeds cuxd_wiring.go:277 in the CUxD bring-up, reached from ccu_wiring.go:720.

stands.title: The backup-id grammar is defined twice with different widths, and one of them breaks the fixed-width suffix invariant the other relies on
stands.evidence: Verbatim. stubs.go:352-360: `// backupTimestampLayout is the fixed-width UTC timestamp appended to every` / `// backup id. …` / `const backupTimestampLayout = "20060102-150405"` … `// backupIDSuffixLen is the length of the "-<timestamp>" suffix backupID` / `// appends: one separator + the 15-char timestamp = 16. backupBelongsTo strips` / `// exactly this to recover the central's safe name.` / `const backupIDSuffixLen = 1 + len(backupTimestampLayout)`. stubs.go:382-384 `func formatBackupID(centralName string, at time.Time) string {` / `return fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s", backupSafeName(centralName), at.UTC().Format(backupTimestampLayout))`. stubs.go:425-430 `func backupBelongsTo(id, safe string) bool {` / `if len(id) <= backupIDSuffixLen {` / `return false` / `}` / `return id[:len(id)-backupIDSuffixLen] == safe`. Second grammar, backup_storage.go:445 `const uploadedBackupPrefix = "upload-"` and :459 `id := uploadedBackupPrefix + now.Format("20060102-150405.000")` — a literal layout, referencing neither backupTimestampLayout nor backupIDSuffixLen (`grep -rn 'backupTimestampLayout|20060102-150405' --include='*.go'` returns exactly stubs.go:352/355/360/383 and backup_storage.go:459). Both live: FilesystemBackupStorage.SaveUploaded is reached from internal/north/rest/handlers/backup.go:406 `entry, err := svc.SaveUploaded(r.Context(), filename, data)` via internal/central/adapter/stubs.go:776; backupBelongsTo is used by the pruner at stubs.go:234 and by ownerCentralName at stubs.go:445, which feeds resolveRestorer (:476), the listing backfill (:567) and the per-central lock (:614).
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, SaveUploaded would render its timestamp with backupTimestampLayout (or assert against backupIDSuffixLen) and the strip would decompose an uploaded id cleanly. Line 459 uses the literal `"20060102-150405.000"`, 19 characters against the 15 the constant declares, and no cross-reference exists in either direction — which is precisely what a real second grammar looks like.
stands.reason: The structural claim holds: one id grammar is stated with a named width in stubs.go and a second, wider one is minted in backup_storage.go with no reference to it, and stubs.go:352's comment (`the fixed-width UTC timestamp appended to every backup id`) is already false for uploaded ids. Benign today, so low. Two corrections to the candidate's text. (1) The damage sentence is stale: resolveRestorer no longer falls back to the legacy restorer as its normal path — stubs.go:461-468 says `That case used to fall through to the legacy single-restorer field, which nothing in production ever set … It now resolves to the only configured central when there is exactly one … and refuses with [hmerr.ErrRestoreTargetAmbiguous] when there are several.` So an uploaded restore succeeds on a single-CCU install and is refused, not silently misrouted, on a multi-CCU one. (2) The isolation is indeed provided by the width rather than the prefix — the pruner at stubs.go:233-236 filters with backupBelongsTo, not with uploadedBackupPrefix, while backup_storage.go:441-444 credits the prefix with `keeps the scheduled-backup pruner from ever treating an imported archive as one of its own rotations`. That comment names the wrong mechanism.
stands.divergence: id `upload-20260902-150405.123` (26 chars, the shape SaveUploaded mints today). formatBackupID's grammar would parse the owner as `id[:len(id)-16]` == `upload-202`; formatBackupID can only ever produce that for a central whose backupSafeName is literally `upload-202`, so ownerCentralName returns "". A minted id for the same clock, `alpha-20260902-150405` (21 chars), strips to `alpha`. The two grammars therefore assign different meanings to the same 16-character strip, and the uploaded one is decomposed into a fragment (`upload-202`) rather than an owner. Read from the source; not executed.
stands.deadCopy: none — SaveUploaded (backup_storage.go:455) and backupBelongsTo/formatBackupID (stubs.go) both have production callers
stands.guard: partial and one-sided: internal/central/adapter/backup_storage_test.go:1516-1521 pins that every *minted* id satisfies backupBelongsTo and keeps a fixed length; backup_storage_test.go:878 only checks that an uploaded id carries the prefix. No test relates the uploaded grammar to backupIDSuffixLen, so changing either width leaves the suite green.

stands.title: Five hand-rolled device-address / channel-number parsers coexist with the canonical pkg/hmtypes helpers
stands.evidence: All five quotes verified verbatim. devices.go:237-243 `func deviceAddressOf(channel string) string { for i := len(channel) - 1; i >= 0; i-- { if channel[i] == ':' { return channel[:i] } } return channel }`. device_pipeline.go:2284-2300 `i := strings.LastIndexByte(addr, ':')` / `n, err := strconv.Atoi(addr[i+1:])` / `return n, true`, and `func channelNumber(addr string) int { if n, ok := splitChannel(addr); ok { return n }; return 0 }`. paramsets.go:348-362 `func channelNumberOf(channelAddress string) int` — reverse colon scan, digit loop, `return 0` on any non-digit and `return 0` when no colon exists. schedule_query_adapter.go:128-143 `func splitChannelAddress(channelAddress string) (device string, channelIdx int)` — same digit scan but `return channelAddress, 0` (the FULL address as the device part) on a non-digit suffix. pkg/hmtypes/address.go:53-64 ChannelNo (`strings.IndexByte`, `if err != nil || v < 0 { return 0, false }`), :70-76 DeviceAddress (`strings.Cut`), :84-99 SplitChannelAddress (channelNo -1 sentinel, "None" handling). Side-by-side use confirmed: device_reloader.go:99 `deviceAddr := hmtypes.DeviceAddress(channelAddress)` vs devices.go:226 `deviceAddr := deviceAddressOf(channelAddress)`. All five are live and heavily called (deviceAddressOf: links.go, paramsets.go, callback_handlers.go, auto_refresh.go, config_export.go, parameter_determiner.go, link_profile.go, device_pipeline.go:1326; splitChannel: device_pipeline.go:421,460,783; channelNumberOf: paramsets.go:285,490,559,591; splitChannelAddress: schedule_query_adapter.go:37,53,67 and schedules.go:306-307).
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, the helpers would agree on every input I could construct. They do not: I found a reachable input (below) where channelNumberOf returns a number the canonical helper explicitly refuses. Conversely, had I found only unreachable disagreements, the verdict would have been the reachability question, not a defect — which is why I checked the address grammar the source itself carries and downgraded two of the candidate's three examples.
stands.reason: The duplication is real, all five parsers are live, and they disagree — but not for the reasons the candidate gives, and the reachable damage is small. REFUTED sub-claims: (a) last-colon vs first-colon can only diverge on an address with two colons, and the grammar the source carries forbids it — pkg/hmtypes/address.go:23 `deviceAddressPattern = regexp.MustCompile(\`^[0-9a-zA-Z-]{5,20}$\`)` (no colon in a device address) and :20 `channelAddressPattern = ...\`^[0-9a-zA-Z-]{5,20}:\\d{1,3}$\`` (exactly one). The LINK peer travels as its own path parameter (rest/router.go:1262 `/devices/{addr}/link-ps/{peer}`), not as a second colon. (b) "X:-1" is never generated: hmtypes.ChannelAddress(dev, -1) returns the bare device address (address.go:43-45) and the root channel's Address is d.Address with Number -1 held separately (device.go:546-551). CONFIRMED sub-claim: channelNumberOf's `return 0` for a colon-less address collides with real channel 0 on a reachable path. Low severity: the one reachable consequence I could evidence is a mislabelled audit row; the visibility-gate consumer is inert for this input because MASTER is not gate-decided (paramsets.go:526-528 `return key != hmenum.ParamsetKeyMaster`).
stands.divergence: Input `"0001ABCD"` (a bare device address, reachable: rest/router.go:1261 routes PUT /devices/{addr}/paramsets/{key} with a free-form {addr}, handlers/paramsets.go:88 `addr := chi.URLParam(r, "addr")`, and device-level MASTER paramsets exist — device_pipeline.go:1831 hydrateDeviceRoot). channelNumberOf("0001ABCD") → 0. hmtypes.ChannelNo("0001ABCD") → (0, false). hmtypes.SplitChannelAddress("0001ABCD") → ("0001ABCD", -1, false). The model's own root-channel number is -1 (device.ChannelNumberDevice, model/device/channel.go:49). Result: paramsets.go:285 writes `ChannelNo: channelNumberOf(channelAddress)` into the audit entry, so a device-level MASTER write is recorded as a channel-0 write, indistinguishable from a real one. Second (function-level, reachability not established): splitChannelAddress("ABC-1:None") → ("ABC-1:None", 0) while hmtypes.SplitChannelAddress("ABC-1:None") → ("ABC-1", -1, false) (pinned at pkg/hmtypes/address_test.go:120-121); I found no production path that produces a "None" suffix, so I do not claim it as reachable.
stands.deadCopy: none — all five have production callers; the pkg/hmtypes helpers are live too (device_reloader.go:99)
stands.guard: none. pkg/hmtypes/address_test.go covers the canonical helpers only; no test compares deviceAddressOf / splitChannel / channelNumberOf / splitChannelAddress against hmtypes.DeviceAddress / ChannelNo / SplitChannelAddress, and no test feeds any of them a bare device address to pin the -1-vs-0 answer.

stands.evidence: Both quotes verified verbatim. internal/model/schedule/simple.go:151-154: `// maxDurationFactor is the maximum allowed numeric factor in a duration string` / `// (e.g. "30s", "30min", "30h"). That is why 30 caps a timed duration rather than` / `// the field.` / `const MaxTimeBaseFactor = 30`, and the measurement at rawconvert.go:736-742: `It justified the swallow with "the CCU rejects a write of any factor past 30 with fault -5". That is false. Writing 31 to 01_WP_DURATION_FACTOR over XML-RPC succeeds and reads back as 31, and so does 32 — a value past the declared MAX and past the five-bit field. The CCU does not validate this field's bound on putParamset at all, so nothing here is refused and the original justification never held.` Liveness: MaxTimeBaseFactor is live (rawconvert.go:1242 inside ParseTimeBaseFactor, and rawconvert.go:759 inside decodeWireDuration, both on the live simple-schedule read/write path). maxDurationFactor is NOT live: its only use is validateDuration (simple.go:172-173), called only from SimpleEntry.Validate (:212), which is reached only from ValidateFor (:229) and Simple.Put (:346) — and repo-wide grep shows no non-test caller for either.
stands.negativeControl: Had the two comments agreed, simple.go:152-153 would attribute the cap to the encoding rather than to a firmware rejection — instead it says `to match CCU firmware limits`, which rawconvert.go:1043-1045 and :736-742 name as the exact claim that measurement disproved. Had maxDurationFactor been live, grep for `ValidateFor(` / `ValidateAll(` / `.Put(` on a schedule.Simple outside _test.go would have found a caller; it found none (internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:872 assigns `s.Entries[e.SlotNo] = ...` directly, bypassing Put).

stands.title: The P1..P6 profile-key grammar is spelled five times and two spellings disagree on P01
stands.evidence: All five quotes verified verbatim at the cited lines. climate.go:355-364 isValidProfileKey uses 'if len(k) < 2 || k[0] != P' then fmt.Sscanf(k, "P%d", &n) and 'return n >= 1 && n <= 6'. schedules.go:1576-1581 isValidProfileID uses 'if len(s) != 2 || s[0] != P' then 'n := int(s[1] - 0)'. rawconvert.go:323-334 is a byte-identical duplicate of copy 1 carrying the comment 'isValidProfileKey mirrors the schedule package helper but is package-local to avoid importing it'. schedule_io.go:122-129 isProfileIDWithinCap repeats the len==2 form with a per-device cap. profile.go:220-231 declares MinProfileIndex=1 / MaxProfileIndex=6 and ValidProfileIndex. All five have production callers: climate.go:193/219/235; schedules.go:1093, 1390; rawconvert.go:304; schedule_io.go:275, 424, 502, 511; profile.go via internal/north/rest/handlers/schedules.go:310 and internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:300.
stands.divergence: Exact input "P01". isValidProfileKey("P01") -> len 3 >= 2, k[0]==P, Sscanf parses n=1 -> true (both copies, climate.go:355 and rawconvert.go:325). isValidProfileID("P01") -> len != 2 -> false. isProfileIDWithinCap("P01", 6) -> len != 2 -> false. The one live sequence that runs lax-then-strict is SchedulesDomain.SetWeekday: schedule_io.go:238 sched.Put("P01", prof) succeeds via isValidProfileKey, then SetSchedule at schedule_io.go:266 passes sched.Validate() (isValidProfileKey again) and is refused at schedule_io.go:275 with the misleading text 'profile "P01" exceeds device cap P1..P6'.
stands.deadCopy: No copy is dead, but the only production function that exposes the disagreement, SchedulesDomain.SetWeekday (internal/central/adapter/schedule_io.go:217), has no caller outside its own file - repo-wide grep for SetWeekday excluding _test.go returns only the definition and its internal error strings.
stands.guard: None. No test compares the five helpers against one another; each is exercised only through its own caller.
stands.negativeControl: Had the two spellings agreed, isValidProfileID("P01") would return true like isValidProfileKey("P01"); it returns false at the len(s) != 2 branch. Had a CCU been able to deliver a zero-padded prefix, climateParamPattern would have to admit it; rawconvert.go:46-48 pins it to ^(P[1-6])_(TEMPERATURE|ENDTIME)_([A-Z]+)_(\d+)$, so RawToClimate can never see "P01" and the read-path half of the damage is impossible.
stands.reason: The duplication and the P01 disagreement are exactly as claimed and verified. The damage story is not: the CCU cannot emit a padded key (regex-bound to P[1-6]), and every REST entry point - SetActiveProfile (schedules.go:1093), SetProfile (schedule_io.go:416), CopyProfileTo (schedule_io.go:491/494), serializeClimateSchedule (schedules.go:1390) - runs the strict check first and returns a clear ErrInvalidProfileID, so no operator ever gets an entry they can open but not save. Downgraded to low: what remains is the maintenance cost the candidate names in its last sentence (a seven-profile device needs five edits) plus one misleading error message on a function nothing calls.

stands.title: The two climate readers use different equality rules when deciding which stretch is the base
stands.evidence:
All four quotes are verbatim at the cited lines. schedules.go:1334-1336 `if sv.endtime <= prevEnd {` / `continue` / `}`; :1351 `if math.Abs(flatSlots[i].Temperature-base) < 1e-6 {`; :1359 `for j < len(flatSlots) && math.Abs(flatSlots[j].Temperature-temp) < 1e-6 && flatSlots[j].StartMin == end {`. rawconvert.go:449 `if temp != baseTemp {`; :452 `} else if temp == current.temp {`.

Both sides are live and fed by the SAME datum. REST/WS: internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:477 `dto, err := parseClimateSchedule(ctx, values)` where `values, err := backend.GetParamset(ctx, channelAddr, hmenum.ParamsetKeyMaster)`. Domain/MQTT: internal/central/adapter/schedule_io.go:337-341 `rawSched, err := weekprofile.ParseClimateRawParamset(values)` then `sched, err := weekprofile.RawToClimate(rawSched)`, from the identical GetParamset MASTER map; second production caller at internal/central/adapter/week_profile_io.go:44-48. Neither copy is dead.

Only the winner rule is shared (schedule.IdentifyBaseTemperatureFromSegments, internal/model/schedule/climate.go:288); the period-building consumer is written twice, independently.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, the two functions would return the same (base, periods) for every paramset I traced — as they demonstrably do for the guard's own degenerate case, which uses temp = schedule.DefaultBaseTemperature and yields base 18.0 / no periods on both sides. Changing only that constant to 21.0 flips one side and not the other, which is the control firing. The other falsifier would have been a single shared period-builder called from both files; grep shows none (simplifyWeekday and slotsToClimateWeekday have no common callee beyond the base-temperature helper).
stands.divergence: Paramset: P1_ENDTIME_MONDAY_1..13 = 0 and P1_TEMPERATURE_MONDAY_1..13 = 21.0 (a 13-slot day in which no cell advances past midnight). REST path: every cell hits `sv.endtime <= prevEnd` (0 <= 0) at schedules.go:1334 and is dropped, flatSlots is empty, base = schedule.DefaultBaseTemperature = 18.0, Periods = []. Week-profile path: ParseSlotTime(0) yields EndTime "00:00", filterWeekdaySlots keeps all 13 (none equals maxScheduleTime "24:00"), identifyBaseTemperature also returns 18.0 (all segments have dur 0), but slotsToClimateWeekday then sees temp 21.0 != baseTemp 18.0 and emits exactly one period {StartTime "00:00", EndTime "00:00", Temperature 21.0}. Same paramset: REST reports 0 periods, the domain model reports 1. Established by hand-tracing both functions line by line — I am read-only and did not execute go test. A second, base-level divergence exists for a weekday carrying TEMPERATURE cells with no parsable ENDTIME (EndTime stays ""): weekprofile/slot.go:163-165 maps toMinutes("") = -1 to schedule.ClimateEndOfDayMinutes and reports base 21.0, while schedules.go:1331 drops the cell for !sv.hasEnd and reports base 18.0 — refuting the comment at schedules.go:1311-1313 that the two paths 'cannot report different bases for the same paramset'. Fleet reachability of either input is unverified: I found no CCU capture or simulator fixture carrying a non-advancing or ENDTIME-less climate cell.
stands.guard: A guard EXISTS, contrary to the candidate's empty guard field: TestClimateBaseTemperatureAgreesAcrossReadPaths, internal/central/adapter/schedules_basetemp_parity_test.go:73. It runs the same raw paramset through parseClimateSchedule and through ParseClimateRawParamset+RawToClimate and compares BOTH BaseTemperature and the full period list (schedules_basetemp_parity_test.go:150 `t.Errorf("periods diverge: REST %+v, week-profile %+v", ...)`). Its three cases are two well-formed days and one all-zero-length day. The degenerate case is neutered by its own constant: climateBaseTempParityZeroLength(schedule.DefaultBaseTemperature) picks the one temperature for which the two paths happen to agree. So the guard pins ordinary-day agreement and would catch a future edit to either merge loop on real data; it does not cover the divergence above.
stands.deadCopy: Neither. Both period builders have live production callers (schedules.go:1300 via parseClimateSchedule at :477; rawconvert.go:309 via RawToClimate at schedule_io.go:341 and week_profile_io.go:48).
stands.reason: Confirmed as a duplication with a real diverging input, but three of the candidate's sub-claims do not survive reading. (1) 'no guard' is wrong — the period lists are already pinned across both paths by TestClimateBaseTemperatureAgreesAcrossReadPaths. (2) The 'only merges stretches that are exactly contiguous' difference is vacuous: schedules.go:1338 sets StartMin = prevEnd for every appended segment, so flatSlots[j].StartMin == end holds by construction and the extra conjunct at :1359 can never be the thing that blocks a merge. (3) The 1e-6-vs-exact difference cannot bite on wire data whose temperatures are literal float64s copied from the paramset — the base is never rounded (climate.go:283-286 says so explicitly), so it equals one of the inputs bit-for-bit; it would take two slot temperatures under 1e-6 apart and not equal, which I found no source for. What does bite is the fourth difference the candidate names correctly: schedules.go:1334 drops non-advancing cells and rawconvert.go has no counterpart, so a degenerate slot map yields different period lists and, in the ENDTIME-less case, different bases. Severity low rather than medium: the divergence needs a malformed paramset whose fleet reachability I could not establish, and ordinary-day drift is already caught by the existing parity guard. The cheap remedy is to widen that guard's degenerate case (a temperature other than DefaultBaseTemperature) rather than to merge the two builders.

stands.title: The WEEK_PROFILE channel-type test is spelled as a regexp and as a HasSuffix in the same package
stands.evidence:
Quotes verbatim at the cited lines. schedules.go:132 `var weekProfileChannelPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`WEEK_PROFILE$`)`, consumed at :140 `return weekProfileChannelPattern.MatchString(channelType)`. week_profile_filter.go:384 and :414 both read `if strings.HasSuffix(ch.Type, "WEEK_PROFILE") {`. A repo-wide grep for `WEEK_PROFILE$` and `HasSuffix(.*WEEK_PROFILE` over non-test Go files returns exactly these three spellings — no fourth.

All three are live. isWeekProfileChannel is called from production at schedules.go:168 (inside SchedulesDomain.FindScheduleChannel) and schedules.go:388 (inside scheduleChannelByType, the no-round-trip fleet listing). canonicalScheduleChannel and deviceHasRegisteredScheduleChannel are called from week_profile_filter.go:356 and :342 inside (*DevicePipeline).normalizeClimateWeekProfiles, itself called from production at internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:908. No _test.go-only copy.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false I would have seen either a single predicate called from all three places (the grep would show one function and three call sites, not one regexp plus two inline HasSuffix), or a semantic difference between the two spellings. Neither appeared. For the divergence half specifically: the control is that a string exists which the two spellings classify differently — I looked for one and can rule it out, since Go's regexp defaults to syntax.Perl without the multi-line flag, so an unanchored `$` means end-of-text (\z), making MatchString of `WEEK_PROFILE$` exactly strings.HasSuffix(s, "WEEK_PROFILE") for every input including strings containing newlines.
stands.divergence: None, and none is possible today: the regexp and the HasSuffix are provably equivalent on every input (see negative control). The duplication is of the rule's spelling, not of a behaviour that already differs. The candidate itself claims only that 'the two agree today', which reading confirms.
stands.guard: None. No test constrains the three spellings against one another — grep over *_test.go for WEEK_PROFILE turns up no case that feeds one channel type through both isWeekProfileChannel and either HasSuffix site. If the rule gained an exception in one place only, nothing would fail.
stands.deadCopy: Neither. All three spellings sit on live production paths (schedules.go:168/388 reached from FindScheduleChannel and the schedule-device listing; week_profile_filter.go:342/384 reached from normalizeClimateWeekProfiles via device_pipeline.go:908).
stands.reason: The quote, the triplication and the liveness all check out, so the finding is confirmed as stated — three independent spellings of one rule, in one package, with no guard tying them. Severity stays low because there is nothing broken now and nothing that can break while both spellings carry the same literal: the exposure is entirely the future-drift path the candidate describes, where an exception added to one spelling would let the resolver (FindScheduleChannel) and the normaliser (normalizeClimateWeekProfiles) point at different channels and park a profile where the reader does not look. That is a real but hypothetical consequence, and the fix is one line each: route both HasSuffix sites through isWeekProfileChannel.

stands.title: Two parsers for one stored document: OutputConfig and mirrorConfig read alarm_outputs.config_json with different field sets
stands.evidence: Quote verified verbatim. config.go:68-70 — `// SysvarName is the CCU system variable a sysvar-mirror output` / `// maintains.` / `SysvarName string \`json:"sysvar_name,omitempty"\``. sysvar.go:215-220 — `// mirrorConfig is the sysvar-relevant slice of the output config.` / `type mirrorConfig struct {` / `SysvarName        string \`json:"sysvar_name"\`` / `SysvarAllowDisarm bool   \`json:"sysvar_allow_disarm"\`` / `SysvarExisting    bool   \`json:"sysvar_existing"\`` / `}`. `grep -rn "sysvar_allow_disarm|sysvar_existing|SysvarAllowDisarm|SysvarExisting" --include="*.go"` returns only sysvar.go:196,197,218,219 plus sysvar_test.go — the two keys exist nowhere in OutputConfig. Both parsers live: outputs/manager.go:181 `cfg, err := ParseOutputConfig(row.ConfigJSON)` and alarm/sysvar.go:188 `cfg, err := parseMirrorConfig(row.ConfigJSON)`; the values reach mirrorTarget at sysvar.go:196-197.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, OutputConfig would carry `sysvar_allow_disarm` / `sysvar_existing` struct tags (grep over *.go would hit config.go), or mirrorConfig would be an alias/embed of OutputConfig. Neither: the grep hits only sysvar.go, and mirrorConfig is a standalone three-field struct.
stands.reason: The structural claim is verified — one stored document, two declared schemas, and the two security-relevant keys live only in the narrower one. The claimed damage, however, is NOT realizable today: the REST write path does not re-encode through OutputConfig. It parses for validation only (internal/north/rest/handlers/alarm_config.go:374 `ocfg, err := outputs.ParseOutputConfig(string(in[i].Config))`, used at :382 solely to reject an empty SysvarName) and then stores the caller's bytes verbatim (:425 `ConfigJSON: string(o.Config)`). The SPA likewise patches a raw record (assets/ui/src/routes/alarm/AlarmOutputs.svelte:301-312 `const cfg: Record<string, unknown> = { ...(o.config ?? {}) };`, writing sysvar_allow_disarm at :773-774 and sysvar_existing at :503), so the keys survive a round trip end to end. That is why I rate this low rather than medium. The escalation condition is concrete and already precedented in the same file: the sibling sensor path DOES re-encode a partial struct — alarm_config.go:270-278 `cfg.AlwaysOn = true` / `patched, err := json.Marshal(cfg)` / `in[i].Config = patched`. The first analogous patch on the output path would silently drop the disarm opt-in.
stands.divergence: Concrete diverging input: a stored document `{"sysvar_name":"AlarmZoneEG","sysvar_allow_disarm":true,"sysvar_existing":true}`. mirrorConfig reads allowDisarm=true, existing=true (sysvar.go:196-197); OutputConfig reads only SysvarName="AlarmZoneEG" and discards the other two entirely — `json.Unmarshal` into OutputConfig leaves no field holding them, so re-marshalling that value yields `{"sysvar_name":"AlarmZoneEG"}`, an output that no longer permits a third-party disarm and no longer marks the variable operator-owned.
stands.guard: None. No test asserts that OutputConfig and mirrorConfig cover the same key set, and no round-trip test re-encodes an output config.
stands.deadCopy: Neither — both parsers have production callers (outputs/manager.go:181, alarm/sysvar.go:188).

Instead both spell the literal `180 * time.Second`, and there is no shared symbol — while the neighbouring optical path demonstrates that the codebase's own convention is a named constant.
stands.reason: Duplication verified, but the second copy is unreachable in production, which is why I hold this at low rather than promoting it. stands.divergence: None. Both literals are 180 s, and no production input reaches config.go:121 at all, so no input can distinguish them.
stands.guard: Partial and one-sided: internal/alarm/outputs/manager_firecycle_test.go:76 `if calls[0].Cfg.Duration != 180*time.Second {` pins the effective duration, but the harness supplies it explicitly (harness_test.go:90 `DefaultSirenDuration: 180 * time.Second`), so the test passes through neither fallback. No test exercises acousticDuration with engineDefault <= 0, and none compares the two constants.
stands.deadCopy: internal/alarm/outputs/config.go:120-122 — the `if d <= 0 { d = 180 * time.Second }` branch has no production caller that can reach it, since every one of the four acousticDuration call sites passes m.defaultSiren, which the constructor guarantees is > 0.

stands.title: PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE is a raw string in the candidate filter and an hmenum constant in the reset mapping
stands.evidence: Quote verified verbatim at both sites. internal/alarm/sensor_candidates.go:159-161 reads `if parameter != hmenum.ParameterState && parameter != hmenum.ParameterMotion &&` / `\t\tparameter != "PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE" {` / `\t\treturn SensorCandidate{}, false` — the third comparison is a bare literal while its two neighbours on the same expression use hmenum constants. internal/alarm/motionreset.go:41-43 reads `case hmenum.ParameterPresenceDetectionState:` / `\treturn hmenum.ParameterResetPresence, true`. pkg/hmenum/parameter.go:126 declares `ParameterPresenceDetectionState        Parameter = "PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE"`. Both sites are live in production, not test-only: sensorCandidateFor is called from internal/alarm/sensor_candidates.go:98 inside `func (s *Service) SensorCandidates` (:90), which is the AlarmPanel method served at internal/north/rest/router.go:1058 `pr.Get("/alarm/sensor-candidates", handlers.ListAlarmSensorCandidates(d.Alarm, d.Labels))` via internal/north/rest/handlers/alarm_sensor_candidates.go:38. resetParameterFor is called from internal/alarm/motionreset.go:72 inside motionResetter.action, and the resetter is wired at internal/alarm/service.go:793 `MotionReset:         newMotionResetter(deps.Registry)` into engine.MotionResetPort (internal/alarm/engine/engine.go:212). Grep for the whole repo shows exactly these two spellings of the datum inside internal/alarm (`grep -rn "PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE\|ParameterPresenceDetectionState" --include="*.go" .`): the literal at sensor_candidates.go:160 and a doc comment at motionreset.go:34, the constant at motionreset.go:42.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, sensor_candidates.go:160 would have read `parameter != hmenum.ParameterPresenceDetectionState`, matching the two constant comparisons on line 159 of the same `if`; I read line 160 directly and it carries the quoted string literal. Had either side been dead, the caller grep would have returned only `_test.go` hits — instead it returned router.go:1058 for the filter and service.go:793 for the reset mapping.
stands.reason: One wire datum — the parameter name of a presence detector's latching state — is written twice inside one package, once as an hmenum constant and once as a quoted literal, and both copies are on live production paths (picker enrollment vs. the reset action lookup). No guard couples them: `grep -rn -i "presence" internal/alarm/*_test.go` returns only internal/alarm/motionreset_test.go:123-124, which drive resetParameterFor through the constant; no test in internal/alarm exercises sensorCandidateFor with PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE at all, so that branch of the filter is uncovered and a drift would be silent in both directions. One correction to the candidate's damage text: renaming the Go *identifier* diverges nothing (the literal does not reference it); the drift needs a change to the constant's *value*, after which motionreset.go follows and sensor_candidates.go keeps matching the old wire name — the presence detector then no longer appears in the enrollment picker. Severity low is right: the value is the CCU's wire parameter name, so it changes only if the firmware name changes, and the failure is a missing picker entry rather than a wrong alarm decision.
stands.divergence: None today: the literal at sensor_candidates.go:160 and the constant value at pkg/hmenum/parameter.go:126 are byte-identical ("PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE"), and `parameter` is typed hmenum.Parameter so the untyped-constant comparison is well-formed. The two copies agree on every input; the finding is the uncoupled duplication, not a present disagreement.
stands.deadCopy: Neither. Both copies have production callers (router.go:1058 → sensor_candidates.go:98; service.go:793 → motionreset.go:72).
stands.guard: None. No test links the picker filter to the reset mapping, and no test in internal/alarm feeds PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE to sensorCandidateFor (internal/alarm/sensor_candidates_test.go has no presence case); motionreset_test.go:123-124 covers only the reset side, through the constant.

stands.title: alarm_codes row decoding exists twice in one file with different failure semantics
stands.evidence: Both quotes verified verbatim (facade.go:409-417 inside pinCandidates, defined facade.go:393; facade.go:489-497 inside parseRow, defined facade.go:489). Both are live: pinCandidates is called from facade.go:190 (Validate), facade.go:259 (MatchDuress) and facade.go:331; parseRow from facade.go:346 inside Rows(), which is called from internal/alarm/service.go:317 and service.go:377. The failure semantics differ exactly as claimed: facade.go:412 `f.log.Error("alarm code perms_json malformed, skipping", ...)` + `continue` versus facade.go:492 `return Row{}, fmt.Errorf("perms_json: %w", err)`, the latter caught at facade.go:347-350 as `f.log.Error("alarm code row malformed, skipping", ...)` + `continue`.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, one of the two blocks would have delegated to the other (as both already delegate the zones half to parseZones at facade.go:417 and facade.go:496) — I would have seen a single `json.Unmarshal([]byte(r.PermsJSON), &perms)` in the file. `grep -n PermsJSON internal/alarm/codes/facade.go` returns it at both 410-411 and 490-491, two independent unmarshals.
stands.reason: Confirmed, but narrower than stated: the zones half of the candidate's knowledge statement is already single-sourced — both sites call `parseZones` (facade.go:513), which carries the "empty string == \"[]\" == every zone" rule in one place. Only the three-line perms_json decode is genuinely duplicated. Severity low: the two paths already diverge on binding_json today and that divergence is arguably correct, so the exposure is a future perms-shaped field being added to one projection and not the other.
stands.divergence: A concrete input where the two already disagree: an enabled pin-kind row with a valid perms_json and hash but `binding_json = "{"` (truncated JSON). parseRow reaches facade.go:501-503 and returns `Row{}, fmt.Errorf("binding_json: %w", err)`, so Rows() logs "alarm code row malformed, skipping" and omits the row entirely from the hardware-intent-routing projection (internal/alarm/service.go:317). pinCandidates never touches r.BindingJSON at all (facade.go:398-430 reads only Kind, Enabled, ValidFromMS, ValidUntilMS, PermsJSON, ZonesJSON, ID, Name, Hash, Duress), so the same row is still returned as a candidate and the PIN still authenticates a disarm. Same row, same store: authenticates on one path, invisible on the other.
stands.deadCopy: neither — pinCandidates is reached from Validate/MatchDuress, parseRow from Rows()
stands.guard: none. No test compares the two projections over the same store row; the codes tests exercise Validate and Rows independently.
