Consumed once ChannelParamsetRules gets exposed` / `// through Registry — F11 P1-10 follow-up.` / `//nolint:unused // see comment above`). Liveness by grep over *.go: UnIgnoreWildcard has exactly one production use, internal/store/visibility/candidate.go:226 `return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s@%s:%s", parameter, paramset, model, UnIgnoreWildcard)` (plus a doc reference in internal/central/queryfacade.go:344). unIgnoreWildcard is live at parser.go:161, parser.go:178, decider.go:665, decider.go:669. channelNoUnknown is live at registry.go:88, model_validator.go:102, decider.go:544, decider.go:580. anyChannelNo has ZERO references outside its own declaration and two comments (rule_containers.go:27, :39) — no production caller and no test caller; grep for `anyChannelNo` in *_test.go returns nothing. Its whole container is equally unbuilt in production: `NewChannelParamsetRules` / `NewModelRules` are constructed only inside rule_containers.go itself (:94, :143) and from model_rules_test.go:276, :323. No test anywhere references either constant by name (grep for UnIgnoreWildcard|unIgnoreWildcard|anyChannelNo in *_test.go: no matches), so nothing pins the two "all" literals to each other.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false I would have seen one of: a single `"all"` const declaration in the package (the grep for `"all"` in internal/store/visibility/*.go returned exactly two const lines, un_ignore.go:11 and parser.go:28); `anyChannelNo` appearing at a call site rather than only in its own declaration and comments; or a test asserting `UnIgnoreWildcard == unIgnoreWildcard`. None of those appeared.
stands.divergence: None today — both "all" literals are byte-identical and both sentinels are -1, so no input separates them at HEAD. I also checked whether a future rename could separate them and could not construct one for the channel position: the parser classifies ANY non-numeric channel token as a wildcard (parser.go:150-156 `default: channelNo = nil; channelNoIsWildcard = true`), so if UnIgnoreWildcard became "any" while the parser's stayed "all", `WildcardPattern("LOW_BAT", VALUES, "HmIP-eTRV-2")` = "LOW_BAT:VALUES@HmIP-eTRV-2:any" still parses with Err=="" and still matches at decider.go:661 (Point 2, `eModelL == modelL && e.ChannelNoIsWildcard`). The only position where the constant's exact value is load-bearing is the MODEL field (parser.go:161, :178; decider.go:665, :669), and the pattern builder never emits a wildcard there — candidate.go:176 passes the concrete model.
stands.deadCopy: internal/store/visibility/rule_containers.go:31 `anyChannelNo` — no production caller and no test caller; the ChannelParamsetRules/ModelRules containers it belongs to are themselves constructed only from model_rules_test.go. channelNoUnknown (decider.go:109) is the live -1.
stands.guard: None. The candidate names TestPatternsRoundTripThroughTheParser (internal/store/visibility/candidate_test.go:254) as the crossing guard; I read it and that claim does not hold. It asserts only `parsed.Entry == nil || parsed.Err != ""` for each pattern from `c.Patterns()`. A realistic rename of UnIgnoreWildcard ("any", "*") leaves the parse successful for the reason above, so the test stays green. It would bite only if the new token contained ':' or '@' (regex no longer matches) or were all-digits (parsed as a concrete channel number). No test references either wildcard constant by name, and none references anyChannelNo.
stands.reason: The factual claim is confirmed: four constants, two identical pairs, all in package internal/store/visibility, all quotes accurate. Severity stays low, but for different reasons than the candidate gives. (1) The "all" pair is live-on-both-sides yet the drift damage the candidate describes — "un-ignore lines the daemon builds but cannot parse" — is not reachable, because the exported constant is only ever emitted into the channel field, where the parser accepts any non-numeric token as a wildcard; the named guard therefore does not protect the round trip either. It is a real deduplication (one exported constant used exactly once, inside the package that already holds the unexported one), not a latent break. (2) The -1 pair is not two live copies: anyChannelNo is dead, carrying a //nolint:unused and a follow-up note, inside a container pair (ChannelParamsetRules, ModelRules) that no production code constructs. That is the stronger half of the finding — a tested-but-unused copy of a sentinel whose live twin lives one file away — and it is what a fix should address first, by deleting the dead constant/container or wiring it, not by unifying two constants that cannot currently disagree in effect.

stands.title: Two identical bool-to-INTEGER helpers and two identical row-scanner interfaces in one package
stands.evidence:
All four quotes verified verbatim, all four in one package (`package sqlite`, confirmed at alarm_incidents.go:5, centrals_store.go:15, alarm_incident_sources.go:25, security_faults.go:4).

Helpers, byte-identical bodies:
- internal/store/sqlite/alarm_incidents.go:205-212 `// boolToInt maps a Go bool onto the 0/1 INTEGER convention used by` / `// the alarm tables.` / `func boolToInt(b bool) int {` / `\tif b {` / `\t\treturn 1` / `\t}` / `\treturn 0` / `}`
- internal/store/sqlite/centrals_store.go:307-312 `func boolInt(b bool) int {` / `\tif b {` / `\t\treturn 1` / `\t}` / `\treturn 0` / `}` (no doc comment)

Interfaces, identical single-method sets:
- internal/store/sqlite/centrals_store.go:257-261 `// scannable is implemented by both *sql.Row and *sql.Rows so the` / `// scanner is shared between Get and List.` / `type scannable interface {` / `\tScan(dest ...any) error` / `}`
- internal/store/sqlite/alarm_incident_sources.go:147-150 `// rowScanner is satisfied by both *sql.Row and *sql.Rows.` / `type rowScanner interface {` / `\tScan(dest ...any) error` / `}`

Liveness — every one of the four has production (non-_test.go) callers:
- boolToInt: 8 call sites in 6 production files — alarm_journal.go:66, recording_overrides.go:88, channel_flags.go:93, security_sources.go:54, alarm_codes.go:66 and :67, alarm_incidents.go:60.
- boolInt: 2 call sites, both production, both inside its own file — centrals_store.go:179 `boolInt(r.TLS), boolInt(r.TLSInsecureSkipVerify), r.PrimaryInterface,` and :180 `... string(behJSON), boolInt(r.Enabled),`.
- scannable: 9 production signatures (alarm_journal.go:149, alarm_sensors.go:146, areas.go:170, alarm_codes.go:119, alarm_zones.go:130, alarm_incidents.go:220, alarm_state.go:111, alarm_outputs.go:147, centrals_store.go:263), reached from production at centrals_store.go:228 and :244.
- rowScanner: 2 production signatures — alarm_incident_sources.go:152 `func scanAlarmIncidentSource(sc rowScanner)` (called at :77 and :111) and security_faults.go:160 `func scanSecurityFault(sc rowScanner)` (called at :116 and :151).

Guard: none. `grep -rn --include='*_test.go' -E "boolInt|boolToInt|scannable|rowScanner" .` returns exactly one hit, and it is not a reference to any of these identifiers: tests/e2e/api_ws_test.go:89 `// command name so log output stays scannable in CI.` — the English word in a comment. `.golangci.yaml` has no `dupl` and no `goconst` entry (grep -i for both returned nothing), so the linter would not flag the duplication either.
stands.negativeControl: Quote check: had the candidate's quotes been stale or invented, `sed -n` at the cited lines would have shown different text — a differing body (a distinct sentinel, an early return, an inverted branch) or a method set that is not `Scan(dest ...any) error`; both files instead matched character for character. Liveness check: had either copy been dead, the grep for its identifier would have returned only its own definition line, or only hits in _test.go files; `boolInt(` instead returned two non-test call sites (centrals_store.go:179, :180) and `rowScanner` two non-test scan functions with four non-test callers. Guard check: had a guard existed, the _test.go grep would have named a test referencing one of the four identifiers, or .golangci.yaml would have carried a `dupl` entry; both came back empty apart from the unrelated English word.
stands.reason: The structural claim is exactly as stated and both pairs are live, so this is confirmed as duplication — but it is duplication with no present divergence, and that bounds the severity. `boolToInt` and `boolInt` are total functions over `bool`: the domain has two elements, and the two copies return the same value for each (true -> 1, false -> 0), so no diverging input exists today and none can be constructed. The two interfaces are structurally identical, so under Go's structural typing every type satisfying one satisfies the other; there is no input that distinguishes them either. The damage is therefore entirely prospective, and the bundle's own framing of it is the accurate one: with no guard and no linter rule, an edit to one 0/1 encoding leaves the other untouched, and the two would then write different encodings into two families of tables in the same database file. The asymmetry says which copy is the redundant one: `boolInt` has two callers, both inside its own file, against `boolToInt`'s eight across six files; `rowScanner` has two users against `scannable`'s nine. Note also that the caller set refutes half of `boolToInt`'s own doc comment at alarm_incidents.go:205-206 ("the 0/1 INTEGER convention used by the alarm tables") — three of its production callers are not alarm tables: recording_overrides.go:88, channel_flags.go:93, security_sources.go:54. That is a separate comment-claim defect, adjacent to this candidate and not part of it.
stands.divergence: None found, and none is constructible. Both helpers are total over `bool`: true -> 1 and false -> 0 on both sides, so the two-element domain is exhausted with no disagreement. The two interfaces declare the same method set, so no type distinguishes them. The candidate's damage is prospective drift, not a present divergence.
stands.deadCopy: Neither — all four have production callers (boolInt at centrals_store.go:179 and :180; rowScanner via scanAlarmIncidentSource called at alarm_incident_sources.go:77 and :111, and scanSecurityFault called at security_faults.go:116 and :151). The narrower copy of each pair is the deletion candidate: boolInt (2 callers, all in its own file) against boolToInt (8 across 6 files), and rowScanner (2 users) against scannable (9).
stands.guard: None. No test in the repo references boolToInt, boolInt, scannable or rowScanner (the sole _test.go grep hit, tests/e2e/api_ws_test.go:89, is the English word "scannable" in a comment), and .golangci.yaml enables neither `dupl` nor `goconst`. Nothing would go red if the two encodings drifted apart.

stands.title: The recovery TCP probe re-derives an interface port as a bare literal instead of using the port table
stands.evidence:
Quotes verified verbatim. ccu_wiring.go:978-983: `// Resolve the CCU's TCP address from the XML-RPC URL so the` / `// TCP-probe stage can dial without knowing the per-interface port.` / `ccuTCPAddr := cc.Host + ":2010" // fallback: CCU homematic2 port` / `if parsed, parseErr := neturl.Parse(url); parseErr == nil && parsed.Host != "" {` / `ccuTCPAddr = parsed.Host // already "host:port"`. The value is consumed live at ccu_wiring.go:990 inside RecoveryStageDeps.TCPProbe: `conn, dialErr := (&net.Dialer{}).DialContext(ctx, "tcp", ccuTCPAddrCaptured)`, installed under `if unit.Recovery != nil` in the per-interface wiring path.

Site B verified: pkg/hmenum/ports.go:34-41 `var DetectionPorts = map[Interface]DetectionPort{` / `InterfaceBidCosRF: {Plain: 2001, TLS: 42001},` / `InterfaceBidCosWired: {Plain: 2000, TLS: 42000},` / `InterfaceHmIPRF: {Plain: 2010, TLS: 42010},` / `InterfaceVirtualDevices: {Plain: 9292, TLS: 49292},`. It is live: ccu_wiring.go:1548 `ports, ok := hmenum.DetectionPorts[iface]` inside interfaceURL, the composer that produces the very `url` the probe parses. So 2010 is held in two places, and the literal follows neither the interface, the TLS variant, nor interfacePortOverride.

Reachability of the fallback branch — the point the candidate left conditional — is real. interfaceURL (ccu_wiring.go:1579-1581) interpolates an operator-supplied remote_path: `if ov := interfaceRemotePathOverride(cc, iface); ov != "" { path = ov }`. That value is validated only by config.go:141 validateRemotePath, whose full reject list is config.go:135 `var remotePathForbidden = []string{"://", "?", "#", ".."}` plus the leading-"/", bare-"/" and "//" checks. A path such as `/RPC%zz` passes every one of them, and I measured net/url on the resulting URL (standalone program, Go stdlib, outside the repo):
  "http://ccu.local:2001/RPC%zz" -> ERR parse "http://ccu.local:2001/RPC%zz": invalid URL escape "%zz"
  "http://ccu.local:2001/RPC2"   -> Host="ccu.local:2001"
So parseErr != nil and the probe falls back to `cc.Host + ":2010"`.
stands.negativeControl: Two independent controls. (1) If the fallback were unreachable, no config-accepted input could make url.Parse fail — I ran the parse for the well-formed case in the same program and it returned Host="ccu.local:2001" (no error), so the measurement distinguishes the two branches rather than always reporting an error. (2) If validateRemotePath rejected "%", the branch would be dead and the verdict would be "dead defensive code" instead; the reject list at config.go:135 is exactly {"://", "?", "#", ".."} and contains no percent check, which I read from the source rather than assumed.
stands.reason: A genuine duplication: 2010 is hmenum.DetectionPorts[InterfaceHmIPRF].Plain, restated as a literal in the recovery wiring, with a reachable path that uses it. Severity is low rather than medium, for two measured reasons. First, the drift damage is near-theoretical — DetectionPorts holds fixed eQ-3 service ports that will not change. Second, the reachable input (a remote_path with a bad percent-escape) already breaks the interface's own XML-RPC client, which builds requests from the same unparseable URL, so the interface is down regardless; the literal only makes the recovery pipeline's TCP evidence describe the wrong service (dials the HmIP-RF port while diagnosing, e.g., BidCos-RF on 2001). That is a misleading-diagnostic defect, not an outage cause.
stands.divergence: Central `host: ccu.local`, interface BidCos-RF (DetectionPorts plain 2001) with `remote_path: /RPC%zz`. interfaceURL returns "http://ccu.local:2001/RPC%zz"; url.Parse returns the error `invalid URL escape "%zz"` (measured), so ccuTCPAddr stays at the literal and the TCP-probe stage dials ccu.local:2010 — the HmIP-RF port — instead of the interface's own 2001. On a CCU without HmIP the dial always fails and the pipeline never leaves TCP_CHECKING; with HmIP present it always succeeds and the pipeline advances on evidence about a different service. Same construction with `cc.TLS: true` dials plain 2010 rather than the table's TLS 42010.
stands.deadCopy: Neither is dead. The literal at ccu_wiring.go:980 feeds the live TCPProbe closure at :990; DetectionPorts is read at ccu_wiring.go:1548 by interfaceURL on every interface bring-up.
stands.guard: None. `grep -rn "ccuTCPAddr|TCPProbe|2010" --include="*_test.go"` finds only tests/contract/connection_recovery_contract_test.go:402, which supplies its own TCPProbe stub and never exercises the address derivation, and adapter_multi_unit_test.go:7451-7458, which asserts interfaceURL honours a :32010 port override but says nothing about ccuTCPAddr. No test would fail if DetectionPorts and the literal drifted apart.

stands.title: Warm-boot hydration re-inserts persisted paramsets with Put, so a patch-table change is not re-applied to the stored rows
stands.evidence: Quote verified verbatim at descriptor_persistence.go:245-248: `// Put, not Add: rows were persisted post-normalisation and` / `// post-patching, so re-applying patches here would double-patch.` / `unit.ParamsetReg.Put(iface, rec.ChannelAddress, rec.ParamsetKey, rec.Paramset)`. Write side confirmed at device_pipeline.go:1951 `reg.ApplyPatches(ch.Device().Model, ch.Address, key, paramset)` followed by :1960 `reg.Put(hmtypes.ParseWireInterfaceID(interfaceID), ch.Address, key, paramset)` (the candidate cited 1946-1956; ApplyPatches is at 1951 and the Put at 1960, so the quoted range is one line short of the Put — the code says what was claimed). Registry semantics, paramset.go:87-118: `Add` does `normalised := hmproto.NormalizeParamset(ps)` then `r.patchRegistry.ApplyParamset(deviceType, channelAddress, psKey, normalised)`; `Put` does `normalised := hmproto.NormalizeParamset(ps)` and stores it with no patch step, doc comment `// For new call sites prefer Add() which also applies patches.` Put cannot patch — it takes no deviceType.
stands.negativeControl: Had the comment's premise been false I would have found a production call site persisting an unpatched paramset. `grep -rn` over internal/ and cmd/ (tests excluded) for ParamsetReg/paramsets Put and Add returned exactly three sites: device_pipeline.go:1960 (Put, immediately after ApplyPatches at :1951), coordinators/device.go:1031 `c.paramsets.Add(iface, channelAddress, key, ps, deviceModel)` (Add patches), and descriptor_persistence.go:247 (hydration itself). Both writers patch, so the sink at paramset.go:100-103 / :114-117 only ever persists patched maps — the premise holds and the check would have reported the opposite had it not.
stands.reason: Confirmed as a cache-invalidation gap, not as a wrong claim: the comment's premise is verified true today. The real, bounded defect is that the SQLite row freezes the patch table's output — no re-patch happens on hydration, so after a patch-table edit the hydrated registry serves the previous release's values until that channel is re-pulled. The window is small: hydrateParamset (device_pipeline.go:1921-1930) always calls `b.GetParamsetDescription` on the wire (CcuBackend.GetParamsetDescription, backends/ccu.go:174-178, has no cache tier), and it runs for every channel and device root on each ingest (device_pipeline.go:1865, :1902-1903), so a normal boot rewrites every row. The stale data survives only until that pull, or indefinitely for a channel the CCU no longer answers for — which is exactly what the warm-boot readers (CheckAndCreateDevicesFromCache at coordinators/device.go:834, the UI-schema consumers named at descriptor_persistence.go:198-201) read. One sub-claim of the candidate is wrong and I am flagging it: hydration is not 'no normalisation' — Put normalises (paramset.go:106-108 `// Paramset is normalised before storage so hashes computed after Put stay stable.`). Only the patching is skipped.
stands.guard: None. No test asserts that a patch-table change invalidates or rewrites persisted paramset rows, and none pins that hydration's Put path is fed only by patched writers — the invariant rests entirely on the two call sites staying patched.
stands.divergence: None found today. Both production writers into the registry patch before the sink sees the map (device_pipeline.go:1951→1960, coordinators/device.go:1031), so no currently reachable input makes the stored row differ from what Add would have produced. The disagreement only materialises after a patch-table edit: e.g. the HM-CC-VG-1 SET_TEMPERATURE case named at device_pipeline.go:1946-1949 (wire MIN/MAX 5.0/30.0 → patched 4.5/30.5) — if that patch were changed to different bounds, a hydrated row written by the previous release would keep serving 4.5/30.5 to every reader until the next live pull for that channel.
stands.deadCopy: Neither. descriptor_persistence.go:247 runs from WireDescriptorPersistence (descriptor_persistence.go:202) and device_pipeline.go:1960 from hydrateChannel/hydrateDeviceRoot; both are production paths.

stands.title: PublishInitialSnapshot's doc says MASTER values are deliberately skipped; the pass it heads publishes them, and a comment 60 lines down describes the retained MASTER paramsets that reached the broker
stands.evidence: Both quotes verified verbatim at the cited lines. The doc, on PublishInitialSnapshot, eventbridge.go:673-676: `// MASTER-paramset values are deliberately skipped: they are // configuration parameters, not runtime state, and are surfaced // through the Config UI / REST paramset endpoints instead of the // MQTT broker.`, immediately above :677 `func (b *EventBridge) PublishInitialSnapshot(ctx context.Context) {`. The code that pass runs: :688 `for _, u := range b.registry.List() { b.publishCentralSnapshot(ctx, u) }` -> :724 `func (b *EventBridge) publishCentralSnapshot(ctx context.Context, u *central.Unit)` -> publishDeviceSnapshot at :836, whose channel loop reads :875-886 `// ADR 0011 phase 1c — also publish MASTER paramset. // MASTER values are seeded once via OnWireValue and // don't generate normal value-change bus events; the // initial-snapshot pass synthesises them so the // \`channels/<ch>/master/<param>/state\` topics actually // contain something.` and :887-888 `for _, dp := range ch.MasterDataPoints() {` / `b.registerAndLoadDP(ctx, centralName, ifaceID, d, ch, channelNo, dp, hmenum.ParamsetKeyMaster)`. A third comment in the same file settles it as observed behaviour, not theory — eventbridge.go:725-734, the readiness gate: `// A central whose readiness-gated bring-up has not latched ready is // still hydrating: its devices already sit in the ModelRegistry with // seeded values, but the visibility passes at the end of finishIngest // have not run yet, so every suppressed parameter still reads // Visible() == true. Snapshotting that window published entire // MASTER paramsets (75-slot week programs, router tables) retained to // the broker. Skip the central; ...` followed by :734 `if !u.IsSouthboundReady() {`. That comment only makes sense if MASTER is published on this pass.
stands.negativeControl: Had MASTER genuinely been skipped, the channel loop in publishDeviceSnapshot would iterate `ch.DataPoints()` alone. The check: `grep -n "MasterDataPoints()" internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go` — it returns :887, inside publishDeviceSnapshot, on the path PublishInitialSnapshot :688 -> publishCentralSnapshot :724 -> publishDeviceSnapshot :836, plus :497 (name restamping, unrelated). And the :725-733 readiness comment would have no reason to name 'entire MASTER paramsets ... retained to the broker' as the thing it prevents.
stands.divergence: Any channel with at least one MASTER data point that survives the MASTER visibility whitelist. A boot snapshot of such a device publishes retained `channels/<ch>/master/<param>/state` topics per :880-882, which the doc at :673-676 says are surfaced 'through the Config UI / REST paramset endpoints instead of the MQTT broker'. The observed extreme is named in the code itself at :730-731: entire 75-slot week programs and router tables retained on the broker during the pre-ready window, which is what the :734 gate exists to prevent.
stands.deadCopy: Neither side is dead code — the contradiction is doc-versus-code, and both PublishInitialSnapshot (the doc's subject) and the MASTER loop at :887 are on the same live boot path. The dead item is the doc sentence itself.
stands.guard: None, and none is possible for a prose claim — comment claims are outside the mechanical guards by design (CLAUDE.md routes them to the pre-release comment-claims sweep). No test asserts either that MASTER reaches the broker or that it does not.
stands.reason: Confirmed as a comment-claims defect: the doc heading the function states the opposite of what the function does, and a second comment in the same file describes the retained MASTER traffic the first denies. Severity low because nothing breaks at runtime — the volume is held down by the MASTER default-deny visibility whitelist and the :734 readiness gate. The cost is a reader's or a later change's wrong model of the MQTT boundary, and the candidate's framing of that cost is accurate: a whitelist edit today widens the broker surface with nothing in the doc marking it as a boundary change.

stands.title: Channel-address composition and parsing are restated in four places in the partition instead of going through one address grammar
stands.evidence: Every cited quote is verbatim. event_source_feed.go:72 `channelAddr := e.DeviceAddress + ":" + strconv.Itoa(e.ChannelNo)`. eventbridge.go:2623 `func parseChannel(channelAddress string) (addr string, number int) {` with `idx := strings.LastIndexByte(channelAddress, ':')`, `if idx < 0 { return channelAddress, 0 }`, `if n, err := strconv.Atoi(channelAddress[idx+1:]); err == nil { number = n }`, `return channelAddress, number`. eventbridge.go:2634 `func deviceAddrAndChannel(channelAddress string) (deviceAddr string, channel int) {` — identical body, first return `deviceAddr = channelAddress[:idx]`. Composers: eventbridge.go:3436 `chAddr := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", address, channelNo)`; mqtt_sink.go:325/:414/:456 `chAddr := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", deviceAddress, channel)`. The claim is understated in one respect: a canonical grammar already exists and is unused here — pkg/hmtypes/address.go:43 `func ChannelAddress(deviceAddress string, channelNo int) string` and :84 `func SplitChannelAddress(address string) (deviceAddress string, channelNo int, ok bool)`, with 36 production call sites repo-wide (internal/north/mqtt/discovery_aggregate.go:449, internal/model/custom/*/topology.go, internal/alarm/*, internal/history/recorder.go:355). Inside internal/central/adapter it is used exactly once in production, device_reloader.go:99 `deviceAddr := hmtypes.DeviceAddress(channelAddress)`, while eventbridge.go:1346/:1394/:1519 and callback_handlers.go:864 call the local deviceAddrAndChannel for the same job. Two more copies of the same parse sit in the partition beyond the four named: schedule_query_adapter.go:128 `func splitChannelAddress(channelAddress string) (device string, channelIdx int)` (hand-rolled digit scan) and device_pipeline.go:2284 `func splitChannel(addr string) (int, bool)`; a fifth lives one package over at internal/central/coordinators/event.go:300. Both eventbridge copies are live: parseChannel has 9 production callers (eventbridge.go:874, 1114, 1142, 1184, 1393, 1518, 2517, 2587, 2880, 3109, 3560), deviceAddrAndChannel 4 (eventbridge.go:1346, 1394, 1519, callback_handlers.go:864). Neither is a dead copy.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, the cited lines would have called one shared helper. Concretely: `grep -rn 'hmtypes.ChannelAddress(|hmtypes.SplitChannelAddress(|hmtypes.ChannelNo(|hmtypes.DeviceAddress(' internal/central/adapter/` would have returned hits at eventbridge.go:2623/2634/3436 and mqtt_sink.go:325/414/456. It returns 3 hits in the whole package, only one of them production (device_reloader.go:99); the other two are auto_refresh_cache_test.go:56 and :101 — the test composes addresses with the canonical helper while production next to it composes them by hand.
stands.reason: The duplication is real and the partition bypasses an existing canonical grammar, so the finding stands. But the candidate's damage narrative does not: I could not reach the 'silently re-targeted at channel 0' failure on any live input. Device.Channels() (internal/model/device/device.go:579) walks only d.channels, and the device-root pseudo-channel is stored in d.rootChannel (EnsureRootChannel, device.go:538-552) and never inserted into that map — so the parseChannel(ch.Address) sites at eventbridge.go:874/1114/2880/3109 never see a colon-less address. And for every ingested channel ch.Number is itself derived by the same last-colon parse (device_pipeline.go:459 `chNum := channelNumber(dd.Address)` → device_pipeline.go:2284 splitChannel), so parseChannel(ch.Address) == ch.Number by construction. The exposure is drift, not a present bug, and it is unguarded across the package boundary.
stands.divergence: The copies disagree today on defined inputs, though I could not show either input reaching the daemon, so treat the reachability as unproven. (1) No-colon / non-numeric suffix: hmtypes.SplitChannelAddress("ABC123") returns ("ABC123", -1, false) — the -1 sentinel plus an explicit rejection flag (address.go:86-88); eventbridge.go:2634 deviceAddrAndChannel("ABC123") returns ("ABC123", 0) with no way to signal rejection. Same split for "ABC123:" and "ABC123:None" (address.go:90 special-cases the literal "None"; the local copy just lets Atoi fail and keeps 0). (2) First vs last colon: hmtypes.DeviceAddress (address.go:71, strings.Cut) and internal/central/coordinators/event.go:300 splitChannelAddress (strings.Cut) take the FIRST colon; eventbridge.go:2634, mqtt_sink.go:71/:162, schedule_query_adapter.go:128 and device_pipeline.go:2285 take the LAST. Input "ABC123:1:2" → hmtypes.DeviceAddress "ABC123" vs deviceAddrAndChannel ("ABC123:1", 2). Both spellings are live in internal/central/adapter (device_reloader.go:99 vs eventbridge.go:1346). (3) Composition of the device-root sentinel: hmtypes.ChannelAddress("ABC123", -1) returns "ABC123" (address.go:44-45) and adapter/schedules.go:1178 scheduleChannelAddress does the same for device.ChannelNumberDevice (= -1, internal/model/device/channel.go:49); eventbridge.go:3436 and event_source_feed.go:72 would emit "ABC123:-1" for the same input.
stands.deadCopy: none — parseChannel (9 production callers) and deviceAddrAndChannel (4, incl. callback_handlers.go:864) are both live, and the canonical pkg/hmtypes helpers have 36 production callers elsewhere in the repo.
stands.guard: internal/central/adapter/eventbridge_helpers_test.go:22-73 pins both local copies, including the malformed cases (`parseChannel("DEV:abc")` want n=0, `deviceAddrAndChannel("DEV001")` want (DEV001, 0)). It pins the local behaviour only — nothing compares either copy against pkg/hmtypes.SplitChannelAddress / ChannelAddress, so the two grammars can drift apart with every test green. No guard exists for that.

stands.title: The event-source feed records a trigger only for one concrete model type, so any other implementation silently loses the fire lifecycle
stands.evidence: Quote verified verbatim at internal/central/adapter/event_source_feed.go:77-86: `// Only concrete sources carry the fire lifecycle; any other` / `// implementation of the interface has no timestamp to record.` / `src, ok := attached.(*modevent.Source)` / `if !ok {` / `return` / `}` … `src.Fire(e.Value.Unwrap())`. The resolution above it is through the interface: queryfacade.go:186 `func (q *QueryFacade) GetEventGroup(channelAddress string, p hmenum.Parameter) device.AttachableEvent`, and the interface itself is two methods only — aggregate.go:28-31 `type AttachableEvent interface { DataPointKey() hmtypes.DataPointKey; EventKind() string }`. Fire is not on it. Both sides live: the feed is constructed and started at the composition root, cmd/openccu-loom/daemon.go:329-331 `eventSourceFeed := adapter.NewEventSourceFeed(reg)` / `eventSourceFeed.Start()` / `defer eventSourceFeed.Stop()`. The same repo shows the sound alternative for the same datum two packages away: internal/store/visibility/operation_mode.go:67 `type operationModeGater interface { SetOperationModeAllowed(allowed bool) }` and :182 `g, ok := ev.(operationModeGater)` — a capability interface over the identical ch.GenericEvents() slice.
stands.negativeControl: Two controls. For the mechanism: had the feed not narrowed to a concrete type, line 80 would have read as an assertion to a capability interface (the shape at operation_mode.go:182) or no assertion at all; it reads `attached.(*modevent.Source)`. For the damage: had a second production implementation existed, `grep -rn 'func (.*) EventKind() string' internal/ pkg/` would have listed a non-Source production type. It lists exactly one production implementation, internal/model/event/event.go:163 `func (s *Source) EventKind() string { return string(s.Kind) }`; the other four hits are all _test.go. So the mechanism is confirmed and the damage is latent, not current.
stands.reason: The narrowing is exactly as described and the fire lifecycle is unreachable through the interface. Today nothing is lost: the only production AttachGenericEvent call site is device_pipeline.go:1999-2001 `if src := modevent.NewSource(ch.Address, hmenum.Parameter(name)); src != nil { ch.AttachGenericEvent(src) }`, so every attached event is a *modevent.Source. I am keeping the severity at low for that reason, not raising it. What makes it more than hypothetical is that a satisfying non-Source object already exists in the tree and the two consumers of the same slice already treat it differently — see divergence. The model layer performs the identical narrowing at aggregate.go:181-186 with the same rationale (`// Gather events and classify by kind. Only concrete *modevent.Source // values can be added to a Group; other AttachableEvent implementations // (e.g. test doubles) are skipped.`), so this is a documented convention rather than a local slip — but the convention is enforced by comment on one side and by a capability interface on the other.
stands.divergence: internal/store/visibility/event_gating_test.go:19-32 defines `type eventSourceWrapper struct { src *event.Source; key hmtypes.DataPointKey }` with `DataPointKey()`, `EventKind()` and `SetOperationModeAllowed(allowed bool)`, and attaches it via `ch.AttachGenericEvent(&eventSourceWrapper{src: src, key: key})` (:48). That one object is the concrete diverging input: handed to internal/store/visibility/operation_mode.go:182 it satisfies operationModeGater and is gated normally; handed to event_source_feed.go:80 the `*modevent.Source` assert fails and Fire is never called, so `last_triggered_event` would stay nil for a channel whose keypress did arrive. It exists only in a _test.go file today, so this is a demonstrated shape mismatch, not a production regression.

stands.title: The MQTT hub publisher re-derives LIST index→label with a different gate than the model's own resolver
stands.evidence: Both quotes verbatim. hub_mqtt_publisher.go:968-992 `func sysvarStateForMQTT(sv *hub.Sysvar, raw any) any {` … `valueList := sv.Meta().ValueList` / `if len(valueList) == 0 { return raw }` / `switch v := raw.(type) { case int: idx = v; case int64: idx = int(v); case float64: idx = int(v); default: return raw }` / `if idx < 0 || idx >= len(valueList) { return raw }` / `return valueList[idx]` — gated on a non-empty ValueList plus a numeric value only, never on ValueType. sysvar_subtypes.go:267-273 `if m.ValueType == hmenum.HubValueTypeList && len(m.ValueList) > 0 { if v.Kind == hmtypes.ValueKindInt { idx := v.Int; if idx >= 0 && idx < len(m.ValueList) { return m.ValueList[idx], true` — gated on ValueType == LIST and on an int kind only. The ValueList fill is type-blind as claimed: hub_wiring.go:1192-1194 `if v.ValueList != "" { valueList = strings.Split(v.ValueList, ";") }` sits outside any ValueType branch, after `valueType := inferSysvarType(v.Type, v.Value)` (hub_wiring.go:1190). Liveness: siteA is live — hub_mqtt_publisher.go:841 `w.PublishSysvar(ctx, centralName, sv, sysvarStateForMQTT(sv, val.Unwrap()))` and :846 the same for `next.Unwrap()`. siteB is NOT live: repo-wide `grep -rn "SensorValue()" --include="*.go" .` returns only internal/model/hub/sysvar_subtypes.go:261 (the definition) and three _test.go files (sysvar_sensor_metric_hub_test.go, sysvar_metadata_race_test.go); its only constructor `WrapSysvar(` likewise appears solely in the definition (sysvar_subtypes.go:308) and in _test.go files.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, one of two things would have shown: (a) sysvarStateForMQTT would have contained a `sv.Meta().ValueType == hmenum.HubValueTypeList` test — it contains no ValueType reference at all (the whole function body is quoted above); or (b) the grep for SensorValue/WrapSysvar would have returned a non-_test.go caller, which it did not. I also grepped the north-bound REST/SPA rendering path to see whether it consumed siteB, and it does not (see reason) — that grep would have named a production file had the candidate's damage path existed.
stands.reason: The duplication and the divergent gate are real and verified. A concrete input on which the two copies disagree today: a sysvar reported by the CCU with a non-LIST numeric type and a non-empty `valueList` — e.g. type "INTEGER", valueList "Aus;An", value 1. parseSysvarValue (hub_wiring.go:1988-1993, `case hmenum.HubValueTypeInteger, hmenum.HubValueTypeList:` → `hmtypes.IntValue`) yields int 1, so sysvarStateForMQTT returns the string "An" while SysvarDpSensor.SensorValue falls through the LIST gate to `case hmtypes.ValueKindInt: return strconv.Itoa(v.Int)` (sysvar_subtypes.go:285) and returns "1". Same for a FLOAT sysvar carrying a valueList, where the adapter additionally truncates via `case float64: idx = int(v)`. Two corrections to the candidate. (1) The stated damage — "published on MQTT as a label but rendered on REST/SPA as its raw number, so the two north-bound planes disagree" — is refuted. REST does not use the model resolver: toSysvarSummary (internal/north/rest/handlers/hub.go:1026-1050) ships `sum.Value = v.Unwrap()` alongside `ValueList: m.ValueList` and no label transform, and the SPA gates exactly like the adapter — assets/ui/src/lib/sysvar-widget.ts:67 `if (sv.value_list && sv.value_list.length > 0) return "select";` runs before any numeric-type test. So the live planes agree; the divergent gate is the model's, and the model's copy is unreachable. (2) Severity is therefore low, not medium: nothing observable breaks when the two drift, because only the adapter copy runs. What the finding does cost is false confidence — internal/model/hub/sysvar_sensor_metric_hub_test.go:53-126 exercises a resolver no production path calls, while the live rule is pinned only by TestSysvarStateForMQTT / TestSysvarStateForMQTT_ScannedListValueResolvesToLabel (internal/central/adapter/hub_mqtt_publisher_sysvar_test.go:71,134). No test compares the two. Not verified, and left as a firmware question: whether a real CCU's SysVar.getAll ever reports a non-empty `valueList` for a non-LIST variable. No fixture in the repo carries the field (`grep -rn '"valueList"'` hits only hub_wiring.go:1091 and tests/contract/jsonrpc_declared_arguments_test.go:50), so the divergence above is proven at code level, not on observed CCU data.

stands.title: The device-details store answers BidCos-RF for every address, and hub bring-up never populates the interface tags
stands.evidence: Both quotes verbatim. hub_wiring.go:523-527: `// Interface tags are NOT populated here because hub_wiring.go's` / `// loadDeviceNames does not read the "interface" field. The` / `// devicedetails.Loader (used by the periodic scheduler job) does` / `// fetch the interface field via Device.listAllDetail; until the first` / `// refresh fires, GetInterface falls back to BidCos-RF (cache.go:174).` cache.go:168-177: `// GetInterface returns the cached interface or [hmenum.InterfaceBidCosRF]` / `// as a fallback.` / `func (c *Cache) GetInterface(address string) hmenum.Interface {` … `if iface, ok := c.interfaces[address]; ok { return iface }` / `return hmenum.InterfaceBidCosRF`. Both halves of the comment's own claim check out: populateDeviceDetailsCache (hub_wiring.go:528-…, production-called at hub_wiring.go:354) starts with `cache.Clear()` (cache.go:257-267, which does `c.interfaces = make(map[string]hmenum.Interface)`) and never calls AddInterface; the Loader does — loader.go:152-158 `iface := hmenum.Interface(d.Interface)` / `if d.Interface != "" && isKnownInterface(iface) { staging.AddInterface(d.Address, iface) } else { staging.AddInterface(d.Address, hmenum.InterfaceBidCosRF) }`, committed via `l.cache.ReplaceWith(staging, time.Now())` (loader.go:212), and NewLoaderForJSONRPC is production-wired at hub_wiring.go:374, ccu_wiring.go:551 and cuxd_wiring.go:247.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, `grep -rn "GetInterface" --include="*.go" .` would have returned a non-_test.go call on a *devicedetails.Cache. Equally, had the seed populated interfaces, populateDeviceDetailsCache would have contained an AddInterface call — it contains none, and Clear() wipes the map first.
stands.reason: Verified as stated, with the reachability sharpened. There is a real divergence inside one live mechanism, not between two copies: for the same address the store answers differently depending on when it is asked. Boot seed → `interfaces` empty → GetInterface("<any HmIP address>") == hmenum.InterfaceBidCosRF; after the 5-minute Loader.Load → GetInterface of that same address == hmenum.InterfaceHmIPRF (loader.go:152-154). The fallback is indistinguishable from a real answer because InterfaceBidCosRF is also a legitimate result — the loader itself returns it deliberately for an unrecognised tag (loader.go:157), so a caller cannot tell 'unknown' from 'genuinely BidCos-RF'. Severity low because the accessor has no production consumer today: nothing observable breaks when the two states disagree. It stays a finding rather than a non-issue precisely because it is pre-broken for the first consumer — on an HmIP-only CCU every device reads as BidCos-RF for the first refresh interval, and cache_test.go:26 pins that default (`zero-state GetInterface must default to BidCos-RF`), so a new caller would inherit a green test over a wrong answer. stands.title: lookupSlotDuration hard-codes a zero-padded key while the parser's grammar accepts unpadded groups
stands.evidence:
Both quotes verified verbatim. schedules.go:777-782: `func lookupSlotDuration(raw map[string]any, slotNo int) (durationBase, durationFactor int) {` / `prefix := fmt.Sprintf("%02d_WP_", slotNo)` / `dBase, _ := coerceInt(raw[prefix+"DURATION_BASE"])` / `dFactor, _ := coerceInt(raw[prefix+"DURATION_FACTOR"])`, preceded by the comment at :775-776 `// Slot keys follow the `<NN>_WP_<FIELD>` grammar; the slot` / `// number is zero-padded to two digits in the wire shape.` rawconvert.go:65-75: `func SimpleGroupNo(key string) (groupNo int, ok bool) {` / `parts := strings.SplitN(key, "_", 3)` / `if len(parts) != 3 || parts[1] != "WP" || parts[2] == "" { return 0, false }` / `n, err := strconv.Atoi(parts[0])` / `if err != nil || n < 1 { return 0, false }`. ParseSimpleRawParamset calls it at rawconvert.go:633 `groupNo, ok := SimpleGroupNo(key)`. The lock fallback quote is right too: lock.go:56 `return LockActionAutoRelockStart`.

Both sides live and both lock read paths do share the helper: schedules.go:761 (REST/WS, parseSimpleScheduleWithDomain) and week_profile_io.go:179 (defaultChannelLoader → MQTT).
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, either SimpleGroupNo would have required two digits (e.g. a `^\d{2}_WP_` pattern) or lookupSlotDuration would have re-derived the key through the same helper. Neither: strconv.Atoi("1") returns (1, nil), so SimpleGroupNo("1_WP_LEVEL") = (1, true), while fmt.Sprintf("%02d_WP_", 1) = "01_WP_" — I checked both spellings against the two functions rather than assuming.
stands.reason: The `<NN>_WP_<FIELD>` key spelling is stated twice with different strictness: the parser's grammar (rawconvert.go:65-75, unpadded-tolerant) and the adapter's re-lookup (schedules.go:778, padded-strict). Severity is LOW, not medium, because the candidate's damage rests on an input I could not find: I checked all 399 device fixtures in ../godevccu/internal/embed/data/paramset_descriptions and every `<digits>_WP_` prefix is zero-padded two digits (`grep -rho '"[0-9]\+_WP_[A-Z_0-9]*"' | sed 's/_WP_.*//' | sort -u` → "01 … "75, no bare "1). The daemon's own encoder also writes padded (rawconvert.go:801 `prefix := fmt.Sprintf("%02d_WP_", groupNo)`, :891 `%02d_WP_WEEKDAY`), and the SPA fixture at assets/ui/tests/e2e/fixtures/visibility-candidates.json:49 uses "01_WP_LEVEL". Whether any CCU firmware or proxy emits unpadded keys is not carried by any source in the repo — the candidate's "On a CCU (or a proxy) that returns unpadded keys" is unverified in those words. The out-of-range direction is safe: SimpleMaxSlot is 75 (simple.go:315-320), so %02d never truncates.
stands.divergence: Function-level, demonstrable but not observed on the wire: key "1_WP_DURATION_BASE" (value 7) plus "1_WP_WEEKDAY" (value 2). weekprofile.SimpleGroupNo("1_WP_DURATION_BASE") returns (1, true) and ParseSimpleRawParamset emits an entry at slot 1; lookupSlotDuration(raw, 1) builds "01_WP_DURATION_BASE", misses, and returns (0, 0). schedule.DetectLockAction(1.0, 0, 0) then returns LockActionAutoRelockStart (lock.go:50-56 fallback) where the real (7,31) pair would have returned LockActionUnlock — an unlock slot read back as an auto-relock start on both lock read planes at once. I found no raw paramset in the repo or the godevccu fleet that actually carries that key spelling.
stands.guard: none. No test feeds an unpadded key through ParseSimpleRawParamset + lookupSlotDuration; the lock cross-plane guard (internal/central/adapter/lock_rule_cross_plane_test.go) would not bite because both planes call the same lookupSlotDuration.
stands.deadCopy: neither — SimpleGroupNo is called from ParseSimpleRawParamset (rawconvert.go:633) and IsParameterName (:101); lookupSlotDuration is called from schedules.go:761 and week_profile_io.go:179.
stands.missingInput: Whether any CCU firmware or reverse proxy returns `<N>_WP_<FIELD>` keys without the leading zero. Not carried by any source in this repo, by the 399-device godevccu paramset fixtures, or by openccu-data. Establishing it needs a live GetParamset(MASTER) capture from a firmware that is suspected of it.

stands.title: The boot initial-load set is split between the coordinator and the adapter, and the coordinator's doc claims it covers every category
stands.evidence:
Doc quote verified verbatim, hub.go:922-926: `// InitHub performs the hub-coordinator initialization sequence. It clears` / `// any stale state from a previous run (sysvars, programs) and triggers an` / `// initial load for every hub data category so the hub model is populated` / `// as soon as the CCU connection comes up.`

InitHub (hub.go:931, live via internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:276 `unit.Hub.InitHub()`) runs exactly eight `.run(` calls — hub.go:938-945: programs, sysvars, inbox, serviceMessages, alarmMessages, installMode, metrics, connectivity. No `h.refresh.systemUpdate.run` and no `h.refresh.bidcosInterfaces.run` appear inside InitHub.

systemUpdate is boot-loaded from the adapter instead — internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:469 `		go runInitialSystemUpdateLoad(unit.Hub, cc.Name, logger)`, with the reason spelled out at :461-468 ("which left a cleanly booted central without firmware data (observed=false) for up to an hour").

bidcosInterfaces has no boot load at all. The only production reference to RefreshBidcosInterfaces is the job slot: cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_jobs.go:90 `		jobs.BidcosInterfacesRefresh = u.Hub.RefreshBidcosInterfaces`. The job is registered at internal/central/jobs.go:615-619 with `Name: "hub.bidcos_interfaces_refresh"`, `Interval: interval`, `Run: gatedRunWithDevicesCreatedGate(...)` and no RunOnStart field, so it takes the zero value false; internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:255-257 `	if j.RunOnStart {` / `		s.invoke(ctx, j)` / `	}` then skips the immediate invocation and the first poll lands one interval later. The default interval is measurable: internal/central/jobs.go:180 `	defaultBidcosInterfaces      = 60 * time.Second` (jobs.go:612-614 applies it when the configured value is <= 0). Only two jobs in the file set RunOnStart at all, both explicitly false (jobs.go:432, :501).

Consumers that read the empty cache in that window: internal/central/adapter/device_admin.go:369 `		info, ok := u.Hub.BidcosInterface(dev.InterfaceID)` (feeding coordinators.FirmwareUpdateRisky at internal/north/rest/handlers/device_admin.go:274) and internal/central/adapter/interfaces.go:58 `				if info, ok := u.Hub.BidcosInterface(e.InterfaceID); ok {`.

Guard: none. The three InitHub tests (internal/central/coordinators/hub_init_test.go:19, :49, :72, plus client_device_event_methods_test.go:302) assert programs/sysvars refresh, the Clear-before-refresh order and error tolerance; nothing pins the slot set against hubRefreshSet's fields.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, InitHub's body would have carried `_ = h.refresh.systemUpdate.run(...)` and `_ = h.refresh.bidcosInterfaces.run(...)` alongside the other eight — I read lines 938-945 and only eight `.run(` calls are there. Had bidcosInterfaces had some other boot load, the repo-wide grep for RefreshBidcosInterfaces would have shown a caller outside the scheduler slot; it shows only daemon_jobs.go:90. Had the job fired at registration, its Job literal would carry `RunOnStart: true` and scheduler.go:255 would invoke it before the first timer; it carries no RunOnStart.
stands.reason: Every element of the claim checks out against the source, and the doc comment at hub.go:924-926 is measurably false: it promises "every hub data category" while the function covers eight of the ten slots declared in hub_refresh.go:55-66. The split is real — systemUpdate's boot load lives in the adapter (hub_wiring.go:469), bidcosInterfaces has none — and no guard ties the two halves together, so an eleventh slot gets no signal about whether it needs a boot load. I can also close the gap the candidate left open: the bidcos window is not unmeasured. The job carries no RunOnStart, the scheduler only invokes immediately when that flag is set, and the default interval is 60 s (internal/central/jobs.go:180), so the duty-cycle / carrier-sense cache is empty for one full interval (60 s by default, or north.* configured value) after the job goroutine starts, during which device_admin.go:369 and interfaces.go:58 read absent. stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, one of two things would have shown: (a) `grep -n "func deviceAddress" internal/central/queryfacade.go` would have found nothing, or the body would have contained `hmtypes.DeviceAddress(...)` — in which case the guard's delegatesToHmtypes() helper (address_rule_single_source_test.go:99) would have excluded the file and address_rule_single_source_test.go:35 would not list it; or (b) the private helper would have had no non-test caller, and `grep -rn "deviceAddress(" internal/central/ | grep -v _test.go` would have returned only the definition line. I observed the opposite in both directions: the LastIndex body at :530, and three production call sites at :156/:190/:280.
stands.reason: The duplication is real and both copies are live, but severity is low rather than the proposed medium: the two helpers agree on every address the CCU grammar permits (device addresses cannot contain a colon — pkg/hmtypes/address.go:23), no diverging input was shown to reach the private copy, and the repo already carries a recorded ratchet entry for this exact file. What is genuinely unprotected is future drift: the existence guard would stay green if hmtypes.DeviceAddress changed semantics, and the fix would silently not reach internal/central.

stands.title: Two authorities write HasSystemUpdate, the 3.49 rule can never change any production value, and no production code reads the flag at all
stands.evidence: Quotes verified verbatim. internal/client/backends/ccu.go:124-130 `// Backup and HasSystemUpdate both route through the ReGa script runner,` / `// which production wires AFTER Initialize() runs (see ccu_wiring.go). If` / `// these were frozen at probe time they would be stuck false, so derive` / `// them from the current runner at call time instead.` / `caps.Backup = b.rega != nil` / `caps.HasSystemUpdate = b.rega != nil` — inside `Capabilities()`, which first loads `b.probedCaps` and then unconditionally overwrites both fields. internal/client/backends/ccu.go:132-140 `// Initialize implements [Initializer]. Backup and system-update capability are NOT set here` … `caps := CapabilityFor(KindCCU); b.probedCaps.Store(&caps)`. internal/client/backends/capabilities.go:283-287 `// System update info requires CCU firmware ≥ 3.49 for the ReGa` / `// get_system_update_info script to be available.` / `if major < 3 || (major == 3 && minor < 49) { caps.HasSystemUpdate = false }`. Sole production call site, internal/client/backends/detection.go:89-93: `isHomegear, version := sniffHomegear(reply)` / `if isHomegear { caps := CapabilityFor(KindHomegear); if version != "" { caps = UpdateCapabilitiesForVersion(caps, version) }` — the CCU fallback at :103-107 returns `CapabilityFor(KindCCU)` with no version adjustment. Two facts I established that the candidate did not: (1) `CapabilityFor(KindHomegear)` at capabilities.go:243-256 does not set HasSystemUpdate at all, so it is already false — the only production invocation of the 3.49 rule can therefore only set false→false, a guaranteed no-op; only `CapabilityFor(KindCCU)` at :208 sets `HasSystemUpdate: true`, and that branch never calls the rule. (2) `grep -rn "HasSystemUpdate" --include="*.go" .` yields hits only in internal/client/backends/{capabilities.go,ccu.go} and _test.go files — there is NO production reader of the flag anywhere. The REST system-update surface (internal/north/rest/router.go:1304-1305, handlers/system_hub.go:43) goes through the Hub coordinator and never consults backend capabilities.
stands.negativeControl: Three checks, each with a stated falsifying result. (a) Had the 3.49 rule reachable a CCU, `grep -rn "UpdateCapabilitiesForVersion"` would have shown a second production call site or one outside `if isHomegear` — it shows exactly detection.go:93 plus capabilities_test.go. (b) Had the Homegear no-op claim been false, `CapabilityFor(KindHomegear)` would have listed `HasSystemUpdate: true` — it does not list the field. (c) Had the flag been consumed, the HasSystemUpdate grep would have returned a hit outside internal/client/backends and _test.go — it returns none, while the same grep shape for sibling flags (`.Capabilities().InstallMode`, `.Backup`, `.LinkOperations`) returns many production hits in internal/client/interface_client_orchestration.go:465-670, which is the negative control for the grep itself being able to find readers.
stands.reason: The structural claim is confirmed and is in fact stronger than stated: the 3.49 gate is not merely bypassed for CCUs, it is unreachable in production for any backend, because its only call site operates on a Capabilities value whose HasSystemUpdate is already false. But the candidate's damage claim is NOT supported and I refute that half: 'the daemon therefore advertises system-update support' has no basis — nothing in cmd/, internal/north/ or internal/central/ reads HasSystemUpdate, so no advertised value exists to be wrong, and the ReGa script would fail at use time regardless of what the flag said. Severity low, not medium: what breaks when these two authorities drift is nothing observable, because the field they fight over is write-only. The honest finding is dead state plus a dead rule pinned by helper-level unit tests, not a user-visible capability lie.
stands.divergence: Concrete input: a CCU reporting SoftwareVersion "3.47.10.20190101" with a ReGa runner wired. UpdateCapabilitiesForVersion(CapabilityFor(KindCCU), "3.47.10.20190101") returns HasSystemUpdate=false (capabilities.go:285; pinned by capabilities_test.go:425-427). CcuBackend.Capabilities() on the same daemon returns HasSystemUpdate=true (ccu.go:129, because b.rega != nil; pinned by ccu_jsonrpc_test.go:167-169). The two authorities already answer opposite for that input today — but the first is never invoked on a CCU, so the effective production answer is unconditionally true, and no code reads it.
stands.guard: internal/client/backends/capabilities_test.go:323 and :414-449 pin the 3.49 threshold on the helper in isolation (3.47→false, 3.49.0→true, 3.55→true, ""→unchanged); internal/client/backends/ccu_jsonrpc_test.go:160-169 pins the runner-derived override. Neither crosses a production path: no test asserts what a CCU backend's HasSystemUpdate is after DetectBackend + Initialize + SetScriptRunner, and none would fail if UpdateCapabilitiesForVersion were deleted outright.
stands.deadCopy: internal/client/backends/capabilities.go:273 UpdateCapabilitiesForVersion is effectively dead: its one production call site (detection.go:93) can only apply it to CapabilityFor(KindHomegear), whose HasSystemUpdate is already false, making every invocation a no-op. Additionally the field itself is dead state — written at capabilities.go:208, capabilities.go:286 and ccu.go:129, read by no production code.

stands.title: The reliability layer parses a CCU wire string and picks a paramset key, contradicting its own "no transport dependencies" charter
stands.evidence:
Every quote in the candidate is verbatim. doc.go:9-10 `// Each primitive is an independent Go type with no transport` / `// dependencies; [InterfaceClient] composes them.` command_tracker.go:12 `	"github.com/SukramJ/openccu-loom/internal/client/backends"`; :127 `	values, ok := backends.ParseCombinedParameter(parameter, value)`; :131 `	return t.AddPutParamset(channelAddress, hmenum.ParamsetKeyValues, values)`.

Both sites are live. `AddCombinedParameter` has exactly one non-test caller: internal/client/interface_client_orchestration.go:326 `c.CommandTracker().AddCombinedParameter(channelAddress, string(parameter), s)` inside `WriteUnconfirmedValue`, which the composition root wires at cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_wiring.go:204 (`entry.Client.WriteUnconfirmedValue(channelAddress, parameter, paramsetKey, value)`) behind seam `client.value_writer_hooks`, fired from internal/client/write_options.go:173. `backends.ParseCombinedParameter` is also live on the receive side (internal/central/adapter/callback_handlers.go:434).

The import is the only cross-package coupling in the package: `grep -rn "client/backends" internal/client/reliability/` returns exactly one hit (command_tracker.go:12); every other production file there imports only stdlib plus pkg/hm* and internal/clock. Measured effect on the dependency graph: `go list -deps ./internal/client/reliability` yields internal/httpx, pkg/hmapi and pkg/hmproto in addition to the packages reliability's own code names. internal/httpx/transport.go:4 documents itself as `// Package httpx holds the daemon's HTTP client construction.` — i.e. the reliability package's graph does reach HTTP-client construction, and only through this one import.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false I would have seen: (a) `grep -rn "client/backends" internal/client/reliability/` empty, and (b) `go list -deps ./internal/client/reliability` free of internal/httpx / pkg/hmapi / pkg/hmproto. I ran the complement as the control: `go list -deps` on each of reliability's other imports (pkg/hmenum, pkg/hmerr, pkg/hmtypes, pkg/hmevent, pkg/hmreliability, internal/clock) — none of the six pulls internal/httpx, hmapi or hmproto, so those three enter solely via command_tracker.go:12. Had `AddCombinedParameter` been dead I would have seen only _test.go hits in the caller grep; instead the single production caller sits on the wired optimistic-update path.
stands.reason:
Structural claim confirmed as stated: a generic in-memory expiry cache in the resilience package decodes a CCU wire shorthand and hard-codes the paramset key, and it does so by importing the sibling backend-strategy package, which is what puts HTTP-client construction into the graph of a package whose doc promises transport independence. The parse itself belongs to the caller's layer — internal/client already imports backends, so moving the two lines into InterfaceClient.WriteUnconfirmedValue and calling the existing AddPutParamset would remove the import entirely.

Severity downgraded from medium to low, because the damage scenario is not reachable today and I found no diverging input (see divergence). Two qualifiers the candidate overstates: (1) `backends` is not itself a transport package — `go list -deps ./internal/client/backends` shows it does not import internal/client/transport/{xmlrpc,binrpc,jsonrpc}; the transport flavour comes indirectly via internal/httpx. (2) doc.go:5-7 enumerates the primitives it speaks of as "circuit breaker, retry …, duty-cycle throttle, request coalescer, and ping/pong tracker" — CommandTracker (like InFlightTracker and the incident sink) is not in that list, so "refutes the package doc" rests on reading "Each primitive" as covering every type in the package rather than the five named. The import fact is unambiguous; the doc contradiction is a reading of scope.
stands.divergence: None found — I looked for one and can name why it cannot exist on the current code. Both production paths that reach the discarded `paramsetKey` argument pass VALUES literally: internal/client/write_options.go:173 `ctFn(interfaceID, channelAddress, parameter, hmenum.ParamsetKeyValues, value)` and internal/client/interface_client_orchestration.go:751 `c.WriteUnconfirmedValue(channelAddress, parameter, hmenum.ParamsetKeyValues, value)`. So the hard-coded ParamsetKeyValues at command_tracker.go:131 agrees with the argument it ignores on every live input today, and no COMBINED_PARAMETER / LEVEL_COMBINED value reaches the tracker with a non-VALUES key. The candidate's "MASTER-paramset components" case is a hypothetical, not an input the repo can produce.
stands.deadCopy: Neither. AddCombinedParameter is reached from production (interface_client_orchestration.go:326 ← daemon_wiring.go:204 ← write_options.go:173); doc.go is the package doc comment.
stands.guard: None. No test constrains the reliability package's import set, and none ties doc.go's "no transport dependencies" sentence to the actual dependency graph. The only import-boundary guard in tests/contract is scoped elsewhere — tests/contract/mqtt_dumb_bridge_test.go:42 `// `internal/model/custom/` that the bridge must not import.` The two reliability contract tests (tests/contract/reliability_observability_test.go, reliability_constants_test.go) cover behaviour and constants, not layering. Consequently the doc sentence and the import can drift further with nothing failing.

Sourced from the DISPLAY_DATA_ICON` / `// VALUE_LIST on the HmIP-WRCD ACOUSTIC_DISPLAY_RECEIVER channel's VALUES` / `// paramset (channel :3)` … `var defaultIcons = []string{`, 32 entries including `"CLOUD_AND_MOOON",` at :92; defaultSounds at :114, 8 entries. textdisplay.go:400-407 `// Validation is` / `// skipped for the static fallback list populated by [New] because the fallback` / `// is incomplete` … `if icon == "" || !t.iconsFromDevice || len(t.availableIcons) == 0 {` / `return nil`; the flag is only set inside SetAvailableIcons (:255 `t.iconsFromDevice = true`), which the registry constructor calls from the runtime paramset (init.go:65-67 `if dp := ch.Parameter(hmenum.ParameterDisplayDataIcon); dp != nil { td.SetAvailableIcons(dp.ParameterData().ValueList) }`). stands.negativeControl: Had the two copies already drifted, comparing the constant against the real device list would have shown a differing label. Two sub-claims of the candidate are wrong and lower the severity. (1) `CLOUD_AND_MOOON` is not stale or a transcription error: it is the firmware's own spelling, and the repo can tell them apart — the same token appears in tests/integration/testdata/model_snapshot_aiohomematic.json:161693 and model_snapshot_openccu-loom.json:741856, and in the reference capture above. (2) The blast radius is narrow: IPTextDisplay is registered for exactly one binding, profiles.go:1430-1437 (`DeviceType: "hmip-wrcd"`, `Channels: []ChannelRoleAssignment{{Channel: 3, Role: ChannelRolePrimary}}`) — the very channel that carries DISPLAY_DATA_ICON — so on a healthy device the runtime list always overwrites the constant and validation is on. stands.title: Registry.RequiredParameters mixes the package-global catalogue into a per-registry answer
stands.evidence: Quote verified verbatim. internal/model/custom/required.go:41-47: `// 2. ProfileConfigs (the global generated catalog).` / `for _, pc := range ProfileConfigs {` / `if pc == nil {` / `continue` / `}` / `collectFromProfileConfig(pc, seen)` / `}`, immediately followed by required.go:49-59: `// 3. Extended configs from registered profiles.` / `r.mu.RLock()` / `for _, profile := range r.items { ... for _, p := range profile.Extended.RequiredParameters() { ... } }`. `ProfileConfigs` is a package-level `var` at internal/model/custom/profile_configs.go:22, not a field of Registry. The method is live: its only production caller is cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_infra.go:105 `si.visReg.SetRequiredParameters(custom.DefaultRegistry().RequiredParameters())`. The per-profile twin, `func (p Profile) RequiredParameters()` at required.go:70, does the opposite — it walks `p.Config` (required.go:73-75) plus Extended — so the same knowledge ("which parameters does a profile require") is derived two different ways and the registry-level derivation never calls the per-profile one. A sharper consequence than the candidate states: step 3 collects only `profile.Extended`, never `profile.Config`, so a registry holding a profile whose Config is not in the global map loses that Config's parameters entirely — which also falsifies the doc claim at required.go:66-67 ("is a subset of the global Registry.RequiredParameters()") for such a registry.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, required.go:42 would have ranged over the receiver (something like `for _, profile := range r.items { collectFromProfileConfig(profile.Config, seen) }`) rather than over the package-level `ProfileConfigs` map, and `NewRegistry().RequiredParameters()` would return only the DefaultDataPoints set. It does not: I read the whole method (required.go:31-62) and `r` is touched only at lines 50-59. Independent control on the guard side: TestRegistryRequiredParametersEmptyRegistry (internal/model/custom/required_test.go:213-227) constructs a registry with no profiles and asserts only that DefaultDataPoints entries are *present* — it passes today while the full global catalogue is also returned, which is exactly the symptom a correctly-scoped implementation would not produce.
stands.reason: The method's answer does not describe the registry it was asked about, and the properly-scoped derivation already exists next to it (required.go:70) but is bypassed. Severity low rather than medium: production has exactly one caller and it passes DefaultRegistry(), where the global catalogue and the receiver's registrations coincide by construction — every `Config:` in profiles.go is a `ProfileConfigs[hmenum.DeviceProfile("…")]` lookup, verified, with no inline literal anywhere. So nothing observable is wrong in the shipping daemon today; the cost is that the whitelist is untethered from the registry and no test can see the difference.
stands.divergence: No output divergence exists today, and I checked rather than assumed. Two ProfileConfigs keys are orphans — "RfSwitch" (profile_configs.go:733) and "IPSimpleFixedColorLight" (profile_configs.go:286), both declared deliberate at tests/contract/device_profile_catalogue_test.go:71 and :76 — so they are walked at required.go:42 while no registered profile references them. But comparing the `hmenum.Parameter*` symbols inside those two blocks against every other block of profile_configs.go yields an empty orphan-only set: every parameter they contribute (COLOR, LEVEL, DURATION_UNIT/VALUE, RAMP_TIME_UNIT/VALUE, STATE, ON_TIME, CURRENT, ENERGY_COUNTER, FREQUENCY, POWER, VOLTAGE) is also contributed by a referenced schema. The structural divergence is reachable only through an isolated registry: `NewRegistry()` (registry.go:238) with nothing registered returns the entire global catalogue plus DefaultDataPoints instead of just DefaultDataPoints. No production path constructs such a registry — every non-test caller goes through custom.DefaultRegistry() (default.go:21-28), which runs RegisterProfiles over the same catalogue.
stands.deadCopy: Neither cited side is dead — required.go:42's global walk and required.go:50's receiver walk both execute on the single production call at cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_infra.go:105. But the correctly-scoped twin is: `Profile.RequiredParameters` (required.go:70) has no non-test caller in this repo (grep for `.RequiredParameters()` outside required.go returns daemon_infra.go:105 and internal/model/custom/required_test.go only), so the whitelist the daemon installs comes from the global mix while the per-profile derivation is exercised by tests alone.
stands.guard: None. All registry-level tests in internal/model/custom/required_test.go (lines 27, 44, 58, 72, 88, 107, 230, 244) build a fully-populated registry via testDefaultRegistry() (line 15) and assert only presence, never absence; TestRegistryRequiredParametersEmptyRegistry (line 213) is the one isolated-registry case and it too asserts presence of DefaultDataPoints only. stands.evidence: All three write-site quotes verified verbatim. cover.go:441 `return c.writer.SetValue(custom.EnsureContext(ctx), c.address, hmenum.ParameterStop, true, hmenum.CommandPriorityCritical)`; lock.go:547 `if err := l.writer.SetValue(ctx, l.Address, hmenum.ParameterLockTargetLevel, label, priority); err != nil {`; blind.go:347 `if err := b.writer.SetValue(ctx, b.Address(), hmenum.ParameterLevelCombined, s, priority); err != nil {` (and blind.go:352 the IP twin with hmenum.ParameterCombinedParameter). Profile-side quotes verified: profile_configs.go:69 `hmenum.FieldStop:              Bare(hmenum.ParameterStop),`, :66 `hmenum.FieldCombinedParameter: Bare(hmenum.ParameterCombinedParameter),`, :244 `hmenum.FieldLockTargetLevel: Bare(hmenum.ParameterLockTargetLevel),`, :593 `hmenum.FieldLevelCombined: Bare(hmenum.ParameterLevelCombined),`. CALLER CHECK — this is where the candidate is wrong, and the truth is a stronger finding: `grep -rn "FieldStop|FieldLevelCombined|FieldCombinedParameter|FieldLockTargetLevel|FieldOpen\b" --include="*.go" .` over the whole repo returns, outside pkg/hmenum/field.go and profile_configs.go, only tests/contract/custom_profile_constructor_resolves_test.go:283/286/331. There is no production consumer of these four Field constants — the read side does NOT resolve them through custom.ResolveSlotOr, contrary to the candidate's `knowledge` line. Nor do they act through visibility: all four are declared with `Bare(...)`, and custom.ResolveFieldValue (profile_schema.go:95-99) returns `isVisible == nil` for a Bare FieldValue, whereupon applyFieldValueToChannel (internal/model/custom/materialize.go:385-389) returns immediately: `param, isVisible := ResolveFieldValue(fv); if isVisible == nil { return }`.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, the write paths would read something like `ch, p := custom.ResolveSlotOr(c.channel, c.group, hmenum.FieldStop, hmenum.ParameterStop)` before SetValue, and the repo-wide grep for hmenum.FieldStop would have returned a production caller in internal/model/custom/cover/. It returned none outside profile_configs.go and one contract test.
stands.reason: Duplication confirmed, with the direction of the defect inverted from the candidate's account. The field→parameter fact is stated twice — once in the profile schema, once as a Go literal at the SetValue call — but the profile copy is inert: Bare entries are skipped by the materializer's visibility pass and no code resolves these four Field constants. So the live answer is the literal, and an operator or porter who edits `hmenum.FieldStop: Bare(...)` in profile_configs.go to name another parameter changes nothing at all — the write still goes to STOP on the CDP's own channel, silently. That is the drift damage, not the read/write mismatch the candidate describes. Severity low: no behaviour can break today, because the schema half cannot influence anything; the hazard is a maintainer trusting a declaration that has no effect. Note that the candidate's supporting precedent is real and quoted correctly (cover/init.go:256-261 routes the RF tilt slot through custom.ResolveSlotOr and finds LEVEL_SLATS rather than LEVEL_2) — but that is FieldLevel2, which does have a production resolver caller, unlike the four write fields.
stands.guard: Partial, one-directional. TestPinnedChannelGroupSchemasAreUnchanged (tests/contract/custom_profile_constructor_resolves_test.go:267) pins IPCover.Fields including `hmenum.FieldStop: bareRef(hmenum.ParameterStop)` (:286) and `hmenum.FieldCombinedParameter: bareRef(...)` (:283), and IPLock.Fields including `hmenum.FieldLockTargetLevel: bareRef(hmenum.ParameterLockTargetLevel)` (:331). It fails if the profile literal is edited; it says nothing if the write-path literal is edited, and it does not compare the two. RfCover's FieldLevelCombined (profile_configs.go:593) is not pinned at all.
stands.divergence: None today: all four profile declarations name exactly the parameter the corresponding write path hard-codes (STOP, COMBINED_PARAMETER, LEVEL_COMBINED, LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL), and all four sit in the primary-channel `Fields:` block, i.e. on the CDP's own channel, which is the address the write paths use (c.address / l.Address / b.Address()).
stands.deadCopy: The profile-schema half. hmenum.FieldStop, FieldCombinedParameter, FieldLevelCombined and FieldLockTargetLevel have no production reader anywhere in the repo, and their `Bare(...)` form makes applyFieldValueToChannel return at materialize.go:388 before touching any data point. stands.title: Level bounds 0 and 1 are held as constants although the descriptor declares LEVEL's MIN and MAX
stands.evidence: Quotes verified verbatim. blind.go:317-322 (inside sendCombined) `if level < 0 {` / `level = 0` / `}` / `if level > 1 {` / `level = 1` / `}` and :323-328 the tilt twin; the identical four-line clamp is repeated at blind.go:259-264 (SetTilt) and blind.go:394-407 (SetCombined). mixins.go:417 `func NewPosition(level float64) Position {` with the same clamp at :418-423, and mixins.go:452 `func NewBrightness(level float64) Brightness {` at :453-458. cover.go:319-321 quoted correctly — but the candidate stopped one line short of the sentence that decides the matter: the full comment at cover.go:319-327 reads `// LEVEL is FLOAT MIN 0.0 / MAX 1.0 with SPECIAL {LOCKED: -0.005}. So` ... `// The remap below is therefore a DOMAIN decision, not a` / `// reading of the wire: it presents locked as fully closed, and lifts` / `// the ordinary minimum to 0.01 so the two stay distinguishable in a` / `// single position number. Keep that in mind before treating either` / `// constant as a wire fact.` ALL SITES LIVE: blind.go clamps sit in SetTilt / SetPosition (→ sendCombined) / SetCombined, all exported command methods; custom.NewPosition is used across the cover, valve and north-bound paths.
stands.negativeControl: Had the duplication claim been false, the clamp would appear once — e.g. sendCombined would call `custom.NewPosition(level).Level()` — and grep for `level = 1` under internal/model/custom/ would return a single site. It returns five (blind.go:318/321 with the tilt twin at 324/327, blind.go:399/402, mixins.go:419/422, mixins.go:454/457). Had the *descriptor* half of the claim been false, generic/bounds.go would not read Descriptor.Min/Max; it does, at bounds.go:23-27.
stands.reason: Duplication confirmed — the [0,1] clamp is restated at five independent sites — but the candidate's damage rationale is refuted on two counts, and the real divergence is a different one. (1) The descriptor's MIN/MAX are already enforced on the LEVEL write path: generic.Float.Set (internal/model/generic/number.go:58-65) calls `checkFloatBounds(f.Descriptor, v)` which reads `parseFloat(desc.Min)` / `parseFloat(desc.Max)` (bounds.go:19-30) and returns ErrOutOfRange, with SPECIAL values bypassing the check (bounds.go:20-22) — so a family declaring another LEVEL range is not "silently truncated" on that path, it is rejected. (2) The HM-Sec-Win handling is explicitly documented as a domain decision rather than a descriptor read (cover.go:322-327), so calling it a missed descriptor read misreads the file's own statement. What I did find is a live disagreement between two sibling command paths for the same public contract. Severity low: out-of-range positions are caller errors, and both behaviours are safe on the wire; what breaks is the caller's ability to predict whether an out-of-range position errors or is silently accepted.
stands.guard: None. No test feeds an out-of-range position to both Cover.SetPosition and Blind.SetPosition and compares outcomes, and no test asserts the clamp bound against a descriptor's MIN/MAX.
stands.divergence: Yes, between the clamping and the non-clamping copy of the same operation. Input: `SetPosition(ctx, 1.5, prio)`. On a plain cover, Cover.SetPosition (internal/model/custom/cover/cover.go:400-425) rejects only NaN/Inf (:401-403), applies no clamp, and hands 1.5 to `c.Set(...)` at :422 → generic.Float.Set → checkFloatBounds → ErrOutOfRange; the caller gets `cover: SET level: ...` wrapping a range error and nothing is written. On a blind, Blind.SetPosition (blind.go:244-249) routes to sendCombined, which clamps 1.5 to 1.0 at blind.go:320-322 and writes COMBINED_PARAMETER `"L2=<tilt>,L=100"` (blind.go:352) — a string parameter, so the descriptor's float bounds never apply. Same method name, same documented 0..1 contract, one returns an error and one silently succeeds. (The divergence holds regardless of whether a given LEVEL descriptor actually carries MIN/MAX: if it does not, checkFloatBounds is a no-op and Cover writes 1.5 raw, which diverges from the blind's clamp just as much.)
stands.deadCopy: Neither — every clamp site named is reachable from an exported command method.
