stands.title: The un_ignore grammar declared in the store already contradicts the parser that owns it
stands.evidence:
Quote verified verbatim. internal/store/sqlite/visibility_unignore.go:14-16: `// VisibilityUnIgnoreStore persists the per-central un_ignore patterns` / `// — \`MODEL:CHANNEL:PARAMETER\` strings (with \`*\` wildcards) that promote` / `// otherwise-hidden parameters into the visible data-point surface.` And :120 `	dedup := make(map[string]struct{}, len(patterns))` is indeed the only processing Replace applies (dedupe blanks + `sort.Strings`, then DELETE + INSERT).

The authority disagrees. internal/store/visibility/parser.go:19-21: `var unIgnoreLinePattern = regexp.MustCompile(` / `\t\`^(?P<parameter>[^:@]+):(?P<paramset_key>[^@]+)@(?P<model>[^:]+):(?P<channel_no>.*)$\`,` — the shape is PARAMETER:PARAMSET_KEY@MODEL:CHANNEL_NO, confirmed by the header comment at :17-18 `// unIgnoreLinePattern is the regex for the complex un-ignore format.` / `// Format: PARAMETER:PARAMSET_KEY@MODEL:CHANNEL_NO`. The wildcard sentinel is the literal string "all", not `*`: parser.go:28 `const unIgnoreWildcard = "all"`, and the model side is matched by equality against it (decider.go:665 `if eModelL == unIgnoreWildcard && entryChannelMatch(e, channelNo) {`), so `*` is not a model wildcard at all; `*` is tolerated only as a non-numeric channel string (parser.go:154-157 `default:` / `// Wildcard string (e.g. "*") — keep nil, mark wildcard.`) and is rejected outright for MASTER (parser.go:172-174 `result.Err = "channel must be numeric or empty for MASTER paramset in '" + trimmed + "'"`).

The canonical writer confirms the real shape: internal/store/visibility/candidate.go:232 `return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s@%s:%d", parameter, paramset, model, channelNo)` and :226 the same with `UnIgnoreWildcard` as the channel.

Both sides are live: sqlite.VisibilityUnIgnoreStore is wired from cmd/openccu-loom/ (visibility_wiring.go, daemon_southbound.go) and consumed by internal/north/rest/handlers/visibility.go; ParseUnIgnoreLine is called from the production PUT handler at internal/north/rest/handlers/visibility.go:227 `parsed := visibility.ParseUnIgnoreLine(line)`.
stands.negativeControl: Had the comment matched the grammar, feeding its documented shape through ParseUnIgnoreLine would have produced a parsed Entry. It produces an error instead (parser.go:107-110). Conversely, had the two been the same knowledge expressed once, the store file would have referenced or imported the parser rather than restating the format; it does neither — internal/store/sqlite/visibility_unignore.go imports only context, database/sql, fmt, sort, time.
stands.reason:
The knowledge-duplication half is confirmed, and in the strongest available form: the two copies do not merely *risk* disagreeing, they already disagree today, in field order, separator and wildcard token.

The candidate's `damage` half is refuted, and I record that rather than carry it forward. The REST PUT does not persist unparseable patterns: internal/north/rest/handlers/visibility.go:216-217 `// Pre-validate every line; collect parse errors but proceed with` / `// the well-formed subset so one typo does not block the whole save.`, :227-235 run ParseUnIgnoreLine and `continue` past any line with `parsed.Entry == nil || parsed.Err != ""` after appending to `parseErrors`, and only the surviving `valid` slice reaches `store.Replace` (:252). The response carries `ParseErrors: parseErrors` (:303). So an operator entering a malformed pattern is told, not silently accepted — the store's laxity is fronted by a validating handler.

What remains is a developer-facing defect: the file a reader opens to learn what the `visibility_unignore` table holds states a grammar that the matcher rejects. Severity low — the drift has already happened and nothing broke at runtime, because no code reads the comment.

No guard: TestDocPurity checks banned tokens and markdown-link integrity, not comment accuracy; per CLAUDE.md the comment-claims sweep is the only mechanism that catches this class, which is precisely how it survived.
stands.divergence: `HmIP-BSM:1:LEVEL` — a string of exactly the shape the store comment declares (MODEL:CHANNEL:PARAMETER). Store side: accepted, deduped, sorted and persisted by Replace without inspection. Parser side (parser.go:107-110, the `!strings.Contains(trimmed, "@")` branch): rejected with `Err = "invalid format: ':' without '@' in 'HmIP-BSM:1:LEVEL'"`, so the REST handler drops it into parse_errors and never persists it. The value the parser actually accepts for that intent is `LEVEL:VALUES@hmip-bsm:1` (candidate.go:232). Second diverging input: `LEVEL:VALUES@*:1` — comment says `*` is the wildcard; parser accepts the line but decider.go:665 compares the model against "all", so it matches only a device whose model is literally `*`, i.e. nothing. `LEVEL:VALUES@all:1` is the working form.
stands.deadCopy: Neither side is dead. sqlite.VisibilityUnIgnoreStore.Replace/List/Patterns have production callers in internal/north/rest/handlers/visibility.go and cmd/openccu-loom/visibility_wiring.go; visibility.ParseUnIgnoreLine has a production caller at internal/north/rest/handlers/visibility.go:227. The store copy of the grammar is a doc comment only — it has no callers by construction, which is why nothing detected its drift.

stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false I would have seen one of two things: (a) the record site at :118 resolving a static sentinel plus key together (e.g. a `noteFor(state)` returning both), so every produced note had an entry in the map — instead the map has no `client disconnected`/`client reconnecting`/`client connecting`/`connection lost: …`/`recovery completed: …`/`recovery failed: …` entry; or (b) the scoring keyed off a typed field of `health.Sample` (a breaker enum) rather than the display string — instead internal/health/client.go:80 does `strings.Contains(note, "breaker open")` on the same string the UI renders. Nothing guards the three couplings that matter: (1) rename the literal at health_wiring.go:139 from "breaker open" to anything else and both i18n tests stay green (they exercise the map, not the record sites), health_wiring_test.go:56-85 asserts only Status (`got.Status != health.StatusUnhealthy`), and internal/health/client_test.go:231-267 uses its own hard-coded literals — while clientScoreCircuit falls to `default: return 1.0`, silently adding 0.3 to the reported ClientScore of an interface with an open breaker; (2) no test requires a newly added static note to appear in healthNoteKeys; (3) no test couples healthNoteKeys to the SPA catalogue — the three Go contract tests that read assets/ui/src/lib/i18n.ts (tests/contract/config_field_labels_test.go, ui_surface_registry_test.go, security_class_labels_test.go) cover config fields, surfaces and security classes, not health.note.*. The SPA copy at i18n.ts:977-986 / 4858-4867 happens to carry all 10 keys in en+de today.

It is not refuted as "two readings of one datum": Note and NoteKey are one datum read two ways *by design* (tracker.go:44-55 says so), but the defect is elsewhere — a third producer in a package that cannot reach the map, already emitting an unmapped static note on the hottest path, plus no guard tying the literals to the substring matchers.

stands.evidence: Both quotes verbatim. device_pipeline.go:990-993: "// Force usage=event on click-event parameters (PRESS_*) of physical / // devices: the reference stack models them as events (HA spawns keypress / // event groups, never generic button entities). Virtual remotes are / // the exception — their press parameters are real clickable actions." — the line 994 call is `p.applyClickEventMarks(interfaceID)`. device_pipeline.go:1178-1186: "// applyClickEventMarks decides the usage of click-event parameters ... mirroring the reference stack's two-object model: each click parameter is BOTH a button // (DpButton) and a keypress event, each with its own usage. The daemon carries // one data point per parameter, so its single usage is mapped as: //   - data_point — button entity AND keypress event". Implementation inputs are device-side: device_pipeline.go:1253 `if !dp.ParameterData().Operations.IsWritable() { setter.SetForcedUsage(hmenum.DataPointUsageEvent) }` plus a custom-DP suppression branch (:1263-1271) and `d.IsVirtualRemote()` (:1215). The mark is HA-shaped only at the consumer: internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:440 "if ev.Category == hmenum.DataPointCategoryButton && ev.Usage == hmenum.DataPointUsageEvent {" → skip the entity, and internal/north/mqtt/discovery_press_button.go:34 "ev.Usage == hmenum.DataPointUsageDataPoint". Both sites live: finishIngest (device_pipeline.go:827) calls applyClickEventMarks at :994 and is called from IngestFromBackend (:672) and IngestNewDevices (:809); no non-test-only path involved.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false I would have seen (a) the pass justified purely by device semantics with no HA entity vocabulary in the comment, and (b) no north-bound consumer branching on `Usage == DataPointUsageEvent`. I found the literal HA sentence at :991-992 and two HA-Discovery branches, so the check discriminates. The same check run against the candidate's *damage* half returned the opposite result, which is the control: internal/north/matter/eligibility/eligibility.go:188-197 and internal/north/matter/endpoint/assembler.go:752-761 switch on Usage but list only Ignored / NoCreate / CDPSecondary / CDPState, so `event` falls to `default: return false` and is NOT hidden from Matter; the raw MQTT plane never reads Usage at all (internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:1966-2019 publishSlotState reads value, bucket and availability only); REST merely re-exports the string (internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:1044). So the check is capable of returning "not inherited", and did, for three of the four consumers named.
stands.reason: The claim as titled holds: an HA-vocabulary button-vs-event classification is computed in the ingest pipeline (internal/central) and stamped onto the domain model as a forced usage, and the only consumers that branch on the `event` verdict are the two HA-Discovery paths in internal/north/mqtt. The damage claim is measurably narrower than stated — Matter's hide gate default-passes `event`, the raw MQTT plane ignores Usage entirely, and REST exposes it as data a client can ignore — and usage=event still returns true from EnabledByDefault/Visible (internal/model/datapoint/base.go:256-262, internal/model/generic/datapoint.go:706-713), so nothing is suppressed outside HA Discovery. That is why I rate it low rather than the candidate's medium: what drifts if the HA rule changes is one HA plane, not a cross-consumer classification. Guard: none for the leak itself; the behaviour is pinned by TestClickEventMarksPreserveEventSuppression (internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline_visibility_test.go:302) and internal/north/mqtt/parity_round1_test.go:240, both of which encode the HA split rather than protect against it.

Two corrections to the candidate's damage narrative, both of which change the shape rather than the direction of the finding. (1) The 'stale role yields an empty list with HTTP 200' path does not exist — no HTTP or WS route reaches GetLinksForLocale; the REST linkable-channels route goes to LinksDomain, and a bad role there is a 400, not a silent 200. stands.title: Home Assistant MQTT-Discovery field names are baked into the domain core's SystemInfo struct tags
stands.evidence:
Quotes verified verbatim. internal/central/central.go:232-238 — `type SystemInfo struct {` / `\tModel    string `payload:"info"`` / `\tVersion  string `payload:"info,alt=sw_version"`` / `\tHostname string `payload:"info"`` / `\tSerial   string `payload:"info,alt=serial_number"`` / `\tURL      string `payload:"info,alt=configuration_url"`` / `\tIsHaApp  bool   `payload:"info,alt=is_ha_app"``. internal/central/central.go:246-249 — `// Deliberately untagged: [internal/payload] skips fields without a` / `// `payload:` tag, which keeps these out of the MQTT-Discovery hub` / `// block. They are a status-page concern, and adding them to the` / `// discovery payload would change a published wire contract.` So the LAYERING fact is real: HA-canonical vocabulary (sw_version, serial_number, configuration_url, is_ha_app) is written into a struct tag inside internal/central.

Liveness of the two sides, by grep: `grep -rn "payload\.For\|payload\.ForWith" --include=*.go .` returns exactly four hits repo-wide, of which only two are call sites, and BOTH pass a device: internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:1422 `info := payload.ForWith(ev.Device, payload.KindInfo, payload.Options{UseAltNames: true})` and internal/north/mqtt/discovery_schedule.go:335 (identical). No caller — production or test — ever passes a `SystemInfo` (or a `*central.Unit`) through the reflection extractor. The `payload:` tags on SystemInfo therefore reach no consumer at all.

The LIVE hub-device block is built elsewhere, from literals in the MQTT adapter: internal/north/mqtt/hub_discovery.go:112 `func hubDeviceBlock(centralName string, info HubInfo) map[string]any {` builds `block := map[string]any{"identifiers": …, "name": name, "manufacturer": "eQ-3", "model": model}` and then adds `block["sw_version"]`, `block["serial_number"]`, `block["configuration_url"]` from `mqtt.HubInfo` (hub_discovery.go:91-104, a struct with fields Name/Model/Version/Serial/URL only). It is fed by hand-written field projection, not by tags: internal/central/adapter/hub_mqtt_publisher.go:641-650 `func hubInfoFromUnit(u *central.Unit) mqtt.HubInfo { si := u.SystemInformation(); return mqtt.HubInfo{Name: u.Name(), Model: si.Model, Version: si.Version, Serial: si.Serial, URL: si.URL} }`, and the same five-field copy again at cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_southbound.go:181-189.

A third copy of the same vocabulary sits in internal/payload/info.go:253-261 (`CentralInfo` with `json:"sw_version,omitempty"` etc.), produced by internal/central/payload.go:18-31 `func (u *Unit) Info() payload.InfoPayload`. That one is declared dead by the code's own comment at internal/central/payload.go:44-50: `It exists to satisfy the [payload.Source] contract ADR 0007 makes mandatory for the central, not because an adapter reads it … The same is true of [Unit.Info] and [Unit.Config].`
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false — i.e. had the SystemInfo tags actually driven the discovery payload — the grep for `payload.For`/`payload.ForWith` would have returned at least one production site handing a SystemInfo or *Unit to the extractor, and `hubDeviceBlock` would have read a tag-derived map instead of the five named `mqtt.HubInfo` fields. It returned two sites, both `ev.Device`. Symmetrically, had the quotes been stale I would have seen different text at central.go:232/246; I read both regions and they match character for character.
stands.reason: Confirmed as a placement defect, but the candidate's damage mechanism is refuted and its severity must come down. The tags are inert: no production (or test) caller extracts SystemInfo through internal/payload, so adding `payload:"info"` to AuthEnabled changes no published byte. The genuine defect is the inverse of what was claimed — three copies of the HA hub vocabulary exist (central.go tags, payload.CentralInfo json tags, mqtt.hubDeviceBlock literals) and only the third is live, while two comments and one test doc-comment assert a coupling that does not exist. Nothing user-visible breaks when they drift, hence low; the cost is a future editor trusting a false comment.
stands.divergence: A central whose SystemInfo is {Hostname: "ccu3", IsHaApp: true, AuthEnabled: true}. The domain-core tags say `hostname` and `is_ha_app` are in the MQTT-Discovery hub block (central.go:235,238) and that AuthEnabled is deliberately kept out of it (central.go:246-249). The published block contains neither `hostname` nor `is_ha_app`: `grep -rn "is_ha_app|\"hostname\""` over the repo returns no hit anywhere under internal/north/mqtt, and mqtt.HubInfo (hub_discovery.go:91-104) has no field for either — hubDeviceBlock emits only identifiers/name/manufacturer/model/sw_version/serial_number/configuration_url. So the two sides already disagree today on two of the six tagged fields, and the untagged-for-safety rationale protects nothing.
stands.deadCopy: internal/central/central.go:232-238 — the `payload:"info"` tags on SystemInfo have zero callers (no payload.For/ForWith site takes a SystemInfo). Second-order: internal/central/payload.go:18 Unit.Info() → internal/payload/info.go:253 CentralInfo is reached only by tests, as internal/central/payload.go:44-50 itself states. The live copy is internal/north/mqtt/hub_discovery.go:112 hubDeviceBlock, fed by internal/central/adapter/hub_mqtt_publisher.go:641 hubInfoFromUnit.
stands.guard: A guard exists but does not bite, contrary to both the bundle's empty `guard` field and the test's own doc comment. internal/central/payload_info_test.go:124-129 says `A `payload:"info"` tag added to either field in a future edit fails here.` The test body (payload_info_test.go:130-164) calls `buf, err := json.Marshal(unit.Info())` — i.e. it marshals the hand-written `payload.CentralInfo`, which has no AuthEnabled/HTTPSRedirectEnabled field and does not read `payload:` tags at all. Adding `payload:"info"` to SystemInfo.AuthEnabled leaves every assertion in that test green. No test anywhere asserts that SystemInfo's tag set matches mqtt.HubInfo or hubDeviceBlock's key set.

stands.title: The south-bound serial read truncates before any consumer sees it; the cited justification is not HA vocabulary and its WebUI premise is unsourced
stands.evidence: Quote verified, with a line offset: the candidate cites runner.go:427-430 and :443-445; the text actually sits at :430-433 and :441-444. Verbatim, runner.go:430-433: `// The CCU may report the full radio-module serial; only the last 10` / `// characters are the canonical hardware serial shown in the WebUI. Clients` / `// embed this value as the central-id slot of their unique_ids, so it must` / `// match that canonical form byte for byte.` and runner.go:441-444: `// Canonical per-CCU serial (last 10, case preserved). Shared with SSDP` / `// discovery via routingkey.CanonicalSerial so the runtime identity and the` / `// discovery identity are byte-identical.` / `return routingkey.CanonicalSerial(result.Serial), nil`. routingkey/canonical.go:34-38 is the single implementation: `func CanonicalSerial(serial string) string { if len(serial) <= serialSuffixLen { return serial }; return serial[len(serial)-serialSuffixLen:] }`. BOTH SITES LIVE: `grep -rn GetSerial --include=*.go | grep -v _test.go` yields exactly one production caller, internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:92 `serial, err := runner.GetSerial(ctx)`; CanonicalSerial has four production callers (ssdp/device.go:94, rest/handlers/discovery.go:217, central/central_registry.go:297, runner.go:444). TRUNCATION IS TOTAL: GetSerial is the only Go reader of the get_serial script, and `grep -rn 'board_sgtin|board_serial|sgtin' --include=*.go` finds no other reader of the CCU board serial (the SGTIN hits in north/rest/handlers/system_hub.go:265 and cmd/openccu-loom/ws_adapters.go:839 are the *paired device's* SGTIN for HmIP LOCAL teach-in, unrelated to the CCU's own). So the full value the script returns exists nowhere after runner.go:444 — the damage claim holds. SUB-CLAIM REFUTED: `unique_ids` is not target-system vocabulary here — it is loom's own first-class routingkey concept (routingkey/canonical.go:64 `func CanonicalUniqueID(serialSuffix, address, parameter, eventPrefix string) string`), and the doc-purity ban list (tests/contract/doc_purity_test.go:127-132) covers legacy-project provenance tokens (`aiohomematic`, `homematicip_local`, ...), not `unique_id`. SUB-CLAIM UNSOURCED: runner.go:431 asserts the last 10 chars are what the WebUI shows; routingkey/canonical.go:20-21 gives a different reason for the same constant — `// virtual-remote keys. Ten characters mirror the legacy entry_id[-10:]` / `// width and stay comfortably collision-free across CCUs.` Neither the repo nor the script carries what the CCU WebUI actually displays.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false I would have seen one of two things, and saw neither: (a) a second production reader of the get_serial script or of /var/board_sgtin returning the untruncated value — grep over all non-test .go files returns exactly one GetSerial caller and no other board-serial reader; or (b) runner.go:444 reading `return result.Serial, nil` with the truncation applied downstream in hub_wiring.go / central_registry.go — the line instead reads `return routingkey.CanonicalSerial(result.Serial), nil`. For the refuted sub-claim, the falsifier would have been a doc-purity ban entry or a comment naming Home Assistant explicitly; doc_purity_test.go:127-132 lists only legacy-project tokens and the word `unique_id` is defined by loom itself at canonical.go:64.
stands.divergence: No numeric divergence is possible between the two cited sites — runner.go delegates to the single implementation in routingkey, so this is not a duplication and the two copies cannot drift. The one concrete divergence I did find is inside the third site: get_serial.fn:2 `!# Output: {"serial":"<10-char serial or 'unknown'>"}` and :5-6 `!# non-empty value. Output is compressed to the trailing 10 chars so` / `!# callers treat it as an opaque identifier.` — but the script body never truncates; it runs `system.Exec("/bin/sh -c 'cat /var/board_sgtin'", &sSerial, &sErr)`, trims, and writes the value whole. Diverging input: a CCU whose /var/board_sgtin holds `3014F711A0001F58A99BC0DE` — the script returns all 24 characters (contradicting its own header), and Go then reduces it to `58A99BC0DE` (the exact pair pinned in runner_test.go:1416).
stands.deadCopy: Neither. Both cited sites have production callers: runner.GetSerial via internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:92 (resolveCCUSerial), routingkey.CanonicalSerial via ssdp/device.go:94, rest/handlers/discovery.go:217 and central/central_registry.go:297.
stands.guard: Two guards pin the truncation AT THE READ SITE, i.e. they pin the very placement the candidate calls wrong: internal/client/rega/runner_test.go:1416 TestGetSerialTruncatesLongSerialToLastTenChars (feeds `{"serial":"3014F711A0001F58A99BC0DE"}`, asserts `58A99BC0DE`) and internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring_serial_test.go:112 TestResolveCCUSerialTruncatesLongSerial (same input, same expectation, through resolveCCUSerial). The rule itself is pinned by internal/routingkey/canonical_test.go:52 TestCanonicalSerial. There is NO guard that any consumer can still obtain the untruncated serial, and none that the get_serial.fn header matches its body.
stands.missingInput: What the CCU WebUI actually displays as the hardware serial. runner.go:431 rests the whole truncation rationale on it ("the canonical hardware serial shown in the WebUI"), routingkey/canonical.go:20-21 gives an unrelated rationale for the same width ("mirror the legacy entry_id[-10:] width"), and neither the repo nor the ReGa script carries the WebUI form. That sub-claim is not performable without reading a live CCU's UI, which is out of scope here; it does not affect the confirmed structural finding.
stands.reason: The structural claim is confirmed by grep, not by reading the comment: routingkey.CanonicalSerial is applied inside the south-bound reader (runner.go:444), GetSerial is the sole Go path to the get_serial script and has exactly one production caller, and no other Go code reads /var/board_sgtin or /var/board_serial — so the untruncated value the script returns is unobtainable anywhere in the daemon. Severity stays low on what breaks, not on how it looks: there is a single implementation of the rule, so nothing can drift numerically, and no current consumer needs the full SGTIN (the only SGTIN consumers handle the paired device's, not the CCU's). The cost is purely informational — a future diagnostic would have to re-plumb the reader — and the placement is additionally cemented by two tests, so moving it is a three-file change. Two of the candidate's supporting arguments do not survive: `unique_ids` is loom's own routingkey vocabulary (canonical.go:64), not Home Assistant's, and doc-purity bans only legacy-project provenance tokens; and the comment's "shown in the WebUI" premise is unsourced and disagrees with routingkey's own stated reason for the same constant. Reported separately in notes: the get_serial.fn header claims a truncation the script does not perform.

stands.title: The client formats north-bound timestamp strings, with the layout literal repeated in one function
stands.evidence:
Quote verified verbatim. internal/client/payload.go:70 `		out.LastFailureAt = c.lastFailureAt.UTC().Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000000Z07:00")` and :75 `		out.LastCallbackAt = c.lastCallbackAt.UTC().Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000000Z07:00")` — byte-identical literals, five lines apart, inside one function `func (c *InterfaceClient) State() payload.StatePayload` (:52). The doc comment cited in the candidate is also verbatim, at :48-51: `// State returns the live client state: state-machine bucket, request / // counters and last-failure / last-callback timestamps. The / // aggregated shape lets the MQTT bridge publish one connectivity / // topic per interface without crossing the metrics layer.`

BOTH SITES LIVE, same code path: `InterfaceClient.State()` is called from production at internal/central/adapter/diagnostics_introspect.go:47 `State:        e.Client.State(),` inside `IntrospectAdapter.ReliabilitySnapshot` (:30), which is served by internal/north/rest/handlers/diagnostics_introspect.go:43 `JSON(w, http.StatusOK, svc.ReliabilitySnapshot(r.URL.Query().Get("central")))`. The struct fields are JSON-serialised strings: internal/payload/state.go:376-377 `LastFailureAt    string `json:"last_failure_at,omitempty"`` / `LastCallbackAt   string `json:"last_callback_at,omitempty"``, and they reach the SPA as strings (assets/ui/src/lib/api/client.ts:2639-2640). No non-test caller other than the diagnostics path exists (`grep -rn "LastFailureAt\|LastCallbackAt" --include=*.go` outside _test.go returns only those two writers plus the DTO).

THIRD COPY: the identical literal is already a named constant in another package — internal/model/generic/payload.go:194 `const timestampLayout = "2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000000Z07:00"`, used at :179 and :182. It is unexported, so internal/client cannot reuse it; the repo therefore carries three copies of the same layout under two spellings.
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, `grep -rn "000000000Z07:00" --include="*.go" .` would not have returned two hits inside internal/client/payload.go (it returned exactly lines 70 and 75, plus the generic constant at :194), and `sed -n '66,78p'` would have shown either a different layout on one of the two lines or a call to a shared helper/constant instead of an inline literal. The grep returning one client hit, or a `timestampLayout`-style identifier at both sites, is the result a false claim would have produced.
stands.reason: The duplication is real and verified verbatim, both occurrences are on the same live path (REST GET /diagnostics/reliability), and nothing pins the format, so drift is possible and silent. Severity stays low because the two copies are five lines apart in one function, are identical today, and the consumer contract (assets/openapi.yaml:14565-14572, `format: date-time`, `description: RFC3339 timestamp of the last request failure.`) is satisfied by any RFC3339 spelling — a drift would change the fractional-second width in one field of a diagnostics dump, not break a parser. The candidate's framing of the damage (presentation knowledge in the south-bound layer) is accurate: the field leaves the client already stringified, so no north-bound encoder can choose.
stands.divergence: None between the two cited sites — the literals are byte-identical. A real divergence exists one level out, in the same layout family, and it refutes a doc comment: internal/model/generic/payload.go:190-193 says `// timestampLayout is the wire format the payload methods emit for / // time fields. RFC3339 with nanoseconds matches the existing JSON / // payload format the MQTT bridge produces in / // [internal/north/mqtt/bridge.go::renderStatePayload].` — but internal/north/mqtt/bridge.go:2164 emits `"modified_at": time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),`. Concrete diverging input: the instant 2026-09-02T10:00:00.000000000Z (nanosecond field exactly 0). The fixed layout prints `2026-09-02T10:00:00.000000000Z`; RFC3339Nano prints `2026-09-02T10:00:00Z`. Source for the semantics, not convention: Go 1.26.6 stdlib, $(go env GOROOT)/src/time/format.go:99-103 — `// A comma or decimal point followed by one or more zeros represents / // a fractional second, printed to the given number of decimal places. / // A comma or decimal point followed by one or more nines represents / // a fractional second, printed to the given number of decimal places, with / // trailing zeros removed.`
stands.deadCopy: Neither. Both cited sites are in one production-reached function; the third copy (internal/model/generic/payload.go:194) is also live via generic payload methods at :179/:182.
stands.guard: None. `grep -rn "000000000Z" --include="*_test.go" .` returns nothing — no test asserts the formatted string. The tests that mention these fields only exercise the time.Time accessor for zero/non-zero and ordering: internal/client/interface_client_deep_test.go:339 TestInterfaceClientNotifyCallbackUpdatesLastCallbackAt, internal/client/interface_client_test.go:134-141, internal/central/adapter/callback_handlers_liveness_test.go:89-107, tests/contract/callback_liveness_contract_test.go:111-142. Replacing the layout at payload.go:70 with time.RFC3339Nano would leave every one of them green.

Had the claimed REST/Matter blast radius been real, a repo-wide grep for HasSinglePrimaryCustomDP would have shown a consumer outside internal/north/mqtt; it shows exactly two non-test hits, discovery_aggregate.go:601 and bridge.go:414.
stands.reason:
The core claim is confirmed as stated: a naming predicate owned by internal/model/device keys on Home Assistant component names, and the reference it is ported from uses a structural key instead, so this is a coupling the project introduced rather than inherited.

The damage claim is narrower than filed, which is why I set severity low rather than the candidate's medium:

- "Adding an HA component to an existing profile changes REST and Matter entity names as a side effect" is REFUTED. HasSinglePrimaryCustomDP has no consumer outside internal/north/mqtt (production hits: discovery_aggregate.go:601, bridge.go:414). internal/model/naming ships no production caller either — its four hits are all _test.go. REST channel summaries (rest/handlers/devices.go:740-775) and Matter never consult it.

- "A custom DP that has no HA component … gains a ch<N> suffix it should not have" is a correct reading of the mechanism but latent, not live: every shipping custom DP returns a non-empty component (textdisplay/topology.go:18 "text", siren/topology.go:23,26,29 "siren", valve/topology.go:21,24 "valve", lock/topology.go:18 "lock", switch/topology.go:20,39 "switch", light/topology.go:18 "light", climate/topology.go:26 "climate", cover/topology.go:24,27,30 "cover"). No current device takes the wrong branch.

What breaks on drift: HA entity names only — a Matter-only or REST-only profile added later, or a change to any HAComponent() string, silently shifts entity `name` between "" and "ch<N>", which churns HA entity_ids for users. Confined to one adapter, no instance today, and the guard pins the names of every shipping profile — hence low.

One property of the current key worth noting without claiming a defect: it merges distinct profiles that share a component — Cover/Blind/Garage all return "cover", Siren/SmokeSiren/SoundPlayer all "siren", Switch/AccessPermission both "switch" — so two structurally unrelated primaries count as one category. Whether any shipping device hosts such a pair I did not establish; the profile registry would have to be read to say.
stands.divergence: No two copies to diverge — this is a single-copy coupling, not a duplication. The measured divergence is against the reference: for a device with two primary custom DPs sharing one HA component, channel.go:836-841 counts 2 and returns false, while aiohomematic/model/support.py:639 would return true whenever `primary_channel == current_channel_no and device_has_multiple_channels is False` regardless of component.
stands.deadCopy: Neither side is dead. Both channel.go:758-765 and channel.go:809-846 are reached in production through internal/north/mqtt/discovery_aggregate.go:601.
stands.guard: internal/model/naming/contract_test.go and tests/contract/naming_contract_test.go both call HasSinglePrimaryCustomDP and pin the resulting display names for shipping profiles (HmIP-PS ch3, HmIP-BWTH ch1, two-switch-primary cases). Neither pins the taxonomy — a change to an HAComponent() string that moves two primaries into or out of one category is not caught unless it happens to move one of the pinned devices. The candidate's guard note is accurate.

stands.title: SPA and Home-Assistant vocabulary is baked into pkg/: mdi: icon names, SPA colour-rule tokens, and an explicitly HA-facing alarm entity
stands.evidence:
Every quote in the candidate is verbatim-correct. pkg/hmui/quantity.go:28 — "// Icon names follow the `mdi:<token>` convention (Material Design"; :110 — "var parameterExact = map[string]Hint{"; :111 — "\t\"STATE\":                     {Icon: \"mdi:circle\", Semantic: \"state\"}," (63 distinct mdi: tokens in the file). Hint carries `StateColorRule string` and the type doc says "The SPA renders Icon + SemanticKind verbatim and looks up StateColorRule against its own rule registry." pkg/hmapi/alarm.go:260-262 — "// AlarmPanelEntity is the alarm-control-panel entity projection: the\n// HA-facing view of one alarm zone (or the aggregate master panel),\n// identical across REST, WebSocket, and MQTT."

Both sites are LIVE in production, neither is test-only. hmui has exactly one production consumer: internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:1083 — "hint := hmui.HintFor(s.Parameter, s.Unit, s.Type, s.ValueList)", surfaced as `UIHint *hmui.Hint `json:"ui_hint,omitempty"`` (devices.go:391). No other non-test Go file references the package. AlarmPanelEntity is constructed at two production sites: internal/north/rest/handlers/alarm.go:714 and internal/north/rest/ws/alarm_panel.go:619.

The SPA does read the tokens verbatim, as the package doc claims: assets/ui/src/lib/sensor-actor/readouts/{Boolean,String,Enum,Numeric,Event}Readout.svelte all do `resolveIconLoose(dp.ui_hint?.icon)`, and assets/ui/src/lib/sensor-actor/state-color.ts:20 does `const rule = dp.ui_hint?.state_color_rule;` then switches on the literal Go-emitted strings ("temp_heat", "humidity_band", "alarm_active", "signal_weak", "particulate_band").
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false I would have seen one of: (a) the cited lines containing something other than mdi:/HA vocabulary — the grep for `mdi:` in pkg/hmui/quantity.go would have returned 0 rather than 107 occurrences; (b) hmui or AlarmPanelEntity referenced only from _test.go, which the caller greps would have shown as an empty non-test result set — instead each returned concrete production call sites; (c) an indirection layer between the Go token and the renderer, which would have shown up as the SPA mapping ui_hint through its own catalogue rather than switching on the literal Go strings in state-color.ts. The token-parity comparison carries its own control: feeding a synthetic token (`mdi:zzz-not-real`) through the same comm pipeline printed it as missing, while the 63 real Go tokens printed nothing.
stands.reason:
The candidate is an accurate, verified layering observation, not a defect — and its own damage estimate is the part that is wrong, in a way worth recording. It predicts that "a second frontend (or a Matter/MQTT consumer) inherits an icon set it does not use". Measured: no second consumer inherits it at all. internal/north/mqtt keeps a wholly independent icon vocabulary (its own HARegistryDescription.Icon field, entity_descriptions.go:47 — "// Icon is a Material Design Icon string (e.g. \"mdi:weather-rainy\")."), and the two tables ALREADY DISAGREE on shared parameters. So the real shape is not "shared pkg catalogue forced on everyone" but "two unsynchronised icon tables, one in pkg/ for the SPA, one in internal/north/mqtt for HA discovery". Each is arguably right for its caller — the MQTT table is the ported HA entity-description registry, the hmui table is the AutoTile classifier — so this is a two-readings-of-one-datum pair, not a duplication defect.

Severity stays low because nothing breaks when the pkg-level vocabulary drifts from a renderer: assets/ui/src/lib/icons.ts:390-397 resolves unknown tokens through `LOOSE_REGISTRY[name] ?? Gauge`, and state-color.ts returns undefined for an unrecognised rule. Drift degrades to a generic icon / no colour, never a crash or a wrong value.

What the verification did surface as the real weakness is the absence of any guard over the cross-language token contract (see `guard`), plus a second, adjacent duplication the candidate did not raise: internal/north/rest/handlers/alarm.go:706-724 and internal/north/rest/ws/alarm_panel.go:611-631 are two field-for-field identical AlarmPanelEntity projection loops with no shared helper, both live.
stands.divergence: Concrete diverging input, parameter DUTY_CYCLE: pkg/hmui/quantity.go:125 returns Hint{Icon: "mdi:speedometer", Semantic: "diagnostic"}; internal/north/mqtt/entity_descriptions_table.go:176 returns Icon "mdi:radio-tower" for Key "DUTY_CYCLE". Same for CARRIER_SENSE_LEVEL: quantity.go:129 "mdi:speedometer-medium" vs entity_descriptions_table.go:228 "mdi:radio-tower". One CCU parameter, two icons, depending on which north-bound surface renders it. NOT diverging: the pkg/hmui-to-SPA contract itself is in sync today — all 63 mdi: tokens emitted by quantity.go are present in LOOSE_REGISTRY in assets/ui/src/lib/icons.ts, and all 5 StateColorRule values (alarm_active, humidity_band, particulate_band, signal_weak, temp_heat) have a matching `case` in state-color.ts.
stands.deadCopy: Neither. Both cited sites have production callers. hmui.HintFor: internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:1083. hmapi.AlarmPanelEntity: internal/north/rest/handlers/alarm.go:714 and internal/north/rest/ws/alarm_panel.go:619.

(2) No vitest imports resolveIconLoose or stateColorFor — grep for either name across assets/ui/src hits only the definition file and the five .svelte consumers, no .test.ts. So a Go-side row added with an icon the SPA does not carry, or a StateColorRule the switch lacks, silently degrades to Gauge / undefined with every gate green. state-color.ts:9-10 states the duty as prose only — "// Adding a rule is a single switch-case below + a row in the Go\n// catalogue. Keep them in sync." stands.title: Home Assistant / MQTT / SPA vocabulary is used to justify domain rules inside internal/store
stands.negativeControl: Had the claim been false, the three cited lines would have read in device/domain terms only (e.g. "…configuration parameters no operator tunes") and the package-wide grep for HA / Home Assistant / MQTT / SPA / REST over internal/store/visibility/*.go would have returned zero non-test hits. For the liveness half: had either cited function been a dead copy, the caller grep would have shown only _test.go hits; instead each has a named production caller (decider.go:292 / reason.go:165, device_pipeline.go:1136, rest/handlers/visibility.go:483).
stands.reason:
The candidate's title and its evidence verify exactly; the quotes are not stale or invented, and every cited site is production-live. Severity stays low because the coupling is textual: no HA/MQTT/SPA symbol reaches the rule data and internal/store/visibility imports nothing north-bound.

But the candidate's escalation — "The AllHiddenReasons case is closer to real coupling — the store's enum order is declared to be the SPA's chip order" — is REFUTED, and in a way that turns the finding into a comment-claims defect rather than a layering one. The SPA does not take chip order from the store, and the two orders already disagree (see `divergence`). Worse, the comment's operative claim "so a new reason appears in the UI without a second enumeration" is false: the vocabulary is re-enumerated in at least five further places, none generated from reasonPrecedence —
  - assets/openapi.yaml:10680-10693 (hand-written `enum:` list)
  - assets/ui/src/lib/api/visibility-types.ts:36-49 (`UnIgnoreReason` union)
  - assets/ui/src/lib/visibility/candidates.ts:40-54 (`REASON_ORDER`)
  - assets/ui/src/lib/visibility/candidates.ts:26-35 (`NOISE_REASONS` subset)
  - assets/ui/src/lib/i18n.ts:1217-1232 (en) and :5127-5141 (de), plus the `reasonVariant` switch at assets/ui/src/lib/components/settings/VisibilityAdmin.svelte:243-255.
What is true is the weaker statement the SPA itself writes at candidates.ts:37-39 ("Reasons the server sends that are absent here are appended in server order, so a new backend category shows up without a frontend release"): a new server reason does render a chip (proved by assets/ui/src/lib/visibility/candidates.test.ts:326-335), but with the raw key `unignore.reason.<x>` as its label — i18n.ts:7814 is `const value = cat[key] ?? EN[key] ?? key;` — an unstyled "muted" variant, and isNoiseReason() false. It would also fall outside the openapi enum and the TS union.

Recommended action is therefore a comment correction at reason.go:109-110, not a rule change: replace the "without a second enumeration" claim with the accurate one (the vocabulary is shipped so an unknown value renders rather than drops; label, order, noise-class and openapi enum are all separately maintained).
stands.guard: None. No test pins the store's reasonPrecedence order or membership against assets/openapi.yaml's UnIgnoreReason enum, the SPA's UnIgnoreReason union, REASON_ORDER, NOISE_REASONS, or the unignore.reason.* i18n keys. tests/contract/testdata/api_surface.json:2393 records `"UnIgnoreReason": []` — the contract snapshot carries no member list, so adding a reason to reason.go changes nothing there. internal/store/visibility/reason_test.go:470-486 (TestAllHiddenReasonsExcludesUnknown) only asserts unknown is absent, the list is non-empty and the slice is a copy. assets/ui/src/lib/visibility/candidates.test.ts:326-335 asserts an unknown server reason is appended — i.e. it pins the divergence-tolerant behaviour, not agreement. tests/contract/visibility_read_only_audit_test.go:46 pins the identifier name `checkMasterParameterIgnored` only.
stands.divergence: Reason `master_gate` vs `week_profile`, and `hidden`. Store order — internal/store/visibility/reason.go:92-105 `reasonPrecedence` = [operation_mode, week_profile, master_gate, device_specific, ignore_list, wildcard_prefix, wildcard_suffix, hidden, channel_restricted, event_suppressed, internal_flag, read_only]. SPA chip order — assets/ui/src/lib/visibility/candidates.ts:40-54 `REASON_ORDER` = [operation_mode, master_gate, week_profile, device_specific, hidden, ignore_list, wildcard_prefix, wildcard_suffix, channel_restricted, event_suppressed, internal_flag, read_only, unknown]. Concrete input: a candidate set containing both a `week_profile` and a `master_gate` group — the store's list returns week_profile before master_gate, presentReasons() (candidates.ts:208-225) renders master_gate before week_profile, because REASON_ORDER is consulted first and the server vocabulary only orders reasons REASON_ORDER does not know. Same for `hidden`: store position 8, SPA position 5. The SPA also carries `unknown`, which AllHiddenReasons explicitly excludes.
stands.deadCopy: None. Every cited site has a production caller: checkMasterParameterIgnored ← internal/store/visibility/decider.go:292 and reason.go:165; ApplyForceSensorMarks ← internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:1136; AllHiddenReasons ← internal/north/rest/handlers/visibility.go:483. The SPA-side REASON_ORDER / NOISE_REASONS / UnIgnoreReason are all reached from VisibilityAdmin.svelte (:87, :63/:147, :9-19).

stands.title: The P1..P6 profile-key syntax rule is written three times in three packages; the copies already disagree on "P01"
stands.evidence: schedule/climate.go:355-364 and weekprofile/rawconvert.go:325-334 are byte-identical bodies: `if len(k) < 2 || k[0] != 'P' { return false }` / `fmt.Sscanf(k, "P%d", &n)` / `return n >= 1 && n <= 6`. rawconvert.go:323-324 admits it verbatim: "// isValidProfileKey mirrors the schedule package helper but is package-local\n// to avoid importing it." adapter/schedules.go:1576-1581 is the third: `func isValidProfileID(s string) bool { if len(s) != 2 || s[0] != 'P' { return false }; n := int(s[1] - '0'); return n >= 1 && n <= 6 }`. grep across the repo returns three definitions and no shared exported helper. weekprofile/datapoint.go:545-552 is the device-derived layer: `for i := 1; i <= dp.profileCount; i++ { if key == fmt.Sprintf("P%d", i) { return nil } }`.

stands.divergence: The candidate's failure mechanism does not hold as written. Changing the store's spelling of "unreleased" is a no-op: the constant has no reader or writer, the value written to the column comes from coordinators.PhaseUnreleased (device.go:1153) and is read back against the same constant (device.go:220). Changing the store's "pending" also cannot "silently re-park configured devices": the coordinator's load treats PhaseUnreleased as the only special case and everything else falls to the parked branch (device.go:219-224), so an unrecognised pending spelling still parks, which is what it already did. The reachable version of the described damage requires editing coordinators.PhaseUnreleased, where old rows holding "unreleased" would load into the parked set — a persisted-value migration hazard, made harder to see by the second declaration, not caused by it.

stands.title: The ping caller_id separator '#' is written as a bare literal on both the producing and the parsing side, with no shared constant
stands.negativeControl: Had the grammar been single-sourced, the grep would have shown one side referencing a shared constant or a parse helper exported from internal/client (which adapter already imports — it calls `entry.Client.WireBoundaryID()` on the very next line, so a shared symbol is available to it); instead each side carries its own `"#"` literal.
stands.reason: Producer and parser of one wire grammar, each deciding the separator independently. This is not the `EnumLabel`/`EnumLabelFromWire` shape (two readings of one datum, each right for its caller) — it is one datum's encode/decode pair, which must agree by construction and today agrees only by coincidence of two literals. Divergence would be silent: `hasToken` false means the PONG is dropped without a wire error, and unmatched PONGs decay interface health. The prose at event.go:494 does drift on the *prefix*: it documents the base as `<iface>` while the producer uses the wire-boundary triple (interface_client.go:746-752, `<instance>-<central>-<interface>`); the parser matches against `WireBoundaryID()`, so the code is consistent and only the comment understates it.

stands.title: The .sbk archive extension is a bare literal at eight decision points in two packages, with no shared constant — but the copies do not currently disagree
stands.evidence: All four cited lines verified verbatim at the cited numbers. backup_storage.go:162 `\t\tif !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".sbk") {` (inside `List`, followed at :175 by `\t\tid := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".sbk")`). backup_restorer.go:136-137 `\tif !strings.HasSuffix(filename, ".sbk") {` / `\t\tfilename += ".sbk"` (inside `buildMultipart`, the restore upload to the CCU). stubs.go:326 `\treturn fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s-%s.sbk", host, version, at.Format("2006-01-02-1504"))` (`ccuArchiveName`). backup.go:269 and :276, both `\t\treturn id + ".sbk"` (`downloadFilename`, the error path and the not-found path). Two further non-test literals the candidate did not list: backup_storage.go:343 `\treturn strings.TrimSuffix(archive, ".sbk") + backupNameSuffix, nil` (`namePathForID`) and backup_storage.go:371 `\tpath := filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".sbk"))` (`pathForID`). No shared constant exists: `grep -rn 'const.*sbk\|= "\.sbk"' --include="*.go"` finds only `backupNameSuffix` and only for the sidecar — backup_storage.go:278 `const backupNameSuffix = ".name"`. The `internal/backup/sbk` package that owns archive identity exports no extension either; its constants are the tar member names, sbk.go:32-38 `// Member names inside the archive, as written by the CCU.` / `const (` / `\tmemberConfig    = "usr_local.tar.gz"` / … The upload path does not gate on the extension at all — handlers/backup.go:391 `\t\tinfo, err := sbk.InspectBytes(data)` validates structurally, and SaveUploaded discards the uploaded name entirely (backup_storage.go:455-457 `func (s *FilesystemBackupStorage) SaveUploaded(` / `\tctx context.Context, _ string, data []byte,`).
stands.negativeControl: Two checks, both able to come out the other way. (1) Duplication: had the claim been false, the grep for `.sbk` in non-test Go would have returned one definition site plus identifier references — exactly the shape the sibling suffix produces, where `.name` appears literally once (backup_storage.go:278) and every other use is `backupNameSuffix` (backup_storage.go:343, and the tests at backup_storage_test.go:672, :716, :769, :1787, :1898). Instead `.sbk` returns eight distinct string literals in non-test code. The control fires: the same grep distinguishes the constant-backed suffix from the literal-backed one in the same file. (2) Divergence: had the copies disagreed I would have seen a differing spelling — a `.SBK`, a `strings.EqualFold` / `strings.ToLower` on one side only, an alternative accepted suffix, or a site appending nothing. Every one of the eight is the identical lowercase `".sbk"` compared or concatenated case-sensitively, so this check returns "no divergence" — and it is the check that would have shown one.
stands.reason: One domain fact — "a CCU system backup archive is named *.sbk" — is decided independently at eight points in two packages (`internal/central/adapter` and `internal/north/rest/handlers`), covering four distinct roles: recognition (List's suffix filter and its TrimSuffix), path construction (pathForID, namePathForID), display-name composition (ccuArchiveName), and the two filenames that leave the daemon (the HTTP download name, the restore multipart name). These are not two readings of one datum each correct for its caller; all eight want the same string, and the file that holds four of them demonstrates the alternative one line away with `const backupNameSuffix = ".name"`. Two corrections to the claim as written. It says "three packages" — it is two: backup_storage.go, backup_restorer.go and stubs.go are all `package adapter` (line 4 of each), only handlers/backup.go is elsewhere. And it undercounts the literals: four, not one, live in backup_storage.go. Severity is low, and deliberately so, because the claim's consequence is conditional, not present. The copies agree today on every input I could construct: uploaded archives get `Filename` "" (backup_storage.go:468-470 `// No display name: the uploaded one is untrusted (see above) and there is` / `// no CCU behind this archive to derive one from. It lists and downloads as` / `` // `<id>.sbk`, which is honest about where it came from.``) so downloadFilename falls through to `id + ".sbk"`, and CCU-taken archives get a `ccuArchiveName` that already ends `.sbk`, so the download name and the on-disk name match. The finding is the fan-out itself: the described failure — a suffix change that misses List, making stored archives invisible while restore still accepts them — is a real property of the current shape, not an observed defect.
stands.divergence: None found. All eight non-test occurrences are the identical lowercase literal `".sbk"`, compared and concatenated case-sensitively; no site accepts an alternative or folds case.

needsInput.title: Profile count is derived twice from the same descriptors with different bounds and tie-breaks
needsInput.evidence: Quotes verified verbatim. schedule_io.go:88-98: 'if n, ok := rawJSONInt(pd.Max); ok && n >= 1 && n <= defaultProfileCap { return n, nil }' and 'if n, ok := rawJSONInt(pd.Max); ok && n >= 0 && n < defaultProfileCap { return n + 1, nil }', with 'const defaultProfileCap = 6' at schedule_io.go:53 - both inside 'for _, ch := range dev.Channels()' and both returning immediately. week_profile_filter.go:498-506: 'if dp := ch.Parameter(hmenum.ParameterActiveProfile); dp != nil { pd := dp.ParameterData(); if pd.Max != nil { if v, ok := parseFloat(pd.Max); ok && int(v) >= 1 { meta.ProfileCount = int(v) } } }' - inside 'for _, ch := range d.Channels()' (week_profile_filter.go:483) with no break and no upper bound. Both decoders are equivalent (rawJSONInt at schedule_io.go:110 and parseFloat at week_profile_filter.go:45 both json.Unmarshal the same json.RawMessage). Both live: MaxProfilesForDevice is called from schedules.go:1097 (SetActiveProfile), schedule_io.go:271 (SetSchedule), :419 (SetProfile), :496/:505 (CopyProfileTo), :374-375 (CopyScheduleTo); deriveWeekProfileMetadata is called from week_profile_filter.go:453 in the boot refinement pass, feeding ProfileDataPoint.ApplyDeviceMetadata (internal/model/weekprofile/datapoint.go:298-305), which sets dp.profileCount, which AvailableProfiles (datapoint.go:441-452) turns into P1..P<profileCount> with no cap.
needsInput.divergence: Exact input: a channel whose ACTIVE_PROFILE ParameterData.Max is 7. MaxProfilesForDevice - rawJSONInt yields 7, the guard 'n <= defaultProfileCap' fails, the WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER branch does not match, the loop ends and schedule_io.go:100 returns 6. deriveWeekProfileMetadata - parseFloat yields 7, 'int(v) >= 1' passes, meta.ProfileCount = 7, so AvailableProfiles returns [P1..P7] to REST (internal/north/rest/handlers/week_profile.go:154), MCP (internal/north/mcp/tools_hub.go:621) and MQTT discovery (internal/north/mqtt/discovery_week_profile.go:71). The operator picks P7; SetActiveProfile rejects it at schedules.go:1093 via isValidProfileID (n=7 > 6) with ErrInvalidProfileID. Second exact input: ACTIVE_PROFILE present on two channels with different Max, e.g. :1 Max=3 and :5 Max=6. Device.Channels() is sorted by address (internal/model/device/device.go:586), so MaxProfilesForDevice returns 3 (first hit, immediate return) and deriveWeekProfileMetadata returns 6 (last hit wins, no break) - the write cap and the advertised count name different numbers on the same device.
needsInput.deadCopy: Neither. Both have live production callers, listed in evidence.
needsInput.guard: None comparing the two. internal/central/adapter/week_profile_refine_test.go exercises deriveWeekProfileMetadata alone (TestDeriveWeekProfileMetadataPrefersActiveProfileOverPointer, ...LooksAcrossChannels, ...RFPointerOnly); internal/central/adapter/schedule_profile_count_test.go and schedule_io_test.go exercise MaxProfilesForDevice alone. No test feeds one descriptor set through both.
needsInput.negativeControl: Had the two agreed, week_profile_filter.go:502 would carry the same '<= defaultProfileCap' bound and a first-wins break; it carries only 'int(v) >= 1' and the loop at :483 runs to completion. And had AvailableProfiles been capped independently, datapoint.go:447-450 would clamp; it builds P1..P<profileCount> unconditionally, so a ProfileCount of 7 does reach the north-bound surfaces.
needsInput.reason: Both halves of the claim - differing upper bound and differing tie-break - verified in the source, both derivations live, no guard. The consequence is the one the candidate names and it is real end to end: an advertised profile the write path refuses with ErrInvalidProfileID. Medium.
needsInput.secondReason:
I could not kill the structural claim and I could not confirm the damage. Refutation attempts that failed: (1) 'two readings of one datum for two callers' does not apply — their fallback semantics do legitimately differ (schedule_io returns 6 when absent as a permissive write default per its doc at :63-68; derive returns 0, which ApplyDeviceMetadata treats as leave-alone per datapoint.go:295), but the upper clamp and the first-vs-last rule are extraction rules with no caller-specific justification, and derive's missing clamp lets it violate the range its own field doc declares, `// ProfileCount is the number of named profiles the device supports (1..6).` at datapoint.go:193. (2) 'the type system forces it' — no; both read hmproto.ParameterData.Max through equivalent decoders. (3) 'one site is dead' — no; both are reached from the production pipeline and from the REST/MCP/MQTT write and read surfaces respectively. (4) 'a shared root-channel asymmetry explains it' — no; refineAttachedWeekProfiles appends RootChannel only to locate the week profile (week_profile_filter.go:444-447), while derive itself walks d.Channels() exactly as MaxProfilesForDevice does. (5) 'the divergence is filtered downstream' — partly: SetActiveProfile's `isValidProfileID` (schedules.go:1576-1582, `return n >= 1 && n <= 6`) hard-caps at 6, so a P7 advertised by derive is rejected there rather than written, which bounds the blast radius to a rejected write with a typed error, not a bad write. That is why I put severity at low rather than the candidate's medium.

What is missing is a single value: whether any Homematic device's ACTIVE_PROFILE (or WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER) VALUES descriptor declares MAX above 6, and whether any device carries that parameter on two or more channels with differing MAX. Both of the candidate's exact inputs hinge on it and neither is derivable from the repo. Asserting either shape would be substituting a plausible convention for a value the source does not carry, which is the failure this pass exists to prevent — so the verdict is needs-input, not confirmed. The structural finding is real and cheaply fixed regardless (give derive the same `<= defaultProfileCap` clamp and the same first-wins rule, or better, have refineAttachedWeekProfiles call MaxProfilesForDevice, which the comment at week_profile_filter.go:79 already claims it does: `// that is refined later by [SchedulesDomain.MaxProfilesForDevice]` — that claim is itself false, the refiner is deriveWeekProfileMetadata).

killed.title: Default-central selection is defined three ways, one of them alphabetical
killed.why: Killed on two of the five bites. Sameness: these are four per-caller policies, each with its own written contract and its own fail mode (backup = documented backward-compatible default with a scoped sibling; maintenance = deliberate refuse-unless-exactly-one; CCU auth = documented tier rule; pickFirstCentral = documented label-only helper) — not one rule implemented four times, so unifying them would change three documented behaviours. Damage: the medium-severity story, an archive minted under a CCU the operator did not pick, cannot occur through the SPA, because BackupList.svelte:108-110 passes triggerCentral precisely when more than one central exists; the unscoped path is left for single-central installs (where all rules agree, as the finding itself concedes) and for a raw API caller who omits the field and gets the documented default. What genuinely survives is smaller than the finding: the phrase `first registered central` is false wording in three comments (stubs.go:46-47, internal/north/rest/handlers/backup.go:29-31, internal/central/adapter/ccu_wiring.go:101-104) since Registry.List sorts by name — a comment-claim fix for the next sweep, not a backlog entry about duplicated selection logic. Second, smaller residue: the CCU-auth resolver's empty-name default is name-sorted on the DB tier and config-ordered on the YAML tier, reachable only with `north.rest.auth.ccu.central` unset on a multi-CCU install.

killed.title: The recovery pipeline's stage timings and reconnect gate are duplicated per transport
killed.why: Killed on sameness and on the divergence evidence. (1) The eight-stage configuration is single-sourced in DefaultRecoveryPipeline; what the two sites supply is a RecoveryStageDeps literal, which is the struct's documented purpose ("injectable function-pointers that back each stage", recovery_stages.go:14-16) and whose doc annotation at :89 names both adapters as its callers. Two callers of one parameterised rule, not two copies of the rule. (2) The residue that IS textually duplicated is two duration literals plus the reconnect closure body; TCPProbe deliberately differs and cuxd_wiring.go:441-443 documents why (`// Same stages as the XML-RPC path, with one difference: the TCP probe dials` / `// CUxD's own BIN-RPC port instead of a CCU interface port`). Each side also captures different variables (ccForRecovery/capturedBackend/capturedInitID vs t.cc/t.backend/t.initID), so the deps literal is the parameterisation point, not accidental copy. (3) The offered proof of realised drift measures a different line. SetHubRefresher sits on the shared coordinator, outside RecoveryStageDeps, with one non-test caller at ccu_wiring.go:975. Deduplicating the two deps literals would not move that line by one character, and both literals already pass the identical LoadData step. The CUxD-only-central asymmetry, if real, is a separate defect about a coordinator-level dependency injected from inside a transport-specific wiring path — not evidence that the duplicated timings drifted. (4) Damage from the residual duplication: cooldown/warmup skew between transports after a connection loss, visible only as reconnect latency and log timing; no invariant, no wire contract, no guard bites.

killed.title: The device-removal eviction policy (30 s bound + skip-on-ModelTeardown) is written out three times
killed.why: Killed on the sameness bite and on its own supporting evidence. (1) The three 30 s constants are a shared shape, not a shared rule: each bounds its own single-row DELETE against its own store, nothing couples them, and drift between them produces no observable behaviour — the drift bite fails outright. (2) The ModelTeardown guard is a real shared rule (ADR 0042), but the bodies are not interchangeable: values/master call `e.store.DeleteDevice(ctx, ev.CentralName, ev.InterfaceID, ev.Address)` against two distinct store types, while channel flags calls a two-argument `e.store.DeleteDevice(ctx, ev.CentralName, ev.Address)` plus an in-memory `e.overlay.DeleteDevice(...)` (channel_flags_evict.go:63) — three subscribers over three concrete store types, which is what forces the repeated conditional. (3) The reason the candidate rated it worth acting on — 'only the channel-flags copy has a ModelTeardown guard test' — is refuted for values_cache by central_bringup_test.go:606, a behavioural test the token grep could not see. The residue that survives is a different, narrower finding and not a duplication one: `WireMasterValuesEviction` has no test anywhere (grep for it returns only master_values_evict.go and cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_southbound.go:296), so the MASTER evictor's teardown guard is genuinely unpinned. That belongs in the backlog as 'MasterValuesEvictor is untested', not as 'a policy is written out three times'.

killed.title: The device-eviction rule is written out three times and the three have already drifted
killed.why: The drift is real but every claimed consequence is impossible on the only live path. The rows the candidate says 'survive reinit' were deleted by cachereset.Service.Clear moments earlier, unconditionally, from the same stores; and a leftover channel description can never re-materialise a device because CheckAndCreateDevicesFromCache skips colon addresses and the device-root description IS deleted by clearModel. So the 'resurrection class the repo has fixed twice' does not apply here, and 'high' is unsupported. What genuinely remains is different and milder, and would have to be re-filed on its own evidence: because clearModel never calls DescRegistry.Delete for channels or ParamsetReg.DeleteChannel for the root address, descriptorSink.forget is never called for those keys (descriptor_persistence.go:85-89, 122-127, 161-171), so their content hashes stay in devHashes/psHashes; the re-pull re-Puts identical content, `unchanged` returns true, and the rows cachereset just deleted are never rewritten — the persisted warm-boot cache stays short its channel-description and device-root-MASTER rows until the content changes or the daemon restarts. That is a degraded warm cache, not a ghost device, and it is the opposite of 'the rows survive'.

killed.title: Device room/function assignment is unioned over channels twice, with different inputs, and the two disagree
killed.why: Two readings of one datum for two callers, not one rule duplicated. The eager stamp is an optimistic local recomputation from the live model immediately after a channel write, where the DeviceDetails cache is by definition stale (5-minute refresh job); the refresh is the CCU-truth reconciler and is the only one that can see device-direct assignments. Neither can use the other's input at its own call site. The claimed loss is not drift but the documented contract, in the very comment the candidate quotes as evidence: device_admin.go:445-449 'the parent device's Rooms are recomputed as the union over all channels; device-direct assignments reappear with the next periodic assignment refresh', reinforced at :478-481. The window is bounded and self-correcting, and the finding also mis-cites the second writer (buildAssignments writes no device field) and the publish line. Finally, the claimed diverging input needs a value the repo does not carry — see missingInput — so even the divergence itself is not demonstrable from the source. Not worth a backlog entry as a duplication finding; if the 5-minute stale window on a device-direct assignment is judged unacceptable, that is a product decision about SetChannelRooms, not a drifted copy.

killed.title: The ENUM-index-to-label projection is implemented twice, verbatim, in the same file
killed.why: The projection is single-sourced in internal/parameter/enum.go:80; the cited sites are two call sites of it, and the specific divergences the finding predicts are structurally impossible because they live in the shared function. The remaining repetition is a defensive type guard whose unilateral change is a no-op on every input the helper already rejects.

killed.title: The custom-DP slot repair rule ("channel 0 means unset") is duplicated between the state and the config publisher
killed.why: The literal duplication is real and I could not kill it on quote, sameness, or liveness. It dies on the damage bite: the two cited copies govern the state and config topics, and the code's own comment (eventbridge.go:2337) records that HA discovery does not read the config topic, so their drift cannot produce the stated 'entity permanently unavailable' outcome — at worst a retained config topic under a different channel path for external consumers. The consequence that would matter (discovery's state_topic pointing at an unpublished topic) belongs to the third site, which is a documented superset with a different contract, not a copy under a same-ness obligation. Per the standing rule that a duplicate whose drift is not observably damaging is not a backlog entry, this is a low-value refactor note, not a medium finding.

killed.title: "Device address = the part before the first colon" is re-implemented four times in this partition while pkg/hmtypes.DeviceAddress is the canonical helper
killed.why: Killed on the divergence and damage bites, with the sameness bite weakening it further. The finding concedes its own case in the diverging-input field: "I found NO input a real CCU emits on which the four disagree". The one input it can name, ":1", is malformed and produces no observable difference — hmtypes.DeviceAddress, deviceOf, channelRegistered and interfaceForChannel all yield "" and then fail closed (registry miss → false, or ""), while buildAssignments' `i > 0` declines to stamp a parent entry keyed on the empty string, which is the *more* correct behaviour of the two, not a bug. So the divergence is not merely unreachable, it is benign where it exists. On damage: the postulated harm is "a future grammar change applied to four of five sites", but SERIAL:CHANNEL is a frozen CCU wire format, and were it to change the event would sweep hmtypes.DeviceAddress's 19 production callers too — a repo-wide migration, not something four adapter-local copies uniquely endanger. The finding's own CCU-mutating vector is already defended at the call site: groups_write.go:210 and :239 both guard `dev == ""` before DeviceRegaID and SetInHeatingGroupMetadata, so the empty result never reaches the CCU. On sameness, the inventory does not hold up in either direction. hub_wiring.go:777 is not a fifth extraction of the rule; it is a guard predicate — "does this address have a non-empty device part before a colon" — inlined to decide whether to stamp a parent, and rewriting it through the helper needs a different expression (`if dev := hmtypes.DeviceAddress(addr); dev != addr && dev != ""`). That leaves three exact behavioural copies, not five implementations. And the partition boundary is arbitrary: there is a sixth identical `deviceOf` at internal/model/device/definitionexport/export.go:211, another inline split at internal/model/hub/generic_data_point.go:146, and one inside pkg/hmtypes itself at datapoint_key.go:66 — so "four times in this partition" describes where the reviewer was looking, not where the duplicates are. This is the case the brief names as not worth a backlog entry: a duplicate that cannot drift on any input the system produces, and whose only drift is invisible and fail-closed. It is a legitimate tidy-up (route the three exact copies through hmtypes.DeviceAddress) but not a defect, and it should not carry medium severity.

killed.title: Profile specificity scoring and the active-profile selection loop are duplicated verbatim in the adapter and the store
killed.why: Killed as a separate backlog item, not as a fact. The duplication is real, but it is not a second finding: these four sites are the inside of matchActiveProfile and Store.MatchActiveProfile, the exact function pair c001 is about, and the scorers have no caller outside them. Any remediation of c001 — unifying the LINK matcher behind one implementation — necessarily consumes these sites, so filing them separately double-counts one duplicate and inflates the count of open defects. Judged on its own terms it also fails the standing bar for a duplication entry: the finding itself states nothing disagrees today, and the drift it points at as its strongest argument belongs to c001. Report it as part of c001's scope, not as an entry of its own.

killed.title: Two encoders for the flat climate MASTER paramset
killed.why: Killed on sameness and on damage. (1) Sameness: the overlap between the two 'encoders' is exactly two format strings for a key grammar the firmware fixes; the rest of the functions do different jobs — the adapter fuses validation + gap expansion over a request DTO (hmapi.ClimateSchedule), the model encodes an already-expanded 13-slot map (rawClimateSchedule) it never built. The finding's own evidence concedes they agree on every element they both emit ('Key grammar, 1-based ordinal and integer-minute ENDTIME agree today'). (2) The claimed divergence is not a drift between two copies of one rule at all: the bare, prefix-less grammar exists only in the adapter, only for a device class (HM-CC-RT-DN) the model path never encodes for. There is no shared rule 'emit prefix-less keys for a bare-schema device' that one copy implements and the other broke — the model layer simply has no bare-schema support, which is a missing feature in a dead path, not a duplication defect. (3) Damage: the scenario 'BuildClimateRawParamset would emit P1_ENDTIME_MONDAY_1 for a bare device, the CCU no-ops, and the operator is told the save succeeded' requires two hypotheticals stacked — someone first wiring the dead model encoder into a production write path, and then pointing it at a bare-schema thermostat. Nothing today can produce it. (4) Drift in the one thing genuinely spelled twice — the P<n>_ key grammar — is visible on both sides independently: changing either format string turns a test red (contract test for the model, adapter tests for both adapter encoders). A duplicate that agrees on every byte, is pinned on both sides, and whose only asymmetry is a feature the dead copy never had is not a backlog entry. The substantive half of this pair — that the two chains behave differently — is already captured by adapter-schedules-c001; c002 adds nothing beyond it.

killed.title: A chirp lasts one second on a siren and two seconds on an MP3 player, decided in two layers
killed.why: Three kills. (1) Sameness: these are two rules that share a shape, not one rule written twice. chirp.go:15-18's own comment scopes itself to the acoustic path — "bounds one confirmation-tone emission ... (S1 applies to every acoustic write)" — and S1 is the device-side auto-off that must travel with an acoustic write. The MP3 constant caps soundfile playback through a different wire parameter on a different device class. A pair of constants that already hold different values, in different units of meaning, is by definition not a copy. (2) Divergence: the claimed diverging input is not one input reaching two copies — it is two different outputs, with two different configs, resolving through two different DeviceResolver methods (`Siren` vs `Sound`, ports.go:84/:87). Nothing routes a single request through both. (3) Damage: the audible consequence rests on a value this repo does not carry. resolver.go:144's Duration is an upper bound, not a synthesised tone length — sound.go:374-375 says so explicitly ("DURATION is only included when the caller explicitly requests it — the device has its own default on-time"), and PlayChirp leaves RepetitionsIndex at its zero value, which sound.go:366-371 writes as the no-repeat label. The actual emission is min(soundfile length, 2 s), and the soundfile lives on the device. "A 2 s MP3 emission every 2 s is a continuous tone" substitutes the convention "duration cap equals emission length" for the one input that would decide it. That the port signature carries no duration (ports.go:76) is a real layering observation, but it is a design note, not a duplicated rule with observable drift.

killed.title: The device-address-from-channel-address rule is written four times inside/around the partition, and one copy uses different semantics than the canonical one
killed.why:
The quotes hold and the helper-level divergence is real (LastIndex vs Cut differ on >=2 colons), but it is unobservable and the count is wrong.

1. Damage: at all three live call sites the derived address is only ever an exact-match key into ModelRegistry, and the untouched full channelAddress is what actually selects the channel. For any two-colon input both semantics end at nil — the caller (alarm/resolver.go:164, alarm/inputs.go:478, adapter/values_cache_flush.go:538, ...) sees "channel not found" either way. Drift that cannot change an observable result is not a backlog entry.

2. Reachability of the diverging state: making the divergence visible requires a device registered under a colon-bearing address; the one production producer explicitly skips those (device_pipeline.go:421). The finding itself concedes the wire grammar cannot produce a two-colon address; what it did not check is that the operator/DB-supplied strings it names still terminate in nil on both paths.

3. Sameness: paramset.go:258 isChannelOf is not a fourth implementation of the derivation rule — it is a boolean containment predicate over (channel, device) that never produces a device address, and hmtypes carries no equivalent to deduplicate it against. The partition holds three statements of the derivation (queryfacade.go:529, central.go:1107, hmtypes/address.go:71), not four.

Residual, non-actionable at this severity: two in-package one-liners restate hmtypes.DeviceAddress, which the same tree already imports elsewhere (coordinators/event.go:543, adapter/device_reloader.go:99). That is a tidiness note, not a semantics divergence.

killed.title: valuesMatch re-derives value equality on raw `any` instead of reusing hmtypes normalization, and mismatches int32/int64 against the event's int
killed.why: Two rules that share a shape, not one datum: valuesMatch is deliberately fuzzy (state_change.go:33-35, :116-117), ParamValue.Equal is deliberately exact (value.go:198). Reusing hmtypes there would break the documented contract, so the dedup premise is wrong. The 'broken for its caller' half dies on liveness: valuesMatch has no production caller at all — the only path to it is gated on WriteOptions.WaitForCallback, which is set true only in two test files. The int32-vs-int default-branch mismatch and the []string `expected == actual` panic are real Go semantics, but neither input can reach the function outside internal/client's own tests, which pass only float64/float32/int/string/bool (interface_client_whitebox_test.go:101-143). Zero observable drift.

killed.title: The 60 s wait-for-confirmation default is a literal at three sites — and a fourth, the operator-facing config field, is never read
killed.why: The claimed divergence cannot occur. There is no configuration path that reaches TimeoutConfig at all — it is an unreferenced struct in internal/config, absent from every config struct, from example.config.yaml, and from the SPA catalogues — so 'timeouts.wait_for_callback: 10s vs the code path' is not an input an operator can supply, and the assertion that 'the two already disagree for every non-default configuration' is unfounded: there is no non-default configuration. That removes both the operator-visible no-op knob and the fourth site's membership in the same knowledge item. What remains is three literals inside one package on a path with no production caller (`grep -rn "WaitForCallback:"` returns zero non-test assignments; cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_wiring.go:186-189 says the same), one of them already shadowed. Drift between them would change nothing observable.

killed.title: The set of "infrastructure" RPC methods is defined twice, and the two copies already disagree
killed.why: Two rules that share a shape, not one rule copied. circuit.go:88-93 states its rule — "must be executed regardless of the circuit breaker state … getVersion / system.* allow diagnostics while the circuit is tripped" — over the breaker's *operationID* namespace, which demonstrably includes non-method pseudo-ops (`check_connection`) and ordinary writes (`setValue`, `putParamset`). classifier.go:109-110 states a different rule — "session / liveness calls that bypass read/write throttles entirely" — over RPC method names, as one of three partitions (readMethods/writeMethods/controlMethods) selecting a throttle pool.
