Nothing in the source asserts the two sets must be equal, and the two named differences are each defensible on the owning mechanism's own terms: getVersion is a diagnostic read that should survive an open breaker but is not a session/liveness call, and ccu.ping is a JSON-RPC liveness spelling for pool routing. The finding's own analysis concedes no diverging input occurs, and my caller trace makes that stronger than it claims: `init` never reaches InterfaceClient at all (central/adapter/xmlrpc_announcer.go:22-23 holds a raw `*xmlrpc.Client` and calls `a.client.Call(ctx, "init", ...)` at :33), and grep finds no production `Call(ctx, "getVersion"` (only tests/integration/*, which drive the raw transport) and no occurrence of the string `ccu.ping` outside classifier.go:119 anywhere in the repo. So most entries in *both* maps are dead on this path; the sets "already disagree" only in entries neither mechanism is ever fed. What remains is a coupling assertion the source does not carry, so treating the two maps as one duplicated rule would be substituting a convention for a stated invariant.

killed.title: HTTP-status classification is written four times across the two HTTP transports and already disagrees on 2xx and on 401/403
killed.why: Killed on three independent bites. (1) Liveness: two of the four cited sites (methods.go:803, :869) have no production caller — only methods_test.go — so the sharper damage claim, that a 401 on the CCU backup/firmware download is misclassified as a backend fault and thereby skips both the relogin branch and the non-retryable short-circuit, cannot occur in a running daemon. The live paths are CcuBackend.downloadBackup and CcuBackend.DownloadFirmware in ccu_extended.go, which classify nothing at all (bare fmt.Errorf, no hmerr sentinel), so they are not fourth and third copies of the classifier either. (2) The diverging input: the candidate's 401-on-CGI is contradicted by the only source statement about that endpoint (ccu_extended.go:662-665 — the CGI answers unauthenticated requests 200 + login page, not 401). I did not verify that comment against a live CCU and do not need to: the candidate offered no source for the 401 at all, and the repo's own reading points the other way. (3) Sameness and damage for the surviving pair: xmlrpc/client.go:193 and jsonrpc/client.go:339 are two rules with one shape, not one rule twice — the JSON-RPC branch is not a classifier but a session-recovery step (invalidateStaleSession / reloginLocked / recursive callOnce) that XML-RPC, using per-request basic auth, has no analogue for. The 2xx difference is real code but has no demonstrated input and no observable damage: for XML-RPC a 204 passes checkStatus and then fails four lines later at DecodeResponse (client.go:174-177), so both transports fail the call and only the error text and sentinel differ. Uncertain-but-unverified, stated as such: whether any CCU or fronting proxy ever emits a non-200 2xx on either endpoint is not answerable from this tree.

killed.title: The VALUES-then-MASTER paramset fallback is implemented twice in the same package
killed.why: Refuted on damage. The quote, the sameness and the liveness all survive — this genuinely is one trivial rule written twice in one package with no type-system excuse. But the severity rested entirely on invisible drift, and that is false: each copy has its own MASTER-fallback test, so any change that drops the rule from either side fails immediately. What remains is eight duplicated lines whose divergence would be caught on first run — a cosmetic cleanup (make resolveDP delegate to ParamFromAnyParamset), not a medium backlog entry, and not a defect. Per the brief, a duplicate whose drift is visible is not worth an entry.

killed.title: Exported cover capability presets duplicate the constructors' inline literals — and the garage pair already disagrees
killed.why: Killed on sameness and on damage. GarageCaps does not duplicate the constructor literal; it duplicates ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/custom/capabilities/cover.py:55-60, which it matches exactly, and init.go:82-83 plus init_test.go:223-225 say so. Deduplicating the two would break the parity assertion — they are two different data (what the reference declares vs. what this daemon's garage actually supports), not one rule stated twice. The claimed observable damage is unreachable: the finding's own grep shows no caller, so no Garage anywhere — production or test — is ever built from GarageCaps, and cdpkind therefore cannot emit `"position": true` for any garage. CoverCaps/BlindCaps agree with the constructors today and are test-fixture-only, so nothing measurable rests on them either. The 'second independent drift' is verified as text (snapshot_pin_test.go:636, generator_test.go:625, reference_compare_test.go:468 all read `caps := custom.CoverCapabilities{SupportsVent: true}`) but is a test fixture choosing its own set inside tests/, not a production restatement — and it does not touch the presets at all.

killed.title: The 153/500 mired range is defined three times in the same package
killed.why: Three constant blocks with one numeric value but three distinct rules — a reference-pinned conversion basis, a Matter clamp, and a production-dead fallback — and no coupling: the per-device range flows from the CCU descriptor into both north planes without touching any of them. The headline divergence (HA min_mireds 152 vs Matter physical min 153) rests on MaxKelvin ≥ 6536, a value that exists in this repo only in payload_discovery_test.go:260 as a test input; no device descriptor extract in the tree carries a COLOR_TEMPERATURE MAX, so whether any real light triggers it is not measurable here. What does survive is a different, smaller defect the finding raised in passing and that is fully derivable from code: on the RF white-point family (RfDimmer_Color_Temp, registered at init.go:74), colorLevel is used only when no COLOR_TEMPERATURE data point resolves (color.go:306-308), which is exactly the case in which kelvinBoundsFromChannel returns (0,0) and the constructor defaults MaxKelvin to 6500 — while Kelvin() returns kelvinFromColorLevel(1.0) = 1_000_000/153 = 6535 (pinned by colortemp_rf_test.go:90) and is not clamped (color.go:321-334). SetKelvin(6500) writes colorLevelFromKelvin(6500) = (500 - 1000000/6500=153)/347 = 1.0 exactly, so the state topic can publish color_temp_kelvin = 6535 above the max_kelvin = 6500 the discovery payload advertises (payload.go:891). That is a state-above-advertised-maximum bug, not the triplicate-constant finding as filed.

killed.title: 'Strip the duplicated device-name prefix' is implemented twice with different trimming
killed.why: Refuted on the damage bite and half of the sameness bite. The code fact (two prefix-strips, different trimming) is real, but neither drift direction is dangerous: the dead copy cannot change any shipped name because normaliseChannelName has zero production callers through any of its five entry points, and the live copy is directly pinned by internal/model/naming/namedata_test.go:101 and :21-27, so the first pass's stated reason for medium ('the surviving copy is unguarded') is false. What remains after the attack is a DIFFERENT finding with a different title, which I flag rather than smuggle in under this id: internal/model/device/naming.go carries an entire obsolete second naming pipeline (normaliseChannelName + DataPointName + DataPointFullName + CustomDataPointName + CustomDataPointFullName + Channel.FullName, all production-dead) and tests/golden/naming_test.go:353-357 certifies it as if it were the product. Its case 1 (tests/golden/naming_test.go:60-72: DeviceName 'Wohnzimmer Licht', ChannelName 'Wohnzimmer Licht-Kanal', Parameter 'LEVEL', WantDpName 'Kanal LEVEL') is not what the live pipeline returns for those inputs -- see the divergence field. That is a live-looking dead feature plus a golden fixture freezing behaviour nobody ships, which is worth an entry under its own title; 'the prefix strip is written twice' is not.

killed.title: The numeric wire-value acceptance set is written out three times in this package
killed.why:
Killed on the divergence and on the sameness; the liveness half is right but supports a different, smaller finding.

The divergence cannot occur. The claimed input — float32(1) on a CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE parameter — is filtered upstream by the type system plus coerceWire. Because no DataPoint is instantiated at float32 and OnWireValue is the only door, RawValue on that parameter yields int32 or string, both of which readChannelOperationModeFrom handles (channel.go:693, :699). The `case float32:` in copies 1 and 2 is unreachable defensive code, not a case copy 3 is missing.

The sameness fails for copy 3. It is a different rule with a different return type: readChannelOperationModeFrom (channel.go:684-705) maps a raw enum value to a *label*, routing every numeric arm through resolveValueListIndex, and carries a `case string:` arm the other two do not. It is the EnumLabel-vs-EnumLabelFromWire shape the brief names — one datum read two ways for two callers. Its numeric arms exist to index a VALUE_LIST, not to coerce a measurement to float64. Three functions sharing the vocabulary of Go numeric types is a shared shape, not a shared rule.

What is real, and smaller than raised: copies 1 and 2 are byte-identical, five arms in the same order, in the same package — availability.go and channel.go are both `package device`, so ParameterFloatValue's inline switch at channel.go:594-606 could call floatFromRaw directly. And ParameterFloatValue has no production caller: grep across the tree finds it only in internal/model/device/channel_parameter_accessor_test.go (six cases at :150-227, including TestChannelParameterFloatValueFloat32 pinning the unreachable arm). Its doc comment at channel.go:578-581 states "Used by the climate discovery builder to read the operator-configured TEMPERATURE_MINIMUM / TEMPERATURE_MAXIMUM bounds" — no such caller exists. That is a dead exported method with a false consumer claim, worth one line in the pre-release comment-claims sweep; it is not a three-way duplicate with live drift.

killed.title: Message set-equality is defined three times, and two of the definitions ignore most fields
killed.why: Three of the finding's load-bearing claims fail against the source. (1) 'One rule written three times with two answers' — the type system forbids a common body: ServiceMessage holds two []string fields so `!=` does not compile, AlarmMessage holds time.Time where `==` is semantically wrong; only InboxDevice is comparable. What remains is one duplicated pair, not a three-way divergence. (2) The named diverging input does not occur on the path claimed: the service-messages refresh is registered with needsDevicesReady=true (internal/central/jobs.go:676) and therefore runs through gatedRunWithDevicesCreatedGate (jobs.go:324-336), which returns nil while `!unit.IsDevicesCreated()`; the job additionally first fires only after its 5-minute slot (defaultServiceMessagesSlot, jobs.go:189), so 'a refresh that runs before the owning channel is registered' has no boot-path window. (3) 'the WS hub-event stream keeps the previous row' is false — that stream never carries rows, only a count, and an enrichment-only change leaves the count identical. What survives is a narrower, differently-shaped defect worth re-filing on its own terms: internal/client/rega/scripts/get_service_messages.fn reads `device_name` from `oChannel.Name()` and rooms/functions from `oChannel.ChnRoom()` / `oChannel.ChnFunction()`, while id/timestamp/counter come from the alarm object (`oAlarm.ID()`, `AlOccurrenceTimeSeconds()`, `AlCounter()`) — so a CCU-side channel rename or room/function assignment changes the enrichment with the identity triple untouched, sameServiceSet returns true, and the retained MQTT raw-plane payload keeps the old names until an unrelated change or a restart. That is a single-plane retained-payload staleness, not a two-plane disagreement, and it does not rest on the InterfaceID race the finding argued from.

killed.title: Two independent flattenings of one slog record — the capture archive and the live-log ring already disagree on records carrying a msg/level/time attribute
killed.why: Killed on the sameness bite, which is the rule this series states explicitly: two readings of one datum for two callers, each right for its caller, are not a duplicate. The knowledge that is genuinely shared — how a slog.Value becomes a JSON-able Go value — is already factored out and called by both: attrValue at capture.go:270-305, invoked at capture.go:254 and livelog.go:128. What is left in each function is not a copy of a rule but the shape its own consumer requires, and the two shapes are mutually exclusive. encodeRecord must produce one flat object because logs.ndjson is grepped and parsed line-by-line and is meant to mirror the daemon's own JSON log; buildLogRecord must keep Msg, Level and Time as typed struct fields because LogRecord is the wire DTO the log viewer receives (json tags at livelog.go:27-33) and because lvl backs Snapshot/Since filtering. A unified flattener would have to pick one namespace and would break the other caller. The divergence the finding cites is a consequence of that split, not drift between copies, and it therefore cannot be fixed by sharing code — which is why it does not belong in a duplication ledger. Two further points weaken the framing as posed. First, the copy the finding calls broken is the one whose behaviour is documented as intentional: capture.go:246-247 states \"Record attributes are written last and win on a key collision, matching slog's own precedence.\" Second, the finding's damage story rests on the live ring being the correct reading and the archive the wrong one, but measured against the daemon's actual log output it is the ring that is the outlier. I read the stdlib: commonHandler.handle writes the built-in time/level/msg keys and then calls state.appendNonBuiltIns(r) with no collision check (toolchain@v0.0.1-go1.26.6 src/log/slog/handler.go), so the inner slog.NewJSONHandler wired at pkg/hmlog/factory.go:171 already emits a line with two \"msg\" keys for callback_handlers.go:805-808, and any JSON parser reading stdout takes the last one — the CCU payload — exactly as the archive does. What does survive, and what I am not asking anyone to discard, is a narrower single-site defect that is not about duplication at all: encodeRecord collapses the stdlib's duplicate key into a map, so the record message \"callback.error\" disappears from logs.ndjson entirely rather than merely losing to the attr, and an operator grepping the archive by message finds nothing where grepping the stdout log finds the line. That is a collision-handling bug in encodeRecord against its own stated contract of matching slog's JSON handler, affecting three known keys (msg, level, time), and it should be filed as its own correctness item with the remedy being a reserved-key rename in encodeRecord — not as a shared-knowledge item whose implied remedy is unification.

killed.title: MASTER-paramset relevance is implemented twice; the ModelValidator copy has no production caller and is fed the wrong channel
killed.why: Refuted on three independent legs. (1) Not a duplicate: decider.go:352 and model_validator.go:116 are two granularities of one datum — a per-(channel,paramset) load gate and a per-parameter surface gate — and the reference the package ports carries the identical pair (model_validator.py:84 key-membership vs parameter_decider.py:270 value-membership) applied in sequence at model/__init__.py:103-120, which registry.go:134+:137 mirrors. (2) The title's liveness claim is wrong: IsRelevantParamset IS called in production via registry.go:134 from internal/central/adapter/paramsets.go:561. Only the two setters are test-only, and that is a separate, already-recorded observation. (3) The claimed divergence is two correct answers to two questions, cannot be produced through the façade (which always passes channelNoUnknown), and cannot change any outcome: with no production setter caller the validator's MASTER branch returns true unconditionally, so the dropped channel argument at registry.go:134 is provably inert rather than latent-with-a-bite.

killed.title: "The sole registered central is the implicit target" is decided independently in two adapters with different failure semantics
killed.why: Killed on the sameness test at the two sites that carried the finding's weight. config_export.go:96 answers a different question — 'which central owns this channel address', documented verbatim at :80-82 and backed by the first-match contract at paramsets.go:601-605 — not 'is there exactly one central'; with it goes the claimed MASTER/VALUES-write-to-the-wrong-CCU consequence, which the candidate had itself labelled unverified (it also needs a value the source does not carry: whether two registered centrals can hold the same device address). daemon_helpers.go:361 is the contract-documented producer of the empty name, not a rival resolver. What remains is four sites sharing a three-line cardinality predicate whose only variation is each domain's own error sentinel — and ADR 0002 plus TestCentralRegistryLookupRequiresName make that per-caller decision deliberate rather than duplicated knowledge. The residual worth logging separately, if anything, is one status-code inconsistency: device_replace maps the ambiguous case to 404 'Central not found' (handlers/device_replace.go:120-123) where rooms maps it to 400 'Central name required' (handlers/rooms_admin.go:54-56).

killed.title: The output driver re-derives an optical-selection default by list position, while the acoustic half of the same paramset is answered by the model from the descriptor
killed.why:
The finding dies on sameness and on both claimed divergences.

Sameness: the two halves are not one rule read twice. DisableAcousticLabel answers "which label silences this channel" — a question the HmIP descriptor does answer, because DEFAULT is DISABLE_ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL. manager.go:476 answers "which label produces the most visible flash" — a question no field of the paramset description carries. There is no model-side function for it (verified against every method on *Siren), so the code cannot be "moved back into the model" — doing so would relocate the same positional convention behind a nicer signature, not remove it. Two different questions, one of which has a descriptor answer, is not a layering asymmetry; it is the descriptor being silent on one of them.

Damage: the medium severity rests entirely on "a silent no-flash burglary failure" for a device whose OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION list is not disable-first/flash-last. The finding declines to assert such a device, and the repo carries exactly one real optical descriptor (siren_selection_wire_test.go:38-41, [DISABLE_OPTICAL_SIGNAL, BLINKING_ALTERNATELY_REPEATING, BLINKING_BOTH_REPEATING]), on which lights[len-1] is a genuine flash pattern. Whether any HmIP siren orders its list otherwise is a value the source does not carry — so the damage half is unverified, not confirmed, and it cannot carry a medium.

What is left after the attack is narrow and different from what was filed: manager.go:473-477 and testfire.go:78-82 hold the same three lines, both live, no divergence today; drift would only make a test fire flash a different pattern than a real fire. That is a low-value tidy-up, not the reported defect. Note also that the layer the finding treats as principled is itself positional at the bottom — action_select.go:71 falls back to `values[0]` — so the asymmetry it names is smaller than stated even on its own terms.

One sub-question survives, and it is not the filed one: `p = lights[len(lights)-1]` is a convention ("last entry is the most conspicuous") standing in for a datum the paramset description does not carry. If that is worth a backlog entry, it should be filed as a positional-convention finding against manager.go:476/testfire.go:81 with the missing input named — the ordering semantics of OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION VALUE_LIST across HmIP siren models — not as a layering asymmetry against siren.go:190.

killed.title: 'Capability unsupported' is detected by error-message string equality, not errors.Is
killed.why: The quote is accurate and the string-equality/doc-comment mismatch is real, but the finding's two load-bearing claims — 'mechanism confirmed and live' and the drift damage landing 'out of the boot-time description fetch' — are both false. All five isUnsupported call sites sit in InterfaceClient wrapper methods with no production caller; the daemon's real description, paramset and device-detail fetches call backends.Operations and the JSON-RPC client directly and never consult isUnsupported. A future wrap of ErrUnsupported in a backend therefore changes nothing observable through this mechanism: the drift is invisible outside the unit tests that construct these wrappers themselves. What actually survives is smaller than the finding and differently shaped: an inaccurate doc comment at :939, a vacuous test (internal/client/interface_client_whitebox_test.go:82 `_ = isUnsupported(wrapped) // either true or false — must not panic`), and four ratchet exemptions in tests/contract/empty_absent_failed_collapse_test.go:33-36 whose justification 'guarded by isUnsupported(err)' defends code the daemon never executes. That last observation is a separate, arguably stronger finding (dead capability-probe wrappers carrying contract exemptions) and should be raised on its own terms rather than as evidence for this one.

killed.title: The ENUM index-to-VALUE_LIST rule is re-derived in model/custom although internal/parameter owns it
killed.why: The finding pairs the wrong two functions and names the wrong owner. custom.EnumLabelValue is the Sensor[int32] sibling of generic.Select.Label (which resolve.go:109 cites by name), not a re-derivation of parameter.EnumLabel: it adds nil and unobserved as distinct falsy outcomes and cannot take EnumLabel's string branch. model/custom already delegates to parameter.EnumLabel where that reading fits (replay.go:70), so the split is deliberate rather than overlooked. What actually recurs across the four sites is a three-line slice-bounds idiom that Go's index semantics force and that carries no policy freedom to drift — and the codebase already diverges deliberately on the adjacent case (generic/action_select.go:151-157: checkEnumIndex permits any idx >= 0 when ValueList is empty), which is direct evidence these sites are not maintained as one rule.

killed.title: The group-slot binder walks only ChannelFields and ignores FixedChannelFields, which the shared resolver honours
killed.why: Three bites land. Divergence: none of the three claimed structural disagreements can be produced by the catalogue as written — `FixedChannelFields` is nil on every profile these binders see (the one non-nil instance, IPTextDisplay at profile_configs.go:473, carries BurstLimitWarning), `Fields`-declared group levels exist only on light profiles whose binder already reads `Fields`, and every group field is declared under exactly one channel key so map order and the AnyChannelOffset sentinel are unobservable. Damage: consequently nothing observable changes today — every path resolves the same channel and parameter. Sameness: the copies are also not a strict re-implementation of `ResolveFieldSlot`. They implement a different predicate — keep scanning channels until one carries the parameter in an acceptable DP shape (`custom.GroupLevelField`, or the `case *generic.Switch: / case *generic.BinarySensor:` switch) — whereas `resolveChannelKeyedField` commits to the first channel that merely *exists* on the device (field_resolve.go:73-83) and cannot resume. A drop-in substitution is therefore not behaviour-preserving in general; it agrees today only because no profile maps a group field onto two channels. "Five copies of one rule" overstates a shared loop shape wrapped around per-caller predicates. What survives is ordinary maintainability debt — a repeated walk-and-find-sibling loop, with light's copy carrying one extra branch its schema needs and the others' schemas do not — not a defect and not, on this evidence, a medium-severity backlog entry. If the concern is future catalogue edits (the catalogue is hand-maintained, profiles.go:4, ADR 0063), the honest instrument is a schema guard asserting that every declared group field lands in a block its binder reads — not a claim that the binders diverge today.

killed.title: The model compensates for a ReGa script's collision behaviour
killed.why:
Refuted on the divergence and on the cross-path contradiction.

1) The stated reproduction does not reproduce. Concrete input A is `POST /sysvars {"name":"HeizungOldVal","value_type":"BOOL"}` — no unit, no description, no value labels. hub_wiring.go:2159-2167 sends that to `SysVar.createBool` over JSON-RPC. `create_system_variable.fn` is not executed, its quit branch at :32-35 is not taken, and the empty-output check at hub_wiring.go:2224 is never reached. The finding's trace names three steps that the input it chose cannot take. Input B ("any sysvar … then POSTed") and input C are stated through the same mechanism and inherit the same error for the BOOL/FLOAT/ENUM shapes a caller would normally send.

2) The sameness argument is a conflation of two different creators. The finding says a second live path "treats the same script behaviour as a feature". It does not: internal/alarm/sysvar.go:273 → coordinators/hub.go:900 → hub_wiring.go:2682 → jsonrpc/methods.go:445 `SysVar.createEnum`, the CCU's own method. Loom's `create_system_variable.fn` is not on that path. So the repo is not simultaneously calling one script's collision no-op an error and an idempotency — the two paths run different code against different CCU entry points, and the alarm comment's own claim about a no-op is about the firmware method, not about the script the model comment describes. (Whether that alarm comment is itself accurate is a separate question: the firmware createenum.tcl carries no existence check, so it is at least unverified — but it is not this finding.)

3) The layering framing does not survive either. The pre-check at hub.go:744 is not script-specific compensation: the native branch it also guards (createBool/createFloat/createEnum) has no collision handling in the CCU firmware at all, so this mirror check is the only duplicate guard the daemon has on either path. Its comment is scoped honestly — "Reject a name the hub already mirrors here" — and the code does exactly that.

Residual, stated as unverified and not what was claimed: for a script-taking flavour only (INTEGER/STRING/ALARM, or any type with a unit, description or custom labels) against a name the mirror does not carry (excluded by sysvar.go:161, internal per hub_wiring.go:1187, or inside the 60 s refresh window), the collision quit branch does produce a 202 for a create that created nothing. That is a real but narrow gap in a best-effort cache check, it is not the input the finding cited, and its severity rationale ("inputs a user can hit without doing anything unusual") is exactly the class of input that takes the native path instead.

killed.title: State-colour rules: Go carries the rule name, the SPA carries every threshold and the ENUM index semantics — and the ENUM half already contradicts the domain
killed.why: Refuted on two independent grounds. (1) The cited mechanism is not the one that fires: parameterHint's "SMOKE_DETECTOR" substring (quantity.go:136) wins at HintFor:49 and enumShapeHint (:65) is unreachable for this parameter. (2) The claimed contradiction collapses once both predicates are read: the Go sites forbid 'index != 0 ⇒ smoke'; the SPA applies 'index != 0 ⇒ not idle ⇒ tint', which is verbatim the domain's own SmokeSiren.IsActive rule (smoke.go:151-158). The structural half of the title is true but is not a duplicate: the thresholds exist only in TypeScript and the rule names only in Go — one datum on each side of an API string, nothing that can drift numerically. Residue worth its own entry, not this one: nothing checks that every StateColorRule emitted by quantity.go has a case in state-color.ts (grep for state_color_rule finds no cross-language guard; an unknown rule silently returns undefined), and the repo carries two contradictory VALUE_LISTs for this parameter — hmenum/smoke_alarm_status.go:11-14 pins four values and says a label no paramset carries gets no constant, while tests/contract/wire_snapshots/{generator,snapshot_pin,reference_compare}_test.go and derived_binary.go assume a five-value list with IDLE_ON at index 1. Which the device declares is a value the repo does not carry consistently; I did not need it, since IsActive treats IDLE_ON as active too.

killed.title: The store decides which CCU parameters are energy meters and which of them are cumulative
killed.why: Sameness fails, and the claimed divergence proves too much. The MQTT rule table is a per-parameter Home Assistant entity description spanning ~200 parameters (water, gas, illuminance, voltage...); energyParameters is the bind list of one SQL filter feeding one fold. They are two rules that share a shape, not one rule copied. Under the finding's own logic the two sets 'already disagree' about WATER_VOLUME (total_increasing, L, :250), GAS_VOLUME (:248), IEC_POWER (:224) and every other classified parameter - a set difference that trivially exists between any two sets with no equality obligation is not drift. Neither existing shared source can produce the store's set: the quantity table omits ENERGY_COUNTER_FEED_IN entirely and the MQTT table folds feed-in onto consumption, so the consumed-vs-feed-in split the endpoint exists to compute has exactly one home today, which is where it is. The one leg the candidate itself conceded is guarded (energy_parameters_test.go:21-48, set equality both ways), and the remaining observation - GET /api/v1/energy ignores IEC_ENERGY_COUNTER and GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER rows the recorder does persist by default (internal/config/config.go:382-390: empty Include records everything numeric) - is a coverage limit of the energy endpoint that assets/openapi.yaml:4536-4539 documents by enumeration, not a duplicated classification that drifted. It is a feature request (kWh and m3 support, plus a new hmenum constant), and belongs in the backlog as one, not as a duplication defect against the store.

killed.title: SPA rendering concepts and hard-coded English/German labels sit inside the LINK parameter classifier
killed.why: Both halves survive as observations and die as defects. The en/de branch is the documented, layer-wide shape of the ui-schema adapter (server resolves labels for the request locale), not a bypass sited in the classifier, and the third-locale cost cannot be incurred at runtime — both catalogues are compile-time embedded with exactly en and de, and the SPA's own catalogue would need the same edit. The three duplicated strings are read by two different mechanisms on mutually exclusive render paths (tabs when >1 keypress group, heading fallback when exactly 1), one deliberately client-resolved so it stays current when the schema refetch is suppressed over a dirty form; drift between them would change a heading in one channel versus a tab in another, with no wire, contract or behavioural effect. That is a cosmetic near-duplicate with a rationale, not a backlog entry. The struct-mixing half the finding already concedes as least damaging: time_selector_type's camelCase spelling is pinned by the published REST contract (assets/openapi.yaml:7906, types.ts:193), so the Go constant cannot be renamed unilaterally regardless of where it lives.

killed.title: cdpkind encodes SPA widget vocabulary inside internal/model — its own doc says the kind is a north-bound concern
killed.why: The doc sentence is stale, the placement is not. A live domain consumer (internal/alarm, no north imports) makes internal/model the correct home; moving the package to north would invert the layering for that consumer. The candidate's own corrected damage story leaves nothing observable: token export is generated behind a CI freshness gate, and the one genuinely silent path it names (a new concrete Custom-DP type falling through the type-switch to KindUnknown — no guard exists for that, confirmed: cdpkind's tests are per-variant tables, no exhaustiveness test over concrete types) is entirely independent of which directory the package sits in. Residual worth at most a comment fix: kind.go:10-11 'The kind is a UI / north-bound concern, not a model concern' is contradicted by internal/alarm/candidates.go:124.

killed.title: REST/WS wire-identity grammar (PARAM@channel) is defined inside internal/model/custom
killed.why: The remedy does not touch the damage. The only damage the finding can still name is the un-guarded leg between the code and the hand-written OpenAPI prose (openapi.yaml:8065, :8093) — and that risk is identical whether the function lives in internal/model/custom or internal/north, because no guard on that leg exists in either place. Moving files creates no guard; if anything is actionable here it is a prose↔code pin, which is a different finding with a different site list. On top of that, the premise is factually weakened (two of four production consumers are in internal/central/adapter, not north) and the uniqueness computation is genuinely model-side. Per the damage bite: a placement that cannot drift observably, whose relocation changes no guard, is not a backlog entry.

killed.title: An HA device_class enum is the model's classification type and the source for a Matter attribute
killed.why: Killed on two independent bites. (1) The divergence is not a defect: the fold of damper/garage into RollerShade is forced by the target enum, not caused by the HA coupling. matter.js TypeEnum (window-covering-cluster.element.ts:151-162) and EndProductTypeEnum (:165-190) carry no damper and no garage member, so a bespoke OpenCCU-Loom cover enum with a first-class Damper constant would fold to exactly the same byte at exactly this call site. The candidate reasoned about the fold without reading the vocabulary it folds into. (2) The divergence is unreachable: coverTypeFor / coverEndProductTypeFor are called only from coverWCServer.MatterRead (matter.go:458/:460), and the only variants a running daemon can put in that field are VariantShutter and VariantWindow — both map to Shutter/RollerShutter, distinct and correct. The one production constructor that sets a folded-group variant (init.go:350, VariantShade) builds a Blind, whose server hard-codes TiltBlindLift/InteriorBlind and never reads the field. So no deployed configuration can produce the byte-identical outcome the candidate describes; the candidate conceded this in its honesty bound and kept medium anyway. Structurally this is also the shape the rules classify as not-a-duplicate: one datum — the cover's physical form — rendered by two callers into two target vocabularies of different granularity (HA device_class, which distinguishes damper; Matter TypeEnum, which does not). VariantString and coverTypeFor are the EnumLabel/EnumLabelFromWire pair, each right for its consumer, not one rule written twice. What survives is real but not a medium defect: the doc comment names an HA enum as the type's provenance, which is a naming/provenance wart on a domain type that in fact classifies physical cover form; and `default-signifies-exhaustive: true` means a future variant added to the iota block would silently take the default branch in both switches, yielding a valid-but-wrong RollerShade rather than a compile error. That is a latent low-severity ergonomic risk on an enum whose last member was added with no device mapping (init.go:314-319 says so explicitly), not an actionable divergence today.

killed.title: Home Assistant vocabulary is the core's own taxonomy in pkg/hmenum and pkg/hmevent
killed.why: The finding's measurable support does not hold. Its severity rationale is a two-part claim — an untyped `State string` can carry an unrecognised token, and nothing tests what happens then — and both parts are false against the current tree: the value space is closed by construction (single producer, two total mapping functions over nine constants), and the unknown-token branch is pinned by a named test that also documents the refusal-to-guess as intended (statemap.go:72-74 states it in the function doc). The Quantity/ValueBehavior half the first pass already recorded as overstated is refuted outright by the adapter tables at internal/north/mqtt/discovery_metadata.go:15-74 and by the pressure→atmospheric_pressure divergence, which I reproduced by reading both files. What remains after both kills is doc-level prose in pkg naming an integration target (quantity.go:87, alarm.go:50, hmevent/alarm.go:138), backed by a design note the comments cite, with real adapters (alarmpanel.StateToken, the mqtt maps) standing between the domain enums and the HA wire — plus one untyped struct field whose codomain no in-repo path can escape. Nothing observable would change if any of it "drifted", because there is exactly one mapping table and one inverse, both in internal/model/alarmpanel/statemap.go. Not a backlog entry.

killed.title: climate_link_peer_refresh re-implements the device-address split instead of calling hmtypes.DeviceAddress, and no guard covers it
killed.why:
Refuted on sameness and on damage-direction.

1. Not one rule. hmtypes.DeviceAddress cuts at the FIRST separator; the closure cuts at the LAST. On the CCU grammar these coincide, but they are different rules, and the repo has already ruled on this exact class: backwards-searching splitters on link paths are recorded as a separate rule that must NOT be folded until what they receive is established. The prescribed remedy ("call hmtypes.DeviceAddress") is the guess the ratchet declines to make — and applying it would change behaviour for multi-separator addresses.

2. The drift story runs backwards. The finding says: if hmtypes.DeviceAddress is corrected for multi-separator link addresses, this copy "silently keeps the old rule" and resolveChannel returns nil. Reading both paths on "A:B:1": the closure returns "A:B" — which is already the multi-separator-tolerant answer such a correction would produce — while hmtypes returns "A". The closure is the forward rule; hmtypes is the site that would need correcting. So the named damage (nil channel, lost Climate peer subscriptions, stale activity field) cannot arise from the drift as described.

3. No divergence on any input that can occur. Under pkg/hmtypes/address.go:20 (`^[0-9a-zA-Z-]{5,20}:\d{1,3}$`) the device part carries no colon, so LastIndex == first colon and both return identically. The two constructed divergences do no damage: "A:B:1" favours the closure (see 2), and ":1" (closure returns ":1", hmtypes returns "") fails `unit.ModelRegistry.Get` either way, yielding the same nil.

4. The "no guard covers it" half is factually right but is not a defect. The guard matches only top-level `*ast.FuncDecl` whose name contains "deviceaddress" (address_rule_single_source_test.go:57-58); `resolveChannel` is a FuncLit inside `WireClimateLinkPeerRefresh`, so it is invisible. That is a coverage gap in the ratchet's bookkeeping — a fourth backwards-searcher carrying the open question the ratchet tracks, unlisted in `addressSplittersOutsideHmtypes` — not evidence that the closure implements the wrong rule. Widening the guard to FuncLits would land this entry in the excused map alongside its three siblings, changing no production code.

killed.title: climate_link_peer_refresh and Unit.RenameChannel run the same registry lookup with opposite splitting rules; neither is visible to the address guard
killed.why: Killed on two of the five bites. (1) Sameness: this is not one rule spelled twice. central.go:1107 reproduces the canonical hmtypes.DeviceAddress rule (strings.Cut, first colon) inline; the climate closure is the deviant one. Pairing them as symmetric copies reverses the polarity — the actionable item is the closure against hmtypes, which is finding #0, and this adds nothing to it. (2) Divergence: input ":1" cannot reach RenameChannel — the address is built as deviceAddr + ":" + itoa(channelNo) after deviceAddr already hit ModelRegistry, and Put refuses an empty address (internal/central/registry/model_registry.go:28-33), so the composed string never starts with a colon. Input "CCU:DEV001:1" reaches it only if a device is registered under a colon-bearing key; no source I read carries that (no production code calls hmtypes.IsDeviceAddress or IsChannelAddress — the only ModelRegistry.Put caller is internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:611, unvalidated), and the finding's own reachability evidence was a test of a different function. (3) Damage: on every key the registry can actually hold, first-colon and last-colon splits of key + ":" + digits are identical, and on any hypothetical diverging address both sites simply miss and return nil / skip. The guard-blindness observation is true but is already the substance of #0.

killed.title: schedule adapter parses the channel-address grammar itself, with different semantics from pkg/hmtypes.SplitChannelAddress
killed.why: Refuted on its load-bearing premise. The finding's novelty is "the guard cannot see them"; a second guard sees them, names them, and pins them by path with the divergence written out. The finding attacked only the name-filtered guard and missed the shape-based one in the same directory — the one written specifically to close that filter's blind spot. The behavioural facts survive but carry no new information: the ratchet already records that the three copies disagree on sentinel and scan direction. Acting on the finding as written would also violate this repo's missing-input rule. Folding the adapter into hmtypes changes the no-channel answer from 0 to -1, and channel 0 is a real CCU channel for device-level parameters, not a sentinel. Which is correct depends on what the WS schedule call sites actually receive — a value neither the code nor the tests carry, which is exactly why the ratchet says "recorded, not blessed". On damage, the residual is thin: a malformed address from a WS client yields a domain lookup miss surfaced as a CommandErrorInternal, not a wrong-device write. Note also that the "three copies, three answers" framing conflates two different contracts: hmtypes.SplitChannelAddress returns an ok flag with -1 meaning "absent" (address.go:84-98), which is a different signature and a different question, not a drifted copy of the same rule. And coordinators/event.go is a documented deliberate variant whose device half already delegates — event.go:543 "return hmtypes.DeviceAddress(channelAddress)", with the channel-half reason stated at :539-542.

killed.title: CCU install-mode flavour 1 is a named constant on the hub path and a bare literal on the device-admin path, both live, in the same package
killed.why: Refuted on damage, and with it on sameness. The quote is accurate and both sites are live, so the finding survives the first two bites — but the two sites are not two writers of one datum that can observably drift, because only one of them reaches the CCU. `mode` is read by exactly one branch of the only CCU-facing backend (ccu_extended.go:105, XML with an empty deviceAddress); the device-admin path is structurally incapable of entering that branch, since both its entry points require a resolvable device address. The candidate's own drift experiment, carried out by reading, changes one call's wire bytes and leaves the other two byte-identical — no behaviour split on the pairing window, no data loss, nothing observable. Candidate declared medium; post-attack it is not worth a backlog entry as a duplication finding. What does remain, and is a different defect, is the false wire-shape comment at device_admin.go:378-381 plus the inert argument it documents — worth raising on its own terms, not as a drift risk.

killed.title: The canonical channel-address builder has zero production callers; six sites hand-build `+ ":0"`, and the channel set for LOW_BAT contradicts the declared device-level set
killed.why: Both halves fail. The builder is unused, so it cannot drift into production; the six ':0' sites are the fixed device-meta channel of a wire grammar pinned by regex and parser, and are half of a much larger population of idiomatic address concatenations. The LOW_BAT 'contradiction' produces no observable difference for any device model the daemon can meet, and the tolerant 0/1/2 scan is reference-sanctioned per-caller behaviour.

killed.title: The hub pseudo-address constants are referenced by no emitter; every unique_id producer passes the bare literal
killed.why: The hazard the finding rests on — edit the constant, emitters stay on the old segment, central prefix silently drops, two CCUs collide in retained HA discovery — cannot reach production: the cross-implementation golden contract test turns red on exactly that edit. What remains is a style nit (literal instead of the named constant) with no measurable failure mode, which is not a backlog entry.

killed.title: Two duration-string grammars with different acceptance; the strict one is test-only, so the lax one is what the REST surface actually enforces
killed.why: Killed on sameness and on the contract premise. The two "30"s are not one constant duplicated — maxDurationFactor bounds the numeral in the incoming string, MaxTimeBaseFactor bounds the wire DURATION_FACTOR after the encoder promotes to a coarser TimeBase, and the source states that distinction explicitly while sourcing the second to the device descriptor corpus (MIN 0 / MAX 31, with 31 reserved for the "Dauerhaft" sentinel at permanentFactor). "100s" is the counter-example: rejected by one, encoded as (SEC_10, 10) by the other, correctly, by design. The finding's distinctive damage claim — that the API accepts input "the contract comment does not allow" — dies on reading the comment, which is an ellipsis-terminated example list that explicitly delegates the mapping to the serializer. And the difference in acceptance is documented as intentional at two separate sites, one of which records the concrete data loss the strict grammar caused when it was on the read path. What remains is that validateDuration is unreachable in production, which is const-720-1's dead SimpleEntry.Validate under a second name, not an independent duplicate-constant defect.

killed.title: The (base 7, factor 31) "permanent" wire pair is declared independently in three packages, and only one of them carries the firmware provenance
killed.why: The quotes survive but the severity argument does not. Drift in this pair fails loudly at the first lock-schedule save (`slot N: invalid duration "31h"`), not silently, so the copies cannot rot undetected -- and the third copy is structurally forced by the weekprofile->schedule import direction. What remains is three literals of a firmware fact that changes only when the firmware encoding changes, with a loud detector already in place. Not worth a backlog entry as stated.

killed.title: OnOffPlugInUnit device type and its LT-gated OnOff block hand-declared in three projection packages
killed.why: Refuted as a separate backlog entry, not on its facts. It is the same duplication counted twice: the device-type constant and the OnOff block live in one const block per package, so a dedup either moves both or neither, and the candidate's own note says to judge them as one. Its factual content is confirmed under const-0x0006-1, which covers the same three packages plus internal/model/custom/light. Acting on both would produce two edits to the same const blocks.

killed.title: The parameter set that triggers an availability republish is decided in the event bridge, separately from the set that computes availability
killed.why: Killed on the divergence bite. The claim is "the copies are already unequal in both directions"; they are not. The relation is a strict superset — {UNREACH, STICKY_UNREACH, CONFIG_PENDING} ⊃ {UNREACH, STICKY_UNREACH} — with no element of the computation set missing from the trigger set. The candidate concedes the only actual extra (CONFIG_PENDING) cannot move `online`, and the consequential direction is stated as a hypothesis ("a reachability input added to isReachableWith and not to the literal switch"), not as something present in the tree. Killed a second time on sameness: these are two questions, not two spellings of one. The bridge asks "which parameter events warrant re-evaluating and republishing availability", and deliberately answers with a superset — CONFIG_PENDING also lifts the `if !online { return }` suppression at :1671-1673, so an offline transition on a config-pending device still reaches the retained topic. The model asks "what is the verdict", and its inputs include hmenum.ForcedDeviceAvailability, which is not a wire parameter and has no place in a trigger set. A set that must contain a non-parameter input cannot be the same set as one keyed on wire parameter names. hmenum.RelevantInitParameters is a fourth list with the same membership but a documented and genuinely different purpose (parameter.go:283-287: the channel-0 parameters the bootstrap pass must fetch, in fetch order) — reconciling the three would force the boot fetch and the republish trigger to move together, which is a coupling, not a fix. What does survive here is smaller and different from the finding: the doc comment at eventbridge.go:1036-1037 ("reports whether a parameter change implies the per-device availability has flipped") is false for CONFIG_PENDING, which never flips the verdict. That is a comment-claim defect for the pre-release sweep, not a duplication to dedupe.

killed.title: "Which parameter spelling means battery low" is decided in five independent places; LOWBAT_SENSOR is in three of them and absent from two live consumers
killed.why: The count and the flagship divergence both fail. (1) Sameness: two of the five sites are not alias sets. internal/parameter/metadata.go is a verbatim port of the reference's parameter→Quantity table (aiohomematic data_point_metadata.py:272) and internal/north/mqtt/entity_descriptions_table.go:180 is one row of the HA discovery registry keyed to an HARegistryDescription payload; neither could delegate to a shared isLowBattery() without still enumerating its own entries. This is exactly the test the candidate itself applied to reject hmenum.DeviceChannel0Parameters, and these two fail it for the same reason. (2) Liveness of the divergence: availability.lowBattery() iterates channels :0/:1/:2 only (availability.go:242). LOWBAT_SENSOR occurs in the corpus solely on :3 and :4, so adding it to that name list would change nothing on the only devices any repo source describes — the omission has no observable effect. (3) Sameness at the semantic level: LOW_BAT/LOWBAT are device-level MAINTENANCE flags; LOWBAT_SENSOR is a VALUES parameter on a SENSOR channel next to HUMIDITY and RSSI, i.e. the battery of an attached sensor. Device availability and device-scoped alarm SensorHealth reading only the device-level flags is a defensible reading of a different datum, not drift. What survives is thin: three literal name lists (classify.go:116-119, availability.go:249, inputs.go:151) with no shared constant and no crossing test. That is a low-severity tidy, not the medium-severity five-way contradiction claimed.

killed.title: The `<digits>_WP_<FIELD>` identity rule is implemented four times with three different group-number boundaries, and the package that documents itself as owning the question is not consulted by the UI filter
killed.why: The duplication is real; every claimed consequence of it dies on reachability. (1) The `X_WP_LEVEL` leg is killed outright by the caller. channel_keys.go:224 has no digit gate, and on `LONG_WP_OPTIONS` it would indeed treat the key as a WP cell and drop it — but FilterRawScheduleByFields has exactly one production caller, schedules.go:1025, and its input `raw` is produced by serializeSimpleScheduleWithDomain, whose keys are built as `fmt.Sprintf("%02d_WP_", slotNo)` (schedules.go:778). The map is daemon-generated and cannot contain a non-digit prefix, so the missing gate is unreachable by construction, not latent drift. (2) The `0_WP_LEVEL` leg rests on an input no repo source carries. Across 77 distinct `_WP_` prefixes in the corpus, every digit prefix is two-digit `01`–`40`; there is no group 0 and no single-digit group. On every key that actually occurs, isSchedulePattern, SimpleGroupNo and ExtractSupportedScheduleFields agree — including on LONG/SHORT_WP_OPTIONS, which all three correctly treat as ordinary parameters. The candidate concedes reachability is unestablished, and that concession is fatal to a divergence claim. (3) What genuinely survives: paramShouldRender does not delegate to weekprofile.IsParameterName, whose doc at rawconvert.go:81-84 names exactly that job ("Callers outside this package use it to keep week-profile cells out of per-parameter surfaces"), and the two grammars would drift silently if the shared shape ever changed. That is a low-severity tidy with a hypothetical failure mode, not the medium-severity three-way contradiction the title asserts.
